title: Peutz-Jeghers Syndrome
abstract:
Clinical characteristics

Peutz-Jeghers syndrome (PJS) is characterized by the association of gastrointestinal (GI) polyposis including distinctive arborized smooth muscle polyps, mucocutaneous pigmentation, and cancer predisposition. PJS-type hamartomatous polyps are most common in the small intestine (in order of prevalence: jejunum, ileum, and duodenum), but can also occur in the stomach, large bowel, and extraintestinal sites including the renal pelvis, bronchi, gall bladder, nasal passages, bladder, and ureters. GI polyps can result in chronic bleeding, anemia, recurrent obstruction, and intussusception requiring repeated laparotomy and bowel resection. Mucocutaneous hyperpigmentation presents in childhood as dark blue to dark brown macules around the mouth, eyes, and nostrils, in the perianal area, and on the buccal intestinal mucosa. Hyperpigmented macules on the fingers and toes are common. The macules may fade in puberty and adulthood. Recognition of the distinctive skin manifestations is important, especially in individuals who have PJS as the result of a de novo pathogenic variant, as these skin findings often predate GI signs and symptoms. Individuals with PJS are at increased risk for a wide variety of epithelial malignancies (colorectal, gastric, pancreatic). Females are at risk for breast cancer, sex cord tumors with annular tubules (SCTATs), a benign neoplasm of the ovaries, and a gastric-type adenocarcinoma (adenoma malignum) of the cervix, a rare aggressive cancer. Males occasionally develop large-cell calcifying Sertoli cell tumors of the testes, which secrete estrogen and can lead to gynecomastia, advanced skeletal age, and, ultimately, short stature if untreated.

Diagnosis/testing

The diagnosis of PJS is based on clinical findings. Identification of a heterozygous pathogenic variant in STK11 by molecular genetic testing confirms the diagnosis and allows for testing of at-risk relatives and prenatal/preimplantation genetic testing.

Management

Treatment of manifestations: Routine endoscopic surveillance with polypectomy decreases the frequency of emergency laparotomy and bowel loss resulting from intussusception. Small bowel imaging includes video capsule endoscopy (VCE) and/or MRI enteroclysis. Magnetic resonance enterography (MRE) may be used if MRI is not tolerated, but MRE is less sensitive than MRI for polyps smaller than 1 cm. Balloon-assisted enteroscopy allows for removal of distal small bowel polyps. Occasionally intraoperative enteroscopy and enterotomy is needed for removal of large distal small bowel polyps. It is advised to remove polyps >15-20 mm or smaller if causing symptoms. Intussusception and malignancies should be treated in the standard manner. Surveillance: Surveillance in people with PJS is preferably done in a center of expertise. Children and adolescents – colonoscopy and upper endoscopy at age eight years; if normal, resume GI surveillance at age 18 years and continue every one to three years. If polyps are detected at initial examination, repeat every one to three years based on size, number, and histopathology of polyps. Small bowel surveillance by VCE or MRI enteroclysis (or MRE if not tolerated) every one to three years based on findings beginning at age eight years. Examination for precocious puberty in females annually beginning at diagnosis or at least by age eight years. Testicular examination and examination for feminizing changes in males annually beginning at diagnosis or at least by age eight years through adulthood. Adults – colonoscopy, upper endoscopy, and small bowel examination by VCE or MRI enteroclysis (or MRE if not tolerated) every one to three years. Clinical breast examination in women every six to 12 months beginning at age 25 years; breast MRI with contrast in women annually from age 25 to 50 years (or if breast MRI with contrast is contraindicated or unavailable, breast ultrasound from age 25 to 30 years and mammography from age 30 to 50 years); consider tomosynthesis and ultrasound for those with dense breast tissue annually from age 30 to 50 years; mammography with consideration of annual breast contrast MRI for dense breasts every one to two years from age 50 to 75 years. Pelvic examination with pap smear and cytology (including those with negative HPV testing) in women annually beginning at age 25 years. Pancreatic imaging with endoscopic ultrasound or MRI is suggested annually beginning at age 40 years in a framework of a study or registry. For lung cancer, provide education regarding signs/symptoms of lung cancer and importance of smoking cessation. Testicular examination and examination for feminizing changes in males annually; testicular ultrasound for those with abnormal findings on examination. Agents/circumstances to avoid: Due to the increased risk for cervical, lung, and pancreatic cancer, smoking should be avoided. Evaluation of relatives at risk: Evaluate apparently asymptomatic older and younger at-risk relatives (including parents, sibs, and children) of an affected individual in order to identify as early as possible those who would benefit from initiation of surveillance, treatment, and preventative measures. If the pathogenic variant in the family is known, offer molecular genetic testing to at-risk relatives. If the pathogenic variant in the family is not known, offer clinical diagnostic evaluations.

Genetic counseling

PJS is inherited in an autosomal dominant manner. Most individuals diagnosed with PJS have an affected parent; some individuals represent apparently simplex cases and may have the disorder as the result of a de novo pathogenic variant. If a parent of the proband is affected and/or is known to have the pathogenic variant identified in the proband, the risk to the sibs is 50%. To date, all reported individuals with pathogenic variants in STK11 have shown clinical manifestations; however, variable expressivity is common among affected family members. If the STK11 pathogenic variant has been identified in an affected family member, predictive testing for at-risk family members and prenatal/preimplantation genetic testing are possible.
authors: Amos CI, Wagner A.

title: 3D Closed‐Loop Navigation of Magnetic Microswimmers Using Vision‐Derived Depth Feedback
abstract: Despite growing interest in autonomous microswimmer navigation, achieving closed‐loop 3D control remains challenging because simple, real‐time depth feedback compatible with standard microscopy is unavailable. This work presents a unified multimodal control framework integrating Model Predictive Control (MPC) with A* path planning for both surface‐bound and free‐swimming locomotion of planar magnetic microswimmers. A propulsion‐only depth regulation strategy uses a signed Fourier‐domain blur metric from a single monocular microscope image to estimate axial position without magnetic gradients or volumetric imaging. This vision‐based method enables real‐time depth estimation and waypoint tracking with minimal computational cost. In experiments, the proposed controller achieved 3D closed‐loop navigation with a median planar error of 12–15 μm and overshoot of 20 ± 5 μm (mean ± SD, n ≥ 20). During fixed‐focus 3D swimming, depth regulation was maintained within an axial working window of approximately 200 μm. For surface locomotion, A*‐guided MPC completed obstacle‐rich routes about 40% faster than reactive MPC while maintaining 100% target‐reach success when a collision‐free path existed. These results demonstrate robust multimode transitions, depth‐aware 3D control, and high‐precision navigation using only propulsion and monocular vision, providing a foundation for future in vitro and ophthalmic applications.

title: 5G succeeds (setting up CCE home delivery service) : pilot study of developing 5G connected CCE home delivery service
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the third most common cancer and the second leading cause of cancer-related mortality. The COVID-19 pandemic has disrupted endoscopy services, leading to prolonged waiting times and an increased risk of delayed CRC diagnoses. To address these issues, the 5G SUCCEEDS pilot study explored the feasibility of delivering Colon Capsule Endoscopy (CCE) directly to patients' homes using advanced 5G technology. This study aimed to determine if CCE could be effectively performed at home, thus eliminating the need for hospital visits. It also assessed patient acceptability of the home-based CCE service, compared its diagnostic efficiency to traditional colonoscopy and evaluated the carbon footprint of different diagnostic pathways. The study was conducted at University Hospital Coventry and Warwickshire, in collaboration with WM5G, NHS Arden& GEM CSU, and Corporate Health International UK. Patients referred from primary care with low to intermediate risk for CRC were invited to participate. A 5G-enabled CCE Smartbox was delivered to their homes, facilitating remote procedure management and communication. The study aimed to recruit 25 patients, and with enhanced connectivity, participants benefited from virtual assistance, real-time equipment monitoring, and faster identification of irregularities. The results indicated that home-based CCE is a feasible and effective alternative to traditional hospital-based procedures. The use of advanced technology improved patient satisfaction and supported a patient-centred approach to CRC diagnostics. This innovative method aligns with the NHS X digital strategy, offering a viable solution to reduce delays in CRC diagnosis while promoting more sustainable and efficient healthcare delivery.

title: A Bio‐Inspired Visual Sensor With UV‐to‐NIR Fusion for Enhanced Recognition in Autonomous Driving Systems
abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional vision systems for autonomous driving are hindered by energy‐inefficient and latency‐prone architectures due to physically segregated sensing, memory, and processing modules. Here, we report a bio‐inspired vision sensor that emulates the spectral adaptation mechanism of the Pacific salmon retina leveraging a van der Waals heterojunction of NbNiTe 5 and black phosphorus (BP). Operating at zero bias, the device exhibits intrinsic wavelength‐dependent antagonistic photoresponses: negative photoconductance under 365 nm ultraviolet illumination (mimicking visual suppression in bright environments) and positive photoconductance under 820 nm near‐infrared light (emulating visual enhancement in dim conditions). This built‐in adaptability enables robust environmental perception across extreme illumination scenarios, from high‐glare daylight to low‐light nights. Furthermore, we integrated this sensor into a full functional system that unifies image perception, non‐volatile storage, and in‐sensor processing. When deployed for traffic scenario analysis, a convolutional neural network trained on features extracted by the sensor achieved 96% classification accuracy, with performance scaling proportionally to the system's noise suppression capability. Our work establishes a practical strategy for high‐contrast bidirectional photonic synapses and highlights the potential of biomimetic systems in neuromorphic vision — particularly for autonomous driving and intelligent surveillance, where reliable operation across diverse spectral environments is critical.

title: A Deep Learning based Severity Grading of Diabetic Retinopathy using Data Fusion Approach
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy is a major contributor to blindness. Traditional diabetic retinopathy detection methods typically rely on time-consuming and manual examination of retinal images. In contrast, modern developments in deep learning have revolutionized this process by enabling automated classification of retinal images with high accuracy. This research introduces a 5-stage severity grading framework for classifying diabetic retinopathy through the use of data fusion and deep learning. This study incorporates 3 openly accessible datasets for diabetic retinopathy analysis: Messidor-2, IDRiD and APTOS 2019. These datasets are first combined and then preprocessing is applied to this fused dataset. CLAHE is used to enhance the overall clarity of images. To counteract class imbalance, we employed SMOTE in the dataset. Augmentation techniques including rotation, zooming and flipping are applied to enhance the diversity of the dataset. For classification, we proposed a Convolutional Neural Network called D-Retino. Composed of four blocks, this model contains fully connected, max pooling and convolutional layers. The model's training process is fine-tuned using the Adam optimization algorithm. D-Retino demonstrated an impressive 95.24% test accuracy in distinguishing between five diabetic retinopathy grades. Moreover, results obtained by this model were benchmarked against some state-of-the-art techniques and D-Retino yielded superior performance.

title: A Hybrid YOLO-NAS Technology in Transforming Autonomous Vehicle Manufacturing
abstract: Object detection, the core fundamental task of the environmental perception module for autonomous driving, still faces a bottleneck that is difficult to break through. Four types of interference, namely severe weather, low illumination, partial occlusion, and sensor noise, all reduce detection accuracy, which in turn weakens the reliability of core decision-making for safe driving. This study proposes a hybrid perception scheme based on YOLO-NAS that meets the indispensable requirement of real-time performance. By integrating the NAS-optimized architecture and connecting multi-step processing in sequence, the scheme improves the robustness of recognition in complex scenarios. The proposed framework was evaluated on the nuScenes autonomous driving benchmark using the official dataset split. Experimental evaluation under daytime, nighttime, and adverse weather conditions demonstrates that the proposed approach consistently achieves detection accuracies of 94–96%, outperforming YOLOv8 (84–89%) and YOLOv7 (79–81%). Overall, YOLO-NAS provides performance gains of approximately 5–10% over YOLOv8 and 13–25% over YOLOv7 while maintaining stable inference and improved robustness against partially occluded objects and challenging visual conditions. These results demonstrate that incorporating NAS into the YOLO detection pipeline improves perception reliability and detection consistency, offering a practical solution for enhancing the safety, robustness, and real-world deployment of autonomous vehicle perception systems.

title: A Multimodal Autonomic Sensing Framework for Objective Assessment of Patient Responses to Dental Pulp Stimulation
abstract: Patient responses to dental pulp testing, ranging from no sensation to intense pain, provide important information for assessing pulp status in endodontic diagnosis. However, pain is a subjective sensory and emotional experience that varies considerably across individuals and can be difficult to communicate. We investigated whether complementary autonomic signals could support objective assessment of responses during dental examination. Forty-nine patients underwent cold pulp testing, yielding no-response, mild-response, and intense-response conditions. The framework integrated ECG-derived skin nerve activity (SKNA) and R-R intervals (RRI), together with electrodermal activity (EDA), using temporal convolutional network encoders with attention-based mid-level fusion. Individual baseline signals and subject-level covariates, including anxiety scores and biological sex, were also incorporated. The framework achieved 80.2% balanced accuracy, 75.2% sensitivity, and 85.2% specificity for binary classification of no response versus mild or intense response. For three-class classification, it achieved 60.0% balanced accuracy and a 58.8% macro-averaged F1 score. Ablation and attention-weight analyses indicated that EDA contributed most strongly to model performance, followed by RRI, while SKNA improved balanced accuracy by approximately five percentage points. Age was significantly associated with model performance. These findings support the feasibility of multimodal autonomic sensing for objective, non-invasive assessment of responses to dental pulp stimulation.
authors: Youngsun Kong; Yubin Choi; Dongjin Song; Dong-Guk Shin; I-Ping Chen; Ki Chon

title: A Multimodal Deep Learning Framework for Early Prediction of Dental Restoration Failure Using Intraoral Scans and Radiographs
abstract: The longevity of dental restorations is affected by a complex interplating factors such as restoration type, tooth morphology, caries activity, marginal adaptation, occlusal loading, periodontal condition, patient-related factors, and the quality of the restoration procedure. Conventional assessment of restoration prognosis is largely based on clinical examination and radiographic interpretation, as well as the experience of the clinician. While artificial intelligence has shown considerable promise in restorative dentistry and prosthodontics, most existing approaches tackle isolated tasks such as caries detection, tooth segmentation, restoration identification, crown design, or prediction based on structured clinical variables. An integrated model that combines three-dimensional intraoral surface information, twodimensional radiographic information, and clinical variables for early restoration-failure prediction is still underexplored. The present study proposes a novel Multimodal Explainable Restoration Failure Prediction Network (MERF-Net) for estimating the probability of restoration failure within a predefined follow-up period. The proposed framework comprises a three-dimensional transformer-based encoder for intraoral scans, a convolutional vision transformer for dental radiographs, and a clinical-feature encoder for patient and restoration characteristics. A cross-modal attention mechanism enables the learning of relationships among morphological, radiographic, and clinical representations. A temporal survival-learning module, in turn, estimates restoration-failure risk across time. The model incorporates SHAP-based feature attribution and Grad-CAM-based visual explanations for providing clinically interpretable evidence for the model's predictions. The proposed system is designed to predict the failure probability and identify high-risk restorations while providing an explanation as to the major contributing factors. The framework is compared with logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, multilayer perceptron, CNN, and conventional survival-analysis models in an illustrative experimental configuration in which the proposed multimodal framework could offer improved discrimination compared with single-modality models. The proposed approach has potential to facilitate personalized recall planning, early intervention, restoration monitoring, and precision restorative dentistry. However, further prospective multi-center validation is required before clinical deployment.

title: A Reproducible Deep Learning Framework for Explainable Cataract Screening from Retinal Fundus Images
abstract: Despite the potential of cataract surgery for visual rehabilitation, cataract is still a major contributor to preventable low vision and specialist-led screening programmers are challenging to implement in communities with poor ophthalmic services. In this study, a research prototype of end-to-end Deep Learning model for binary classification of cataract from retinal fundus images was developed and tested. This contribution is not a new backbone architecture, but rather a reproducible pipeline, which combines the data integrity checking, ophthalmic images standardization, class-aware transfer learning, validation-only threshold selection, statistical evaluation, explainable artificial intelligence, and deployable single image inference. The public collection on Kaggle was examined and the duplicate repository tree was removed and 400 unique images (300 normal, 100 cataract) were isolated. Each image was then resized to 224×224 RGB with black padding in order to preserve aspect-ratio and CLAHE was used to enhance the images. The training, validation and test images were acquired by a fixed stratified split, which resulted in 280 training, 60 validation and 60 test images. The classes were trained using the same class weighted fashion in ResNet50, VGG19 and InceptionV3. Both VGG19 and ResNet50 model got 88.33% test accuracy at the traditional 0.50 threshold, with VGG19 having the highest ROC-AUC (0.9259) and specificity (95.56%) while ResNet50 had higher sensitivity (73.33%) and F1-score (75.86%). A validation-only Youden-J threshold of 0.03 resulted in a shift of the final operating point of VGG19 towards screening sensitivity – 86.67%, with accuracy of 78.33%, specificity of 75.56%, F1-score of 66.67%, ROC-AUC of 0.9259, and PR-AUC of 0.8752. Two thousand iterations of the stratified bootstrap, paired comparisons, calibration analysis and review of the confusion matrix were performed. All the test images were explained using the grad-CAM, but the faithfulness using occlusion was mixed so it was interpreted with caution. The package reproduced exactly all the test probabilities and decisions and it is now possible to do quality-aware single-image screening. This system should not be considered to be a clinically validated system, but rather an explainable research prototype. It has a clear and strong advantage in the seamless integration of the following features: model comparison, threshold trade-offs, error analysis, deployment auditing, and all on a limited fundus dataset.
authors: Zahid Aziz; Abdullah Zahid

title: A Self-Adaptive Deep Learning Architecture for Autonomous Intelligence and Decision-Making in Complex Computational Environments
abstract: Intelligent systems that can adapt their decisions to changes in operating conditions are needed in dynamic computational environments, and conventional predictive models could fail if the states in the environment and the utility of the decisions change. This study developed and evaluated a reward-adaptive deep learning architecture for autonomous action selection under heterogeneous computational conditions. Sequential state, action, reward and throughput records were used and a quantitative computational design was applied. The benchmark performance was analysed in the context of DARA, ID and MIN policies, and the state-dependent decision behaviour was analysed with correlation and non-parametric statistical tests. A baseline deep neural network was compared with an architecture where the reward is adapted based on the training/validation/testing data, obtained from separate scenarios. Reward and autonomous action selection were highly related to the environmental state. The reward-adaptive model improved test accuracy from 0.5427 to 0.5946, macro F1 from 0.2876 to 0.3543, and weighted F1 from 0.5571 to 0.5763, although balanced accuracy decreased from 0.4414 to 0.3770. The mean expected reward was 8.80% higher than the baseline model. Two unseen scenarios showed improvement in generalization performance and one showed a decrease, indicating scenario-dependent adaptation. The results show that reward-guided deep learning can improve autonomous decision-making, both predictive and utility, and that it is still essential to have strong evaluation over heterogeneous states and action distributions.
authors: Rijo Jackson Tom; Junith Ahmed S; Indira Ramarao; Annu Sharma; Swaraj Satish Kadam; Baraka Mushubila Kamuhabwa; Murali Krishna Puttagunta

title: A Strategic Guide to AI in Healthcare
abstract: A Strategic Guide to AI in Healthcare provides a complete strategic architecture for understanding and implementing artificial intelligence across hospitals, health systems, and governments. While AI is advancing rapidly, most organisations lack the strategic frameworks, organisational readiness, and implementation know-how to adopt it safely and at scale. The book is therefore structured around the adoption journey. Part I builds awareness and technical literacy, sets out the landscape, and explains why so many AI integrations fail. Part II focuses on hospital-level strategy and implementation, with chapters on building the business case, AI literacy and training, running pilots, scaling to enterprise, workforce transformation, and governance and ethics. Part III extends these themes to government and national strategy, covering regulatory navigation, national data infrastructure and interoperability, and cybersecurity. Each of the 17 chapters combines theory with practitioner case studies (Mayo Clinic, Kaiser Permanente, the NHS AI Lab, WannaCry, Synnovis), structured exercises for executive education, and implementation checklists usable directly in board meetings, AI Governance Councils, and procurement reviews. A timely and important resource, the book will be essential reading for anyone responsible for the strategic development of hospitals or healthcare systems and for researchers in this field. Included with the text are updated online supplemental materials for faculty use including PowerPoint Slides and an instructor's manual, available at www.routledge.com/9781041373964 .
authors: Muthu Ramachandran

title: A Transnasal Endoscope for Robotically Assisted Gastroscopy
abstract: A robotic transnasal endoscope (TNE) is developed to improve minimally invasive access to the upper gastrointestinal (GI) tract and support early cancer detection. The device is 4.25 mm in diameter and is designed to be compatible with transnasal access while preserving diagnostic and interventional capability achievable with bigger peroral access devices. The distal segment incorporates permanent magnets that enable precise remote manipulation through externally applied magnetic fields. A tendon‐driven variable stiffness mechanism provides high compliance during navigation and controlled stiffening for enhanced pushability, stability, and shape control. The feasibility of using the TNE for upper GI endoscopy is demonstrated through in vitro and in vivo evaluations. The robotic TNE achieves full navigation of the upper GI tract, including retroflexions, pyloric passage, duodenal access, and tissue biopsy. Robust maneuverability is maintained across stiffness states, confirming reliable control during complex motions. This approach has the potential to increase patient acceptance of routine screening and expand access to minimally invasive GI interventions.
authors: Alexandre Mesot; Michelle Mattille; Sean Lyttle; Shannon Melissa Chan; Philip Wai Yan Chiu; Quentin Boehler; B.J. Nelson

title: A Two-Element Capsule Antenna for Near-Field Polarization MIMO in Wireless Capsule Endoscopy
abstract: Multiple-Input-Multiple-Output (MIMO) technology is considered to be a viable method for spectral efficiency and data rate enhancement in wireless communications. This article presents a two-element capsule antenna with orthogonal current distributions for polarization multiplexing in a wireless capsule endoscopy (WCE) application at 915 MHz. The proposed antenna was evaluated in a MIMO link where it served as the transmitter and an existing on-body antenna was the receiver. The performance was assessed in two distinct environments: an anatomically accurate human body model using full-wave (FW) simulations, and a homogeneous liquid tissue phantom, using both FW simulations and measurements. The former was used to evaluate the performance in a realistic environment and to demonstrate the superiority of the proposed capsule antenna against existing two-element antennas in the literature, while the latter aimed at verifying the antenna design by comparison of simulated and measured MIMO links. We studied channel capacity and eigenvalues for the comparisons. The MIMO link with the proposed antenna provided nearly doubled median channel capacity relative to a baseline single-input-single-output link, consistently in the simulations and measurements. Our results prove the suitability of the proposed antenna for polarization multiplexing and, in terms of channel capacity, establish it as the best conformal two-element capsule antenna design at 915 MHz.
authors: Pyry Kiviharju; Lauri Vähä-Savo; Clemens Icheln; Kenichi Takizawa; Katsuyuki Haneda

title: A case of reccurrent cytomegalovirus infection after kidney transplantation: a challenge in diagnosis and management
abstract: Introduction. Cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection is one of the most frequent infectious complications in kidney transplant recipients. It typically occurs within the first months after transplantation, particularly in high-risk serostatus mismatch cases (D+/R-) [1]. Despite antiviral prophylaxis, recurrent CMV infection can develop and is associated with increased morbidity, risk of graft dysfunction, and indirect effects such as opportunistic infections and acute rejection [2]. Case presentation. A 50-year-old woman underwent a deceased-donor kidney transplant. The donor was CMV seropositive, while the recipient was seronegative. Valganciclovir prophylaxis was initiated for 6 months. Immediate graft function was observed. From the early post-transplantation period onward, the patient developed recurrent CMV infections spanning several years, primarily manifesting as severe anemia in the absence of CMV DNAemia. The infection was diagnosed mainly by capsule endoscopy showing gastrointestinal involvement. Discussion. This case highlights recurrent CMV infection, where standard blood-based diagnostic methods were insufficient. Their sensitivity is reduced in cases of localized, tissue- invasive disease. Tissue-invasive CMV disease can occur without detectable viremia, but with other various manifestations depending on the organ involved [3]. Despite appropriate prophylaxis with valganciclovir, recurrent CMV disease continues to be reported, reflecting the limitations of current preventive strategies [2]. Conclusion. CMV disease cannot be excluded solely on the basis of negative laboratory findings. Persistent or unexplained clinical abnormalities, such as anemia - should prompt investigation for tissue-invasive disease. Endoscopic, histopathologic evaluation remain essential diagnostic tools in such contexts.
authors: Žygimantas Mickus; Eglė Dalinkevičienė

title: A case report: an unusual case of ulcerative intestinal IgG4-related disease with clinical features overlapping with probable intestinal Behcet’s disease
abstract: BACKGROUND: IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) is a systemic fibroinflammatory condition characterized by IgG4-positive plasma cell infiltration, typically presenting with organ enlargement or tumor-like masses. Luminal gastrointestinal involvement is rare, and ulcerative lesions are even less common. Overlap syndromes of IgG4-RD with other immune disorders have been reported, but overlap of its clinical features with those of intestinal Behcet's disease has not been documented. CASE PRESENTATION: A 62-year-old man with a history of recurrent oral ulcers presented with sudden hematochezia and hypovolemic shock. Imaging revealed sclerosing mesenteritis, and endoscopy identified multiple small intestinal ulcers. Histopathological examination of the resected intestinal segment demonstrated dense infiltration of IgG4-positive plasma cells (70/HPF, IgG4⁺/IgG⁺ ratio 42.3%), confirming intestinal IgG4-RD. The patient also met diagnostic criteria for probable intestinal Behcet's disease based on recurrent oral ulcers, crateriform intestinal ulcers, and histologic evidence of vasculitis. Following partial enterectomy and postoperative immunosuppressive therapy (prednisone and cyclophosphamide), the patient achieved sustained remission with no recurrence during the one-year follow-up. CONCLUSIONS: This is the first reported case of concurrent intestinal IgG4-RD and probable intestinal Behcet's disease. The overlapping presentation expands the clinical spectrum of IgG4-RD and suggests a potential pathogenic link between these two immune-mediated conditions.
authors: 战澍楷; Jing Yang; Wenlong Liang; Hongli Huang; Yongjian Zhou

title: A circRNA-microRNA-Pdcd1 axis drives microglial activation and retinal ganglion cell degeneration
abstract: Abstract Retinal ganglion cell (RGC) degeneration is the primary cause of vision loss, driven by the complicated effects of intrinsic neuronal damage and neuroinflammation. However, current single-target therapies fail to address these dual pathological challenges. CircRNAs, functioning through ceRNA networks, represent a multi-target intervention due to their stability. Here we show that, using whole‑transcriptome sequencing of optic nerve crush (ONC), we bioinformatically predicted nine candidate ceRNA networks. Among these, the network centered on circAgtpbp1 was significantly up-regulated post-injury, independent of its host gene. Mechanistically, circAgtpbp1 functions as a ceRNA by sequestering miR-3098-3p, thereby de-repressing the translation of PD-1 ( Pdcd1 ). In the ONC model, this upregulation of PD-1 protein amplifies microglial activation, creating a pathogenic non-cell-autonomous inflammatory amplification loop that drives RGC degeneration. Our findings not only uncover a novel circRNA-mediated mechanism in neurodegeneration but also identify the circAgtpbp1-miR-3098-3p-Pdcd1-microglia axis as a promising therapeutic target for neuroprotective interventions.
authors: Lanfang Sun; Xiaoyu Ke; Jingjing Yu; Jinfei Wei; Jiayi Gu; Zhou Wanchen; Yixin Cen; Jin Huang; Xiaoling Zhang; Jiaming Zhang; Shuo Zhang; Xiaojiang Liu; Yangyang Ji; Wentao Yan; Shaohui Pan; Meng Zhou; Wencan Wu

title: A comparative in vitro study on the accuracy of robotic arm mode versus dynamic navigation mode of an autonomous dental implant robot in the posterior mandibular region
abstract: Abstract Objective To investigate the application efficacy of the robotic arm mode versus the navigation mode of an autonomous dental implant robot in posterior mandibular implant surgery. Methods A total of 80 custom-designed resin models were divided into an experimental group (robotic arm mode) and a control group (dynamic navigation mode), with 40 models in each group. Implants were placed under the robotic arm mode and dynamic navigation mode, respectively. Postoperative cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) was performed to measure the deviations between the actual implant positions and the preoperatively planned positions, comparing the accuracy of the two modes in different types of unilateral posterior mandibular defects. Results: A total of 120 implants were placed in 80 models. In the robotic arm mode group, the entry point deviation, endpoint deviation, and angular deviation were 0.68 ± 0.22 mm, 0.76 ± 0.27 mm, and 1.24 ± 0.50°, respectively. In the dynamic navigation mode group, these deviations were 1.02 ± 0.31 mm, 1.12 ± 0.44 mm, and 2.36 ± 0.71°, respectively. Conclusion 1. Both the robotic arm mode and dynamic navigation mode showed high implant accuracy, indicating that both modes can be used for patients with different types of posterior dentition defects. 2. The accuracy of robotic arm mode-assisted implant surgery was significantly superior to that of dynamic navigation mode, suggesting that the robotic arm mode of the dental implant robot offers advantages in precision control.
authors: Honghong LIU; kunming LIU; mengmeng YOU; yingying ZHANG; Yanqing Wang; Zhihong Zhang

title: A diagnostic cascade from cholecystitis to Meckel's diverticulum rupture: a case report.
abstract: Background: Meckel's diverticulum (MD) is the most common congenital anomaly of the gastrointestinal tract, yet it rarely becomes symptomatic in adults. Perforation is an uncommon and often overlooked complication that may mimic more frequent abdominal conditions, particularly in the postoperative setting. MD presenting shortly after unrelated laparoscopic surgery is exceptionally rare and can pose a significant diagnostic challenge. Case presentation: A 36-year-old woman presented with acute right upper quadrant pain and was diagnosed with calculous cholecystitis. She underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy and was discharged after an uncomplicated recovery. On postoperative day 3, she returned with abdominal distension, bilious vomiting, and persistent pain. Imaging revealed a port-site hematoma but no clear source of obstruction or leak. Due to sustained leukocytosis and clinical deterioration, diagnostic laparoscopy was performed, revealing bilious peritonitis and a necrotic, perforated MD with terminal ileal herniation. Diverticulectomy was completed, and the patient recovered fully. Discussion: Perforated MD can closely mimic postoperative ileus, small bowel obstruction, or biliary pathology, leading to delayed diagnosis. Imaging modalities frequently fail to detect this condition, underscoring the limitations of relying solely on radiologic evaluation when symptoms persist. Although a direct causal link to recent laparoscopic surgery cannot be confirmed, postoperative mechanical and perfusion-related changes may contribute to diverticular compromise in susceptible individuals. Conclusion: This case highlights the need to consider MD complications in patients who deteriorate unexpectedly after abdominal surgery. When clinical findings are discordant with imaging, early diagnostic laparoscopy remains essential for accurate diagnosis and timely intervention.
authors: Lotfollah Abedini; Taha Negahdari; Sepehr Moradi; Reza Hosseinpour

title: A duodenal mass with biliary obstruction in a 60-year-old man
abstract: In Asia, widespread early detection through endoscopic screening has resulted in higher diagnosis rates of asymptomatic duodenal-type follicular lymphoma (DFL).However, no standardized guidelines exist for diagnosing and managing DFL, and ongoing debates persist regarding the optimal treatment strategies.This retrospective observational study was conducted between February 2018 and July 2024.Endoscopic examination revealed small whitish nodular lesions in the second portion of the duodenum.Seven patients (58.0%) underwent involved-site radiation therapy.Two patients (17.0%) with stage IV disease underwent chemotherapy with rituximab combined with cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisolone.Another two (17.0%) received chemotherapy with rituximab combined with cyclophosphamide, vincristine, and prednisone.One patient (8.0%) was treated with rituximab monotherapy.During a median follow-up of 30.2 months, no cases of disease progression were observed.Although radiation and chemotherapy are effective treatments, the slow progression of the disease may make a watch-and-wait strategy appropriate.
authors: Jun Heo; Min Kyu Jung; Yoo Na Kang

title: A lightweight hybrid CNN framework with Multi-filter feature selection and Selective Opposition-based Grey Wolf Optimization for gastrointestinal image classification
abstract: Abstract Gastrointestinal disease detection through endoscopic imaging has become a critical research area in computer-aided medical diagnosis. Accurate classification of endoscopic images remains challenging due to high intra-class variability and visual similarity across pathological categories. In this work, an efficient deep feature extraction and optimization-based framework for automated gastrointestinal image classification using the Kvasir v1 and Kvasir v2 datasets is proposed. Initially, multiple pretrained convolutional neural network models were evaluated as baseline feature extractors. To achieve a balance between classification performance and computational efficiency, an ensemble of MobileNetV2, EfficientNet-B0, and ConvNeXt-Tiny was employed to extract complementary deep features from endoscopic images. The fused feature representation achieved an initial classification accuracy of 96.12% on Kvasir v1 and 95.43% on Kvasir v2. To reduce feature redundancy and enhance discriminative capability, a hybrid filter-based feature selection strategy combining Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion, Laplacian Score, and Elastic Net was applied. The selected features were further refined using a novel Selective Opposition-based Grey Wolf Optimizer, which improved exploration capability and enabled effective identification of the most informative feature subset. The optimized features were finally classified using a multilayer perceptron classifier. Experimental results show that the proposed framework achieved superior classification accuracies of 97.51% on Kvasir v1 and 97.06% on Kvasir v2, outperforming baseline CNN models and conventional feature fusion approaches. These results demonstrate that the integration of lightweight deep feature extractors, hybrid feature selection, and metaheuristic optimization provides a robust and computationally efficient solution for automated gastrointestinal image classification across multiple benchmark datasets.
authors: Aheli Dutta; Saikat Basu; Koushik Majumder; Mihir Sing; Krishnendu Mahata; Sanjay Chakraborty

title: A lightweight portable ultrasound robot for autonomous liver sonography
abstract: Autonomous ultrasound robots could improve access to liver disease screening but remain limited by anatomical variability, respiratory motion and bulky hardware. Here, we present a lightweight robotic liver ultrasound system with a 588-g decoupled end-effector controlled by a sonographer-informed AI agent. The robot attaches directly to the abdomen, maintaining stable force and controlled motion during breathing and patient-side disturbances. Trained on sonographer trajectories, the agent integrates spatial, tactile and visual feedback to navigate discontinuous acoustic windows and acquire standard imaging planes. Evaluations in 102 healthy participants and 17 patients yielded clinically interpretable images and anatomical measurements closely matching clinical references. We also deployed the system for hepatic echinococcosis screening in a high-altitude, low-resource setting on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and evaluated its performance in dynamic scenarios, including vehicle-based scanning. These findings support portable, patient-mounted robotics for standardized ultrasound beyond specialist settings. Liver ultrasound is operator-dependent. Here, the authors develop a lightweight, patient-mounted robot for autonomous liver scanning in clinical, remote and mobile settings, with results comparable to those gathered by experienced sonographers.

title: A novel minimally humanized mouse model of aniridia for preclinical evaluation of CRISPR gene editing strategies
abstract: Introduction Aniridia is a rare congenital vision-loss disorder primarily caused by variants in the paired box 6 ( PAX6 ) gene. Current treatments do not maintain vision long term, nor address the underlying disease mechanism. CRISPR-mediated genome editing holds great promise for treating genetic diseases but requires demonstration of efficacy on human DNA to support translational relevance. The aim of this work was to generate and test a minimally humanized mouse model of aniridia, carrying a FLAG-tagged Pax6 and the most common recurring pathogenic aniridia-patient variant, introduced for the first time in mice. Methods Ocular assessments (gross examination, slit lamp imaging, and fluorescent and confocal microscopy) were performed in mice homozygous for humanization and heterozygous for the variant, paralleling patients. Mice were examined immediately post-wean and at adulthood, with the former chosen as a likely time for treatment initiation. As an exploratory proof-of-principle, a lipid nanoparticle-delivered adenine base editor (ABE8e) was tested to demonstrate the utility of the model. Results Ocular assessments revealed the expected phenotypes for an aniridia mouse model, supporting successful generation and phenotypic validation of the humanized mouse. The ABE8e treatment resulted in a modest correction (4.8% ± 0.4% SEM) of the pathogenic variant in clinically relevant ex vivo cortical neurons. Discussion Although designed for the development of genome editing therapies, this humanized mouse is also applicable to other therapies requiring interaction with human DNA or RNA. It also enables evaluation of nonsense-suppression drugs since the readthrough proteins retain the FLAG tag. More broadly, this methodology is applicable to other pathogenic variants for aniridia, CRISPRa approaches, and other genetic diseases for which CRISPR-based therapy holds promise.
authors: Seyedeh Zeinab Mirjalili Mohanna; Andrea J. Korecki; Pardis Kazemian; Tess C. Lengyell; Bethany A. Adair; Blair R. Leavitt; Elizabeth M. Simpson

title: A personalized 2D/3D image registration pipeline for automated knee registration using single-plane moving fluoroscopy
abstract: Abstract Accurate knee joint kinematics are essential for biomechanical research and clinical assessment. Single-plane fluoroscopy is one of the most accurate tools for measuring in vivo joint motion, but manual estimation of three-dimensional bone pose from individual fluoroscopic frames remains labor-intensive and time-consuming. In this study, we present a personalized 2D/3D image registration pipeline for automated registration of knee fluoroscopic images acquired using single-plane moving fluoroscopy. The proposed framework combines pose standardization across acquisition sessions, subject-specific learning-based pose estimation, and differentiable-rendering-based pose refinement. Tested using fluoroscopic datasets of both natural knees and knee implants together with a PyTorch3D-based differentiable renderer, we trained subject-specific pose estimation networks for both anatomy types. Evaluation against manually matched reference poses showed mean initial in-plane translation differences of approximately 1.1–2.1 mm and geodesic rotation differences of 1.3–3.6 $$^\circ$$ with mask-only input, while out-of-plane translation differences remained larger, as expected in single-plane imaging. Gradient-based refinement using gradient correlation coefficient (GCC) further reduced the disagreement with the manual reference poses, resulting in sub-millimetre in-plane translation differences and sub-degree rotational differences, with over 95% of test frames satisfying the predefined success criterion that both the femoral and tibial registrations had absolute in-plane translation differences below 1 mm in both $$T_x$$ and $$T_y$$ and a geodesic rotation difference below 1 $$^\circ$$ . These results quantify agreement with the existing manual registration workflow rather than independently validated anatomical pose accuracy.
authors: Jinhao Wang; Xia Li; Saša Ćuković; Florian Vögl; William R. Taylor

title: A quantum-inspired cross-attention fusion network for multi-class eye disease classification from retinal fundus images
abstract: Automated screening of blinding eye diseases from colour fundus photographs is an active area of medical image analysis, yet many reported systems are validated on a single dataset and offer limited insight into their internal decision process. This study introduces QICAF-Net, a dual-branch deep learning framework that couples a Swin Transformer global-context branch with an EfficientNet local-lesion branch and fuses their representations through a novel Quantum-Inspired Cross-Attention Fusion (QICAF) module. The QICAF module reformulates cross-attention using the mathematical formalism of quantum states: token features are amplitude-encoded as complex unit vectors, transformed by a learnable norm-preserving unitary gate, compared through a fidelity-inspired similarity, normalised by a Born-rule measurement rule, and combined through an entanglement-inspired bilinear interaction. All operations are executed as classical linear algebra on conventional graphics hardware; no physical quantum computer and no quantum speed-up are claimed. The model was trained and evaluated on a balanced four-class retinal dataset of 4,217 fundus images spanning cataract, diabetic retinopathy (DR), glaucoma and normal categories. Under stratified five-fold cross-validation with six-view test-time augmentation (TTA), QICAF-Net attained a macro-F1 of 0.9358 ± 0.0113, an accuracy of 0.9367 ± 0.0112 and a macro one-versus-rest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.9914 ± 0.0023; a three-seed evaluation of the full model gave a macro-F1 of 0.9420 ± 0.0071. An 18-run multi-seed component ablation (six fusion configurations × three seeds) confirmed that the quantum-inspired components achieve accuracy statistically indistinguishable from strong classical fusion baselines, and a paired three-seed significance test between QICAF-Net and a matched dual-branch concatenation model returned no statistically significant accuracy difference (paired t-test p = 0.887; Wilcoxon p = 1.000). Against five single-backbone baselines under an identical preprocessing and TTA protocol, QICAF-Net was competitive but did not exceed the strongest backbones (Swin-Tiny 0.9583, ViT-Small 0.9487). The principal contribution of the module is therefore a novel and interpretable formulation rather than a raw accuracy gain. External validation on a heterogeneous independent cohort (N = 3,907) showed heterogeneous cross-dataset transfer — better preserved for cataract and normal and substantially degraded for glaucoma; under an observed external-domain shift the diabetic-retinopathy sensitivity fell to 39.61%, and under colour-constancy correction with six-view TTA the external accuracy was 0.8741 (95% CI 0.8633–0.8841) and the macro-F1 0.7188 (95% CI 0.6969–0.7398). Two complementary explainability methods together with visualisation of the QICAF attention indicated that the model attends to clinically plausible regions, most strongly the optic nerve head for glaucoma. Calibration, quantitative explanation-faithfulness (deletion/insertion) and profiler-based computational analyses were additionally performed. QICAF-Net is thus presented as an interpretable and transparently evaluated framework whose accuracy is on par with established fusion strategies while contributing a new attention formulation to the retinal imaging literature.
authors: P. Abinash; Krishnamoorthy N

title: A rare cause of massive gastrointestinal bleeding in a renal transplant recipient—CMV small-bowel ulcer: a case report
abstract: A 26-year-old renal transplant recipient presented to our unit with passage of fresh and altered blood. He was on multiple immunosuppressants including mycophenolate mofetil, tacrolimus, and prednisolone. He was profoundly anaemic on admission, requiring up to 10 units of packed cell transfusion. Oesophagogastroduodenoscopy and colonoscopy showed no bleeding source. Subsequent enteroscopy showed several ulcers in the ileum, while biopsy showed cytomegalovirus viral inclusions. He was treated with a 3-week course of valganciclovir. Re-scope 1 month after the enteroscopy showed that the ulcers were largely healed.
authors: Tony Lam; Kwok Yung Yuen

title: A robust lightweight deep learning network with deformable convolutions for efficient segmentation of optical coherence tomography images
abstract: Introduction: Manual segmentation and evaluation of optical coherence tomography (OCT) images are difficult and rely on specialist training, which limits the output in a busy clinic. While automatic segmentation can ease this burden, the deep models that currently lead the field tend to be too heavy for routine deployment on standard clinical hardware. A further obstacle is the unusual geometry of OCT data: instead of compact objects on a background, the structures of interest form long, undulating tissue strata that extend horizontally across the whole frame, and this layout is poorly matched to convolutional kernels designed for ordinary photographs. Methods: We address both issues with LiDeOCTNet, a compact segmentation backbone tailored to the layered nature of OCT. Within a reduced UNet, we introduce learnable sampling offsets so that each kernel can reshape itself locally and trace the curved, irregular interfaces between tissues. To assess the design, we evaluate the network on three OCT collections covering retinal as well as endoscopic acquisitions. Results: Across all three, LiDeOCTNet surpasses a parameter-matched UNet baseline and approaches the accuracy of much heavier benchmarks such as TransUNet, despite using about 750× fewer parameters and running roughly 7.4× faster at inference. Discussion: Together these properties point to LiDeOCTNet as a practical option for real-time OCT analysis pipelines, including embedded and resource-limited devices.
authors: Mehmood Nawaz; Syed Muhammad Tariq Abbasi; Sheheryar Khan; Muhammad Ameer Hamza; Khadija Bibi; Syeda Aimen Abbasi; Muhammad Daud; Muhammad Asim; Wu Yuan

title: A self‐retaining mouth prop for intraoral access during periodontal surgery in rat models: A technical note
abstract: BACKGROUND: Rodent models are widely used in oral health research; however, maintaining stable and effective intraoral retraction in the small oral cavity is challenging. Manual retraction methods often lead to procedural instability, operator fatigue, and increased tissue trauma during rodent oral surgery. METHODS: A stainless-steel wire mouth prop incorporating helices for self-retention and auxiliary lateral soft tissue displacement prongs was fabricated. 32 adult Wistar albino rats were randomly allocated to two groups (n = 16 each). In the experimental group, procedures were performed using a custom mouth prop, and the control group underwent conventional manual retraction. Outcomes included time to achieve adequate retraction, slippage events per procedure, operator fatigue scores, and complication rates. Student's t-test was used for statistical analysis of retraction time, and the Mann-Whitney U test was used for slippage frequency, and fatigue scores. Statistical significance was determined using a Bonferroni-adjusted threshold of p < 0.017. RESULTS: Retraction time was significantly shorter in the experimental group (2.5 ± 0.6 min) than in control group (6.3 ± 1.2 min, p < 0.001). Slippage events per procedure were markedly lower with mouth prop (0.1 vs. 3.4 ± 1.1, p < 0.001). Operator fatigue scores were also reduced (2.4 ± 0.8 vs. 7.2 ± 1.4, p < 0.001). Complication rates were significantly lower in the experimental group (p = 0.024). CONCLUSION: The proposed custom-made mouth prop demonstrated favorable procedural handling characteristics during rat intraoral surgery and may serve as a practical, low-cost refinement tool for improving intraoral access and procedural stabilization in experimental oral research settings.
authors: Saravanan Sampoornam Pape Reddy; Delfin Lovelina Francis; Vivek Kumar Thakur; Balaji Manohar; Shaili Pradhan; Shesh Nath Rai

title: ABO-Med: Accelerated Bilevel Optimization for Few-Shot Medical Image Classification
abstract: In recent years, bilevel optimization has been widely used in a variety of machine learning tasks. However, prior bilevel optimization algorithms generally require the computation of second-order information, which limits their practical scalability. Only recently has a first-order paradigm for bilevel optimization been established, attaining near-optimal theoretical guarantees for solving bilevel optimization problems. In this paper, we propose ABO-Med, a scalable instantiation of this paradigm for few-shot learning, by incorporating it into the model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML) framework and tailoring it to medical image classification. We also introduce Medical Adaptive RandomAugment (MedRAug), a modality-aware augmentation strategy designed for medical images. Theoretically, ABO-Med establishes the optimality of MAML-type meta-learning approaches. Empirically, ABO-Med outperforms prior baselines on several public medical datasets, with gains of 1.99% to 18.76%, while MedRAug further improves the average accuracy by 2.20% to 6.34%. Additional cross-domain experiments, augmentation ablation studies, backbone ablation studies, and training efficiency analysis further validate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed method.
authors: Ruoxuan Shi; Sheng Yang; Zhengxing Su; Xiaoyang Hou; Yating Liu

title: ACCESS2 study: the potential for autonomous AI to mitigate disparities in diabetic retinopathy screening in youth
abstract: Minority and underserved youth are less likely to undergo diabetic retinopathy screening, yet more likely to have diabetic retinopathy. We hypothesize that autonomous artificial intelligence-based diabetic eye exams could mitigate screening disparities in minority youth. This prospective study enrolled 397 White and non-White youth with type 1 (72%) and type 2 (28%) diabetes at diabetes care visits. Participants underwent autonomous artificial-intelligence diabetic eye exams and optical coherence tomography imaging. The primary outcome is equivalence in screening completion between White and non-White youth. The secondary outcome is diagnostic accuracy of AI against prognostic standard. At baseline, participants in the White cohort were more likely to have completed a prior diabetic eye exam (79.8% v 61.8%, p < 0.0001). Following the artificial-intelligence intervention, 99.5% in the White cohort and 98% in the non-White cohort completed the autonomous artificial-intelligence diabetic eye exam, demonstrating equivalent screening completion after implementation. When compared to standard grading, AI demonstrated sensitivity of 100% (95% CI: 67.6%, 100%), and specificity of 76% (95% CI: 71.4%, 79.9%) for detecting more than mild diabetic retinopathy. Implementation of autonomous AI at the point of care increases access to and completion of diabetic eye exams, achieving equivalent screening completion among White and non-White youth, suggesting the potential to reduce disparities in diabetic retinopathy screening. Study Registration: NCT05463289. This study demonstrates that autonomous AI screening for diabetic retinopathy can achieve equivalent screening completion among white and non-white youth with T1D, suggesting the potential to reduce disparities in diabetic retinopathy screening.
authors: Risa M. Wolf; Roomasa Channa; T. Y. Alvin Liu; Elizabeth A. Brown; Lee A. Bromberger; Neha Parimi; Anum Zehra; Dhruva Patel; Bernard Pan; Yoohee Claire Kim; ALIYAH SHEHADEH; Harold P. Lehmann; Michael D. Abràmoff

title: AGRO-SUVIDE: Agentic Robotics for Surgical Viscoelastic Debridement
abstract: Augmented dexterity has the potential to reduce the fatigue experienced by surgeons during repetitive surgical tasks. In this paper, we propose the first AGentic RObotics framework for SUrgical VIscoelastic DEbridement (AGRO-SUVIDE), the repeated removal of small fragments attached to a viscoelastic substrate. Leveraging the self-improving and coding capability of agents, AGRO-SUVIDE adopts a modular framework. Specifically, the demonstration analysis module automatically identifies recurring skills from a single expert demonstration, using both visual and kinematic information. The construction module then builds each skill, either as a procedural model-based skill the agent codes against a scaffolded library or as a model-free policy-based skill. At runtime, the monitoring module composes the skills into a loop-style graph sized to the number of fragments it observes, then verifies pre- and post-conditions of each skill to decide whether to advance or retry. We evaluate AGRO-SUVIDE through 340 physical trials on the da Vinci Research Kit (dVRK). AGRO-SUVIDE achieves an average single-fragment removal success rate of 85%, completing consecutive three-fragment removal at 60% and at 95% with one human intervention. It further generalizes to unseen five-fragment scenarios with an average success rate of 80% for single-fragment removal. Project page: https://surgical-robotics.github.io/AGRO-SUVIDE/
authors: Shutong Jin; Ziyang Chen; Preethi Satish; Medow Shen; Gary S. Guthart; Florian T. Pokorny; Ken Goldberg

title: AHICF: A GENERALIZABLE AND INTELLIGENT HYBRID DEEP LEARNING FRAMEWORK FOR AUTOMATED DIABETIC RETINOPATHY CLASSIFICATION AND CLINICAL DIAGNOSIS
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is one of the major causes of preventable blindness globally however, automated DR grading algorithms tend to suffer from poor generalization in heterogeneous clinical datasets due to issues of domain shift, imaging heterogeneity, and class imbalance. In this paper, AHICF is introduced, a hybrid deep learning model for automatic DR grading and clinical decision-making. AHICF consists of retinal feature extraction from CNNs, Vision Transformers, and clinical handcrafted features, followed by feature optimization with a multi-objective method based on NSGA-II algorithm and a confidence-weighted ensemble classifier. To increase generalization capability for unseen target datasets, supervised domain adaptation on limited samples of target datasets is employed. The effectiveness of the model was validated on three publicly available retinal image datasets (APTOS, IDRiD, and Messidor) through in-distribution testing, cross-dataset evaluation, leave-one-dataset-out out-of-distribution detection, ablation study, statistical analysis, image quality assessment, and causal class-balance analysis. From experimental results, reliable performance in the source domain and significant decrease in performance degradation for the unseen target domains were observed after adaptation. However, generally speaking, AHICF seems to present itself as a very promising approach for automatic diabetic retinopathy grading which can be generalized across different datasets and demonstrates domain adaptation behavior showing its certain but not yet complete robustness; however, more validation on large clinical cohorts is needed.
authors: Himansu Sekhar Rout; Saravana Kumar S

title: AI BASED HAND GESTURE CONTROLLED ROBOT
abstract: The proposed system presents an advanced AI-based hand gesture controlled telepresence robot designed for operation in hazardous and inaccessible environments. The system enables a remote operator to control a robotic rover using real-time hand gestures without the need for physical controllers or wearable devices. It integrates computer vision techniques using OpenCV and MediaPipe for accurate skeletal hand tracking and gesture recognition. A dual-processing architecture ensures efficient handling of high-definition video streaming and gesture interpretation with minimal latency. The robot provides real-time visual feedback through wireless video transmission, enabling safe navigation and monitoring. The system ensures intuitive control, improved safety, and enhanced operational efficiency. This solution is highly applicable in disaster management, industrial inspection, and healthcare environments where human presence is risky or limited.
authors: Aaditya Kumbhar; Shriya Joshi; Kaustubh Badave; Avinash D. Harale
venue: International Journal of Mechanical Engineering Research and Technology

title: AI Rickshaw: A Secure, Geofenced, Solar-Assisted Autonomous Electric Rickshaw for Bangladesh and the Displacement Risk to the Lowest-Income Transport Workers
abstract: Bangladesh moves on rickshaws: a quarter of Dhaka's trips are made by cycle or battery-assisted rickshaw, and one to two million battery-run three-wheelers in the capital each support a driver from one of Bangladesh's lowest-income informal transport workforces. This article presents AI Rickshaw, a reference design for a driverless, app-summoned, solar-assisted electric rickshaw (AIR-1) that keeps the traditional three-wheel form, and uses it as a Bangladesh-specific case study in embodied artificial intelligence. Four contributions are made. First, a reference architecture adapted to lane-less, low-speed, high-density traffic. Second, software-enforced traffic compliance: geofenced operation in which highways, restricted roads, wrong-way movement and out-of-zone trips cannot be planned or executed, so that regulation becomes executable rather than merely instructive. Third, an integrated cyber-physical security architecture for theft, tampering, unauthorised control and passenger emergencies, in which a hard-wired safety microcontroller is the sole validated actuator gateway, so that compromise of the back end does not directly confer actuator authority. Fourth, an argument, with scenario evidence, that embodied AI, the combination of perception, robotics, electric actuation and digital platforms, can threaten the lowest-income manual occupations and not only knowledge work: under the base adoption scenario, substantial displacement of Dhaka's drivers could occur by 2041, and a just-transition framework of a per-vehicle-day levy, garage franchising, microfinance co-ownership and evidence-gated deployment is proposed. Solar energy is treated as assisting, not primary, supply. No physical prototype has yet been built; every quantitative value carries its evidence type, and the next phase is a hardware prototype validated in a private geofenced environment.
authors: Md Israfeel

title: AI driven oral cancer diagnosis from clinical imaging and computational pathology to precision therapeutics
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a computational approach for analysing the complex and heterogeneous data generated across oral cancer diagnosis and management. This narrative review provides an integrated overview of AI applications from early oral lesion detection, computational pathology, prognostic assessment, and precision therapeutics. It describes how machine learning and deep learning process clinical photographs, digitized histopathological images, whole-slide images, radiological examinations, and molecular or clinical data to generate task-specific outputs. The review covers AI-assisted identification of suspicious oral lesions, histopathological detection of oral epithelial dysplasia and oral squamous cell carcinoma, assessment of tumor differentiation, characterization of disease progression, and prediction of treatment response for therapeutic stratification. Particular attention is given to the relationship between the input data, computational task, and clinically relevant output rather than to model architecture alone. Although several studies report high diagnostic performance, much of the current evidence remains based on retrospective datasets and internal validation, while external, multicentre, and prospective evaluations are comparatively limited. Major challenges include dataset quality and representativeness, domain shift, annotation variability, interpretability, and integration into clinical workflows. Future progress will require patient-level evaluation, multicentre validation, multimodal integration, uncertainty-aware prediction, and prospective assessment of clinical utility. This review outlines the evolving role of AI as a potential decision-support framework across the oral cancer care pathway.
authors: Shreyas Agarwal; Baijnath Das; ShivMohan Singh; Bina Pani Gupta

title: AI in Endo-Bariatrics
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly influencing the field of endo-bariatrics by bringing greater precision, personalization, and efficiency to the management of obesity and metabolic diseases. This chapter examines how AI can be integrated across endoscopic bariatric and metabolic therapies (EBMTs from patient selection, to pre-procedure planning, intra-op support, and long-term follow-up. Traditionally, EBMT outcomes have often depended on the operator’s experience, which can lead to variability in results and a lack of standardized practice. AI technologies such as machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, and predictive analytics can help overcome these limitations by enabling more data-driven decisions, automatic recognition of anatomical structures, and real-time procedural support. In the pre-procedure stage, AI can assist with advanced imaging analysis, volumetric assessment, and simulation models that help clinicians plan individualized treatment strategies. During procedures, AI-assisted visualization systems, robotic support, depth sensing, and predictive tools for complications may improve procedural safety and consistency. Post-procedure, AI-enabled mobile applications and wearable device can allow continuous monitoring of patients, provide behavioral guidance, and help detect complications at an early stage, and improve long-term outcomes. Aditionally, AI may also improve workflow efficiency, reduce costs, standardize training, and help expand access to EBMTs. However, wider use of AI in endo-bariatrics faces several challenges such as concerns about data bias, lack of transparency, medico-legal responsibility, and unequal global access. Therefore, careful evaluation of AI systems is essential for safe implementation. AI has the potential to shift endo-bariatrics from a largely technique-dependent field to a more predictive, data-driven, and precision-based discipline.
authors: Bhavneet Singh Bhalla; Murtaja Satea; Adolfo Pérez Bonet; Valeria Atenea Costa Barney; Christian A. Macias; Lina Alami; Pavit Singh

title: AI-Assisted Multiclass Kidney CT Pathology Classification for Urological Imaging: An Optimized Hybrid Deep Learning Framework
abstract: Kidney CT imaging plays a central role in the urological diagnosis of renal cysts, calculi, solid tumors, and normal renal parenchyma. Although deep learning has shown promise for automated CT-based kidney pathology classification, existing approaches frequently rely on single-architecture models and lack systematic hyperparameter optimization, limiting both performance and reproducibility. This study aimed to develop and internally evaluate an optimized hybrid deep learning framework for multiclass kidney CT pathology classification in urological imaging, focusing on cyst, stone, tumor, and normal categories. A curated multiclass kidney CT dataset of 9,574 images was split into training (6,368), validation (1,997), and test (1,209) sets across four classes: Cyst, Normal, Stone, and Tumor. Four convolutional backbones-ResNet50V2, EfficientNetB3, DenseNet121, and Xception-were fine-tuned under a two-stage transfer learning protocol. Hyperparameters for each backbone were independently optimized using the Optuna framework with AdamW optimization and label smoothing. Class imbalance was addressed using weighted loss. Test-time augmentation was applied at inference. Two hybrid decision strategies were evaluated: validation-driven weighted soft voting and a logistic regression stacking learner. This was an internal computational validation study using a same-source dataset split; no external cohort was available. On the internal same-source held-out test set, ResNet50V2, Xception, the weighted ensemble, and the stacking model achieved perfect performance (100% accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and one-vs-rest ROC-AUC). DenseNet121 and EfficientNetB3 showed near-ceiling results. These outcomes may reflect strong class separability within the analyzed dataset and should be interpreted with caution in the absence of external validation. Ensemble strategies provided consistent performance gains over weaker individual backbones, particularly for the Stone class. The proposed optimized hybrid deep learning framework achieved strong internal performance for multiclass kidney CT pathology classification across urologically relevant categories. The findings suggest that architecture diversity and systematic hyperparameter optimization can substantially improve predictive robustness. External multi-center validation is required before clinical implementation in urological imaging workflows. The framework may serve as a candidate decision-support tool for radiologist-assisted interpretation of kidney CT findings, provided prospective validation is conducted. A revision-stage integrity audit found no byte-identical, pixel-identical, or repeated Roboflow source-identifier overlap across the predefined splits; however, two cross-split pairs showed very high structural similarity (SSIM >= 0.995), and patient-level independence could not be verified because patient identifiers were unavailable. Accuracy uncertainty was additionally quantified using 95% Wilson score confidence intervals.

title: AI-Assisted and Robotic Ultrasound for Vein and Vascular Mapping: A Scoping Review of Clinical Applications, Automation and Haemodialysis Access.
abstract: This scoping review will map the current evidence on artificial intelligence-assisted, automated, autonomous and robotic ultrasound technologies relevant to pre-operative haemodialysis-access vessel mapping. Pre-operative vascular mapping for haemodialysis access requires more than recognition of a vessel within an individual ultrasound image. A clinically useful examination may require appropriate image acquisition, identification of arteries and veins, continuous tracking of named vessels, assessment of vessel calibre and depth, recognition of branches, tributaries and perforators, dynamic and Doppler assessment where appropriate, evaluation of image quality and examination completeness, and reconstruction of the findings into a clinically actionable vascular map. Artificial intelligence, computer vision and robotic ultrasound systems have demonstrated a growing range of individual capabilities, including vessel segmentation, automated measurements, vessel tracking, robotic probe manipulation and three-dimensional vascular reconstruction. However, these component technologies should be distinguished from an end-to-end system capable of performing a complete clinical vessel-mapping examination. The primary objective of this review is therefore to determine which components of a clinically complete pre-operative haemodialysis-access ultrasound vessel-mapping examination have been demonstrated using artificial intelligence, computer vision, robotic ultrasound or autonomous ultrasound acquisition, and which required clinical competencies remain insufficiently validated. The review will distinguish direct evidence from haemodialysis-access and AVF/endoAVF applications from enabling evidence derived from closely related vascular-ultrasound technologies. Particular attention will be given to acquisition, probe control, anatomical recognition, continuous vessel tracking, quantitative measurement, vascular topology, Doppler and dynamic assessment, image-quality assurance, uncertainty and failure detection, examination completeness, three-dimensional reconstruction, map generation and the continuing requirement for expert sonographer input. The review will follow current JBI methodological guidance for scoping reviews and will be reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR. The anticipated output is an evidence map of current technological capabilities and a proposed evidence-informed, sonographer-led competency framework describing the capabilities that would require validation before an AI-assisted or autonomous system could be evaluated against expert sonographer-performed pre-operative vessel mapping.

title: AI-DRIVEN OCULOMICS: RETINAL IMAGING BIOMARKERS FOR SYSTEMIC DISEASE - FROM CARDIOVASCULAR RISK TO NEURODEGENERATION AND FOUNDATION MODELS
abstract: Introduction and aim: The retina offers a unique, non-invasive window into systemic vascular and neurological health. Deep-learning algorithms applied to retinal photographs and optical coherence tomography (OCT) can predict cardiovascular events, detect chronic kidney disease, estimate biological age, and identify neurodegenerative diseases - a field termed oculomics. This review synthesizes current evidence on AI-driven oculomics across cardiovascular, cardio-renal-metabolic, neurodegenerative, and aging domains. Materials and methods: A narrative review was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar for studies published 2018-2026. Original research, validation studies, and major reviews on AI-based prediction of systemic disease from retinal imaging were included. Results: Deep-learning models trained on fundus photographs predict major adverse cardiovascular events and ten-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk with areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCs) of 0.70-0.89. Chronic kidney disease detection achieves AUROCs of 0.85-0.94. Alzheimer’s disease classifiers reach AUROCs of 0.93 in development cohorts and 0.73-0.91 in external validation, while Parkinson’s disease detection achieves AUROCs of 0.77-0.92. Retinal age-gap independently predicts mortality. Self-supervised foundation models (RETFound, VisionFM, EyeFound, RETFound-Green, MIRAGE, V-JEPA) show state-of-the-art performance, with volumetric OCT (V-JEPA) reaching AUROCs of 0.94. Conclusions: AI-driven oculomics is a rapidly maturing field with strong translational potential. Despite encouraging accuracies, prospective validation, algorithmic bias, regulatory approval, and clinical integration remain key challenges. Future work should prioritize multi-ethnic cohort studies, cost-effectiveness analyses, and regulatory pathways.

title: ARCGym: Benchmarking Deep Reinforcement Learning in Autonomous Robotic Colonoscopy
abstract: Simulations for learning-based autonomous colonoscopic navigation focus mainly on fully actuated capsule robots, failing to capture the contact-rich navigation of long and flexible clinical colonoscopes. We present the Autonomous Robotic Colonoscopy Gym (ARCGym), an open-source reinforcement learning environment and benchmark for image-based navigation in clinically derived deformable colon anatomies. ARCGym supports multiple types of colonoscope robots, spanning capsule robots and flexible endoscopes, with this work focusing on flexible endoscopes including magnetic-driven tip actuation and clinically used proximally translational actuation. This work includes five CT-reconstructed colons representing typical clinical scenarios, a set of clinically meaningful navigation subtasks, and unified success metrics. We introduce a reward combining depth-based lumen alignment with a lumen-visibility score to improve learning under occlusions. Experiments across tasks, robots, and anatomies show that autonomous navigation remains challenging for both magnetic-driven and proximal-insertion flexible robots, with proximal-insertion actuation remaining an open problem.
