title: Artificial intelligence in gastroenterology practice: Current perspectives and emerging prospects
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly changing the landscape of gastroenterology by improving disease detection, diagnosis, risk stratification, prognostication, and clinical decision-making.Machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, large language models, and multimodal data integration have facilitated the development of accurate diagnostic and predictive algorithms for a wide spectrum of gastrointestinal and hepatopancreatobiliary diseases.In upper gastrointestinal diseases, AI has enhanced the detection and characterization of gastroesophageal reflux disease, Barrett's esophagus, esophageal cancer, gastric neoplasia, and gastroesophageal varices.The use of AI in capsule endoscopy has facilitated small intestinal mucosal lesion detection and reduced reading time.Computer-aided detection and diagnosis systems have improved adenoma detection and polyp characterization in colorectal diseases, while AI is increasingly being applied to molecular profiling and prognostic modeling in colorectal cancer.In inflammatory bowel disease, AI facilitates more objective endoscopic and histologic assessment, as well as prediction of disease outcome and treatment response.Promising AI-based radiomics, digital pathology, biomarker discovery, and risk prediction models have been emerging in pancreatic, biliary, and liver diseases.Large language models and multimodal AI may further enable integration of heterogeneous information and support personalized decision-making.Computer-aided quality assessment represents an emerging application for standardizing procedural quality in endoscopy.Several AIassisted platforms have received regulatory approval with ongoing integration into clinical practice.However, title: Artificial intelligence in gastrointestinal endoscopy: From technical performance to clinical translation
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is being increasingly used in gastrointestinal endoscopy for lesion detection, optical characterization, procedural quality monitoring, multimodal assessment, clinical decision support, and documentation. The strongest clinical evidence supports computer-aided detection during colonoscopy and selected applications for upper gastrointestinal neoplasia. Randomized trials have shown that AI can increase adenoma detection and assist in real-time lesion recognition. However, the benefits observed in controlled studies are not always reproduced in routine practice. Evidence for optical diagnosis, invasion depth assessment, inflammatory bowel disease, capsule endoscopy, pancreatobiliary endoscopy, and endoscopic ultrasonography remains heterogeneous, and many systems have been evaluated, mainly using retrospective or selected datasets. However, technical performance alone does not establish clinical value. Higher sensitivity, specificity, and diagnostic accuracy may not lead to safer decisions, more efficient workflows, or better patient outcomes. False-positive alerts, automation bias, correction burden, geographic and platform dependence, limited external validation, and poor workflow integration can affect real-world performance. Vision-foundation models, multimodal systems, and large-language models extend AI beyond single-task image analysis to reusable representations, automated reporting, and well-defined clinical support. Their clinical transferability remains uncertain because of domain shifts, data leakage, unsupported generation, and variable performance across settings. This review examined the evidence from gastrointestinal endoscopy using two complementary dimensions: clinical function and stage of evaluation. The clinical function describes the role of AI in the endoscopic pathway. Stage of evaluation distinguishes among retrospective internal testing, independent external validation, prospective clinical evaluation, interventional evaluation, and real-world or post-deployment assessment. We also use reasoning-aligned AI to describe systems whose tasks, intermediate representations, evidence integration, and outputs are organized around clinically meaningful observations and decisions, without implying human-like cognition or causal reasoning. Wider adoption should depend on independent validation, prospective evaluation of complete human–AI workflows, appropriate clinical oversight, operational reliability, governance, economic value, and reproducible benefits in routine care.
authors: Wenxin Xue; Xueying Wang; Tongrui Yang; Honggang Yu

title: Artificial intelligence in ophthalmic optical coherence tomography angiography: a bibliometric analysis
abstract: AIM: To analyze research landscapes, hotspots, and trends in artificial intelligence (AI) applied to ophthalmic optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) from 2015 to 2024, aiming to reveal global collaborations and guide future research. METHODS: We retrieved publications from Web of Science Core Collection using AI and OCTA-related search terms. After screening, 237 articles were analyzed with CiteSpace (version 6.3.R1) for co-citation, collaboration, and keyword burst analysis. RESULTS: Annual publications grew rapidly since 2017. China (94 publications) and the US (86 publications) were the most productive and influential countries. Research focused on: deep learning algorithms and vessel segmentation, ocular disease diagnosis including diabetic retinopathy and glaucoma, and automated vascular quantification and multimodal imaging. Key limitations included small sample sizes and limited algorithm generalizability. CONCLUSION: The integration of AI with OCTA has significantly advanced the automation and precise quantitative analysis of ophthalmic vascular imaging, demonstrating substantial potential for diagnosing various retinal and choroidal diseases. Future efforts should focus on developing more robust and interpretable AI models, conducting large-scale, multi-center clinical validation, and establishing standardized imaging and analysis protocols to ultimately realize the widespread adoption of AI-OCTA technology in routine clinical practice.
authors: Si-Yuan Zhu; Qing Zhang; Wei-Hua Yang; Wei Chi

title: Artificial intelligence in orthodontics: clinical maturity, evidence gaps, and emerging applications—a narrative review
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming orthodontics by enhancing diagnostic accuracy, supporting clinical decision-making, and facilitating digital workflows. This narrative review provides a comprehensive overview of current AI technologies and their applications in orthodontics, including diagnostic imaging, treatment planning, treatment monitoring, patient communication, education, and emerging generative AI tools. The available evidence indicates that automated cephalometric landmark detection and cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) segmentation have among the most advanced technical and external-validation evidence bases in orthodontic AI, whereas digital-model analysis has demonstrated high technical performance but more limited independent validation. However, no application met the predefined criteria for higher clinical maturity because prospective clinical effectiveness remained insufficiently established. Other emerging or experimental applications include AI-assisted treatment planning, remote monitoring, large language models (LLMs), and robotic systems, for which evidence remains predominantly retrospective, technical, feasibility-based, or early clinical. However, much of the current evidence is derived from retrospective studies, technical validation investigations, and proof-of-concept reports, with limited prospective clinical data demonstrating improvements in treatment quality, efficiency, or long-term patient outcomes. Important challenges remain regarding data quality, algorithmic bias, external validation, explainability, patient privacy, and regulatory oversight. Overall, AI should currently be regarded as a clinician-supervised decision-support tool rather than a replacement for professional expertise. Future progress is likely to depend on robust prospective clinical trials, transparent reporting, and responsible integration of AI into evidence-based orthodontic practice and the broader digital transformation of dentistry.

title: Artificial intelligence in pediatric endoscopy for hereditary polyposis syndromes: promises and challenges.
abstract: Children with hereditary polyposis syndromes require long-term endoscopic surveillance to reduce risks of gastrointestinal complications: malignancy, bleeding, and obstruction, among others. However, surveillance remains challenging because of variable lesion distribution, subtle morphology, interobserver variability, and the burden of repeated procedures throughout the patient's lifetime. Artificial intelligence has transformed adult endoscopy, but its application in pediatric polyposis is less defined. This review summarizes current evidence and explores potential applications for children with hereditary polyposis syndromes. In adult colonoscopy, meta-analyses and randomized trials demonstrate that artificial intelligence improves adenoma detection rates (ADR) and reduces missed lesions, though evidence linking these benefits to meaningful reductions in colorectal cancer incidence remains insufficient. In capsule endoscopy, artificial intelligence demonstrates high sensitivity for lesion detection while substantially reducing review time. Pediatric data remain limited, with no studies specific to hereditary polyposis syndromes, but early studies support feasibility. Potential applications include automated polyp detection, localization, burden quantification, and longitudinal comparisons across surveillance examinations. Artificial intelligence has significant potential to improve polyp detection, diagnostic consistency, accuracy, efficiency, and longitudinal disease monitoring in pediatric hereditary polyposis syndromes. Development of pediatric-specific datasets and prospective, multicenter, and outcome-driven validation studies will be essential before widespread clinical implementation.
authors: Kennedy Tham; Nicholas Norris; Srisindu Vellanki; Isabel Rojas; Claudia Phen

title: Artificial intelligence-driven imaging in sickle cell retinopathy: Advancing early detection, risk stratification, and precision ophthalmology
abstract: Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a disorder of genetically inherited red blood cells (RBCs), wherein it is manifested clinically as sickling of RBCs, due to polymerization of hemoglobin S. SCD patients frequently face RBCs clumping, blocking of blood vessels and capillaries along with persistent hemolysis.Sickle cell retinopathy (SCR), is a SCD associated disorder in the peripheral retina, responsible for several features like vasoocclusion, ischemia, vitreous hemorrhage and neovascularization within the retina and adjoining regions.While these are manageable features, some severe cases report retinal detachment and ultimately vision impairment in patients.As early signs of SCR are not usually manifested visually, its early diagnosis becomes the limiting factor for devising effective management strategies in patients.Artificial intelligence (AI) assisted deep learning models have very recently being utilized and provides a promising alternative in assisting early diagnosis, staging, and monitoring disease progression.Traditional retinal imaging methods like fundus photography, fluorescein angiography, optical coherence tomography and optical coherence tomography angiography scans have always assisted ophthalmologists to make clinical decisions for patients.Recently, these methods were being used to train AI models for easy and efficient analysis of such scans.As a growing field, works in this area have transitioned our understanding of image analyses and promises a fast, objective and efficient interpretation.This review discusses; how traditional methods captures structural damages to peripheral retina and summarizes recent research work done in this field to integrate AI driven models based on deep learning and machine learning.We summarize here AI based strategies for SCR screening and diagnosis, while underlining their clinical applicability, utilities and future translational promises towards ascertaining personalized ophthalmology.

title: Assessment of uncertainty estimation and distillation for reliable 3D dental mesh segmentation in orthodontics
abstract: Abstract The integration of deep learning into computer-aided orthodontic treatment planning has enabled automated tasks such as tooth segmentation from 3D dental models. However, the reliability of these systems remains a concern due to their black-box nature and tendency toward overconfident predictions. In this work, we present a comprehensive evaluation of uncertainty estimation methods for tooth segmentation on 3D intraoral scans. We investigate several state-of-the-art neural network architectures combined with uncertainty estimation techniques including predictive entropy, Monte Carlo dropout, test-time augmentation, deep ensembles, and evidential deep learning. Evaluation on the Teeth3DS benchmark, supplemented with synthetically incomplete scans and a custom out-of-distribution dataset, shows that sampling-based approaches, particularly deep ensembles, provide the most reliable uncertainty estimates. In contrast, entropy-based methods and evidential deep learning often produce overconfident predictions and fail to identify major segmentation errors. We further demonstrate that uncertainty estimation can detect out-of-distribution samples such as scans with artifacts or missing regions. Although deep ensembles provide the most reliable uncertainty estimates, their computational cost limits practical deployment. We therefore investigate uncertainty distillation and show that a single student model can achieve ensemble-like uncertainty quality with only one forward pass.
authors: Lucas Krenmayr; Reinhold von Schwerin; Daniel Schaudt

title: Association between salivary alkaline phosphatase and inflammatory periodontal diseases among adolescents in the European North of Russia
abstract: The high prevalence of periodontal inflammatory diseases (PID) among adolescents underscores the need to develop simple, non-invasive methods for their timely detection. Oral fluid is considered a promising diagnostic substrate, enabling the assessment of various biomarkers, particularly alkaline phosphatase (ALP), which is involved in inflammatory and reparative processes in periodontal tissues. However, there is a paucity of studies analyzing the diagnostic significance of this enzyme. Objective. To investigate the association between salivary ALP levels and clinical signs of PID in individuals aged 15–17 years permanently residing in the European North of Russia. In a cross-sectional study, participants (n = 439) residing in the Nenets Autonomous Okrug (n = 171), the Komi Republic (n = 146), and Murmansk Oblast (n = 121) underwent a dental examination with recording of periodontal parameters (bleeding, dental deposits, presence of periodontitis) and provided mixed saliva samples for subsequent determination of ALP activity. Data analysis was performed using Poisson regression models; unadjusted and adjusted (for sex, age, and place of residence) relative risks were calculated, and linear trends were assessed across quartiles of ALP distribution. Results: а direct statistically significant association was observed between enzyme concentration and the number of sextants exhibiting bleeding in the multivariable regression model, p for trend = 0.037. No statistically significant association was found between ALP levels and the likelihood of detecting periodontitis (p for trend = 0.404) or dental calculus (p = 0.521). Our results suggest that elevated ALP levels in the oral fluid of adolescents are associated with a greater prevalence of gingival bleeding. This suggests that this parameter may serve as a potential indicator of the severity and extent of generalized inflammation in periodontal tissues, although it is not specific for a diagnosis of periodontitis. Further prospective studies are required to definitively establish the clinical and diagnostic utility of ALP and to justify its application in routine clinical practice.

title: Association between socioeconomic status and dental caries in adolescents – a systematic review of cohort studies
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Early adolescence is a critical period for caries initiation, underlining the need for updated knowledge on effective caries indicators. This systematic review of cohort studies aimed to assess the association between socioeconomic status (SES), involving a wide range of indicators, and dental caries in adolescents aged 12-19. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Four databases (MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science) were systematically searched for relevant publications from January 1, 2000, through December 5, 2025. SES and SES proxy indicators were parental education, income, and occupation, and adolescents' school type, their social capital, and immigrant background. Composite SES indicators combined the aforementioned variables. The risk of bias was evaluated using a modified Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. RESULTS: Studies (n = 21) from 11 countries across five continents were included, covering approximately 66,000 adolescents. An inverse relationship was documented between caries and mothers' education (six of seven studies), fathers' education (three of four studies), and parental income (three of six studies). School type (three studies), social capital (two studies), immigrant background (four studies), and composite SES indicators (five of six studies) were also linked to caries. However, the effect measures and definitions of exposures and outcomes were not consistent. CONCLUSIONS: An inverse association was observed between maternal education and caries, while corresponding associations with fathers' education and parental income were weaker and less consistent. This type of association was also observed for adolescents' school types, their social capital, and composite SES indicators. Immigrant background served as a caries predictor. However, the substantial heterogeneity in the included studies did not allow for meta-analyses and limited definite conclusions. The findings underscore the need to develop and validate robust composite SES measures applicable across diverse global contexts.

title: Augmented and mixed reality as auxiliary tools in dental procedures and their integration with artificial intelligence: A scoping review
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To map and synthesize the scientific evidence regarding the use of Augmented Reality (AR) and Mixed Reality (MR) as auxiliary tools in dental procedures, and to examine the extent to which Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been integrated into these workflows. DATA: A scoping review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA-ScR guidelines and the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) recommendations. The study selection and data extraction processes were carried out by two independent reviewers, with disagreements resolved by consensus. SOURCES: Searches were performed in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for studies published up to June 2025. STUDY SELECTION: Fifteen studies were included from a total of 1,457 records identified. Most of the evidence was concentrated in implant dentistry, where MR-based dynamic navigation achieved sub-millimetric accuracy (e.g., three-dimensional entry deviation of 0.417 mm) and outperformed the freehand technique. Improvements in angular accuracy (up to 72% among inexperienced operators) were observed in orthodontic mini-implant placement, and more conservative tissue removal was reported in endodontic access and in tooth preparation. In zygomatic implant placement, however, the freehand technique was not surpassed in apical or angular accuracy, and accuracy improved only when robotic stabilization was added. Artificial Intelligence was identified in a minority of the included studies and, where present, was restricted to preparatory stages of the workflow, namely automated segmentation, image registration, and planning support, rather than to intraoperative execution. CONCLUSIONS: AR and MR were applied predominantly as intraoperative visualization and navigation aids and showed accuracy superior to freehand execution, whereas AI functioned as an enabling technology confined to the preparatory stages of the workflow. Given the predominance of in vitro and proof-of-concept designs, these findings indicate technical feasibility rather than established clinical effectiveness, and multicenter randomized trials with independent validation of the systems remain necessary before clinical adoption can be established.
authors: MATHEUS PINÓS; Newton Sesma; Giovani Flach; Eduardo Mukai

title: Augmenting colonoscopy with artificial intelligence and robotic assistance: a human-factors scoping review toward a task-based shared autonomy paradigm
abstract: Colonoscopy is central to colorectal cancer prevention but remains a high-demand psychomotor and cognitive procedure, characterized by operator dependency, variable performance, and substantial physical and mental workload. Increasing evidence links procedural quality and safety to clinician-related factors, including musculoskeletal strain, fatigue, and non-technical skills. Concurrently, artificial intelligence (AI) and robotic technologies are emerging as potential tools to address these limitations. We conducted a scoping review with narrative synthesis of literature on human factors, ergonomics, AI, robotic technologies, and shared autonomy in colonoscopy and surgical robotics. Evidence synthesis: Colonoscopy performance remains limited by non-negligible miss rates and variability driven by both technical and human factors. Ergonomic constraints and cognitive workload contribute significantly to operator strain and may affect vigilance and decision-making. AI systems-including computer-aided detection (CADe), diagnosis (CADx), and quality monitoring-have demonstrated improvements in detection metrics and procedural standardisation, although concerns regarding cognitive offloading and potential deskilling persist. In parallel, emerging robotic and soft-robotic platforms aim to enhance navigation, improve procedural ergonomics, and reduce operator musculoskeletal strain, although clinical evidence remains limited. These technologies converge within a task-based shared-autonomy paradigm integrating physical, perceptual, and cognitive augmentation, with different procedural tasks operating at different levels of human-system control. A task-based shared-autonomy framework may provide a coherent model for integrating AI and robotics into colonoscopy while preserving human supervision and clinical judgement. Future developments should prioritise human-centred design, workflow integration, and multidimensional evaluation strategies to ensure safe and effective clinical implementation.

title: Automated Multi-Class Retinal Disease Detection Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks And Transfer Learning
abstract: Early detection of ocular diseases is essential for preventing progressive visual impairment and reducing the burden of avoidable blindness. However, conventional retinal screening depends heavily on trained ophthalmologists and manual interpretation of retinal images, which can limit the scalability and accessibility of screening services. This study presents an automated deep-learning framework for the multi-class classification of retinal fundus images into four categories: cataract, diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, and normal. The proposed model employs transfer learning using a pre-trained EfficientNetB3 convolutional neural network as the feature-extraction backbone. To improve disease-specific feature learning while limiting overfitting, the deeper layers of the backbone were fine-tuned and combined with global average pooling, batch normalization, dropout regularization, and fully connected classification layers. The retinal image dataset was screened for corrupted files, divided into training, validation, and test partitions, and subjected to training-specific augmentation using horizontal flipping, rotation, zooming, and contrast variation. Model performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The proposed classifier achieved a test accuracy of 99.58%, demonstrating strong classification performance across the four retinal categories. The trained model was further integrated into a full-stack web application consisting of a React-based frontend and Flask-based backend. A pre-inference image-validation mechanism was incorporated to identify unsuitable, non-retinal, or severely degraded image inputs before classification. The developed framework demonstrates the potential of transfer-learning-based deep neural networks for scalable and accessible preliminary retinal disease screening. Nevertheless, independent external and prospective clinical validation is required before the system can be considered suitable for real-world clinical use.

title: Automatic Trajectory Planning from Preoperative MRI images Using the AI-Optimized RRT* Algorithm for Robotic Breast Ultrasound
abstract: Ultrasound imaging is the most widely used technique for detecting and diagnosing breast cancer, as it provides real-time images in a non-invasive and inexpensive manner. However, performing ultrasound examinations requires experienced and well-trained operators either for probe manipulation during acquisition or during image interpretation, which makes this technique dependent. This dependency requires the employment of sonographers with extensive training and experience, which may limit access to this technique in remote areas and also expose experts to serious health issues due to repetitive movements. To overcome these difficulties, robotic ultrasound systems have emerged in recent years to enable conventional ultrasound examinations to be performed in an automated and standardized way. Our study contributes to this field through an integrated approach to automated planning of robotic breast ultrasound trajectories. This approach is based on the application of a developed version of the rapidly-exploring random tree (RRT) trajectory planning algorithm to pre-operational threedimensional (3D) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) images. We performed simulations with the three versions of the algorithm RRT, RRT* and RRT* with 30% reinforcement learning (RL) on two different patients. The results obtained demonstrate the potential of the RRT algorithm with 30% RL to obtain optimized trajectories with high fluidity and a short path while ensuring total and homogeneous coverage adapted to different complex breast morphologies.

title: Automation dependence in AI-assisted colonoscopy: impact of system reliability and surgeon experience on navigation performance.
abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly introduced into endoscopic navigation, understanding how operators use and respond to AI suggestions is essential for designing safe and effective human-AI collaboration. This study investigated the effects of AI reliability and operator experience on task performance and cognitive responses in a simulated colonoscopy navigation task. A virtual simulation paradigm was used, in which 27 interns and experienced doctors completed a navigation direction judgment task under three AI reliability conditions (high, medium, and low) and a no AI condition. Navigation accuracy, task completion time, subjective trust, cognitive load, and compliance with incorrect AI prompts were recorded. The results showed that AI reliability significantly affected navigation performance and subjective trust. High reliability AI improved task accuracy and efficiency, particularly among less experienced operators. However, when AI reliability decreased, participants' performance declined, and interns showed higher compliance with incorrect AI prompts than experienced doctors. Notably, this behavior occurred even when subjective trust decreased, suggesting a potential mismatch between trust evaluation and AI following behavior. This could be interpreted cautiously, as higher compliance among interns may reflect both rational reliance under high task difficulty and the risk of inappropriate reliance when AI reliability is insufficient. These findings indicate that AI-assisted endoscopic systems should not only improve navigation performance but also support appropriate reliance calibration. Differentiated support strategies may be needed for operators with different levels of experience, especially in scenarios involving training or novice operators.

title: Autonomous Reconfigurable Modular Conductive Hydrogels for Adaptive and Degradable Bioelectronic Interfaces
abstract: ABSTRACT Bioelectronic interfaces are increasingly used in medical devices for tissue stimulation and sensing. Transient bioelectronics seek the same functionality in temporary systems, yet most available materials are nondegradable, stiff, and require surgery or external removal. Achieving tissue‐like softness, smooth injectability, stable mixed conductivity, and reliable short‐term bioresorption within a single biocompatible matrix remains challenging. Here, we decouple injectability from bulk conductive performance using a modular reconfiguration strategy. High‐filler‐content hydrogels are converted into lyophilized modules that can be resuspended, injected through a standard syringe, and then autonomously reassemble in situ into a cohesive conductive network, recovering 90% of conductivity after freeze–drying, fragmentation, and reconfiguration. The platform uses a fully degradable tannic‐acid‐crosslinked poly(vinyl alcohol) matrix with molybdenum and molybdenum trioxide nanoparticles as co‐functional fillers. Mixed ionic/electronic conduction arises from redox‐active tannic acid–Mo(VI) complexes (ionic transport) and semi‐percolated Mo nanoparticles (electron hopping). The optimized formulation matches extracellular‐matrix mechanics (Young's modulus 0.03 MPa; failure strain 998%) and fully degrades within 120 h under simulated physiological conditions. In a human skin explant wound model, conformal integration enables charge transfer, reaching 0.02 A at across a 1 cm defect.

title: Autonomy, Operating Domains, and Validation in Robotic Ultrasound: Transferable Lessons and Structural Limits from Autonomous Vehicle Development
abstract: Diagnostic ultrasound is among the most portable and least expensive of the major imaging modalities, yet its reach is constrained by the availability and physical capacity of skilled operators: between 85 and 90 percent of sonographers report work-related musculoskeletal pain, and approximately one in five sustains a career-ending injury [1, 2, 3]. Robotic ultrasound systems have advanced substantially in response and learned acquisition policies now approach expert-level performance on individual anatomical targets [4, 5]. Progress in the field is, however, characterized using autonomy taxonomies inherited from surgical robotics [6, 7, 8]. These are frameworks that describe how much of a task a machine performs while remaining largely silent on the population in which that performance was demonstrated. Across the studies examined in this review, performance metrics are routinely reported, whereas explicit specification of operating conditions is considerably less common.

title: Avoiding the Automation Trap: Designing Human-Centred AI Workflows for Dental Manufacturing
abstract: This industrial case study explores integrating machine learning into high-volume dental manufacturing. Such technologies profoundly influence existing technician workflows and laboratory operations. To address this, a legacy software audit using a localised Cognitive Dimensions of Notation (CDN) framework identified high Repetitive Viscosity, Hidden Task Status, and Workflow Rigidity. This diagnostic phase was driven by structured workshops with the digital technicians. These failings hindered quality control and forced technicians into redundant tasks. To resolve these issues, the project co-designed a human-in-the-loop application that replaced modal menus with a unified 3D editor layout, eliminated hidden states with a visual column-based progress queue, and introduced state serialisation to support flexible task management. Qualitative evaluation confirmed that these design choices effectively resolved the identified cognitive frictions by reducing interaction costs and preventing repetitive editing tasks. While improvements to backend algorithms halved baseline processing time, successful digital transformation relies equally on workflow redesign and end-user engagement. Ultimately, this method of adapting, localising, and running workshops provides a technique that can be deployed across a wide range of industrial settings when faced with the challenge of the AI-assisted automation trap. This is of particular importance in industrial sectors where machine learning-based solutions risk threatening existing work practices and disrupting established processes.
authors: Salman Ahmed; Chris Roast; Ajmal Gharib

title: Awareness and Utilization of AI-Powered Smile Design Software Among Dental Students: A Pilot Study
abstract: Background and objectiveArtificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly influencing dental diagnosis and aesthetic planning.AI-driven smile design tools allow dentists to replicate aesthetic outcomes using facial and dental data.However, implementation remains limited in Indian undergraduate dental education, particularly in resourceconstrained regions.This study aimed to assess the awareness and attitudes of undergraduate dental students in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, toward using AI-driven smile design tools. MethodsA cross-sectional pilot study was conducted among 30 undergraduate dental students in Thiruvananthapuram using a validated questionnaire distributed via Google Forms.For this study, "awareness" was operationalized as self-reported recognition of AI applications in smile design, and "utilization" was defined as self-reported encounters with patients requesting AI-assisted treatment or personal willingness to adopt AI tools.The survey included multiple-choice, Likert-scale, and dichotomous questions assessing awareness, attitudes, and perceived clinical implications of AI in smile design.Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and chi-square tests. ResultsA majority of the participants (23/30, 76.6%) had heard of AI applications in smile design.Positive attitudes were prevalent: most participants believed that AI could reduce treatment duration and improve clinical judgment (27/30, 90%), and all participants felt that AI could elevate service quality (30/30, 100%).Additionally, 24/30 (80%) participants agreed that AI positively impacts prognosis, and 26/30 (86.6%) anticipated increased patient curiosity and inflow.Most respondents (27/30, 90%) supported the inclusion of AI in theoretical classes, and 22/30 (73.3%) were willing to modify their clinical setup for AI integration.However, 27/30 (90%) expected potential troubleshooting or errors, and only 11/30 (36.6%) reported encountering patients who requested AI-based treatment tools. ConclusionDental students in Thiruvananthapuram demonstrated substantial awareness and positive attitudes toward AI-powered smile design tools, recognizing their potential to enhance service quality, treatment efficiency, and patient engagement.However, these findings should be interpreted in light of the pilot design, small convenience sample, and single-district setting.Despite this readiness, concerns regarding technical limitations and current patient demand highlight the need for structured AI integration into dental curricula and supervised clinical implementation.
authors: Shradha Anil Kuzhivilayil; Midhun K R; Suhana Rahman P A

title: Beyond Anti-VEGF: Toward Integrated Precision Care in Diabetic Retinal Disease
abstract: Diabetic retinal disease (DRD) remains one of the leading causes of preventable vision loss worldwide and continues to represent a major global public health challenge despite remarkable therapeutic advances over the past two decades. Intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) therapy has revolutionized the management of diabetic macular edema and proliferative diabetic retinopathy, significantly improving visual outcomes and reducing vision-threatening complications. Nevertheless, a substantial proportion of patients exhibit incomplete anatomical or functional responses, require frequent lifelong intravitreal injections, or experience disease progression despite adequate VEGF suppression, underscoring the biological heterogeneity of DRD. Growing evidence recognizes DRD as a chronic neurovascular disorder extending beyond a purely microvascular disease. Inflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, neurodegeneration, vascular instability, and progressive retinal ischemia interact throughout disease progression. Concurrently, advances in multimodal retinal imaging-including optical coherence tomography (OCT), OCT angiography (OCTA), ultra-widefield imaging, and artificial intelligence-assisted image analysis-have enabled the identification of imaging biomarkers that improve diagnosis, prognostication, and individualized therapeutic decision-making. The therapeutic landscape has expanded considerably beyond conventional anti-VEGF therapy. Corticosteroid implants, dual-pathway inhibitors, sustained drug-delivery systems, vitreoretinal surgery, laser photocoagulation, and emerging pharmacological approaches have broadened treatment options. Increasing evidence supports tailoring therapy according to retinal phenotype, imaging biomarkers, inflammatory status, ischemic burden, and systemic metabolic factors rather than relying on uniform treatment algorithms. This review summarizes recent advances in the understanding and management of DRD, emphasizing pathophysiology, multimodal imaging biomarkers, pharmacological therapies and delivery systems, vitreoretinal surgery, systemic risk-factor optimization, artificial intelligence, and emerging therapeutic strategies. Finally, we introduce Integrated Precision Care (IPC) as a proposed conceptual and research framework that integrates conventional disease staging with multimodal retinal imaging, biological phenotyping, systemic risk assessment, treatment burden, and patient-specific characteristics. IPC is not intended to replace established stage-specific guidelines or to function as a prospectively validated therapeutic algorithm; rather, it provides a hypothesis-generating structure for testing whether multidimensional integration can improve risk stratification, therapeutic selection, durability, patient-centered outcomes, and long-term vision.
authors: Jesús Hernán González-Cortés; Jesus Emiliano Gonzalez-Cantu; Alper Bilgic; Francesc March de Ribot; Aditya A. Sudhalkar; Laurent Kodjikian; David E. Pelayes; Thibaud Mathis; Jesús Mohamed-Hamsho

title: Bibliometric Mapping of Transforaminal Research in Clinical Neurology: Publication Trends, Intellectual Structure, and Global Collaboration Networks
abstract: Objective: This study aimed to reveal the bibliometric profile, conceptual structure, and scientific collaboration patterns of articles containing the term “transforaminal” in their titles in the Web of Science (WoS) Clinical Neurology category. Methods: The title field was searched for “transforaminal” in WoS (data retrieved on 23 September 2026); 1,430 records restricted to the Clinical Neurology category and Article document type were analyzed. Publication distributions by year and journal and the most cited studies were assessed through performance analysis; keyword co-occurrence and institutional and country-level co-authorship analyses were performed using VOSviewer. Results: Publication output increased particularly after 2013 and peaked at 129 publications in 2025. World Neurosurgery was the most productive journal, with 222 publications (15.524%). Most of the highly cited publications concerned transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion (TLIF). In the keyword network, “transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion” was the most central concept, with 476 occurrences and a total link strength of 1,226. The United States stood out at the country level with 594 publications, 18,910 citations, and a total link strength of 122; China and South Korea were also major centers of output. Conclusion: Although transforaminal research has historically centered on TLIF, minimally invasive/endoscopic surgery, decompression, radiculopathy, and interventional pain management are prominent themes, with selected endoscopic keywords more frequently represented in recent publications. The findings show that publication productivity, citation impact, and international collaboration represent distinct bibliometric dimensions.
authors: Eylem Burcu Kahraman Özlü

title: Biodigital Transformation in Dentistry: From Diagnosis and Biological Preservation to Multidisciplinary Rehabilitation
abstract: Advances in digital technologies have expanded diagnostic and treatment possibilities in dentistry while making the preservation of biological tissues and collaboration among specialties increasingly important. This book, *Biodigital Transformation in Dentistry: From Diagnosis and Biological Preservation to Multidisciplinary Rehabilitation*, was prepared to address these developments from an integrated perspective. It follows a scientific progression from biodigital diagnosis and clinical decision-making to preventive care in pediatric dentistry; from the preservation of the pulp and natural dentition to periodontal and orthodontic treatment; and from digital prosthetic planning to implant-supported rehabilitation. Written by contributors from different dental specialties, the chapters examine both the clinical applications and the limitations of current technologies. We hope this book will serve as a valuable resource for dental students, residents, academics, and clinicians, and we thank all the authors for their knowledge, time, and contributions.

title: Bioresorbable batteries for transient ingestible bioelectronics
abstract: Abstract Ingestible and implantable electronic devices are transforming personalized healthcare by enabling real-time sensing, targeted therapy and diagnostic capabilities. However, powering these systems remains a major challenge owing to biocompatibility concerns and the environmental impact of conventional batteries. Here we present a bioresorbable magnesium–molybdenum trioxide (Mg–MoO 3 ) paper battery that delivers high electrochemical performance under physiological conditions and safely degrades over time. The battery provides a peak open-circuit voltage of 1.84 V and supports capsule-scale ingestible electronic systems incorporating bioresorbable power sources for two key gastrointestinal applications: battery-assisted radio-frequency identification tags for wireless medication tracking and capsule systems for electroceutical therapy. In vivo studies in swine models have demonstrated robust operation within the gastrointestinal tract and compatibility with clinically relevant use cases. This study establishes a foundation for safe, high-performance and bioresorbable power sources in biomedical electronics, enabling retrieval-free, eco-friendly devices that eliminate electronic waste in the gastrointestinal environment.

title: Boundary-complexity-guided adaptive weighting for single-image unsupervised superpixel segmentation
abstract: Abstract Superpixel segmentation provides an important mid-level representation for computer vision, but accurate boundary adherence remains difficult in images with weak contours, cluttered backgrounds, and complex textures. We propose a boundary-complexity-guided adaptive weighting framework for single-image unsupervised superpixel segmentation, termed AW-Super. The proposed Enhanced Boundary Feature Extraction Module (EBFEM) fuses semantic edge cues with gradient-based local structural information to produce a continuous complexity map, which is then used to reweight the optimization objective spatially. As a result, the method imposes stronger boundary-sensitive constraints in structurally complex regions while encouraging shape regularity in relatively homogeneous areas. We further introduce an adaptive stopping criterion into the Deep Image Prior optimization process, replacing a fixed iteration schedule with an image-dependent termination rule. Experiments on BSDS500 and SBD under matched superpixel budgets ( $$N=50$$ –500) demonstrate high boundary recall together with competitive overall segmentation performance, without requiring dataset-level training or ground-truth superpixel annotations. An additional cross-domain evaluation on DRIVE retinal images against SLIC and SEEDS further supports the applicability of AW-Super beyond natural-image benchmarks.
authors: Nannan Wang; Qianyi Zhang; Yongxia Zhang; Wei Wei

title: Bronchoscope Tip Localization With Learned Airway Constraints and an Open Source Simulator
abstract: Accurate bronchoscope localization is challenging because airway images contain limited texture and similar views across branches. We present BronchoLoc, a learning‐based framework that combines monocular video with a preoperative CT centerline graph to estimate the 3D bronchoscope tip position. Local visual tracking and global sequence context constrain predictions to the airway anatomy. The accompanying open‐source BronchoSim simulator generates synchronized images, depth, and trajectories (Traj) for training and evaluation. Averaged across Traj, localization RMSE was 5.65 mm in simulation with 82.8% branch selection accuracy and 8.72 mm in the physical phantom. Together, BronchoLoc and BronchoSim provide a framework for developing and evaluating image‐based airway localization.
authors: Emanuele Nicotra; James Davies; Bibhu Sharma; Adrienne Ji; Kefan Zhu; Phuoc Thien Phan; Nigel Hamilton Lovell; Thanh Nho Do

title: Budget-Constrained Fault-Tolerant Mutual Visibility for Autonomous Robots under the Mobility Fault Model
abstract: We investigate the mutual visibility problem for a swarm of $n\ge3$ autonomous mobile robots under the budget-constrained mobility fault model. The robots are opaque, so if three robots are collinear, the middle robot obstructs the visibility between the other two. Each robot is assigned a finite movement budget, reflecting its limited energy, that bounds the total distance it may traverse during the execution. Moreover, an arbitrary number of robots may become permanently immobile due to mobility faults. The objective is to design a distributed algorithm that enables the non-faulty robots to coordinate their movements so that, within a finite time, every non-faulty robot attains unobstructed visibility of all robots in the system, including the faulty ones, while respecting the prescribed movement budget. We consider luminous robots operating under the $\mathsf{SSYNC}$ model with non-rigid movements, without any agreement on their local coordinate systems, and equipped only with a {\it common fixed reference point}. We present a deterministic distributed algorithm that solves the problem despite an arbitrary number of mobility faults. The algorithm guarantees mutual visibility for the non-faulty robots, respects the movement budget of every robot, provides collision-free movements for the robots, and uses only 12 light colors.
authors: Prakhar Shukla; Animesh Maiti; Shivam Kumar; Subhash Bhagat

title: CAD/CAM Technologies, Three-Dimensional Printing, and Contemporary Dental Materials
abstract: CAD/CAM technologies have transformed the production of fixed prosthodontic restorations from a craft based on manual skill into a standardized and measurable digital process. This chapter addresses, for dental students in their clinical years and for early-career clinicians, the fundamental principles of CAD/CAM systems, digital and artificial intelligence-assisted restoration design, milling and three-dimensional printing technologies, contemporary restorative materials, the factors influencing material selection, accuracy and quality control in digital manufacturing, and the biocompatible and smart materials of the future, in the light of the current and verified literature. The digital workflow comprises three interdependent links—data acquisition, design, and manufacturing—and the quality of the final restoration is limited by the weakest link in the chain. Although milling remains the gold standard for definitive restorations, additive manufacturing has become established for interim restorations, models, and surgical guides, and it is a rapidly maturing alternative for definitive restorations. On the material side, the rise of monolithic zirconia, the diversification of lithium silicate glass-ceramics, and the establishment of resin-matrix ceramics in minimally invasive applications offer the clinician a broad range of options with varying levels of evidence. Current systematic-review and meta-analytic evidence shows that AI-assisted design shortens design time and improves reproducibility, but that human oversight remains indispensable. Clinical success depends on manufacturing the right material with validated parameters for the right indication and applying it with an appropriate adhesive or conventional cementation protocol. Accuracy should be defined by its trueness and precision components, marginal fit should be evaluated against clinical acceptability thresholds, and quality control should be maintained at every link of the digital chain. The graded, bioactive, self-healing, and stimuli-responsive materials of the future, together with additively manufactured ceramics, signal a transition from passive to smart materials in restorative dentistry.
authors: Muhammed Mustafa Akar; Alptuğ Kendirci

title: CHALLENGES AND MEDICAL-SOCIAL RATIONALE FOR DENTAL CARE IN THE CONTEXT OF SOCIO-ECONOMIC TRANSFORMATIONS IN UKRAINE
abstract: Introduction. The article analyzes problematic aspects of the organization of dental care for the population of Ukraine in the context of socio-economic transformations. Medical and social approaches to improving the accessibility and effectiveness of dental care are substantiated, taking into account the current challenges facing the healthcare system.Aim. The aim of the study is to substantiate the medical and social aspects of the organization of dental care in Ukraine in the context of socio-economic transformations, identify systemic gaps in financing mechanisms and access to services within the framework of the Medical Guarantees Program, and determine strategic directions for optimizing the sector through the integration of dental prevention into the primary health care system.Materials and methods. To achieve the stated aim, a comprehensive approach was applied using the following methods: bibliographic-semantic and analytical methods, system analysis, and comparative analysis.Results. Dental care in Ukraine operates under a mixed model with limited public coverage, which, for adults, is largely limited to emergency interventions, while children and eligible groups are provided with a broader range of services. Insufficient funding, regional inequalities in access, and fragmentation of the system were identified. The integration of dentistry into primary health care remains limited, and the preventive role of family physicians is only partially implemented, reducing the effectiveness of early detection and population-level prevention.Conclusions. The role of family physicians in the provision of dental care remains only partially implemented due to insufficient training, a lack of integrated clinical protocols, limited financial incentives for preventive activities, and fragmentation of the healthcare system. Improving the effectiveness of dental care requires expanding NHSU service packages, integrating dental prevention into primary health care, enhancing the training of family physicians, and implementing interdisciplinary collaboration.
authors: Viktor Y. Yelenskyi

title: CROPS: Cosserat-Rod-Based Co-Design of Soft Slender Programmable Material Systems for Biomedical Applications
abstract: Programmable slender structures that deform in response to external stimuli represent a class of emerging material systems, with applications in soft robotics, minimally invasive surgery, wearable electronics, and deployable structures. In biomedical applications, the on-demand design of slender structures, encompassing both their material layout and actuation, is instrumental in leveraging their large deformation and multiphysics actuation for meeting patient-specific design requirements. However, owing to geometric and material nonlinearities, their structure-actuation-response relationship is highly non-intuitive and entails resource-intensive computation. This renders trial-and-error and conventional design approaches largely intractable for addressing patient-specific needs. To this end, we present a Cosserat-rod-based design optimization framework for the autonomous design of programmable slender structures. Capitalizing on the Cosserat rod representation, the end-to-end differentiable framework is demonstrated on two case studies: (i) design of swellable stents that morph to the shape of carotid vessels; (ii) co-design of the remnant magnetization and the applied field of magnetically-active catheters to reduce the force exerted on the patient-specific vessel wall during insertion. As the actuation types, the swelling of gel-elastomer composites and the magnetic actuation of hard-magnetic composites are considered. Additionally, the contact of the rod with itself and its surroundings is accounted for. The proposed framework presents an autonomous design platform for material-structure-actuation co-design of soft slender material systems that support large deformation and multiphysics actuation, with contact addressed.
authors: Aaditya Chandrasekhar

title: Can Annotation‐Free Deep Learning Detect Periapical Bone Rarefactions on Panoramic Radiographs? A Paired Diagnostic Validation Study
abstract: ABSTRACT This study aimed to compare an annotation‐free deep learning (DL) model with human evaluators for detecting periapical bone rarefactions (PBRs) on panoramic radiographs (PRs) and to assess the clinical acceptability of AI‐supported dental imaging. A mixed‐methods diagnostic validation was conducted using 238 PRs, equally distributed between images with ( n = 119) and without ( n = 119) PBRs. Model performance was compared with that of four calibrated dentists: two oral and maxillofacial radiologists and two endodontists. The reference standard was based on internationally accepted radiographic criteria applied by calibrated researchers under expert supervision, with final classifications verified by the principal investigator. Diagnostic performance was assessed using standard diagnostic metrics, chance‐corrected agreement statistics and receiver operating characteristic analysis, while clinical acceptability was explored through questionnaires and thematically analysed semi‐structured interviews. At the sensitivity‐oriented decision threshold of 0.27, the DL model achieved a sensitivity of 0.924, a specificity of 0.109, an accuracy of 0.517, a precision of 0.509 and an F 1‐score of 0.657. Threshold‐independent binary discrimination was moderate (ROC‐AUC = 0.726). Human evaluators showed more balanced profiles, with accuracy ranging from 0.655 to 0.752 and F 1‐scores from 0.654 to 0.779. Professional perception was generally favourable, although responses varied among evaluators. The annotation‐free DL model showed high sensitivity and moderate discrimination for PBR detection. Although low specificity limits autonomous use, the findings support annotation‐free learning as a potentially scalable strategy, warranting further training with larger and more heterogeneous datasets.

title: Can We Really See the World in Three Dimensions? An Exploratory Study with Finger Alignment Task and Ponzo Illusion
abstract: Abstract Stereopsis is the perception of depth when two 2-dimensional (2D) images of an object from slightly different angles align with corresponding retinal positions in both eyes. However, when we consider the blind spot (BS), a new set of challenges arises. In binocular vision, one eye’s higher visual areas compensate for the other’s non-receptive region. However, our brain only receives information from one image patch in the BS region, and another visual patch does not contribute to constructing a comprehensive 3-dimensional (3D) representation of the scene. This suggests that the brain adeptly manages this dimensional transition. We aimed to determine the extent to which we perceive 3D across our entire field of view (FoV). We employed the Ponzo illusion, a stimulus relying on visual depth cues (pictorial depth cues), and an eye-tracking technique to assess participants’ accurate fixation and eye movement patterns. The participants attempted to align their index fingers before a chart paper to create a Horopter-like setup, supporting the hypothesis about our capacity for stereoscopic perception. The results of our exploratory pilot study with two specific tasks revealed that our ability to perceive depth diminishes beyond approximately 8° of retinal eccentricity (in the horizontal meridian) in both halves of the visual field centered around the fovea. This limitation is not apparent in our day-to-day experience.
authors: Amrita Mukherjee; Avijit Paul; Kuntal Ghosh

title: Capsule endoscopy: Emerging technologies and future clinical applications
abstract: Capsule endoscopy has evolved from a diagnostic tool for small bowel evaluation into a complex platform with expanding diagnostic and prognostic potential.This mini review aims to summarize recent advances in capsule endoscopy and explore potential clinical applications and future directions of this technology.The introduction of pan-enteric capsule endoscopy has enabled comprehensive evaluation of the entire gastrointestinal tract in a single, minimally invasive examination, supporting treat-to-target approaches and improving disease phenotyping in inflammatory bowel disease.Artificial intelligence (AI) represents one of the most important recent developments in capsule endoscopy.Deep learning algorithms have demonstrated high accuracy in lesion detection while reducing reading times.More recently, AI has been applied to automated inflammatory activity scoring, bowel cleansing assessment, and computer-assisted reporting, facilitating standardized interpretation and improving report quality.Magnetically controlled capsule endoscopy has further expanded the role of capsule technology by enabling active navigation within the upper gastrointestinal tract.Recent innovations include detachable-string systems for esophageal examination, remote 5Gassisted capsule navigation, and integration with AI-assisted image analysis, opening new perspectives for noninvasive evaluation from mouth to anus.Experimental robotic capsule prototypes have explored the feasibility of interventional functions, including tissue sampling and targeted drug delivery.These technologies remain at the preclinical stage, and their potential clinical applicability requires further investigation.
authors: Clelia Marmo; Maria Elena Riccioni

title: Carbon dots derived from traditional Chinese medicines: a novel therapeutic strategy for ocular diseases
abstract: Carbon dots (CDs) represent a novel category of zero-dimensional carbon-based nanomaterials featuring favorable biosafety in vitro and in acute animal studies. They also exhibit distinctive optical properties and diverse pharmacological activities. Synthesized via eco-friendly green routes using traditional Chinese medicines (TCMs) and their extracts, TCM-derived carbon dots (TCM-CDs) display distinct properties compared to conventional nanocarriers. Benefiting from their inherent nanostructures, abundant surface functional groups, and nanozyme-like activity, TCM-CDs can deliver intrinsic therapeutic effects without loading exogenous drugs or relying on residual herbal ingredients. They possess multiple bioactivities, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antibacterial and neuroprotective effects, which make them potential non-invasive therapeutic candidates for refractory ocular disorders. A growing body of studies has validated the promising therapeutic efficacy of TCM-CDs in animal models against autoimmune uveitis, retinal lesions, and optic nerve injuries, highlighting their encouraging preclinical findings that warrant further investigation toward clinical translation. Focusing on the intrinsic therapeutic capacity of TCM-CDs, this review systematically summarizes their core functional mechanisms and research progress in ocular disease intervention, discusses prevailing academic controversies and unresolved research bottlenecks in this field, and proposes prospective developmental directions. This work intends to offer comprehensive theoretical evidence and guidance directions for subsequent mechanistic investigations and clinical translation of TCM-CDs in ophthalmic research.
authors: Tingyu Yang; Zongqi Feng; Xiao Zhang; Lihui Zhang; Yu Su; Ruihua Liu; Rina Sa; A Lamusi

title: Case Report: Giant adult rhabdomyoma of the parapharyngeal space: diagnostic and surgical pitfalls
abstract: Background: Adult-type extracardiac rhabdomyoma is a rare benign skeletal-muscle neoplasm that most often arises in the head and neck but is exceptional in the parapharyngeal space, where it may mimic salivary or neurogenic tumours. Case presentation: A 67-year-old man presented with a 6-month history of progressive dysphagia, globus sensation, and mild hoarseness. Computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated an approximately 9-cm, well-circumscribed right parapharyngeal mass with relatively homogeneous internal characteristics and mild-to-moderate enhancement. Because direct glottic exposure was inadequate, tracheotomy-assisted airway management preceded complete excision through a right lateral transcervical approach. Histopathology showed large polygonal cells with abundant eosinophilic granular cytoplasm. The tumour was positive for desmin and smooth-muscle actin, with focal MyoD1 and myogenin expression, a low Ki-67 labelling index, and negative S-100 staining, supporting adult-type rhabdomyoma. Recovery was uneventful, and magnetic resonance imaging at 6 and 12 months showed no recurrence. Conclusion: Adult rhabdomyoma should be considered in the differential diagnosis of a well-circumscribed parapharyngeal mass in an older adult. Integrated radiological and pathological assessment, careful airway planning, complete conservative excision, and long-term surveillance are central to management.
authors: Bingyi Dai; Hongyang Qu; Rong Liu; Changling Sun; Xiao Yin

title: Cell-autonomous restoration of splicing homeostasis and RP11 phenotype in patient-derived RPE and retinal organoids by PRPF31.AAV gene therapy
abstract: Mutations in the PRPF31 gene cause retinitis pigmentosa type 11 (RP11), a progressive blinding disease triggered by defects in the spliceosome, the cellular machinery responsible for RNA processing. Although gene replacement holds therapeutic promise, it remains unclear whether it can effectively rescue both primary target cell types across different disease stages. Here we show that viral-mediated delivery of PRPF31 to patient-derived retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) cells and 3D retinal organoids restores RNA splicing activity and reverses core cellular pathology. Gene delivery cleared toxic protein aggregates, restored essential RPE functions, including structural polarity, cilia integrity, and cellular waste clearance, and boosted light-evoked activity in photoreceptors. Notably, robust rescue was achievable even in mature cells, whereas combining gene therapy with autophagy-activating drugs offered no added benefit. These findings demonstrate that restoring splicing homeostasis alone drives functional recovery, supporting a broad clinical window for PRPF31 gene therapy in RP11.
authors: Maria Elia; Valda Pauzuolyte; Μαρία Γεωργίου; Mark Basche; Carina Hansohn; Elton J. R. Vasconcelos; Robert Atkinson; Sushma Grellscheid; Colin A. Johnson; Gerrit Hilgen; Henning Urlaub; Alexander J. Smith; Sina Mozaffari‐Jovin; Robin R. Ali; Majlinda Lako

title: Changing Colorectal Cancer Epidemiology Demands a Risk-Adapted European Screening Strategy
abstract: European colorectal cancer screening remains largely age-defined despite changing epidemiology, heterogeneous risk, non-participation and finite colonoscopy capacity. European guidance already anticipates risk-based thresholds, intervals and test allocation; how to test these across heterogeneous health systems remains unresolved. We propose a four-decision policy and research framework, not a validated clinical protocol, addressing when screening should begin or recur, which first-line test should be offered, what result or risk trajectory should trigger escalation, and how diagnosis and treatment should be completed. Quantitative faecal immunochemical testing (FIT) should remain a principal population-based strategy and high-quality colonoscopy the confirmatory and therapeutic standard, while national programmes may differ. Previous quantitative FIT results, age, sex, family history, comorbidity and screening behaviour can be prospectively evaluated as modifiers of interval and threshold. Multitarget stool tests, blood-based cell-free DNA, microbiome or volatile-organic-compound classifiers, colon capsule endoscopy and CT colonography should address defined pathway failures rather than act as interchangeable competitors. Because evidence for risk adaptation remains modelled or observational, implementation should proceed only through prospectively governed pilots. Evaluation should prioritise sustained participation, advanced neoplasia removed, interval cancer, colonoscopy use, equity and societal cost. Risk adaptation should optimise existing workflows through prospectively validated programmatic rules, not unvetted diagnostic layers.
authors: Anastasios Koulaouzidis; Ramesh Pulendran Arasaradnam; Pablo Cortegoso Valdivia; George Koulaouzidis; Ervin Tóth; Wojciech M. Marlicz

title: Classification of cystoid macular edema status from retinal vasculitis fluorescein angiography images using a convolutional neural network
abstract: Introduction: Cystoid macular edema (CME) is a vision-threatening complication of retinal vasculitis, a rare inflammatory disease for which large imaging datasets are difficult to obtain. Detection of CME on fluorescein angiography (FA) requires expert interpretation, motivating automated image-based approaches to support clinical decision-making. Deep learning methods, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have shown strong performance in medical image analysis but are constrained by limited labeled data in rare diseases. Transfer learning may mitigate this limitation by adapting pretrained models to small, task-specific datasets. Methods: We analyzed 207 de-identified late-phase 55° FA images from 117 patients with retinal vasculitis. The primary target was concurrent patient-level CME status, established through specialist review of clinical records and optical coherence tomography obtained at the same clinical visit as FA. A patient was classified as CME-positive when CME was present in at least one eye. An ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18 was evaluated using five-fold nested, patient-level cross-validation. Within each outer-development cohort, 144 candidate configurations were compared by four-fold inner cross-validation and selected according to mean inner-validation AUROC. Each selected configuration was evaluated only on its corresponding untouched outer-test fold. Results: Across 117 pooled patient-level outer-test predictions, the model-selection pipeline achieved an AUROC of 0.708 (95% CI, 0.610-0.802), an AUPRC of 0.626 (95% CI, 0.493-0.755), and an accuracy of 0.726 (95% CI, 0.641-0.803). Sensitivity was 0.694 (95% CI, 0.558-0.822), specificity was 0.750 (95% CI, 0.643-0.853), and the F1 score was 0.680 (95% CI, 0.563-0.780). Exploratory Grad-CAM analysis visualized regions associated with model predictions. Discussion: The nested model-selection pipeline showed moderate discrimination with a relatively balanced operating profile and slightly higher specificity than sensitivity. Clinically relevant false-positive and false-negative errors, together with the absence of external validation, preclude clinical deployment.
authors: Celina Wang; Koushani Chakrabarty; Stephen D. Anesi; Peter Y. Chang

title: Clinical Reasoning: A 60-Year-Old Woman With Fever, Headache, Diplopia, and Unilateral Periorbital Swelling
abstract: Evaluating delayed vascular complications after a focal cranial infection can be diagnostically challenging. In this case, a 60-year-old woman with approximately 1 month of recurrent gingival swelling and pain later developed fever and headache, followed by horizontal diplopia and progressive unilateral periorbital swelling. Examination showed a left abduction deficit and conjunctival chemosis. Cerebral angiography obtained during evaluation demonstrated severe narrowing of the cavernous segment of the internal carotid artery. Although the patient improved clinically after antimicrobial therapy, routine follow-up imaging 1 year later revealed a new vascular lesion at the site of the prior arterial abnormality. This case highlights the importance of interval neurovascular follow-up imaging when cavernous internal carotid artery abnormalities are identified during the initial presentation of febrile ophthalmoplegia.
authors: Naijimiding Rexiati; Naijimiding Rexiati; Shihao Jiang; Aximujiang Axier; Nizhamidingjiang Rexiati; Nizhamidingjiang Rexiati; Riqing Su; Zengliang Wang; Pahaerding Balatiniyazi; Aisha Maimaitili

title: Clinical and CBCT Based Evaluation of Residual Ridge Length in Posterior Partially Edentulous Mandibular Arches for Dental Implant Planning
abstract: Dental implants have proved to be one of the most reliable methods for treating partially edentulous patients.Successful placement of dental implants in posterior regions of the mandible requires careful evaluation of ridge length, width, and height of residual bone relative to the inferior alveolar nerve and mental foramen.Clinical examination alone does not give an exact idea of the residual ridge anatomy due to morphological variations and ridge resorption following tooth extraction.Cone Beam Computed Tomography (CBCT) is an important diagnostic tool providing high-resolution, three-dimensional images of the alveolar bone with minimal distortion and radiation.This research discusses the significance of residual ridge length analysis for implant therapy in posterior partially edentulous mandibular arches, the anatomy of ridges, methods for evaluating ridge length, importance of CBCT in implantology, patterns of ridge resorption, measurements, clinical application, disadvantages, and prospects of digital planning in implant therapy.The article concludes by comparing clinical examinations with radiographic techniques in ridge length determination and concludes that radiographic examinations prove better than clinical methods.Importance of digital workflow integration, guided implant surgery, and artificial intelligence-based imaging to enhance implant treatment results is also pointed out in the article.Evaluation of the residual ridge length becomes vital in defining the size of the implant, its inclination angle, number of implants, and necessity of performing bone augmentation.

title: ColoACT: Multi-Cue Action Chunking for Smooth Autonomous Colon Navigation on a Self-Propelled Endoscopic Robot
abstract: Autonomous colonoscopic navigation can reduce operator burden and the risk of loop formation or tissue trauma, but remains challenging due to deformable anatomy, weak-texture and specular endoscopic visuals, and contact-rich viscoelastic interactions. Existing methods either rely on geometry-driven pipelines, which are efficient and interpretable yet brittle due to manually engineered features and switching logic, or adopt learning-based policies, whose inferred depth/geometry can become temporally inconsistent or overly smooth under weak texture and specular highlights while simulation-trained variants (e.g., deep reinforcement learning) may further suffer from a sim-to-real gap. We propose ColoACT, an autonomous navigation system that integrates an RGB-D-E based Action Chunking Transformer policy (ColoACT policy) for a compact self-propelled Bevel-Gear-Based Endoscopic Robot (BGER). The ColoACT policy augments RGB with estimated relative depth and a gradient-based pseudo-elevation map to enhance fold-ridge saliency and other high-frequency geometric cues, and enables smooth continuous control of the BGER by predicting overlapping action chunks and fusing them via temporal ensembling. In different \textit{ex-vivo} porcine colons (approximately 60 cm), our system achieves success rates of 85.4\% and 72.5\% in straight and curved segments, respectively, and achieves 70\% success in 90-degree turns and 60\% in double-bend sequences, with feasibility further demonstrated in challenging triple-bend segments. The project page is available at: https://Adamhu1.github.io/ColoACT/.

title: Colon capsule endoscopy and cost-effectiveness across colorectal care: a valuable filter, but a poor universal substitute
abstract: Colon capsule endoscopy (CCE) is a patient-friendly, minimally invasive alternative to conventional colonoscopy, but its value depends on pathway performance rather than diagnostic accuracy alone. This narrative review examines the cost-effectiveness of CCE across colorectal cancer screening, symptomatic investigation, incomplete colonoscopy, post-polypectomy surveillance, inflammatory bowel disease monitoring, and AI-supported implementation. Targeted literature searches were performed in PubMed and official guidance sources through 6 July 2026. Across broad screening populations, CCE is not yet cost-effective compared with biennial faecal immunochemical testing (FIT) or 10-yearly colonoscopy; contemporary Dutch MISCAN modelling found all CCE screening strategies dominated at full adherence, largely because unit cost and follow-up colonoscopy burden remained high. The dominant economic problem is pathway duplication: a 2025 meta-analysis found a pooled follow-up endoscopy rate of 42%, and contemporary UK/Scottish service data showed that about half of patients required further optical endoscopy or sigmoidoscopy. CCE may offer conditional value after incomplete colonoscopy, in lower-risk symptomatic triage, and in carefully selected surveillance pathways where a negative or low-risk capsule result may avoid, defer, or focus colonoscopy. Evidence from Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis monitoring is encouraging but should not be extrapolated uncritically to colorectal cancer screening or dysplasia surveillance, where biopsy and therapy remain decisive. AI-assisted CCE may reduce reading time and improve polyp detection, but robust lifetime cost-effectiveness models are still needed. The current evidence supports CCE as a pathway-dependent filter, not a universal substitute for colonoscopy.
