title: Online Multimodal Workload Assessment in Contact-Rich Physical Human-Robot Interaction
abstract: Contact-rich physical human--robot interaction (pHRI) imposes time-varying demands associated with physical interaction, motor regulation, and physiological response, motivating continuous assessment of interaction workload. This paper presents an online multimodal assessment framework that integrates interaction wrench, planar tool-center-point (TCP) kinematics, and skin conductance level (SCL) into four interpretable workload-related factors. Their relative contributions are adjusted using path curvature to reflect changes in motion demand and task progression to account for gradual physiological variation over time. The framework was evaluated with 24 participants across 18 controlled combinations of temperature, acoustic noise, and illuminance under two admittance-control modes. Strict leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) evaluation used standardized pupil diameter ($\mathrm{PD}_z$) as an independent physiological reference and included comparisons with static variants and representative state-of-the-art learning-based baselines. The proposed framework achieves a cohort-mean $30\,\mathrm{s}$ block-wise Spearman correlation of $ρ_{30}=0.308$ with the physiological reference, with positive subject-level correspondence in 23 of 24 participants. Its overall performance is comparable to the state-of-the-art learning-based baseline. At the same time, our framework keeps the assessment process transparent through explicit workload-related factors and defined weighting rules, while outperforming the corresponding fixed-weight formulation. The framework also maintains consistent performance across the two tested admittance-control modes. These results support a transparent and interpretable approach to continuous interaction workload assessment in contact-rich pHRI.
authors: Yanyi Chen; Fan Yang; Min Deng

title: Open ultrasound foundation model for robust segmentation and clinical measurement across heterogeneous settings
abstract: Ultrasound is the most widely deployed imaging modality worldwide, yet clinical AI remains fragmented into narrow single-task models that fail when device, operator, or anatomy changes. Here we present SonoCorpus, an open resource unifying 456,963 images and 1,626,085 expert masks from 53 public datasets spanning 24 clinical applications and 17 countries, and SonoBase, an interactive segmentation foundation model pretrained on it. Across fifteen evaluation datasets introducing new organs, devices, operators, and geographies, SonoBase outperforms SAM2, MedSAM2, and the concept-promptable MedSAM3 on every dataset and matches per-dataset specialist models trained on the same data; on fully external data it exceeds the accuracy these baselines achieve on their own in-distribution benchmarks. Ejection fraction derived from its segmentations falls within inter-observer variability (6.63\% error), with fewer misclassifications at the defibrillator-candidacy threshold than either promptable baseline (13\% versus 18--42\%); fetal head-circumference (1.81~mm) and gestational-age (1.2 days) errors fall below inter-observer variability. Where a baseline fails outright, one in four test cases, SonoBase recovers a usable segmentation in 81\% of them, including on handheld probes operated by minimally trained users in two low- and middle-income countries (Sierra Leone and Tanzania). Five labeled examples can help the model adapt to a new setting, and the identical training protocol transfers well to newer models such as SAM3, locating the advantage in ultrasound-specific pretraining rather than any single architecture. To ensure reproducibility and enable the community to build on SonoBase as a platform, we release all checkpoints, optimizer states, data-split indices, deduplication hashes, and starter code at https://github.com/AlfredQin/sonobase.
authors: Chao Qin; Fahad Shahbaz Khan; Salman Khan; Sarim Ather; Siddiq Anwar; Rao Muhammad Anwer; Shadab Khan

title: Orofacial pain disorder or trigeminal autonomic cephalalgia? Insights into pathophysiology and implications in medicine and dentistry
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This narrative review highlights the importance of orofacial pain considerations in the differential diagnosis of trigeminal autonomic cephalalgias (TACs)/trigeminal autonomic orofacial pains (TAOPs). In addition, we provide novel insights into the pathophysiology of the presentation of TACs in the maxillary (V2) and mandibular (V3) trigeminal distributions (TAOPs). BACKGROUND: TACs are lifelong disorders characterized by severe unilateral head pain accompanied by cranial autonomic phenomena. However, the head pain experienced may refer to the face, be present solely in the orofacial region as TAOPs, or even be experienced as a toothache. These presentations, involving V2/V3, may resemble disorders of diverse etiology and pathophysiology that may share some similarities with TACs, confusing the patient while relating symptoms, and creating a diagnostic dilemma for the clinician potentially leading to misdiagnosis. Moreover, TACs pathophysiology has not been discussed in relation to V2/V3 presentations (TAOPs). METHODS: A literature search was performed on PubMed/Scopus to find relevant literature about TACs and TAOPs, and case reports of orofacial presentations. Deep reanalysis of several of our published articles on preclinical models of TACs was conducted to assess potential of V2-V3 components. RESULTS: TACs orofacial presentations are not as common but if present can lead to misdiagnosis with significant consequences. Patients presenting TACs involving the midface as TAOPs experience an important delay for a correct diagnosis including multiple and diverse health provider visits, with a risk of having well-intended but misguided procedures. Differential diagnosis considerations need to include dental/odontogenic causes, sinusitis, temporomandibular disorders, Eagle syndrome, trigeminal neuralgia, and migraine (orofacial migraine, neurovascular orofacial pain). A reanalysis of preclinical data provides novel insights into this orofacial involvement. In two TAC-specific preclinical neuronal populations, recording either trigeminal or superior salivatory nucleus neurons, it was observed that ~20% and 37.5% of neurons, respectively, had cutaneous receptive fields that included or were exclusively within the V2-V3 trigeminal division. Whereas the numbers are not large, these demonstrate that even in rodent models in neuronal populations that could be considered TAC-like, they can extend to, or exclusively involve, the facial region, similar to TAOPs. CONCLUSION: The potential presence of TACs in the orofacial region can be observed from preclinical models to the clinical setting. The International Classification of Headache Disorders (ICHD) needs to recognize this additional localization, as well as the intraoral one, including dental structures. Education about TACs/TAOPs in the medical and dental setting is vital. Evidence has shown that dentists are one of the first providers that are seen by this patient population due to similarities with dental pain. The dentist specialized in orofacial pain is a key ally in the identification of TACs/TAOPs. The medical/neurology and dental/orofacial pain settings have a great opportunity and responsibility to work together to stop years of pain in this patient population.
authors: Marcela Romero‐Reyes; Simon Akerman

title: Outcomes and Reclassification Patterns in Inflammatory Bowel Disease Unclassified: A Multicenter Study Matched With Ulcerative Colitis From Spanish ENEIDA Registry
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIM: Around 10% of patients with inflammatory bowel disease do not fulfill the diagnostic criteria for Crohn's disease (CD) or ulcerative colitis (UC). These cases are labelled as inflammatory bowel disease unclassified (IBDU). The aim of the study was to compare therapeutic requirements in patients with IBDU and UC and to identify predictive factors of reclassification. METHODS: This was a multicenter retrospective cohort study based on the ENEIDA registry. Patients diagnosed with IBDU or indeterminate colitis between January 2010 and December 2016 were included. All cases were matched by sex, age at diagnosis, and disease extent with at least two UC patients from the same hospital. The Kaplan-Meier method was performed to assess diagnostic changes during follow-up. Fine-Gray competing-risks regression analysis identified predictive factors of reclassification. RESULTS: Two hundred and nine IBDU patients and 465 UC patients were included. After a median follow-up of 90 months, no significant differences were observed in the use of immunomodulator (37.3% vs. 37%, p = 0.934) and advanced therapies (29.2% vs. 23.9%, p = 0.143) between IBDU and UC. No statistical differences were found in the surgical rates (5.7% vs. 4.7%, p = 0.579). Overall, 59 IBDU patients (28.2%) were reclassified (30 UC and 29 CD). Baseline extensive colitis was associated with a lower probability of subsequent reclassification to UC (SHR: 0.33; 95% CI: 0.12-0.91). No independent predictive factors for reclassification to CD were identified. CONCLUSIONS: Therapeutic management of IBDU and UC patients tended to be similar. Two-thirds of patients remained classified as IBDU.

title: Overview of Persistent Inter-Professional Rivalry Within the Laboratory Medicine Practice Domain of Tertiary Healthcare Institutions in Nigeria: A Narrative Review
abstract: The persistent inter-professional rivalry within the laboratory medicine practice domain of Nigerian tertiary healthcare institutions constitutes a systemic crisis that undermines diagnostic accuracy, jeopardizes patient safety, and disrupts healthcare delivery. This longstanding conflict between the Medical Laboratory Scientists (MLS) and the laboratory-based physicians (Clinical Pathologists) centers mainly on operational independence, leadership in clinical laboratories, and statutory boundaries. This review examines the historical, legal, educational, and socio-political causes of this rivalry in Nigerian tertiary healthcare settings. Historically, laboratory medicine practice functions shifted from physician-led to specialized, autonomous scientific roles, leading to overlapping claims over laboratory and clinical consultation domains. Conflicting laws—such as the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria (MDCN) Practitioners Act and the Medical Laboratory Science Council of Nigeria (MLSCN) Act—have created parallel regulatory frameworks, resulting in ongoing legal disputes at the National Industrial Court. These dynamics foster operational silos, strikes, and diagnostic errors, often causing preventable misdiagnoses. To transform this rivalry into collaborative clinical efforts, the article recommends a comprehensive approach that includes legislative reforms, separation of administrative and clinical roles, formal interprofessional education in training, and joint governance boards in tertiary healthcare settings. Ultimately, resolving this conflict is vital to achieving international standards and protecting Nigerian patient care from interprofessional conflicts.
authors: Collins Amadi; Roy Amadi; Sasha Amadi; Elena Amadi; Comfort John

title: PAPEL PROGNÓSTICO DAS ARMADILHAS EXTRACELULARES DE NEUTRÓFILOS NAS DOENÇAS INFLAMATÓRIAS INTESTINAIS
abstract: As doenças inflamatórias intestinais (DII), especialmente a retocolite ulcerativa e a doença de Crohn, apresentam curso clínico crônico, heterogêneo e recidivante, com risco variável de atividade persistente, falha terapêutica, complicações e recidiva. Embora parâmetros clínicos, endoscópicos, histopatológicos e laboratoriais sejam utilizados no acompanhamento desses pacientes, permanece a necessidade de biomarcadores capazes de contribuir para a estratificação de risco. As armadilhas extracelulares de neutrófilos (NETs) participam da inflamação e do dano tecidual nas DII, porém ainda são limitadas as evidências que relacionam seus componentes a desfechos clínicos de valor prognóstico. Esta revisão integrativa objetivou sintetizar as evidências disponíveis sobre a associação entre biomarcadores relacionados às NETs e desfechos clínicos relevantes em pacientes adultos com DII. A busca foi realizada nas bases PubMed, Scopus e Embase, utilizando os termos “Neutrophil Extracellular Traps” OR “NETs” AND “Inflammatory Bowel Disease” AND “Prognosis”. Foram incluídos estudos clínicos publicados entre 2020 e 2025, em inglês, disponíveis na íntegra, que avaliaram marcadores de NETs em adultos com DII. Foram excluídos revisões, relatos de caso, resumos de congressos, teses, editoriais, estudos pré-clínicos, duplicatas, estudos pediátricos e trabalhos sem relação com a pergunta da revisão. A seleção foi organizada na plataforma Parsifal e compreendeu identificação dos registros, triagem por títulos e resumos, remoção de duplicatas e leitura dos textos completos. Dos estudos incluídos foram extraídos autores, ano de publicação, delineamento e principais achados relacionados ao prognóstico. Foram identificados 63 registros, sendo 12 no PubMed, 23 no Scopus e 28 na Embase; após as etapas de seleção, três estudos compuseram a síntese final. title: PREFERENDO: a preference for the full picture in pediatric capsule endoscopy
abstract: The PREFERENDO consensus provides a valuable framework for pediatric endoscopy reporting [1]. Its capsule domain already includes preparation quality, completeness, lesion description and interpretation. The opportunity for refinement lies in connecting these fields to the endorsed scores. We suggest an implementation principle: each reported score should include the information needed to understand what it measures and how examination quality constrains its interpretation.
authors: Anastasios Koulaouzidis; Ervin Tóth; Wojciech M. Marlicz

title: Paradigm shifts in prostate biopsy strategies in the era of precision medicine
abstract: The escalating global burden of prostate cancer necessitates continuous refinement of diagnostic strategies. Although prostate biopsy remains the gold standard for diagnosis, key procedural aspects, including biopsy template, guidance methods, and biopsy route, remain subjects of ongoing debate. Current approaches have yet to achieve the dual goals of high sensitivity and high specificity in diagnostic performance. In recent years, ongoing advancements in related fields have generated substantial clinical evidence, offering further insights into optimizing biopsy strategies. This review provides a synthesized framework for navigating the paradigm shift from traditional, standardized biopsy toward personalized, precision-based approaches. We not only trace the evolution of biopsy techniques but also offer a comprehensive, in-depth exploration of how patient-specific factors, such as prostate volume, prostate-specific antigen density, and Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System scores, can inform individualized biopsy decisions, thereby providing practical clinical guidance. In addition to critically evaluating conventional biopsy paradigms, we systematically examine emerging biopsy strategies and synthesize high-quality studies at the forefront of this field. Finally, against the backdrop of the artificial intelligence era, we highlight the transformative potential of artificial intelligence and robotic platforms across the diagnosis. By integrating current development and future directions, this review offers a structured framework for personalized biopsy decision-making, ultimately aiming to achieve both high sensitivity and high specificity in individualized prostate cancer diagnosis.
authors: Chenhui Tang; Zhen Liang; Weigang Yan

title: Pediatric inflammatory bowel disease: a review of current research
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), comprising Crohn’s disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis, is a growing global health challenge, with approximately 25% of cases diagnosed before the age of 20. These chronic immune- mediated disorders result from complex interactions between genetic predisposition, environmental triggers, gut microbiome alterations, and immune dysregulation. Pediatric IBD presents with more extensive disease than adult-onset cases, with unique manifestations including growth failure and delayed puberty. Diagnosis relies on clinical assessment, fecal calprotectin, and endoscopic evaluation. Contemporary management emphasizes treat-to-target strategies using exclusive enteral nutrition (60–80% remission rates) and biologic therapies for moderate- to-severe disease. Anti-TNF agents remain first-line biologics, while ustekinumab has recently received Food and Drug Administration and European Medicines Agency approvals for pediatric CD based on the UNITI Jr trial, and emerging data on JAK inhibitors further expand the therapeutic landscape. This review provides a comprehensive overview of disease subtypes, pathophysiology, diagnostics, and evidence-based treatment strategies.

title: Perception of Special Needs Dentistry Amongst Allied Dental Professionals in Australia
abstract: OBJECTIVE: In Australia, Dental Therapists (DTs), Dental Hygienists (DHs) and Oral Health Therapists (OHTs) encounter Special Needs (SN) patients in their clinical practice. This study investigates their perception, training, working experience and referral patterns within Special Needs Dentistry (SND). MATERIALS AND METHODS: Paper-based questionnaire was distributed to a systematically selected sample of 1000 registered DHs, DTs and OHTs who were members of professional bodies in Australia. Respondents were included irrespective of age, gender, length of working experience and country of graduation. Data analysis consisted of Chi-squared regression analysis (p < 0.05) using IBM SPSS Windows Version 29.0 (Melbourne, Victoria, Australia). RESULTS: A response rate of 49.8% (215 DTs, 107 DHs and 163 OHTs) was obtained. A significantly larger proportion of OHTs (59.5%) was aware of SND as a specialty compared to DHs (45%) and DTs (41.9%) (p < 0.05) and hence OHTs referred to SND specialists more often than other groups. In addition, 73.6% of OHTs, 63.6% of DHs and 40% of DTs had both didactic and clinical training in SND (p < 0.05). All the categories stated lack of training and continuing professional development (CPD) in SND as the main reasons for not treating SN patients. They therefore expressed interest in attending related CPD training (OHTs: 90.2%, DHs: 88.8% and DTs: 88.3%). CONCLUSIONS: OHTs demonstrated greater awareness, training, working experience and referral in SND than DHs and DTs; however, training gaps across all groups highlight the need for strengthened undergraduate education and accessible CPD in SND. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Understanding the perception of allied dental professionals regarding SND is crucial for improving access to and the quality of care for patients with special needs. Prior research has highlighted gaps in training and confidence levels amongst general practitioners; however, little is known about the perspectives of allied professionals. This study provides valuable insights into their awareness, perceived roles and educational needs, emphasizing the importance of inclusive team-based care.
authors: Jessica Francis; Gelsomina L. Borromeo

title: Periodontal Phenotype and Soft Tissue Management in Multidisciplinary Treatments
abstract: In contemporary dentistry, achieving successful, aesthetic, and sustainable treatment outcomes relies heavily on the accurate analysis of soft tissue dynamics and the periodontal phenotype by clinicians. This book chapter comprehensively examines the strategic role of periodontal phenotype and soft tissue management at the intersection of various dental disciplines, including orthodontics, implantology, and prosthodontics. Within the scope of the study, the historical evolution of the periodontal phenotype concept is first addressed, defining its position in modern dental practice. Subsequently, current clinical evaluation and diagnostic methods are detailed to ensure precise treatment planning. The core body of the chapter optimizes the most critical components of multidisciplinary approaches: maintaining tissue stability before and after tooth movement in orthodontic-periodontal relationships, enhancing long-term implant success through peri-implant soft tissue management and phenotype modification techniques in implantology, and preserving gingival health by ensuring the biological compatibility of restorative margins at the prosthetic interface. The final section provides comprehensive decision trees to guide clinicians swiftly in daily practice and discusses future horizons in the field. Consecutively, this study offers an evidence-based framework aimed at preventing tissue recession, optimizing aesthetics, and achieving biologically compatible, predictable results in complex multidisciplinary cases.
authors: Mevlüt Furkan Sadeler

title: Perspectives of Indonesian dental practitioners on application of artificial intelligence in dentistry
abstract: Limited evidence exists about the knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions of Indonesian dental practitioners with regard to artificial intelligence (AI). A cross-sectional survey was performed among 235 licensed dentists throughout Indonesia, assessing their attitudes on the potential benefits and barriers of AI in dentistry, and its perceived influence on their profession. A “positive attitude – knowledge gap” was observed: attitudes towards AI were very positive (79.6% good), with comparatively low levels of basic AI knowledge (54.3% good). Dentists are positive towards the impact of AI on their professional efficiency (86.4%) and accuracy (82.1%), but remain concerned over the potential barriers of its implementation, specifically the ambiguity in legal liability (82.1%), high cost (77.0%), and data security issues (71.9%). The majority of dentists do not believe that AI will replace them (65.5%), but most worry that the use of AI may erode their skills (54.9%). There is strong support for curricular change (83.4%). Overall, Indonesian dentists are amenable to AI but are currently limited by low knowledge and many AI-related barriers. To increase its adoption, future efforts should focus on promoting practitioner education, as well as increasing confidence in legal and regulatory structures.

title: Photobiology in ophthalmology: from evolutionary adaptation to translational therapeutics
abstract: Life has evolved under continuous exposure to solar light, and the emergence of the eye during the Cambrian period is thought to have accelerated biological diversification. Beyond vision, light acts as a biological regulator of metabolism and tissue organization. To elucidate ocular disease mechanisms and develop new therapies, we have investigated how light is sensed by the eye and coupled to physiological and pathological responses. This review reexamines the eye as a photoreceptive organ and summarizes recent advances showing how light input governs retinal metabolism, refractive development, and visual restoration. First, we describe how retinal light reception is linked to oxygen-dependent metabolic control. As one of the most oxygen-demanding tissues, the retina relies on hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) signaling to coordinate angiogenesis, mitochondrial metabolism, fibrosis, and neuronal survival. Beyond pathological neovascularization, disrupted light-metabolic coupling contributes to neurodegeneration and subretinal scarring. Screening of natural compounds identified HIF regulators with therapeutic efficacy, and optical approaches were developed to detect hypoxia-induced intraocular cytokines noninvasively. Second, we show that environmental light regulates ocular growth in ways beyond image formation. Violet light activates nonvisual photoreception via OPN5-expressing retinal ganglion cells, engaging an OPN5-EGR1 pathway that preserves choroidal thickness and suppresses axial elongation through coordinated retina-brain-choroid-sclera interactions. Third, we demonstrate that light itself becomes therapeutic through optogenetic visual restoration. Chimeric rhodopsins confer high-sensitivity light responsiveness to surviving inner retinal neurons and have recently entered first-in-human clinical evaluation for advanced retinitis pigmentosa. These findings establish photobiology as a unifying framework for translational ophthalmology.

title: Pitfalls in the Diagnosis and Classification of Crohn’s Disease: Misdiagnosis, Overdiagnosis, and Misclassification
abstract: Crohn's disease (CD) remains challenging to diagnose and classify accurately despite advances in endoscopy, cross-sectional imaging, intestinal ultrasound, and inflammatory biomarkers. Earlier diagnosis and treat-to-target strategies have improved outcomes but have also increased the risk of misdiagnosis, overdiagnosis, and misclassification of disease activity or severity. Misdiagnosis may expose patients without CD to unnecessary immunosuppressive therapy while delaying recognition and treatment of the true underlying condition, including drug-induced enteropathy, bile acid malabsorption, irritable bowel syndrome, and other disorders of gut-brain interaction. This is particularly relevant in tuberculosis (TB)-endemic regions, where intestinal TB remains one of the most challenging mimics of CD. Overdiagnosis commonly results from overinterpretation of nonspecific symptoms, incidental terminal ileitis, or isolated endoscopic and histological abnormalities. Elevated fecal calprotectin lacks specificity, whereas a low value provides stronger evidence against CD, although it does not reliably exclude isolated small-bowel disease. Misclassification most often reflects underestimation of disease severity, particularly when standard ileocolonoscopy fails to detect proximal small bowel or transmural disease or when discordant endoscopic and cross-sectional imaging findings are not appropriately reconciled. This review examines the major diagnostic and classification pitfalls in CD and proposes a practical, multidisciplinary approach based on integrating complementary investigations, longitudinal reassessment, and diagnostic reconsideration when uncertainty persists.
authors: Gülden Bilican; Biljana Brezina; Mohmmed Tauseef Sharip; Sreedhar Subramanian; Abdullah Mutlu; Tarkan Karakan; Mehmet Cindoruk; Çağdaş Kalkan; Nurulamin M Noor

title: Pixels to precision: Deep learning in dental imaging
abstract: Dental imaging is fundamental to diagnosis, treatment planning, and follow-up in Oral Medicine and Maxillofacial Radiology. Although conventional radiographic interpretation remains dependent on professional expertise, diagnostic performance may be influenced by observer variability, image quality, workload, and the subtle nature of early pathological changes. The development of Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning (DL), has introduced new approaches for automated analysis of dental and maxillofacial images. This narrative review discusses the evolution, principles, applications, clinical relevance, limitations, and future directions of deep learning in dental imaging, with emphasis on intraoral radiography, panoramic radiography, cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT), and related imaging modalities. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have demonstrated applications in dental caries detection, periodontal bone assessment, periapical lesion detection, tooth identification and numbering, jaw lesion analysis, anatomical segmentation, and treatment planning. More advanced architectures, including U-Net, residual networks, object-detection models, three-dimensional CNNs, and emerging transformer-based systems, have expanded the scope of automated image interpretation. However, the rapid growth of research has also highlighted important limitations, including small and heterogeneous datasets, inconsistent annotation, retrospective study designs, limited external validation, algorithmic bias, and difficulties in explaining model predictions. Importantly, high algorithmic accuracy does not necessarily translate into clinical effectiveness. Future research should therefore focus on diverse multicentre datasets, external and prospective validation, explainable AI, multimodal systems, ethical governance, and meaningful human-AI collaboration. Deep learning is most appropriately viewed as an adjunctive clinical decision-support technology that complements rather than replaces professional diagnostic judgment.
authors: Ananya Sapra; Dr Suman Sen

title: Polyzwitterion with Imidazole for Ultralow‐Power Organic Photoelectric Synaptic Transistors Achieving Multicolor Robot Vision and Dynamic Recognition
abstract: ABSTRACT Neuromorphic in‐sensor vision demands photoelectric synaptic transistors that co‐localize optical sensing and electrically tunable plasticity in a compact device, thereby simplifying artificial visual sensing circuits. Electrolytes and ionic liquids are widely employed as dielectric layers for neuromorphic transistors; however, cation–anion pairs without covalent bonds typically suffer from ion‐migration, ion replacement, and electrochemical reactions. These processes lead to current leakage, elevated power consumption, and irreversible drift, while photo‐modulation is further attenuated by exciton–polaron quenching. Here, to stabilize ionic charges and suppress ion‐migration, a polyzwitterion, poly(3‐(1‐vinyl‐3‐imidazolyl)‐propanesulfonate), is used as a single medium to unify electro‐ and photo‐synaptic functions, thereby simplifying the components and interfaces of the multilayer device. The aromatic conjugated imidazole ring stabilizes the cationic charge, and the covalently tethered cation–anion pair prevents long‐distance ion‐migration, ensuring strong cation–anion dipole polarization and reversible charge trapping. This enables robust multi‐wavelength photo‐synaptic modulation coupled with electro‐synaptic plasticity. The resulting organic photoelectric synaptic transistors achieve ultralow event energy consumption down to 10.95 aJ and support application‐relevant in‐sensor demonstrations, including encrypted image decoding, color‐guided robotic manipulation, pedestrian‐speed recognition, and motion prediction. These findings are poised to accelerate the development of multifunctional photoelectric synaptic devices and integrated sensing‐computing hardware architectures for artificial visual systems.
authors: Jingpeng Wu; Yi Zhao; Chaoxiong Guo; Pengyu Du; Xian Tang; Zechen Liang; Yiyu Chen; Xin Wang; Laju Bu; Guanghao Lu

title: Posterior segment imaging clues to systemic malignancy: a phenotype-to-confirmation narrative review
abstract: Systemic malignancies may affect the posterior segment through metastatic, paraneoplastic, hematologic or lymphomatous, and treatment-related mechanisms. Because routine ophthalmic imaging rarely establishes the underlying etiology, its principal clinical value is to identify suspicious patterns, prioritize competing diagnoses, and guide further investigation. This narrative review synthesizes malignancy-related posterior segment findings and proposes a clinically oriented phenotype-to-confirmation framework for multimodal interpretation. A literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for publications from January 2000 to May 18, 2026. The review included choroidal metastasis, paraneoplastic retinopathies and choroidopathies, vitreoretinal lymphoma, hematologic infiltration, leukemic retinopathy, and anticancer therapy-related toxicity. Owing to heterogeneity in disease entities, imaging protocols, diagnostic confirmation, and study designs, the evidence was synthesized qualitatively. Findings were organized into five suspicion-triggering phenotypes: exudative choroidal mass, RPE-choroidal remodeling, vitreoretinal infiltrative, diffuse neuroretinal dysfunction, and treatment-imprint phenotypes. Each phenotype was linked to its principal mimickers and to appropriate additional investigations, including targeted multimodal imaging, electrophysiology, ocular-fluid analysis, molecular testing, or systemic oncologic reassessment. These phenotypes should not be regarded as validated diagnostic categories, but as clinical entry points for differential exclusion and diagnostic escalation. Artificial intelligence may eventually support image registration, lesion tracking, and longitudinal comparison; however, its role in these rare and heterogeneous disorders remains investigational.
authors: Nikola Denda; Sofija Davidović; Nemanja Maletin; Kristina Veljkov; Aleksandar Raskovic; Ljiljana Jovančević; Siniša Babović

title: Pou2f2 enhances retinal ganglion cell survival and axon regeneration after optic nerve injury
abstract: Retinal ganglion cell (RGC) degeneration and the limited regenerative capacity of mammalian central nervous system axons result in irreversible vision loss in optic neuropathies. Identifying intrinsic regulators that promote both neuroprotection and axon regeneration is critical for developing effective therapies. This study identified POU domain class 2 transcription factor 2 (Pou2f2) as a previously unrecognized regulator involved in RGC biology. Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of developing mouse and human retinas showed that Pou2f2 is enriched in RGC clusters and suppressed by an RGC fate suppressor in the mouse retinal progenitor cell culture. Pou2f2 protein was detected in mouse RGCs and optic nerves, where its expression decreased following optic nerve crush (ONC). In primary RGC cultures, AAV2-mediated Pou2f2 overexpression enhanced neurite outgrowth, whereas Pou2f2 knockdown reduced neurite length. In vivo, intravitreal injection of Pou2f2 overexpression AAV2s increased axon regeneration, improved RGC survival, and partially preserved RGC function after ONC. Bulk RNA sequencing data revealed early activation of cytoskeletal growth pathways and later upregulation of DNA repair-associated genes, whereas immunostaining and in vitro analyses suggested activation of AKT/mTOR signaling following Pou2f2 overexpression. Together, these findings identify Pou2f2 as a promising molecular target for gene-based therapies for RGC degenerative diseases, including glaucoma and other optic neuropathies.
authors: D. N. Stavropoulos; Chia-Chun Liu; Shining Wang; Chi-Yu Chen; Mishal Rao; Laman Mirzaliyeva; Hui-Chun Cheng; Ya-Ling Lin; Andrew M. Williams; Yuan Pan; Takaaki Kuwajima; Jeffrey Louis Goldberg; José‐Alain Sahel; Kun‐Che Chang

title: Prevalence of Pathological Lesions and Normal Variations in the Oral Mucosa among Geriatric Patients at the University Veracruzana
abstract: Objective: To determine the prevalence of pathological lesions and variants of normalcy in the oral mucosa among geriatric patients who visited the University of Veracruz. Materials and Methods: A descriptive study was conducted by analyzing clinical records of 34 patients treated in two groups of the Geriatric Dentistry Educational Experience during the period from August to December 2024; To evaluate the association between variables (age, presence of chronic degenerative diseases, and sex), Fisher's exact test was used, with a statistical significance level of p < 0.05. Results: 32.4% had at least one pathological lesion, and 85.3% had at least one variant of normal. No statistically significant association was identified between the variables and the presence of lesions and/or variants. Conclusions: The study characterized the oral lesions present in the geriatric population. The findings highlight the importance of a systematic intraoral examination in geriatric dentistry.
authors: Claudia Citlalli Yanez Cedillo; Claudia Olguín Yobal; Dra Mercedes Soledad Briceno Ancona; Jacinto Izquierdo Jacome
venue: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)

title: PrimeScientist: Strategic Allocation of Research Effort in Autonomous Research
abstract: Autonomous research agents aim to automate scientific workflows, from proposing ideas to conducting experiments and analyzing results. Yet current AI and research agents can propose more directions than available resources allow them to pursue. Moreover, each attempt could consume substantial resources, requiring agents to reconsider how to invest in subsequent research. Thus, deciding how to invest research effort strategically should be a defining capability of autonomous research agents. Accordingly, we introduce PrimeScientist, which jointly determines research direction and resource investment across successive research attempts. Specifically, we formulate this challenge of strategic research effort allocation as a sequential decision problem where remaining resources should explicitly guide the research policy. We first introduce an executable plan tree that preserves competing plans and their outcomes across attempts. Building on this representation, we propose an adaptive MCTS-based allocation policy that balances exploration and exploitation using experimental feedback and remaining resources. Comprehensive evaluations across AI research, systems and code optimization, and machine learning engineering show that strategic allocation improves research quality and sample efficiency together. Across 12 AI research tasks, PrimeScientist improves average reward by 10.3% with 50.6% fewer research attempts than AutoResearch under the same resource budget. We believe making research effort allocation an explicit optimization target establishes effective resource use as a core research capability for autonomous agents to drive scientific breakthroughs at scale.
authors: Xinle Yu; Fan Bai; Kaiser Sun; Hengshuo Miao; Abhay Anand; Zhongyan Luo; Kun Zhou; Zhen Wang

title: Printing‐Assisted Integration of Thermal, Fluidic and Electrical Components in Implants for Focal Brain Cooling
abstract: The limitations of electrical neuromodulation are driving the development of neuroprosthetic systems enhanced with complementary modalities. A key technological challenge however remains the integration of the necessary hardware components (optical, thermal, fluidic, electrical) into miniaturized implants. Here we present a design framework, inspired by fast prototyping, that promises to reduce the complexity, fabrication time, and device bulk of multimodal neural interface systems. By combining extrusion-based 3D printing of silicones and discrete electronic components, we integrated thermal neuromodulation and electrical recording capabilities in soft packages suitable for placement on the cortical surface of rodents. When linked to an autonomous auxiliary driver unit, these packages establish rapid, stable and localized hypothermia together with ElectroCorticoGraphy (ECoG) recording. In a rodent model of epilepsy (4-aminopyridine), we demonstrate hypothermia-induced suppression of seizure-like activity. Our approach may advance the clinical translation of focal hypothermia as an alternative therapy for drug-resistant focal epilepsies.
authors: S R Moore; N. King; Aruã Clayton Da Silva; Clare Howarth; Jason Berwick; Thomas Edward Paterson; Ivan Rusev Minev

title: Prospective multicenter evaluation of an autonomous robotic ultrasound system integrated with AI-assisted thyroid nodule assessment
abstract: This prospective multicenter study evaluated feasibility, agreement, image quality, and workflow of a fully autonomous robotic ultrasound (US) system (FARUSS) integrated with an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted platform for thyroid nodule management. From March 2024 to August 2025, 262 participants from three institutions underwent conventional US followed by FARUSS. FARUSS used a 6-degree-of-freedom robotic arm and deep learning-based scanning; Aitrox-USIP analyzed US images for nodule detection and American College of Radiology Thyroid Imaging Reporting and Data System (ACR TI-RADS) categories. Sonologists evaluated image quality, consistency, and management. Agreement was assessed using weighted kappa ( κ ) and intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC). FARUSS showed good agreement with conventional US for thyroid measurements (ICC, 0.757–0.798) and 85.6% consistency in key nodule identification, but required longer examination time (202 s vs. 147 s; p < 0.001). Aitrox-USIP reduced analysis time (183 s vs. 254 s; p < 0.001), and sonologist revision improved agreement with conventional US-based ACR TI-RADS assessment ( κ , 0.754–0.879). FARUSS-based screening avoided 74.8% of unnecessary on-site US examinations but missed 19.2% of fine-needle aspiration biopsy (FNAB) recommendations. Image quality-based triage mitigated missed FNAB recommendations in exploratory simulation. FARUSS integrated with AI-assisted assessment may support thyroid US screening workflows, contingent on expert oversight.

title: Prospects for respiratory training with immersive technologies and biofeedback in patients of outpatient dental practice
abstract: This study evaluates the effectiveness of structured respiratory training using virtual reality (VR) and biofeedback for reducing psychophysiological tension in patients of outpatient dental practice. Thirty-four patients were enrolled in this pilot randomised study and allocated to a main group (training with VR and biofeedback, n=17) and a comparison group (n=17). In the main group, breathing awareness increased from 35.8±7.5 to 41.4±9.0 points (p=0.052 by the sign test and p=0.011 by the Wilcoxon signed-rank test) and relaxation self-efficacy increased from 4.8±3.6 to 7.0±3.5 points (p=0.043 by the sign test and p=0.006 by the Wilcoxon signed-rank test). Between-group comparison of changes showed a statistically significant advantage of VR-assisted training for the gain in breathing awareness (p=0.038 by the Mann–Whitney U-test); no between-group difference was found for relaxation self-efficacy (p=0.092). The findings suggest that a single session of respiratory training with immersive technologies and biofeedback promotes the development of breathing self-regulation skills. Given the sample size, the single-session design and the use of non-validated scales, these data are preliminary and require confirmation in larger studies assessing anxiety, autonomic measures and treatment adherence.
authors: И.Р. Ганжа; Nikolay V. Popov; A.A. Blazhnova; Alexander Vladimirovich Zakharov; Igor V. Shirolapov; Elena Khivintseva

title: QGLH-Net: quality-guided local-global hierarchical deep learning framework for oral disease classification using intraoral images
abstract: Dental diseases are a widespread yet under-recognized health problem worldwide, and oral health problems are associated with several systemic conditions including diabetes, cardiovascular disease and depression. Early diagnosis is crucial but depends on access to the trained dental professionals, which is difficult in underserved and resource-limited communities. This study proposes QGLH-Net (Quality-Guided Local-Global Hierarchical Network), a dual-stream deep learning framework that classifies oral diseases at six classes (gingivitis, caries, ulcer, calculus, tooth discoloration and hypodontia) from intraoral images while addressing the challenges of image quality, class imbalance and spatially localized lesion features. Experiments were conducted on publicly available Kaggle Oral Diseases dataset. Following quality filtering and deduplication, 3,076 images were retained and stratified into 2,153 training, 461 validation, and 462 test images. QGLH-Net framework introduces a dual-stream design combining ResNet-50 global branch selected because it achieved the highest macro-F1 among the tuned baselines, while for local branch a lightweight ResNet-18 is used operating on Grad-CAM-guided regions. Unlike post-hoc Grad-CAM visualization approaches, QGLH-Net uses Grad-CAM derived information to generate a complementary local input stream and integrate it with quality-aware curriculum and hierarchical supervision. Hierarchical supervision jointly optimizes six fine-grained disease classes and three coarse anatomical categories. Training further incorporates a two-stage quality-guided curriculum and a dynamic class-balanced focal loss in which inverse-frequency class weights are adapted using class-specific false-negative and false-positive rates, together with supervised contrastive learning. QGLH-Net achieved a best observed accuracy of 98.27% and macro F1-score of 0.9691, has a per-class F1-score ≥ 0.955. Paired statistical evaluation against the strongest ResNet-50 baseline yielded p = 0.152 for accuracy and p = 0.441 for macro-F1; therefore, the observed improvements are interpreted as performance gains rather than statistically confirmed superiority. Minority-class recall estimates showed wider 95% confidence intervals, particularly for caries (0.759–0.979) and tooth discoloration (0.750–0.978), reflecting their limited test support. End-to-end inference required approximately 117.1 ms per image (~ 8.5 images per second) on an NVIDIA Tesla T4 GPU. Beyond classification, we also explored how model outputs could be made more directly usable in a clinical workflow. As an additional proof-of-concept element, AI-assisted reporting module built with CrewAI and Google’s Gemini-1.5 Flash was implemented as a post-classification interface; it does not contribute to reported classification performance and has not undergone formal clinician-based evaluation. QGLH-Net is presented as an explainable screening and decision-support oral disease classification framework for intraoral-image assessment rather than an autonomous diagnostic system, with further clinical validation required before deployment.
authors: Jannat ul Mava; M. Usman Ashraf; Abdullah Alourani; Khlood Shinan; Hanan E. Alhazmi; Iqra Ilyas

title: Quality-Aware Uncertainty-Guided Graph Refinement for Reliable Diabetic Retinopathy Grading and Glaucoma Co-Detection
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) and glaucoma together are leading causes of preventable, irreversible blindness worldwide. Automated screening systems face three barriers to safe clinical deployment: no per-prediction reliability signal, no ability to flag degraded input images before inference, and no consideration of inter-sample relational structure during feature learning. We propose a quality-aware, uncertainty-driven graph-refined hybrid network (QA-GUNet) that addresses all three simultaneously via: (i) a MobileViT backbone for hybrid local-global feature extraction; (ii) a prototype-augmented Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) that refines embeddings using both batch- and training-set prototype anchors for reliable single-image inference; (iii) a Monte Carlo Dropout-based uncertainty module yielding a calibrated predictive variance per instance; and (iv) a jointly-trained image quality assessment (IQA) head that gates output on poor-quality fundus images. The core contribution is a prototype-augmented GCN inference strategy that removes batch dependence by computing each test image's neighborhood against a fixed memory bank of M=200 class-representative prototype embeddings, overcoming a major limitation of prior batch-dependent graph approaches. Trained and evaluated on APTOS 2019 (3,662 images, five-class DR grading) with external validation on Messidor-2 and EyePACS, and extended to four-class multi-disease detection, QA-GUNet achieves 98.45% ± 0.21% accuracy, ECE = 0.024, and identifies 92.3% of misclassified cases as high-uncertainty; excluding the highest-uncertainty 10% of predictions raises accepted-sample accuracy to 99.31%. These results establish QA-GUNet as a statistically rigorous, externally validated, reliability-aware framework that moves ophthalmic AI beyond single-point accuracy reporting toward clinically actionable triage.
authors: Chethan H V
venue: Journal of Intelligent Decision Making and Information Science

title: RAUL: Reference-Assisted Ureteroscopy Localization for Skill Assessment
abstract: Objective: Incomplete navigation of anatomy during ureteroscopic kidney stone surgeries can contribute to repeat interventions. While skilled surgeons have lower reintervention rates, there are no objective metrics to quantify scope-navigation performance to evaluate when a trainee becomes skilled. This work aims to recover ureteroscope trajectories from endoscopic video and derive navigation metrics to quantify differences in skill. Methods: We propose RAUL, a reference-assisted reconstruction framework for recovering ureteroscope trajectories from ureteroscope videos only in phantoms. For each phantom, we use a slow, high-quality reference exploration video to generate a reference reconstruction. We localize subsequent exploration videos against this reference. We evaluate localization accuracy against electromagnetically tracked scope pose. We compute navigation metrics from phantom exploration trajectories to compare surgical residents across experience levels. Results: The proposed reference-assisted framework achieves a mean translation root mean square error of $0.5 \pm 0.1$ mm across 9 phantoms. Compared to standard Structure-from-Motion (SfM), the proposed pipeline increases frame-wise localization coverage from $50.5 \pm 14.9\%$ to $86.1 \pm 7.2\%$ of all video frames. The reconstructed trajectories revealed significant differences between high- and low-experience trainees in established navigation metrics. Conclusion: RAUL enables substantially more complete recovery of ureteroscope trajectories from videos compared to standard SfM pipelines, enabling trajectory-based skill assessment without additional tracking equipment. Significance: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first use of video-only recovery of ureteroscope trajectories without external tracking sensors for skill assessment, supporting scalable automated assessment of ureteroscopy navigation skill.
authors: Fangjie Li; Mai N. Bui; Charan Mohan; Michael I. Miga; Matthieu Chabanas; Nicholas Kavoussi; Jie Ying Wu

title: ROBOTICS IN ENDODONTICS: AN INTEGRATIVE REVIEW OF AUTONOMY AND TRANSLATIONAL READINESS
abstract: Background: Existing syntheses of endodontic robotics import autonomy terminology from implant robotics, separate the macro- and micro-robotic literatures, and report performance without appraising the evidence. Methods: This integrative review searched PubMed to 31 July 2026, supplemented by Google Scholar and citation tracking, purposively selecting 61 records graded on the OCEBM 2011 hierarchy and assigned technology-readiness levels. No human participants or animals were involved; ethical approval was not applicable. Conclusion: The bottleneck is translational rather than conceptual.
authors: Prabhav Patel; Aabha Bhaskar Rawal; Zalak Patel

title: Rare Disease Classification in Video Capsule Endoscopy
abstract: Video capsule endoscopy offers a non-invasive way to examine the small bowel, however, the rare but clinically important findings that appear only in less than 1\% of labelled frames, provide very less signal for detection. As a result, while models can achieve high overall performance, they almost completely miss these rare findings. We condition each frame's decision on evidence from the rest of that patient's video, not on the frame's own posterior alone, supplying information a single frozen frame can never contain. Building upon Expected Gain Arbitration, a per-frame, macro-F1-optimal correction over the confusion matrix, we further compose it with video-disease-presence conditional resulting in our decoding method Hierarchical Conditional-Expected-gain (HCE). We evaluate HCE on two independent VCE datasets, Kvasir-Capsule and GALAR, against a static temporal-smoothing baseline and an optimal-transport (OT) frame-level correction. HCE significantly improves rare-class recall over a temporal-smoothing baseline on GALAR (2.7--3.1x; 95\% CI excludes zero in both scopes) and shows a similar, though not statistically confirmed, gain on Kvasir-Capsule (up to 3.4x). Against OT, HCE still improves rare-class recall in all four evaluation settings (+0.016 to +0.029), and additionally improves macro-F1 and MCC.
authors: Amit Patel; Debesh Jha

title: Real-Time Image Processing Fpga Based Clahe Image with I3C And Machine learning Algorithm for Medical Applications
abstract: Image processing is vital in modern embedded system, Applications such surveillance, medical imaging, industrial inspection and autonomous navigation requires image enhancement technique which improves visibility, feature detection and accuracy. This project presents a high-speed pipelined Field programmable gate array (FPGA) architecture for the Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) algorithm which is interfaced with I3C protocol using Block RAM (BRAM) and Verilog HDL for FPGA platforms. Where the system reads image data stored in BRAM, and CLAHE based image processing is performed and enhanced image is stored in output BRAM, an I3C protocol is interface is integrated for allowing external devices or controllers to access the enhanced image data efficiently. Experimental results show that the image CLAHE algorithm utilizes less power area on selecting ZYNQ (ZCU104) FPGA board on Vivado. In real-time image processing, the demand for efficient solutions has surged with the proliferation of applications spanning from autonomous vehicles to medical diagnostics. This study addresses the imperative need for accelerated machine learning algorithms to enhance the processing speed of image-related tasks. The research focuses on leveraging Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) to implement hardware acceleration, exploiting their parallel computing capabilities. The advent of machine learning in image processing has revolutionized various industries, yet real-time applications encounter computational bottlenecks. This research delves into hardware acceleration using FPGAs to overcome these constraints, offering a novel approach to expedite machine learning algorithms. Traditional software implementations of machine learning algorithms often fall short in meeting real-time processing requirements. This research aims to bridge this gap by exploring FPGA-based hardware acceleration, addressing the performance limitations hindering the seamless integration of machine learning into real-time image processing systems. While exist in gliterature acknowledges the potential of FPGA-based acceleration, a comprehensive exploration of its application for real-time image processing is lacking. This research fills the void by present in gad tailed method and empirical results, contributing to the limited body of knowledge on FPGA-accelerated machine learning in the of image processing. The study employs a systematic approach, integrating machine learning algorithms onto FPGAs through hardware description languages. The implementation is optimized to exploit parallelism inherent in FPGAs, resulting in a tailored hardware solution for real-time image processing. Comparative analyses against software implementations provide insights into the performance gains achieved. The experimental results demonstrate a significant enhancement in processing speed, validating the efficacy of FPGA-based hardware acceleration for machine learning algorithms in real-time image processing applications.

title: Recent advances in dentistry
abstract: Dentistry has entered a transformative era, driven by rapid technological innovation, interdisciplinary research, and a growing emphasis on patient-centered care. The past decade has witnessed remarkable progress across diagnostic, therapeutic, and preventive domains, reshaping both clinical practice and academic inquiry. This book, Recent Advances in Dentistry, seeks to capture these developments in a structured and comprehensive manner, offering readers a panoramic view of the evolving landscape of dental science. The chapters assembled herein highlight the convergence of digital technologies, biomaterials, nanoscience, and regenerative medicine with traditional dental practice. From the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into diagnostic workflows, to the revolution brought by CAD/CAM systems and 3D printing, dentistry is increasingly defined by precision, personalization, and efficiency. Advances in smart biomaterials and nanotechnology promise enhanced durability and biocompatibility, while innovations in orthodontics, pediatric dentistry, and caries management continue to refine patient outcomes across age groups. Equally compelling are the strides made in endodontics and periodontology, where regenerative approaches and novel instrumentation are expanding therapeutic possibilities. The domain of implantology and esthetic dentistry has been reshaped by digital planning, guided surgery, and minimally invasive techniques, ensuring both functional and aesthetic excellence. Emerging modalities such as laser therapy, photobiomodulation, robotics, and augmented reality further underscore the dynamic future of dental practice.

title: Recon2Servo: Robotic Ultrasound Visual Servoing via Learned Image-to-Motion Inference
abstract: Ultrasound visual servoing is essential for autonomous robotic ultrasound, yet 6-DoF probe control from 2D B-mode images remains challenging due to limited and ambiguous out-of-plane motion cues. Existing methods typically rely on anatomical priors or handcrafted visual features, limiting their generalizability across imaging targets. Inspired by trackerless 3D ultrasound reconstruction, we propose Recon2Servo, a visual servoing framework that learns image-to-motion inference directly from B-mode images for 6-DoF probe control. A DINOv3 encoder with low-rank adaptation and a bidirectional relation module estimate the relative probe pose between current and target images to guide iterative closed-loop target-view alignment. The framework combines supervised relative-pose learning, reconstruction-guided closed-loop adaptation, and bounded residual pose correction to improve motion inference during servoing. Evaluations on a public dataset and an in-house dataset collected from 12 healthy volunteers using different ultrasound systems demonstrate its effectiveness in reconstructed-volume servoing. Additional real-robot demonstrations of target-view alignment and dynamic tracking on a human forearm are provided in the supplementary video: https://youtu.be/qwsOdI-GMYk.

title: Recurrent Bleeding Due to Ileal Angiodysplasia: Clinical Case
abstract: Small bowel bleeding is a rare clinical condition that remains difficult to diagnose and manage. Due to its recurrent nature and limited accessibility, identifying the bleeding source may require complementary diagnostic investigations [1,2]. This study aimed to present a challenging case of recurrent small bowel bleeding and highlight the role of repeated multimodal diagnostic evaluation. A literature review using the PubMed database and analysis of a clinical case were performed. We included English-language articles published in the last decade. A 72-year-old woman with recurrent severe anaemia and suspected gastrointestinal bleeding underwent repeated endoscopic, radiological, and surgical investigations. Capsule endoscopy and SPECT/CT indicated a possible bleeding site in the ileum, however, angiography and diagnostic laparotomy failed to identify the source. A loop ileostomy was created to facilitate further localization and endoscopic access in case of recurrent bleeding. When bleeding recurred, enteroscopy via the ileostomy identified a bleeding ileal angiodysplasia, and successful endoscopic haemostasis was achieved with clips. In conclusion, recurrent small bowel bleeding may remain undetected despite repeated diagnostic investigations. When clinical suspicion persists or bleeding recurs, repeated and multimodal evaluation is necessary [3,4]. In this case, enteroscopy through the ileostomy enabled identification and treatment of the previously unconfirmed bleeding source.

title: Regulating AI in medical imaging and diagnostics in Bangladesh through ethical and legal doctrinal analysis
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming medical imaging by enhancing diagnostic accuracy, efficiency, and accessibility. In Bangladesh, where healthcare systems face infrastructural constraints and workforce shortages, AI presents both significant opportunities and complex ethical and legal challenges. This study adopts a doctrinal approach to examine the governance of AI in medical imaging, analyzing national legal instruments and advancing medico-legal areas, the Draft Bangladesh National AI Policy 2026–2030, and professional ethical codes in light of international frameworks such as WHO guidance, UNESCO recommendations, and the EU AI Act. The analysis moves beyond descriptive assessment to explore why regulatory gaps persist, identifying structural factors including limited regulatory capacity, fragmented legal frameworks, and reliance on externally developed technologies. Key challenges include inadequate data protection, weak informed consent mechanisms, unclear accountability in AI-assisted decisions, and inequitable access to digital health technologies. The study also highlights the limitations of existing professional ethics frameworks in addressing algorithmic decision-making. It proposes context-specific reforms, including comprehensive health data legislation, AI-specific ethical guidelines, and institutional oversight mechanisms. By linking ethical principles with practical governance, the study offers actionable insights for policymakers to support responsible and equitable AI integration in Bangladesh’s healthcare system.

title: Reported Retinal Detachment in Anti-VEGF-Treated Retinopathy of Prematurity: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
abstract: Objectives: To estimate the incidence of reported retinal detachment (RD) after primary anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) treatment for retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) and to explore study-level factors associated with RD incidence. Methods: PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched up to 24 May 2026, for English-language studies reporting RD outcomes after anti-VEGF monotherapy for ROP. Pooled incidence was estimated with a random-effects model using Freeman–Tukey double arcsine transformation. Heterogeneity, subgroup differences, publication bias, and leave-one-out sensitivity were assessed. Results: Twenty-seven studies (5598 eyes; 135 RD events) were included, comprising twelve case series, thirteen cohort studies, and two randomized controlled trials; thus, the evidence was predominantly retrospective. The pooled RD incidence was 1.4% (95% CI, 0.5–2.7%; I2 = 80.8%). The estimate remained stable on leave-one-out sensitivity analysis; the exclusion of Tong et al. markedly reduced heterogeneity. Higher RD incidence was observed in Asian studies, single-center studies, and studies with predominantly Zone I ROP or aggressive ROP (AROP). Incidence varied by postmenstrual age at treatment, gestational age, birth weight, and anti-VEGF agent. No significant publication bias was detected. Conclusions: RD after primary anti-VEGF therapy for ROP is uncommon but sight-threatening, with higher incidence associated with greater disease severity and postmenstrual age. Prolonged, risk-stratified follow-up is warranted for infants with Zone I or AROP. Standardized RD definitions, subtype classification, and severity-adjusted prospective comparisons are needed.

title: Research on Aided Reading System of Digital Library Based on Text Image Features and Edge Computing
abstract: With the rapid development of library informatization, traditional text information retrieval service methods have been unable to meet the needs of users. Therefore, personalized assisted reading technology has attracted wider attention, as it can discover hidden associations by mining user information, book information, and user operation logs, and recommend the acquired knowledge to users. In order to improve the service quality and experiences of users, this paper presents a digital library assisted reading system that combines text image features and edge computing. Firstly, the digital library reading assistance system framework is proposed based on edge computing technology, which will improve the service quality and information transmission level of the digital library. The auxiliary reading model of the digital library is presented based on text image features and an RBF neural network. Detailed simulation results verify the applicability and efficiency of the proposed scheme.

title: Retina as a window to systemic hypertension: From hypertensive retinopathy to artificial intelligence-driven microvascular biomarkers
abstract: The retinal microvasculature is the only vascular bed in the human body that can be visualised directly, non-invasively and repeatedly in vivo . Because retinal arterioles share embryological origin, calibre and autoregulatory physiology with the cerebral and coronary microcirculation, hypertension-induced retinal changes offer a unique window onto systemic small-vessel disease. For this narrative minireview, PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, Scopus, Web of Science and IEEE Xplore were searched from database inception to April 30, 2026 for peer-reviewed English-language human studies of hypertensive retinopathy, quantitative retinal vascular biomarkers, multimodal retinal imaging and artificial intelligence (AI) applied to fundus images; population-based cohorts, individual-participant meta-analyses and AI studies reporting external validation were prioritised, and evidence was synthesised thematically and tabulated for cross-study comparison. Classical hypertensive retinopathy, graded for over eight decades by the Keith-Wagener-Barker and Scheie systems, has been supplemented by quantitative measurement of retinal vessel calibre and by geometric parameters such as fractal dimension and tortuosity. Large population cohorts have established that these parameters predict incident hypertension, stroke, coronary heart disease and mortality independently of conventional risk factors. Optical coherence tomography (OCT), OCT angiography and adaptive optics have extended assessment to the capillary and cellular level, while deep learning has enabled automated retinopathy grading and direct inference of blood pressure and cardiovascular risk from fundus photographs. Critically, the high accuracies reported on small private datasets are not reproduced on the first public benchmark, where the best algorithms achieved only fair agreement, and no randomised evidence yet shows that acting on a retina-derived biomarker improves outcomes. Clinical translation therefore depends on measurement standardisation, prospective multicentre and multi-ethnic external validation, explainable models, defined referral pathways from an abnormal retinal screen to blood pressure confirmation and cardiovascular risk management, and clarity on the regulatory status of software that infers systemic disease from ocular images.
authors: Yehya Tlaiss; Serena Akiki; Naynawa Moussawi; Reine Zeidan; Abbas Zghaib; Issam FASSIH

title: RetinaSC: Retinal Semantic Communication Framework for Diabetic Retinopathy Detection
abstract: This paper presents a lightweight semantic com- munication framework for diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading from fundus images pertaining specifically to the APTOS2019 dataset. The framework includes semantic encoder designed using ResNet34, U-Net, MobileNetV2, and EfficientNet-B0 architectures. Further, the trained models are used to train the same framework for IDRiD dataset using transfer learning approach. Such a framework will enable the telemedicine sector in the early detection of DR and prevent total blindness. The results reveal that for APTOS, task-oriented semantic systems can achieve satisfactory robust performance (more than 0.8 weighted F1 score for ResNet34 and EfficientNet-B0) across different channels. In particular, considering the trade-off between complexity, latency, throughput, and F1 score, MobileNetV2 is the best model with weighted F1 score of 0.76-0.78 for both task and reconstruction- oriented modules and end-to-end latency of only 8.162 ms.
authors: Avani Shinod; Rangineni Rushitha; Asqeem Nas; Anirban Bhowal; Shikha Baghel

title: Retinal Microvascular and Peripapillary Profiles in Mild Autonomous Cortisol Secretion Versus Nonfunctioning Adrenal Adenomas
abstract: Background/Objectives: Mild autonomous cortisol secretion (MACS) is associated with increased cardiometabolic morbidity, but its relationship with the retinal microcirculation is unknown. We compared retinal and peripapillary microvascular parameters between MACS and nonfunctioning adrenal adenoma (NFA) and, secondarily, examined their associations with continuously modeled post-dexamethasone cortisol. Methods: In this single-center, retrospective, cross-sectional study, 98 patients (45 NFA, 53 MACS) were included, and optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) and structural OCT data from one eye per patient were analyzed. The primary outcome was whole-image deep capillary plexus (DCP) vessel density. Multivariable models were adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, and cardiometabolic comorbidities; secondary analyses were corrected using the Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate (q values). Results: OCTA was evaluable in 89 patients. The primary outcome did not differ significantly between groups in the main analysis (NFA vs. MACS, 48.64 ± 5.71% vs. 47.31 ± 5.77%; adjusted difference −1.29 percentage points, 95% CI −3.97 to 1.38; p = 0.339) or in any sensitivity analysis. In secondary analyses, superior retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness was greater in MACS (β = 17.38 µm; q < 0.001) and increased with ln(post-dexamethasone cortisol) (β = 13.74 µm; q = 0.010). Higher ln(post-dexamethasone cortisol) was also associated with lower parafoveal DCP (β = −2.72 percentage points; p = 0.013) and inside-disc radial peripapillary capillary vessel density (β = −3.13 percentage points; p = 0.026), which did not survive multiplicity correction; no superficial capillary plexus sector was associated with either exposure (all p ≥ 0.37). Conclusions: MACS was not significantly associated with whole-image DCP vessel density. The secondary associations with continuous cortisol are cross-sectional and hypothesis-generating and require prospective confirmation.

title: Retrofitting AI to Minimally Invasive Therapy
abstract: Integrating Artificial Intelligence ( AI ) into surgical practices is essential to address the growing shortage of healthcare professionals. However, implementing AI within the surgical environment presents practical challenges due to the specialized and confined nature of operating rooms. To effectively introduce these advanced technologies, an approach through Frugal Engineering and retrofitting is essential, ensuring that innovations can be integrated into the operating room in a sustainable and cost-efficient manner. This doctoral thesis explores different ways of retrofitting AI to minimally invasive treatment and diagnostics in three clinical scenarios, presented in five main contributions. The first two contributions cover two directions for radiation reduction in Endovascular Aneurysm Repair (EVAR ). In the HEX project, Electromagnetic Tracking (EMT) is fused with fluoroscopic imaging by utilizing AI for object tracking. Further, AI-based error compensation for EMT is discussed. PATRONUS is the second contribution of this work, which proposes a patient-specific, radiation-free training setup for EVAR. The training setup makes use of AI for various steps in the imaging pipeline to render pseudo-X-rays of transparent 3D-printed phantoms inside a black-box simulator. Potentials of AI-enhanced Simulation-Based Medical Education (SBME) are identified, and the idea of utilizing PATRONUS as a safe test-bed for retrofit AI is discussed. In the third and fourth contribution, Edge AI for Wireless Capsule Endoscopy (WCE ) is investigated as a means of retrofitting AI in a miniaturized setting. Our works titled eNCApsulate and NCALab are discussed, which aim to bring data-driven Visual Odometry (VO) to the capsule device by leveraging Neural Cellular Automata (NCAs). The final contribution of this thesis presents Cryotrack, a retrofit approach for intra-operative planning in percutaneous thermal ablation, which is evaluated in a clinical phantom study.
authors: Henry Krumb

title: Risk factors for inadequate bowel preparation and quality improvement strategies in colonoscopy: a narrative review
abstract: Colonoscopy is the gold-standard screening test for colorectal cancer, yet its diagnostic yield relies heavily on adequate bowel preparation. Despite standard protocols, 20%–30% of procedures still have inadequate cleansing, which lowers adenoma detection, prolongs procedures, increases repeat examinations, and wastes resources. Preparation quality is influenced by multiple interacting factors: patient characteristics (age, comorbidities, medication use, adherence), regimen features (purgative type, dose, split-dose scheduling), and healthcare delivery (education quality, appointment timing). Most previous studies have examined these factors in isolation, leaving a gap in integrated, evidence-based guidance. This narrative review synthesizes current knowledge on determinants of preparation quality, with emphasis on emerging strategies such as risk-stratified protocols, low-volume purgatives, digital health tools (mobile apps, SMS reminders), and AI-based real-time assessment. We aim to provide a practical framework for individualized preparation, thereby improving both the efficiency and quality of colonoscopy-based screening.
authors: Shanshan Ma; Xinyu Zhou

title: Robotic Computer‐Assisted Dental Implant Surgery Versus Free‐Hand and Guided Techniques: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
abstract: BACKGROUND: Robotic computer-assisted implant surgery (r-CAIS) aims to improve implant placement trueness, but existing reviews include heterogeneous designs, and no review has exclusively synthesized RCTs to date. This review aimed to evaluate the positional trueness and clinical outcomes of r-CAIS compared with free-hand implant surgery (FHIS), dynamic computer-assisted implant surgery (d-CAIS), and static computer-assisted implant surgery (s-CAIS), through a systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Electronic searches were performed in major biomedical databases from inception to March 2026. Only RCTs were eligible. Risk of bias was assessed using the RoB 2 tool and certainty of evidence was rated using the GRADE framework. Meta-analyses were performed using a random-effects model where feasible. RESULTS: Seven RCTs enrolling 529 implants were included. Moderate-certainty evidence demonstrated significantly improved positional trueness with r-CAIS over FHIS across all deviation parameters, with the largest effect observed for angular deviation (MD = -4.56°; 95% CI -6.25 to -2.86). High certainty evidence showed a significant angular deviation advantage of r-CAIS over d-CAIS (MD = -0.77°; 95% CI: -1.33 to -0.21), while platform and apical deviations did not differ significantly. All comparisons with s-CAIS were non-significant, rated low to very low certainty from a single small trial. Operative time evidence was very low certainty, precluding any directional conclusion. Early implant retention ranged from 93.3% to 100% across all modalities with no meaningful between-group differences. CONCLUSIONS: r-CAIS improves implant positional trueness compared with free-hand surgery, supported by moderate certainty evidence, with a high certainty angular deviation advantage over dynamic navigation. However, improved trueness has not been shown to translate into better clinical or patient-reported outcomes. Wider clinical use should depend on long-term, multicenter RCTs using standardized patient-centered outcomes.
authors: Sultan Ainoosah; Radwan Algabri; Omar M. Alaryani; Ahmad Abdulkareem Alnazzawi; Ahmed E. Farghal; Ahmed Yaseen Alqutaibi

title: Robotic Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided Geometric Modeling of Soft Tissue: 3D Representations for Data-Driven Closed-Loop Shape Control
abstract: In medical robotics, data-driven soft-tissue shape control requires deforming tissue toward desired morphologies through sequential physical interactions. This challenge is particularly important in microscale manipulation, where localized deformation is difficult to observe, represent, and control, while physics-based models can be computationally expensive and difficult to adapt to realistic environments. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) provides high-resolution volumetric perception of tissue deformation, but target-conditioned control requires effective representations of both observed and desired tissue states. In this work, we introduce an OCT-guided data-driven framework for tissue shape control, learned from user-guided demonstrations and executed with closed-loop OCT feedback. We study full-volume, tissue-masked sparse-volume, and voxelized point-cloud representations, with or without residual conditioning, using deterministic (Explicit) and generative diffusion (Diffusion) policies. Across 12 configurations and 576 phantom rollouts on 3-DoF depth and 6-DoF directional tasks, OCT-derived 3D representations support both Explicit and Diffusion policies, with performance depending on representation and residual conditioning. Residual conditioning reduces directional Shape RMSE from 0.748 to 0.555 mm for full-volume Diffusion, while voxelized point-cloud Explicit with residuals achieves 0.534 mm for depth and 0.443 mm for directional control, with comparable accuracy at intermediate unseen targets and consistent performance across deployments. We further evaluate the framework in 60 ex vivo porcine rollouts, extending to biological tissue with final geometric errors comparable to human demonstrations. These results establish volumetric OCT as current and goal representations for learned closed-loop tissue shape control across deterministic and generative action models.
