This work establishes a proof‐of‐concept platform for standardized acquisition and analysis of process‐resolved chewing data, offering a route toward objective, data‐driven assessment of masticatory function and, with larger population datasets, personalized oral rehabilitation and healthcare decision‐making.
authors: Xiaoxuan Xue; Zhan Gao; Jun Wang; Yizhang Yang; Kewei Zhang; Chao Yang

title: A case report of Mirizzi syndrome type II in a patient with situs inversus totalis treated with laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
abstract: Introduction: Situs inversus totalis (SIT) is a rare congenital condition characterized by complete mirror-image transposition of the thoracic and abdominal organs. Mirizzi syndrome is an uncommon complication of cholelithiasis that can substantially increase the technical difficulty of cholecystectomy. Importance: The coexistence of SIT and Mirizzi syndrome is exceedingly rare and presents unique challenges related to altered anatomy, operative orientation, and surgical ergonomics. Case presentation: A 30-year-old man with SIT, Kartagener syndrome, Hirschsprung disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, pre-hypertension, and primary biliary dyskinesia presented with worsening abdominal pain despite prior biliary stent placement. Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography demonstrated cholelithiasis with an impacted gallstone at the gallbladder neck, consistent with Mirizzi syndrome, gallbladder distention, biliary ductal dilation, and a low medial insertion of the cystic duct. Laparoscopic cholecystectomy was performed using mirrored port placement, with the surgeon positioned on the right side of the patient. Intraoperatively, an aberrant left hepatic artery was found in close association with the cystic duct and gallbladder, preventing safe attainment of the critical view of safety. A dome-down approach was therefore used to complete the operation safely. The patient recovered without complications. Clinical discussion: Published reports and a meta-analysis of laparoscopic cholecystectomy in patients with SIT demonstrate that minimally invasive management is feasible and safe despite the challenges posed by mirrored anatomy, altered ergonomics, and anatomic variation. Conclusion: Preoperative imaging, mirrored port placement, and alternative dissection strategies, such as the dome-down approach, may facilitate safe laparoscopic management of Mirizzi syndrome in patients with SIT.
authors: Amy Lo; Trista Reid; Daryhl Johnson; Steven Satterly

title: A flexible silicone elastomer/copper oxide nanocomposite for current-mode X-ray dosimetry: Synthesis, characterization, and performance evaluation
abstract: Flexible, polymer-based nanocomposite dosimeters have attracted growing interest for radiation monitoring in diagnostic radiology because of their mechanical conformability and potential for low-cost, large-area fabrication. While silicone-based detectors loaded with heavier metal oxides have previously been explored, the dosimetric behavior of room-temperature-vulcanizing (RTV-2) silicone elastomer reinforced with copper oxide nanoparticles — which differs from these systems in both filler chemistry and cure mechanism — has not been systematically characterized. In this work, a flexible silicone/copper oxide nanocomposite was fabricated and evaluated, for the first time, as a current-mode X-ray dosimeter. Copper oxide nanoparticles were synthesized by a simple precipitation method and incorporated into the silicone matrix at weight fractions ranging from 0 to 36.4 wt percent. Structural and chemical characterization confirmed the formation of phase-pure, monoclinic copper oxide nanoparticles with an average crystallite size of 27–29 nm, dispersed within the amorphous silicone network as submicron aggregates (mean Feret diameter 253 ± 86 nm within the composite, from 121 measured particles). Under 60 kV diagnostic X-ray irradiation, the nanocomposite exhibited a stable, nearly linear photocurrent response over a dose-rate range of 2.8–12 mGy/min. Among the compositions evaluated, the sample containing approximately 27.6 wt percent copper oxide showed the best overall dosimetric performance, with a sensitivity of 0.102 ± 0.014 nA/(mGy/min) and a noise-limited detection threshold of 0.25 mGy/min; given that the composition-dependent variation in photocurrent (∼11%) is comparable to the measurement uncertainty, this composition is best regarded as a favorable rather than a definitively optimized formulation. The enhanced sensitivity relative to the unfilled matrix is attributed primarily to the higher photon-interaction probability associated with the increased effective atomic number introduced by the copper oxide phase. The devices showed good short-term repeatability, with a relative standard deviation of 1.01% over repeated irradiation cycles, and a signal-to-noise ratio exceeding 90 at an applied bias of 400 V. These results indicate that silicone/copper oxide nanocomposites constitute a cost-effective, mechanically flexible platform for low-energy X-ray dosimetry, with performance comparable to other polymer–metal oxide systems reported in the literature.
authors: Farideh Keyvani; Leila Gholamzadeh; Shahryar Malekie; Sedigheh Kashian

title: A highly reproducible, safe cranial window surgery for targeted in vivo manipulations in the adult zebrafish telencephalon
abstract: Experimental surgery is one of the most fundamental fields of biomedical research, recreating clinical conditions on living organisms similar to clinical patients, to facilitate the design of novel therapies. For modeling neurological and psychiatric disorders, the majority of operative techniques mandatorily include craniotomy for consecutive interactions with the open brain. The most wide-spread methodology involves stereotactic surgery in rodents, implementing a specific head holder, attached to the coordinate table, providing the precise animal head positioning according to the brain structures topology. Despite the high efficiency, such systems require complex instrumental skills and long procedure duration per animal even for simple implantation protocols. Hence, novel alternative model species could be a valuable supplementary tool for such manipulations. Therefore, the zebrafish (Danio rerio) fits perfectly, due to its low cost, easy husbandry, rapid development, optic transparency, and high genetic and physiological similarity to rodents and humans. Furthermore, the everted zebrafish telencephalon provides excellent accessibility to critical mammalian-like structures involved in emotion processing and cognition. However, conventional avian- or rodent-inspired craniotomies in adult zebrafish often trigger inadvertent disruption of the brain vessels network, resulting in high operative mortality. A novel, geometry-driven, non-lethal cranial window protocol preserving neurovascular integrity and ensuring 90-100% post-operative survival is presented to overcome above mentioned limitations. This rapid, simple, and high reproducible technique opens new avenues for precise region-specific in vivo neurosurgery, high-throughput psychopharmacological screening, and neurostimulation in a powerful non-mammalian model species
authors: Konstantin N. Zabegalov

title: A new fluidic MEMS-based mercury ion sensor for water sources
abstract: Mercury detection is essential for ensuring the safety and environmental responsibility of clean energy technologies. This sensor can be used to detect mercury in water sources to remove the toxic pollutant from water effectively. Our proposed sensor addresses this demand by accurately detecting mercury ions through its mass-sensitive properties. The novelty of this sensor stems from two key aspects: first, the incorporation of a highly mercury-sensitive gold layer on the active area to enhance its capabilities and specificity to mercury ions; and second, its unique integration with a digital microfluidic system without any pump and microchannel. This system is fully compatible with microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) technology and can be used in conjunction with, or as part of, clean energy systems. This integration is crucial as it facilitates the delivery of deionized water droplets containing mercury ions to the sensing area. The sensor employs comb-drive electrodes to actuate its resonator in an in-plane mode, which causes its surfaces to slide parallel to the liquid interface. This leads to the mass and stiffness changes in the central resonator and consequently, a measurable frequency shift. Finite element analysis of the mechanical behavior of the sensor demonstrated a quality factor of 651 at a resonance frequency of 351.96 kHz for the resonator. Furthermore, the sensor exhibits a high sensitivity of approximately 105 Hz/ppb, highlighting its potential for trace mercury detection.
authors: Mahnaz Mehdipoor; Reza Hadjiaghaie Vafaie; Sahar Zinatloo‐Ajabshir

title: A quasi-zero stiffness triboelectric vibration sensor for high-fidelity vibration characterization
abstract: Triboelectric nanogenerator-based vibration sensors offer a promising solution for large-scale, distributed vibration monitoring in mechanical equipment and civil infrastructure. However, their performance is often compromised by inherent structural resonance, which introduces frequency-dependent sensitivity and distorts broadband vibration waveforms. In this work, we present a quasi-zero stiffness triboelectric vibration sensor (QZS-TEVS) that extends the post-resonance operational region towards ultralow frequencies, facilitating high-fidelity broadband vibration characterization. Specifically, an ultralow resonant frequency is realized via the QZS characteristic of the tailored harmonic curved beam. This strategic resonance shift broadens the flat-response bandwidth, thereby effectively suppressing resonance-induced distortion. The QZS-TEVS exhibits a nearly constant displacement sensitivity of 0.31 V/μm over 10-300 Hz, with a frequency measurement accuracy of 99.98%. Furthermore, the QZS-TEVS achieves precise reconstruction of arbitrary vibration waveforms. This work shifts the design paradigm from resonance-driven energy maximization to high-fidelity characterization and provides a high-precision scheme for self-powered, multidimensional condition monitoring within the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT).
authors: Zhengyu Li; Xingyu Chen; Liye Zhao; Jiawen Xu

title: A rare guest in the hernia sac: Preoperatively diagnosed Amyand’s hernia with gangrenous appendicitis
abstract: Amyand's hernia is a rare clinical entity defined by the presence of the vermiform appendix within an inguinal hernia sac, with acute appendicitis occurring in this setting being exceptionally uncommon. We report the case of a 57-year-old male who presented with pain in a known right inguinal hernia. Clinical evaluation demonstrated an incarcerated right inguinal hernia, and contrast-enhanced computed tomography showed an inflamed appendix herniating into the right inguinal canal, consistent with acute appendicitis within an Amyand's hernia. The patient underwent urgent laparoscopic exploration, which confirmed an acutely inflamed, gangrenous appendix partially contained within the hernia sac. A laparoscopic appendectomy was successfully performed, and the appendix was reduced from the hernia sac. Given the gangrenous nature of the appendix and concerns regarding microperforation and potential infection, inguinal hernia repair was deferred. The patient recovered without immediate complications. This case highlights the diagnostic value of preoperative imaging, the feasibility of a minimally invasive approach, and the importance of individualized surgical decision-making for Amyand's hernia. In selected patients with acute appendicitis and suspected perforation within the hernia sac, laparoscopic appendectomy without concurrent hernia repair can be considered, minimizing operative risk while allowing staged definitive hernia management.
authors: Carolina Baz; Kevin Connors; Selma Siddiqui

title: A reusable strawberry stem based on hot melt adhesives for robotic harvesting applications
abstract: Robotic strawberry harvesting has achieved significant progress, with decades of research leading to commercial deployments and prototypes capable of autonomous fruit detection, grasping, and stem cutting. However, its development remains limited by the lack of a reusable, realistic crop testbed, making system validation difficult due to limited field access, crop waste, and large sample requirements. Here, we present a reusable strawberry stem made from Hot Melt Adhesives (HMAs) enabling repeated cutting, healing, and detachment. We show that the artificial stem reproduces the static behavior of real stems when its diameter is increased by 2.0 × − 3.0 × , achieving curvature errors between 3.39% and 11.01% of stem length (normalized RMSD), confirming close agreement with their biological counterparts. Furthermore, the healing behavior is analyzed by evaluating the consistency of the cutting force required to sever the stem and the peak tensile load required to detach it across repeated cycles. Fabrication repeatability is assessed by measuring the variability of peak cutting force across independently fabricated stems from the same mold. Although HMA does not fully match the stem’s natural stiffness, the surrogate replicates its static behavior at a larger diameter, providing a practical, low-cost, reusable medium for standardized harvesting tests. Juan Espejel Flores and colleagues develop a reusable self-healing strawberry stem surrogate based on hot-melt adhesives for repeatable robotic harvesting experiments. The surrogate reproduces the static behavior of real strawberry stems through geometric scaling while enabling repeated cutting, healing, and reuse in a low-cost experimental platform.
authors: Juan Pablo Espejel; Leonardo Guevara; Srikishan Vayakkattil; Luis Arturo Soriano; Carlos Juárez-Balderas; D A Perez-DeLaMora; Marcello Calisti

title: A wearable closed-loop insulin micropump toward a miniaturized artificial pancreas for diabetes
abstract: The application of a fully autonomous artificial pancreas faces fundamental constraints from the bulky mechanical drives of conventional insulin pumps and the spatially separated glucose sensing unit. Herein, we report a wearable closed-loop insulin micropump that enables a miniaturized artificial pancreas for diabetes treatment. It seamlessly integrates an electrochemical micropump with an optical glucose-responsive microneedle (MN) sensor. The core actuation module features a novel semi-dry sandwich electrode configuration combined with a highly elastic latex membrane and a groove-type epoxy sealing architecture. This structural paradigm shift effectively eliminates bulk fluid flow and ensures robust hermeticity for precise, electrolysis-gas-driven, microliter-scale dosing with a precision of 0.5 μL. For continuous glucose monitoring, a polyvinylpyrrolidone/polyvinyl alcohol (PVP/PVA) hydrogel MN array functionalized with 9-anthracene boronic acid (9-ANB) is employed. The specific binding of interstitial glucose triggers measurable fluorescence quenching, which is precisely digitized by an integrated XYZ true-color sensor (detection range: 0-600 mg/dL). Comprehensive in vitro and in vivo evaluations demonstrate the platform's predictable, programmable delivery kinetics and excellent biocompatibility. In type 1 diabetic mouse models, a smartphone-controlled system by autonomously and effectively suppressed postprandial glycemic spikes, maintaining glycemic fluctuations within 25 mg/dL. This highly integrated, miniaturized design offers a compelling paradigm shift for next-generation, patient-friendly diabetes management systems.
authors: Ziyu Kuang; Xiangbin Kong; Tan Cao; Rui Lin; Zhihe Long; Tianyou Jiang; Xianchun Jin; Xinyu Xue; Zhangzhi Zhao; Meihua Chen

title: ALGORITHMIC SECOND OPINIONS IN PRIMARY CARE DERMATOLOGY: TRUST DYNAMICS AND AUTOMATION BIAS ACROSS SKIN LESIONS AND ERUPTIONS
abstract: Dermatological complaints constitute a significant portion of primary care consultations, encompassing a broad spectrum from infectious exanthems and inflammatory rashes to malignant neoplasms. The recent integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into primary care settings promises to bridge the diagnostic accuracy gap between General Practitioners (GPs) and board-certified dermatologists. However, the socio-technical dynamics of how GPs calibrate trust in AI diagnostic suggestions remain poorly understood. This study investigates human-computer interaction, focusing on diagnostic confidence and automation bias, when physicians are provided with an AI-generated "second opinion." Utilizing an explanatory mixed-methods design, 50 clinicians—comprising 25 GPs (Novices in specialized dermatology) and 25 Dermatologists (Experts)—evaluated a curated dataset of 40 diverse macroscopic and dermoscopic clinical cases, including viral rashes, fungal infections, inflammatory dermatoses, and skin tumors. To assess automation bias, the AI assistant was programmed to provide deliberately incorrect diagnostic prompts in 20% of the cases. Quantitative results demonstrate a profound experience-based divergence. GPs, operating under higher diagnostic uncertainty, exhibited severe automation bias, frequently overturning correct initial diagnoses to align with erroneous AI prompts. Conversely, dermatologists demonstrated resilient diagnostic confidence but exhibited instances of algorithmic aversion, often rejecting the AI entirely due to its "black box" nature. The findings emphasize that deploying AI in primary care requires shifting focus from algorithmic accuracy to human-centered interface design, specifically integrating Explainable AI (XAI) paradigms to ensure safe and synergistic clinical decision-making.
authors: Jakub Klepacz; Radosław Swędrak; Zuzanna Dobrakowska
venue: International Journal of Innovative Technologies in Social Science

title: Abnormal behavior perception in elderly care scenarios based on multimodal generative adversarial networks
abstract: In view of the limitations of the existing elderly care anomaly perception methods, which mostly rely on single visual mode and shallow stitching multi-source sensing features, such as insufficient accuracy of long-time progressive anomaly recognition, easy mode collapse of multimodal training, and insufficient utilization of non visual sensing information, this paper proposes a multimodal wgan GP anomaly perception method combining CNN-LSTM spatio-temporal double branch coding. The framework integrates five kinds of heterogeneous sensor data, including vision, inertial IMU, bed pressure, physiological signs and environmental audio, and adaptively allocates the weight of each mode to complete the cross modal feature alignment based on the dual attention of space and time; The shared generator based on the fusion of spatial and temporal two-way sub generators only learns the distribution of normal behavior, and uses multimodal attention discriminator to distinguish the true and false features; Wgan GP gradient penalty and modal imbalance correction item were introduced to stabilize the confrontation training, and the weighted reconstruction error and discriminant confidence were fused to construct a joint abnormal score. Four core abnormalities, including falling, falling out of bed, long-term wandering and physiological index disorder, were identified by dynamic threshold. The experimental results show that the AUC roc of the complete model in this paper can reach 0.978 ± 0.003, the F1 score is 95.64 ± 0.47%, the false positive rate is 2.13 ± 0.24%, and the false negative rate is 3.05 ± 0.30%; Ablation experiments showed that F1 score decreased significantly after removing inertia, bed pressure or audio modes, which confirmed that such non visual modes had complementary contributions to information, and the complete model had stronger scene adaptability and engineering landing value. Not applicable.
authors: Xinbo Zhao

title: Accelerator-based BNCT as a drug–device regimen: system engineering, clinical evidence, and regulatory considerations
abstract: Boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT) is a binary, tumor-selective radiotherapy modality that combines preferential delivery of boron-10 to tumor tissue with neutron irradiation to generate high-linear energy transfer particles in situ . The field has undergone a defining transition from reactor-based neutron sources to accelerator-based BNCT (AB-BNCT), enabling hospital-based deployment, broader clinical translation, and renewed global interest in indications with substantial unmet needs, particularly recurrent head and neck cancers and gliomas. However, AB-BNCT is intrinsically a drug–device regimen, requiring coordinated evaluation of the boron agent, neutron irradiation system, and dedicated treatment planning software, supported by end-to-end quality management, commissioning and routine quality assurance, and postmarket surveillance. This review summarizes the system-engineering foundations and current global landscape of AB-BNCT. We outline the therapeutic principle and key subsystems, including accelerator neutron sources, beam shaping assembly, patient positioning and setup, beam/dose monitoring, treatment control, and Monte Carlo–based BNCT treatment planning. We synthesize clinical evidence from reactor-era feasibility studies, accelerator-era registration programs, and emerging real-world evidence, including the Japanese Phase II registration study reporting an objective response rate of 71.4% in patients with unresectable recurrent or locally advanced head and neck cancer and subsequent nationwide postmarketing evidence. We also compare regulatory classification and approval pathways across the European Union, United States, Japan, and China. Finally, we discuss regulatory considerations relevant to the evaluation of BNCT devices in China. Continued advances in boron agents, accelerator engineering, and standardization, together with accumulated regulatory experience, may support broader clinical implementation of AB-BNCT. Further accumulation of evidence integrating beam physics, dosimetry, and clinical outcomes may facilitate cross-jurisdictional understanding and the continued clinical development of AB-BNCT.
authors: Zehua Wang; Yue Wang; Yan Jiang; Qing Zhang; Xiaofang Gu; Lu Liu

title: Active Visual Perception: Opportunities and Challenges
abstract: Active visual perception enables an intelligent system to improve perception by controlling how visual evidence is acquired. However, differences in how studies define active perception and evaluate its benefits make approaches difficult to compare across tasks. This review first clarifies the field’s functional scope by examining whether an action is selected for its expected effect on subsequent visual evidence and whether the resulting observation informs a later decision. This definition distinguishes active observation acquisition from processing fixed inputs and guides the selection of representative literature. Within this scope, this review develops an analytical framework organized around four questions. It begins with what evidence the task requires, examines which actions can obtain that evidence and how a candidate observation should be valued, and considers how the next sensing action should be selected and executed. New observations then update the perceptual state and guide subsequent decisions, forming a closed loop that provides a common basis for comparing methods across applications. To examine how their benefits can be demonstrated, this review assesses whether existing datasets support observation selection, how interactive environments enable controlled comparisons, and what physical platforms reveal about execution feasibility. It further examines how baseline comparisons can establish whether adapting observations is necessary and whether informed selection offers benefits beyond simpler sensing strategies. These considerations underpin an evaluation framework that links improvements in visual evidence to downstream task outcomes while accounting for acquisition costs and risks. Its core value is to help isolate the contribution of sensing decisions and determine whether their benefits justify the resources required. The analysis concludes that predicted observation value does not guarantee that useful evidence can be acquired through feasible actions, while task success alone cannot establish the benefit of active observation selection. Further progress requires reliable value estimation and planning over longer decision sequences under physical and resource constraints. It also requires grounding semantic reasoning in acquired evidence and maintaining effective collaboration under imperfect communication, with these capabilities verified through reproducible evaluation of the complete perception and action loop.
authors: Yian Li; Xiaoyu Guo; Hao Zhang; Jiayu Chen; Shuiwang Li; Xiaowei Dai

title: Adaptive Robotic Skill Transfer System
abstract: Abstract Adaptive robotic skill transfer concerns the reuse of learned behaviour across machines, tasks and operating environments while preserving interpretable performance boundaries. This monograph develops a research architecture in which task representations, embodiment adapters, uncertainty estimates and independent execution controls jointly determine whether a transferred skill may operate. Ten research themes connect the supplied bibliography to five chapters on foundations, statistical explanation, machine learning, scalable engineering and sectoral governance. The analysis distinguishes transferable task structure from robot-specific actuation and separates adaptation performance from evidence of safe execution. Twenty-five mathematical models formalize distinct research questions, including representation alignment, causal transfer effects, calibration, scheduling, provenance and deployment value. The proposed evaluation programme uses grouped experiments, held-out embodiments, explicit resource budgets and staged physical validation. Its implementation pathway combines a versioned skill registry with local runtime supervision, auditable adaptation and reversible release procedures. Manufacturing, logistics, assistive systems and field robotics illustrate how environmental and institutional conditions alter transfer requirements. The central conclusion is that useful transfer must be demonstrated as a conditional improvement over credible baselines, with failure recovery and responsibility included in the comparison. The book offers research protocols and a technical invention disclosure for further implementation and examination; it does not report completed robotic experiments. Keywords adaptive robotics, skill transfer, embodiment adaptation, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, causal inference, uncertainty quantification, domain shift, digital twins, safety supervision, multimodal fusion, edge intelligence, continual learning, federated learning, reproducibility, model governance, provenance, scheduling, human oversight, industrial automation, research design, assurance
authors: Murali Krishna Pasupuleti

title: Adductor Longus Tendon Repair and Lengthening for the Treatment of Core Muscle Injury: A Step‐by‐Step Surgical Technique
abstract: Abstract Core muscle injury is an increasingly recognized condition that causes groin pain, most commonly in young, active adults. Multiple surgical interventions have been described, including rectus abdominis repair and/or adductor longus lengthening, generally reserved for recalcitrant cases. This article presents a step‐by‐step guide to an open adductor longus repair and lengthening. By performing an anatomic tendon repair combined with controlled lengthening at the musculotendinous junction, this approach aims to minimize recurrence while providing sustained pain relief.
authors: Roger Quesada-Jimenez; Talha Syed; Alexandra M. Assimos; William M. Moore; Andrés Maldonado‐Rosales; Etan P. Sugarman; Benjamin Gilbert Domb

title: Advanced Drug Delivery Systems: Barriers and Emerging Strategies for Clinical Translation
abstract: Advanced drug delivery systems, including nanoparticles, liposomes, hydrogels, and hybrid composites, promise substantial improvements in targeted therapy and reduced systemic toxicity, yet their clinical translation remains limited. We conducted a systematic literature review covering publications from 2016 to 2025, employing a structured extraction framework across nine domains to evaluate platform design, biological barrier penetration, and translational outcomes. Our analysis reveals that hybrid composite systems consistently face greater manufacturing scalability constraints and regulatory ambiguity compared to single component platforms such as liposomes and lipid nanoparticles, which have achieved Phase III trials and market approval. Smart stimuli responsive hydrogels in chronic inflammatory diseases demonstrate improved therapeutic indices through reduced systemic exposure and enhanced local efficacy, although formal ED50 or TD50 values were not reported in primary studies. Living drug delivery systems pose higher immunogenicity risks than biomimetic alternatives, with standardized testing protocols existing for synthetic coatings but lacking quantitative acceptable ranges. Multi scale computational modeling, including a physiologically based pharmacokinetic model for blood brain barrier penetration, achieved strong validation with a correlation coefficient of 0.848, indicating improved translational feasibility. Chemical modification of natural polymers, particularly hyaluronic acid, yields route dependent improvements for example, thiolation produced a twenty fold increase in mucosal deposition, while sulfation enhanced transdermal bioavailability ten fold. The primary contribution of this work is a comprehensive synthesis identifying cross cutting translational barriers manufacturing complexity, regulatory uncertainty, and incomplete immunogenicity validation that inform future development priorities. These findings underscore the necessity for standardized characterization protocols, advanced computational modeling to bridge in vitro and in vivo performance, and strategic chemical modification approaches tailored to specific administration routes.
authors: Nucky Indra Praja; Callista Putri Nabila
venue: Journal of Regenerative Medicine and Molecular Innovation

title: Advanced piezoelectric nanogenerators for next-generation self-powered nano-bio sensors
abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) material-based piezoelectric nanogenerators (PENGs) are emerging as efficient energy-harvesting devices that convert mechanical stimuli into electrical energy. Owing to their tunable electronic, mechanical, and structural characteristics, 2D materials, including TMDs, MXenes, h-BN, etc, offer significant advantages in flexibility, durability, and low-power operation, making them highly suitable for next-generation self-powered systems. This review systematically highlights recent advances in 2D material-based PENGs, emphasizing fabrication strategies, performance optimization, electromechanical coupling enhancement, and their applications in self-powered nano-biosensors. The interdependence between material properties, device architecture, and measurement conditions is comprehensively analyzed to establish robust structure-performance relationships. Furthermore, critical challenges, including low output power, signal instability, integration complexity, and the lack of standardized evaluation protocols, are systematically analyzed. Emerging strategies to enhance energy-harvesting efficiency, signal reliability, and device scalability are also highlighted. Overall, this review establishes a unified framework for the rational design and advancement of high-performance 2D PENGs, providing key insights for their practical implementation in portable, wearable, and autonomous self-powered systems.
authors: Abhay Singh; Manish Sharma; Rajesh K. Gangwar; Ajeet Kumar Kaushik; Sanjeev Kumar K. Sharma

title: All-fiber wireless auscultation garment for cardiopulmonary diagnostics
authors: Qianyi Li; Ziang Li; Xiaoyu Zhang; Hakan Akgün; Swetika Chaturvedi; Hooi Khee Teo; Kamalesh Anbalakan; David Sim; Kenneth Michael Chew Yun Chi; Kee Thai Yeo; Derek John Hausenloy; Tural Khudiyev

title: Amortized Feedback Planning: Turning Model-Based Rollouts into Executable Policies
abstract: Closed-loop planning accounts for future observation-dependent actions but can be expensive to repeat at deployment. Bellman-gradient (BG) refinement differentiates conditional rollouts through an existing actor, corrects the current action, and stores the result in an executable policy. A backward sweep reuses deployed future feedback; full-horizon rollouts in an identified Gaussian belief model need no learned value critic. A nonlinear error recursion links quadratic continuation error, local correction, and policy storage. A controlled non-LQG example exhibits second-order policy accuracy with consistent storage, while ideal affine LQG admits exact backward recovery. In nonquadratic thrust, BG reduces actor cost by 2.47-3.20% and remains within 0.13-0.53% of the tested feedback MPC; original policies execute in 5-6 microseconds in a seed-0 native audit. With matched storage, BG attains competitive plant costs at about one ninth (arm) and one sixtieth (docking) of feedback-teacher-plus-student construction time on one GPU, excluding shared learning and node preparation. Richer common maps substantially narrow some student-BG gaps. These results expose the roles of learned feedback, local correction, and storage in executable control.
authors: Jeonggyu Huh

title: Analytical modelling of In0.25Ga0.75N nanowire HEMT utilizing FEM analysis and SRH recombination for breast cancer biomolecule
abstract: This work establishes a finite element drift–diffusion framework that integrates polarization sheet charge boundary conditions and Shockley–Read–Hall (SRH) recombination to accurately model an InGaN nanowire HEMT biosensor. The formation of the two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) and two-dimensional hole gas (2DHG) is a result of both spontaneous and piezoelectric polarization at the subband discontinuities of the InGaN/GaN interface. Analysis reveals that the overall effect of the 2DEG and 2DHG significantly influences the filling of quantum levels, with maximum sheet carrier charge densities of approximately 1.5 × 10⁻ 13 cm −2 occurring at a distance of 2 nm, followed by a secondary peak around 13.5 nm. The electrostatic potential assessments indicate a notable energy band bending of − 3.0 eV at 5 nm at the heterojunction interface. The sheet density is calculated using a combination of Schrödinger–Poisson equations and quantum-corrected drift–diffusion methods, which are then integrated over the confinement region. The biosensing mechanism is effectively incorporated as a surface charge density at the gate dielectric’s top boundary, resulting in a threshold voltage shift that is influenced by quantum, electrostatic effects and the charge density profile. The coupled system comprises Poisson’s equation along with continuity equations for both holes and electrons. This setup includes drift–diffusion currents and SRH recombination, while the interface jump conditions necessitate the inclusion of polarization charges. By meticulously parameterizing material properties such as subband offsets, effective sheet carrier densities, total polarization constants, mobilities and trap lifetimes, the simulation successfully reproduces I d –V g characteristics, 2DEG/2DHG distributions, electrostatic effects, charge density profiles, as well as wave functions and wave probability density functions corresponding to quantum energy levels relevant to breast cancer-related biomolecular interactions. This comprehensive modelling framework lays the foundation for advancing the design and effectiveness of biosensors aimed at detecting critical biomolecular signals.
authors: N. Anbuselvan; Lini Lee; Kah‐Yoong Chan

title: Application of 3D reconstruction combined with 3D printing and CBL + SP in teaching gynecologic malignant tumors
abstract: Objective The synergic effect of integrating diversified teaching methods [3D visualization technology [3D reconstruction and printing], case-based learning [CBL]. and standardized patients [SPs]] in the clinical teaching of gynecologic tumors was determined. Methods A case-control study design was proceeded in our hospital between September 2023 and March 2025 for clinical undergraduate interns and training physicians. They were divided into two groups: CBL + SP teaching mode ( n = 54); and CBL + SP + 3D teaching mode ( n = 54). A theoretical exam and a self-designed subjective questionnaire survey were used for the quantitative evaluation of teaching effectiveness. Results The average score of the CBL + SP + 3D group in the theoretical exam was significantly higher than the CBL + SP group ( P < 0.001). Students in the CBL + SP + 3D group performed significantly better than students in the CBL + SP group ( P < 0.001)in the subjective grading: learning interest, classroom participation, self-learning capacity, comprehensive analytic capacity, clinical thinking capacity, effectiveness of visual teaching aids, and simulation of clinical consultation scenarios constructed using SP. The total score of satisfactions in the CBL + SP + 3D group was significantly higher than that in the CBL + SP group ( P < 0.001). The total scores by the teachers on the students' performance in the CBL + SP + 3D group was significantly higher than that in the CBL + SP group. Conclusion The CBL + SP + 3D model established a teaching system with integration of “virtualization + material object + interaction,” which enabled significant improvement in the learning interest of students and enhanced student stereoscopic cognition of the complex anatomy of gynecologic tumors and the pathologic structures, and deepened comprehensive thinking and clinical case analysis capacity.
authors: Yaoxiang Zhong; Haikun Yang; Tingting Liu; Lvyang Li

title: Artificial Intelligence Models for Early Disease Detection Using Clinical Data
abstract: In a variety of chronic and acute diseases, earlier detection of disease is a major determinant of better patient outcomes, better treatment costs savings and reduced mortality.The current diagnostic process, mostly manual, manual interpretation of clinical data, is limited by the capacity of the human mind, by inter-observer variability and by the amount of data produced by modern healthcare systems.Artificial Intelligence (AI) that leverages machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) capabilities has become a rapidly evolving technology that can help uncover patterns within very large, heterogeneous and high-dimensional clinical datasets, well in advance of what traditional methods could accomplish.In this research paper, a thorough investigation of AI models for early disease detection from medical data, such as laboratory results, electronic health records (EHR), vital signs, and medical image metadata is conducted.We examine the theoretical underpinnings of important classifiers like Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machines, Random Forests, Gradient Boosting methods, Artificial Neural Networks, Convolutional Neural Networks and Long Short-Term Memory networks and compare their performances using the metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC).A systematic procedure of data acquisition, data preprocessing, feature engineering, model training, model validation and interpretability is suggested and illustrated using simulated experiments.The results show that ensemble and deep learning algorithms (especially XGBoost and CNN) are more accurate at forecasting than traditional statistical models, but they are less interpretable and more demanding in terms of resources.The paper also highlights these issues of data privacy, class imbalance, explainability of AI models, and clinical integration, and proposes directions for future research such as federated learning, explainable AI, multimodal data fusion for early disease detection, among others.
venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: Artificial Intelligence for Clinical Competence Assessment Compared with Human Examiners: A Systematic Review and Exploratory Meta-Analysis of Agreement, Reliability, And Validity
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being used to assess clinical competence, yet its measurement performance relative to human examiners remains uncertain across professions, tasks, and assessment formats. This systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis evaluated agreement, association, reliability, validity, score differences, classification performance, and human-human benchmarking for AI-based assessment of human clinical competence. Searches identified 29 eligible reports representing 27 independent studies across medicine, dentistry, nursing, pharmacy, and paramedicine. Owing to substantial heterogeneity in measurement methods, most outcomes were synthesized narratively. Two independent studies reported Spearman correlations and were included in an exploratory random-effects meta-analysis despite differing substantially in clinical assessment context using Fisher z transformation and restricted maximum likelihood estimation. The pooled AI-human association was ρ = 0.82 (95% CI, 0.55-0.93). The two correlations were numerically similar (I² = 0%), but between-study heterogeneity could not be estimated reliably because only two studies were available. This estimate should be interpreted cautiously as a cross-context summary of association rather than a common clinical effect. Direct agreement varied markedly across studies, and favorable correlations or reliability estimates sometimes coexisted with systematic score differences or disagreement near decision thresholds. Performance appeared strongest in structured, rubric-based tasks and more variable for communication, non-technical skills, and context-dependent judgments. Human-reference quality, input equivalence, model choice, and validation design also influenced interpretability across studies. The available measurement evidence is most compatible with human-supervised formative, supplementary, second-rater, or quality-assurance applications; autonomous high-stakes use requires stronger external validation, reproducibility, and decision-level safety evidence.
authors: Abdulmohsen M Alomair

title: Artificial intelligence in male infertility from diagnosis to treatment
abstract: Male factors account for almost half of all infertility cases and afflict approximately 186 million men globally, presenting a substantial and increasing public health burden. Semen analysis is the standard of care for assessing male fertility, but subjective visual interpretation results in > 25–30% inter-observer variability and precludes non-destructive assessment of sperm DNA fragmentation (SDF). Machine learning, a branch of artificial intelligence, has the potential to streamline semen assessment and clinical decision-making throughout male infertility care by providing automated, data-driven approaches that are objective, efficient, and precise. Guided by the PRISMA 2020 statement, the manuscript included research from PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar. Two independent reviewers screened all retrieved records according to pre-specified inclusion criteria to identify peer-reviewed publications describing applications of machine learning, deep learning, artificial neural networks, natural language processing, computer vision, and explainable artificial intelligence to semen analysis, fertility status prediction, or assisted reproductive technologies. Artificial Intelligence techniques consistently outperformed conventional semen assessment methods for sperm count, motility, morphology, and predictive analyses. Feedforward Spectral Neural Networks classified sperm concentration with 93% accuracy, while a Fast Region-based Convolutional Neural Network classified sperm motility with 97.37% accuracy; both surpassed inter-observer agreement achievable through WHO-based manual visual analysis. VGG16-pretrained CNNs identified sperm morphology with a true positive rate of 94.1%, however, performance declined substantially to 62% when validated on an independent external dataset. Deep learning models demonstrated the capacity to predict SDF non-destructively, high concordance to TUNEL assay and sperm chromatin structure assay reference standards (r = 0.97, p < 0.001). Machine Learning classifiers specifically, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Random Forest, and CatBoost, showcased AUCs of 0.998 for the prediction of male fertility status. Furthermore, explainable artificial intelligence techniques such as SHAP and LIME improve the clinical interpretability of machine learning model outputs, an important step toward regulatory acceptance. These techniques can also be integration with computer-assisted sperm analysis systems, smartphone-based semen analysis, sperm sorting for intrauterine insemination, microTESE, ultrasonography, and multi-omics data platforms. Limitations of the current literature include retrospective study designs, single-centre data sources, small sample sizes, lack of external validation, and heterogeneity in image acquisition, outcome measures, and performance metrics. Included studies face challenges relating to algorithmic bias, insufficient model explainability, data security and governance, and the absence of standardized regulation or AI-specific reporting frameworks. Future work should prioritise prospective multicentre studies employing multimodal artificial intelligence that integrates imaging data with genomic, transcriptomic, hormonal, and electronic health record inputs, as well as federated learning and international collaboration to establish standardised and internationally recognised regulatory guidelines. In conclusion, artificial intelligence has the potential to transform clinical decision-making for patients presenting with infertility by enabling objective, high-throughput, and personalised assessment of semen samples. However, these tools should be used to augment rather than replace clinical expertise until models have been prospectively validated across diverse populations and have received appropriate regulatory clearance. Not applicable.
authors: Anuradha Dhull; Monika Lamba; Aryan Dahiya; Sushama Tanwar

title: Artificial intelligence in musculoskeletal surgery: Bridging innovation and evidence-based practice
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as one of the most transformative technologies in modern medicine, reshaping how diseases are diagnosed, treated, and monitored.In musculoskeletal (MSK) surgery, AI is rapidly progressing from research laboratories into routine clinical practice through applications in diagnostic imaging, pre-operative planning, robotic-assisted procedures, post-operative monitoring, and clinical workflow optimization.These developments have generated considerable enthusiasm because they promise greater precision, improved efficiency, and increasingly personalized patient care.However, technological innovation alone should not define clinical progress.The increasing availability of machine learning algorithms, deep learning models, computer vision, and generative AI offers unprecedented opportunities to enhance MSK practice.Nevertheless, successful implementation requires more than sophisticated algorithms.Clinical usefulness depends on robust validation, transparency, patient safety, ethical governance, and demonstrable improvements in patient outcomes.The challenge facing orthopedic surgeons is therefore not whether AI should be incorporated into practice, but how to integrate it responsibly while preserving clinical judgment, professional accountability, and evidence-based decision-making.Growing evidence suggests that successful implementation requires thoughtful integration into clinical workflows while ensuring that surgeons remain central to patient care and decision-making.[1][2][3] FROM INNOVATION TO CLINICAL PRACTICEMSK surgery has traditionally relied on the integration of patient history, physical examination, imaging, biomechanics, and surgical expertise.AI introduces an additional analytical dimension by enabling computers to identify complex patterns within large datasets that may not be readily apparent to clinicians.Recent advances in machine learning and deep learning have expanded AI applications across the entire patient journey, including diagnosis, operative planning, intraoperative navigation, rehabilitation, outcome prediction, administrative documentation, and research support.[4][5][6][7]
authors: Anchal Thakur; Yash Partap
venue: Journal of Musculoskeletal Surgery and Research

title: Association of alkaline phosphatase and segmented neutrophils count with low appendicular lean mass in middle-aged women: Evidence from an American cross-sectional survey
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Sarcopenia is associated with an increased risk of frailty, falls, and mortality. Women exhibit distinct characteristics in appendicular lean mass and metabolism compared with men, and hormonal changes may further accelerate appendicular lean mass. This study aimed to identify key blood biomarkers associated with appendicular lean muscle mass index adjusted by body mass index (ALMBMI) in women and to explore their potential relationship with chronic inflammation. METHODS: Based on NHANES 2015-2018 data from middle-aged women, the ALMBMI was calculated. A multimodal machine learning framework was constructed using elastic net logistic regression and generalized linear models (GLMs) to screen core variables affecting ALMBMI. Weighted quantile sum (WQS) regression and Bayesian kernel machine regression (BKMR) jointly determined variable weights and effect directions, and restricted cubic spline (RCS) models characterized dose-response curves to identify key blood indicators and their magnitudes of change associated with low appendicular lean mass risk. RESULTS: A total of 1,082 participants were included in this study. Following variable screening, 12 variables were identified as significantly associated with ALMBMI. WQS regression indicated that segmented neutrophil count (weight: 0.25) and alkaline phosphatase (ALP) (weight: 0.22) were the predominant factors associated with low ALMBMI. BKMR analysis, which assesses all variables jointly, identified segmented neutrophil count (36.0%), and ALP (27.6%) as the core variables. RCS analysis revealed that segmented neutrophil count and alkaline phosphatase showed an L-shaped trend with ALMBMI, with inflection points at 4.00 (1000 cells/μL) and 76.00 IU/L, respectively. In each case, the curves plateaued to the right of the inflection point. Relative to participants classified as having low ALMBMI according to FNIH criteria, those with normal ALMBMI exhibited reductions of 16.01% in ALP and 11.17% in segmented neutrophil count, respectively. CONCLUSION: Among middle-aged women, higher segmented neutrophil count and ALP levels were identified as positive correlates of low ALMBMI, with both biomarkers demonstrating threshold phenomena. Such hematological alterations are consistent with chronic low-grade inflammation, underscoring their potential utility in early sarcopenia screening and prevention.
authors: Shanlan Yang; Jiaofeng Wang; Dayoung Kim; Han Xu; Sheng Zhou; Fan Yang; Zhijun Bao

title: Beyond Sensitivity: A Perspective on Transitioning Photonic Sensors into Real-Life Applications
abstract: Photonic sensing encompasses technologies at markedly different levels of maturity. Fiber-optic sensing systems are already widely deployed in infrastructure, energy, transportation, and industrial monitoring, whereas many integrated biosensors and plasmonic, metasurface, and wearable platforms remain at laboratory or early translational stages. This review critically examines the factors that have enabled some photonic sensing technologies to achieve sustained deployment while continuing to constrain others. Practical performance is considered not only in terms of the optical transducer but also through molecular recognition, sample composition, environmental cross-sensitivity, fabrication variability, optical interrogation, microfluidics, packaging, calibration, electronics, and data processing. Established, transitional, and emerging platforms are comparatively assessed across healthcare, environmental monitoring, industrial process control, structural monitoring, and security applications. Real-life readiness is evaluated through analytical validity, selectivity, reproducibility, stability, dynamic range, response time, manufacturability, usability, and total system value. An application-driven framework is proposed in which sensing architecture, recognition chemistry, sample handling, interrogation, packaging, and validation are co-designed according to the intended operating environment. The analysis shows that successful deployment depends on robust system integration, reproducible manufacturing, application-specific validation, and a clear practical advantage rather than record sensitivity or nominal detection limits alone. Future evaluations should therefore use representative samples, independently manufactured devices, realistic operating conditions, standardized reporting protocols, and comparisons with established analytical methods.
authors: Muhammad Ali Butt

title: Beyond morphology: A review of heterogeneous mechanisms and precision risk management in left ventricular non-compaction/left ventricular hypertrabeculation
abstract: Left ventricular non-compaction/left ventricular hypertrabeculation (LVNC/LVHT) has traditionally been regarded as a congenital cardiomyopathy caused by arrested myocardial compaction during embryogenesis. However, this classical concept is increasingly challenged by mounting clinical and basic evidence, in view of its marked heterogeneity in clinical presentation, imaging features, and genetic background. This review systematically synthesizes relevant research from recent years to propose that LVNC/LVHT is better understood not as a single discrete disease entity, but as a morphological endpoint resulting from diverse etiologies and mechanisms. This review critically appraises the phenotypic pitfalls of current imaging diagnostic criteria, highlighting the clinical dilemma of concurrent over-diagnosis and under-diagnosis that leads to inappropriate management. It then delineates two distinct pathogenic pathways: A developmental pathway associated with mutations in genes such as TAZ and MYH7 and dysregulation of signaling pathways including transforming growth factor-β and neuregulin 1–erythroblastic leukemia viral oncogene homolog; and an acquired/adaptive pathway linked to hemodynamic load-induced myocardial remodeling. Based on these insights, we propose an integrated classification framework subdividing LVNC/LVHT into development-driven, load-adaptive, and idiopathic benign trabeculation subtypes to resolve long-standing diagnostic confusion. We further introduce a multimodal risk stratification system incorporating cardiac structure and function, electrophysiology, genetics, circulating biomarkers, and systemic factors. This strategy aims to shift LVNC/LVHT management from a morphology-based, one-size-fits-all paradigm toward mechanism-guided, individualized precision care. Finally, we outline future directions, including validation of risk models, mechanistic studies, updated guidelines, and integration of artificial intelligence and multi-omics, to establish a novel precision diagnostic and therapeutic framework for LVNC/LVHT.
authors: Changying Zhao; Ran Ran; Shiquan Sun; Tao Shi; Yang Yan; Guoliang Li

title: Beyond physical access: disability-inclusive primary health care as a test of health equity in Sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: Disability inclusion in primary health care is not a peripheral issue but a fundamental test of whether health systems in sub-Saharan Africa are advancing health equity and universal health coverage. Persons with disabilities experience persistent and overlapping barriers across the care pathway, including physical inaccessibility, unaffordable services, inaccessible information, poor provider communication, stigma, weak referral systems, and limited access to rehabilitation and assistive technology. These barriers are intensified by poverty, gender inequality, rural residence, and under-resourced health systems, producing avoidable inequities in access, quality, continuity, and financial protection. This commentary argues that disability-inclusive primary health care should be reframed from a narrow focus on physical access to a broader agenda of health-system accountability. Drawing on recent evidence from sub-Saharan Africa, it highlights how exclusion is embedded in routine system design, financing, workforce capacity, data systems, and governance. The paper further argues that meaningful inclusion requires disability-disaggregated monitoring, accessible communication, reasonable accommodation, provider training, strengthened referral pathways, financing for rehabilitation and assistive products, and formal participation of persons with disabilities and their representative organizations in planning and oversight. Disability-inclusive primary health care is therefore not a specialist add-on, but a core measure of whether universal health coverage reforms are genuinely equitable, people-centered, and resilient. Embedding disability inclusion into routine primary health care performance systems offers a practical pathway to stronger accountability and more inclusive health systems across sub-Saharan Africa.
authors: Mohamed Daud Mohamed; Yakub Burhan Abdullahi; Abdikadir Ahmed Hassan; Iqro Omar Ibrahim; Liibaan Abdulahi Sudi; Nuradin Abdullahi Sheikh Rashid

title: Beyond static perception: Animals, neurons and synapses move to compute efficiently
abstract: Neurons are often modelled as immobile systems that transmit information through chemical and electrical signals constrained by noise and bandwidth. However, this static view contrasts with biological reality, in which dynamical processes operate across scales, from whole-animal movements to motion at the subcellular level. Here, we combine recent experimental observations with biophysically realistic modelling to show that neural information processing, beyond electrochemical signalling, is dynamically shaped by motion, from morphodynamic ultrastructural changes to whole-body movements. In this framework, ultrafast mechanical adjustments in cellular and synaptic structures interact with retinal, eye, head, and body movements to accelerate encoding and enhance precision. Movement across scales dynamically alters the waveforms, latencies, refractoriness and ultrastructural organisation of quantal sampling events. These changes improve signal fidelity and extend spatiotemporal resolution, enabling neurons to generate reliable, high-speed representations with minimal delay. Through active sensing and morphodynamic sampling, animals can therefore enhance the speed and reliability of sensory representations. This perspective, in which self-generated movements across multiple scales enhance encoding and perception, offers new insight into how the brain achieves efficient, predictive and noise-resistant computation while providing a foundation for future experimental tests and biologically inspired AI designs. We first explain how motion-coupled encoding improves neural performance, focusing on edge computing in early sensory systems. We then extend these ideas more speculatively, proposing how motion-coupled sampling may have influenced the evolution of neural architectures at multiple levels, potentially contributing to efficient predictive cognition.
authors: Mikko Juusola; Jouni Takalo; Joni Kemppainen; HaDi MaBouDi; Bruce Yi Bu; Shashwat Shukla; Yiyin Zhou; Aurel A. Lazar; Gonzalo G. de Polavieja
