title: Evaluating Perceptions of AI-Simulated Patients as an Adjunct to Peer-Based Clinical Case Practice in Undergraduate Medical Education: A Mixed Methods Survey Study
abstract: AI-simulated patients are an emerging educational tool that may provide learners with accessible opportunities to practise clinical consultations independently.This study explored participants' perceptions of AI-simulated patients compared with traditional peer-based practice, focusing on perceived effectiveness, acceptability, usability, and self-reported confidence.A questionnaire-based study was conducted involving final-year medical students and Foundation Year 1 (FY1) doctors.Participants used AI-simulated patient cases and completed a questionnaire comprising quantitative ratings and qualitative free-text responses about their experiences.Quantitative responses were analysed descriptively, while qualitative responses were examined to identify key themes in participants' perceptions.Participants reported their experiences of the usability and perceived educational value of AI-simulated patients, including their perceived benefits and limitations compared with peer-based practice.Qualitative feedback provided further insight into the perceived advantages of independent practice and immediate feedback, alongside limitations in human interaction and communication.These findings reflect participants' self-reported perceptions rather than objectively measured changes in knowledge or clinical performance.AI-simulated patients may offer a useful adjunct to traditional peer-based practice by providing an accessible and flexible means of practising clinical consultations.Although participants' perceptions suggest potential benefits for self-directed learning and confidence, these outcomes were not objectively assessed.Further research incorporating objective measures of knowledge, clinical performance, and communication skills is required to establish the educational effectiveness of AI-simulated patients.
authors: Pegin Poulose; Dayana Paulose; David Bourne

title: Evaluation of DeepSeek with a RAG-based knowledge base in preoperative assessment for arthroplasty to improve the decision-making accuracy of junior physicians
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients undergoing elective joint replacement are mostly elderly individuals with multiple chronic diseases. These patients have a higher risk, so preoperative assessment for joint replacement is vital for surgical safety but remains challenging for junior physicians. This study aimed to evaluate the decision-making performance of different versions of DeepSeek (Chat and R1) and their knowledge base (KB)-enhanced schemes in perioperative risk assessment and their impact on junior physicians' decision-making quality. METHODS: A total of 292 anonymized medical records from joint replacement patients were retrospectively analyzed. A professional knowledge base was constructed using 21 perioperative management guidelines and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) technology. The performance of four models (DeepSeek-Chat, DeepSeek-Chat + KB, DeepSeek-R1, and DeepSeek-R1 + KB) was compared in ASA scoring, RCRI scoring, surgical tolerance judgment, and risk prediction. These indicators are related to specific decisions in joint replacement surgery, including preoperative optimization before elective TKA/THA, mitigation of infection risk, planning of VTE prophylaxis, and indication for postponing elective arthroplasty, etc. Senior physicians evaluated model performance using a Likert scale. A 5 × 5 balanced Latin square crossover design was used to assess the impact of model assistance on junior physicians' clinical decision-making. RESULTS: No significant difference was found in ASA scoring accuracy (p > 0.05). For RCRI scoring and risk stratification, DeepSeek-R1 models (79.1%-79.7%) outperformed Chat models (56.5%-66.0%, p < 0.05). In surgical tolerance assessment, DeepSeek-R1 + KB showed relatively better performance, with significantly better predictive precision (p = 0.0284) and a lower missed diagnosis rate (p = 0.005) compared to the Chat models. The R1 series also showed higher predictive efficiency (87.2%-86.4% vs. 63.6%-61.8%, p < 0.05). The R1 models showed better performance than Chat models in medical comprehension, retrieval accuracy, and reasoning logic. After adjusting for physician variability and patient case mix, the DeepSeek-R1 + KB showed a statistically significant improvement over independent decision-making (OR = 1.58, p = 0.004), as well as the DeepSeek-R1 and Chat series. CONCLUSION: The DeepSeek-R1 model, with chain-of-thought reasoning, shows a marginal advantage over the Chat version in preoperative assessment for joint replacement. As a cost-effective clinical auxiliary tool, its integration with a professional knowledge base scheme can optimize the decision-making quality of junior physicians, particularly in terms of providing helpful and comprehensive decision support and providing novel insights for individualized assessment in the context of precision medicine.
authors: Haibo Wu; Mingzhuang Hou; Gongkai Chen; Zhenlin Wen; Changao Yang; Songlin Li; Xiangfei Meng; Peilai Liu; Qunshan Lu

title: Evaluation of the Reliability and Quality of Nursing Care Plans Produced by Artificial Intelligence Models for Patients Experiencing Anaphylactic Shock: A Methodological and Exploratory Investigation
abstract: AIM: This study aimed to develop and validate a ChatGPT 4.0 and DeepSeek V3 model-supported nursing care plan for patients with anaphylactic shock. METHODS: The type of study is methodological and exploratory research. The research consists of three phases and six steps. Phase 1: Patient Scenario Development: (1) literature review and (2) scenario creation. Phase 2: Nursing Care Plan Development: (3) identification of patient care needs and (4) generation of a scenario-based nursing care plan by AI. Phase 3: Validation of the Nursing Care Plan: (5) expert review and validation of the AI-generated nursing care plan and (6) assessment of the nursing care plan's readability. ChatGPT 4.0 and DeepSeek V3 were employed to create nursing care plans. The Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation scale was utilized to evaluate the quality of nursing care plans. The intraclass correlation coefficient was utilized to assess the inter-rater reliability of the evaluation tool. The analysis of readability was conducted utilizing the Ateşman, the Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, the Gunning Fog Index, and the Simple Measure of Gobbledygook formula. RESULTS: A notable difference emerged between the models in the Nursing Assessment section, as experts assigned higher scores to ChatGPT 4.0 (p < .005). No significant differences were found among the artificial intelligence models in other sections (p > .05). DeepSeek V3 exhibited an elevated readability level, indicated by a Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of 13.19, a Gunning Fog Index of 17.20, and an Simple Measure of Gobbledygook score of 9.91. CONCLUSION: Nursing care plans designed with artificial intelligence support are sufficiently readable and applicable for nurses. Cite this article as: Soylu, A., & Soylu, D. (2026). Evaluation of the reliability and quality of nursing care plans produced by artificial intelligence models for patients experiencing anaphylactic shock: a methodological and exploratory investigation. Florence Nightingale Journal of Nursing, 34, 0162, doi: 10.5152/FNJN.2026.25162.
authors: Ayşe Soylu; Dilek Soylu

title: Evolution of Diagnostic and Surgical Standards for Thoracic Outlet Syndrome in Elite Athletes: From Case Report Insights to Modern Vascular Surgery Algorithms
abstract: Background. Thoracic Outlet Syndrome (TOS), particularly venous TOS (vTOS), is a career-threatening neurovascular condition in elite athletes. A historical case of an elite Polish skier highlighted how incomplete decompression led to premature career termination. Aim. To review the evolution of diagnostic, endovascular, and surgical strategies for athletic TOS over the past decade and propose a modernized Return-to-Play (RTP) algorithm based on SVS guidelines. Material and methods. A systematic review of PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, and APCZ UMK databases (2015–2026) was performed, focusing on vTOS management, robotic resections, and ultrasound-guided blocks. Results. Published athletic cohorts demonstrate high rates of return to competitive sport following appropriate surgical decompression, although reported outcomes vary according to TOS subtype, athletic population, surgical technique, and the definition of return to play. In professional baseball players, 79% returned to the same or a higher level of competition following surgery (Chauhan et al., 2024). Minimally invasive approaches, including robotic first rib resection and VATS, may reduce surgical morbidity while providing adequate decompression in appropriately selected patients. Conclusions. Early complete surgical decompression is the current gold standard for athletes with vTOS. Incorporating robotic techniques and dynamic vascular imaging optimizes clinical outcomes and preserves athletic careers.

title: Fabrication of Ultrasensitive Aluminum Oxide Nanoparticle Sensors for Potentiometric Determination of Ondansetron Dihydrate Hydrochloride in Pure and Pharmaceutical Forms
abstract: A highly precise potentiometric method for trace determination of Ondansetron dihydrate hydrochloride (OND) has been developed and established. A highly sensitive sensor of coated wire modified with aluminum oxide (Al2O3) was developed by incorporating trace amounts of (OND) with the ion-pairing reagent phosphomolybdic acid (PMA). Under the test conditions, the sensor exhibited a near-Nernstian response towards the drug over a linear range of 1.0×10-10to 1.0×10-2mol L-1with limit of detection of 5.0x10-11 mol L-1 and slope of +59.30±0.05 mV decade-1for (OND-PMA) coated wire sensor. The potentiometric sensor electrode showed stability up to 65 days and fast responsive time of 14 s. However, the developed potentiometric sensor for OND showed high selectivity to the mentioned drug in presence of various inorganic and some pharmaceutical species. The sensor response remained constant in a suitable potential at various pH from 2.5 to 9.0. Statistical analysis confirms that this potentiometric method is relatively very accurate and reproducible. The developed procedure was successfully applied to measure OND levels in both pure form and many commercial drug samples.
authors: Dheaa Shamikh Zgear; Muataz Ali; Amina M. Abass; Rami A. Abdel‐Rahem

title: Fatigue Reliability
abstract: Fatigue Reliability revolutionizes how we predict and prevent the invisible threats posed by fatigue failure—the silent, progressive weakening of materials under repeated stress that threatens everything from aircraft and bridges to wind turbines and medical devices. The book transforms fatigue reliability into a dynamic, adaptive science that evolves with real-world data. Presenting a unified framework, this volume integrates classical fatigue theories with probabilistic methods, structural health monitoring, and AI/ML techniques. At its core is a closed-loop approach connecting physics-based modeling, real-time data collection, and intelligent decision-making algorithms. This system-level methodology addresses complex interactions among materials, loading conditions, and environmental uncertainties while tackling nonlinear and data-limited scenarios that challenge conventional approaches. What distinguishes this work is its transformation of fatigue reliability from static prediction to continuous adaptation. By bridging rigorous theoretical foundations with practical engineering tools, it enables reliability assessments that update dynamically as new information emerges from operating systems. Designed for researchers, engineers, and graduate students, this book advances fatigue reliability from a static prediction problem to a dynamic, adaptive discipline.
authors: Yongming Liu

title: Feasibility of Using a Multi-Agent LLM System to Correct Annotations and Support Low-Effort Activity Labeling
abstract: Accurate measurement of behaviors is critical for research in human-computer interaction, ubiquitous computing, and personal health informatics, because it underpins many health tracking and intervention systems. Most data collection studies, however, still rely on participants' self-reports and manual annotations, which often under- or over-estimate activity duration and type, and require substantial effort from researchers to clean and validate. An automated system that can combine passive sensing data with participants' self-reports might detect inconsistencies and suggest corrections. We introduce GLOSS4HAR, a multi-agent LLM-based system designed to mimic human sensemaking and assist researchers in cleaning and refining activity annotations. We demonstrate the potential of GLOSS4HAR in two key tasks: (1) correcting and reconciling participant self-annotations, and (2) triangulating passive sensing data with different forms of lightweight self-reports to generate accurate activity timelines. Our evaluation shows that GLOSS4HAR improves annotation quality by up to 9.9% in F1 score and can reconstruct activity timelines that align with human annotations at 75-92% F1. Based on our findings, we discuss the implications of our work for the next generation of activity annotation systems that might use human-AI collaboration.

title: Forensic Medicine in the Modern Era: Principles, Applications, Emerging Technologies, Challenges and Future Directions
abstract: Forensic medicine is a discipline within forensic science that focuses on deceased bodies, particularly the time since death, the cause of death, the manner of death, and the mode of death. It further supports investigations by providing detailed information about the incident, including confirmation of the type of weapon used to commit the crime. Its scope goes beyond the customary forensic autopsy and encompasses medicolegal death investigation, clinical examination of living individuals, interpretation of injuries, assessment of sexual assault, forensic toxicology, identification of unknown persons, documentation of abuse, and evaluation of medical evidence for judicial proceedings. In this mini review, we will examine advanced techniques currently used in forensic medicine and how they enhance investigations, making the process easier for the investigating officer. At present, rather than relying solely on conventional approaches, investigators are increasingly adopting newer advancements such as virtual autopsy. Virtual autopsy offers valuable noninvasive documentation and can enhance the detection of skeletal and certain traumatic findings; however, the available evidence does not justify replacing conventional autopsy universally. In this review article, we will discuss all the new techniques that are useful in the field of forensic medicine and can also assist forensic investigations.
authors: Rohini Dharela; Abhijato Chatterjee; Saarsanth Philem; Davik Chaturvedi; Altamash Nomani; Manraj S. Grover

title: From Prototype to Sustainable Food Production: Translational Barriers and Design Priorities for Agricultural Biosensing Systems
abstract: ABSTRACT Agricultural biosensors could advance sustainable food production by enabling timely detection of crop stress, pathogens, nutrient imbalances, and environmental contaminants. Despite decades of research, however, robust commercial biosensing platforms remain uncommon because analytical performance under controlled conditions does not necessarily translate into dependable field operation or measurable sustainability benefits. Sensors affected by fouling, calibration drift, unstable biorecognition elements, ambiguous biological signals, or frequent replacement may increase cost and material consumption without improving management decisions or reducing agricultural inputs. This perspective article examines the technical, biological, operational, and socioeconomic barriers that limit the transition of agricultural biosensors from laboratory prototypes to resource‐efficient decision‐support systems. It considers performance standards, recognition‐element durability, plant–device biocompatibility, validation practices, user education, and uncertainty communication across open fields, controlled‐environment agriculture, plant wearables, and in vivo platforms. A sustainability‐oriented framework is proposed that connects analytical validity and operational reliability with decision relevance, maintainability, lifecycle considerations, and responsible resource use. Future progress will require biological co‐design, realistic multiscale validation, multimodal data integration, modular and repairable devices, actionable user interfaces, and transparent communication of uncertainty. Agricultural biosensors should ultimately be evaluated not only by their ability to detect target analytes but also by whether they enable reliable interventions that reduce resource consumption, environmental burdens, production risks, and avoidable waste.
authors: Frank Efe Erukainure; David B. Langston; Zachary M. Easton; Blake N. Johnson; Abhilash Kumar Chandel

title: From local practices to national narratives: the micro-construction of Ningxia’s medical cooperation with Benin and China’s health diplomacy in Africa
abstract: Background China’s health diplomacy with Africa is a core part of China-Africa cooperation. Existing studies mostly focus on macro-level strategies and policies, lacking micro-level analysis of local actors and a bidirectional examination of mechanisms linking local practices and national narratives.Objective This study takes Ningxia’s over 40-year medical aid to Benin as a case, explores the interaction between local actions and national narratives, and reveals the micro-construction path of province-country linkage.Methods A single-case embedded research design was employed, drawing on in-depth interviews, policy documents, and official reports, and qualitative coding was conducted in NVivo 14.Results Ningxia implements national health and South–South cooperation strategies through institutionalised dispatch, distinctive technologies, and cultural interactions. Local practices appear to verify and enrich national narratives, and preliminary evidence suggests they can contribute to national policy discussions. Nevertheless, the structure and operation of the associated feedback mechanism remain to be further explored. This interactive process proceeds through four pathways: institutionalised organisation, embodied engagement, emotional communication, and technological innovation.Conclusions The Ningxia-Benin case reveals the provincial level as a crucial intermediary in health diplomacy, where local actions co-construct national narratives. This micro-level foundation enhances the resilience and popular legitimacy of China-Africa health cooperation, extending multi-level diplomacy theory beyond top-down implementation to a co-constitutive framework.
authors: Hongmei Cui; Yue Zhang; Jingwen Yang; Xiuyuan Zhang

title: From state estimation to active intelligence: safety-aware battery management for electric vehicles
abstract: Battery management systems (BMSs) are increasingly required to convert incomplete electrical and thermal measurements into safe control actions rather than merely report battery states. This Mini Review focuses on two deployment questions that connect electrochemistry with control: how electrochemical states can be made observable with affordable diagnostics, and how charging, thermal, balancing, and health objectives can be arbitrated when their constraints conflict. We compare physics-based, equivalent-circuit, and data-driven representations using reported quantitative benchmarks, and show why cross-dataset accuracy alone is insufficient evidence of deployability. Particular attention is given to electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), distribution of relaxation times (DRT), galvanostatic intermittent titration technique (GITT), and active pulse diagnostics as routes for linking measurable responses to interfacial kinetics, resistance growth, and transport limitations. A layered vehicle-edge-cloud architecture is proposed in which a deterministic safety supervisor enforces voltage, temperature, lithium-plating, power, imbalance, and uncertainty limits before performance optimization. The same framework is then examined for solid-state, lithium-sulfur, and sodium-ion batteries, where pressure, observability, and chemistry-specific calibration introduce new constraints. We conclude with a testable short-, mid-, and long-term roadmap centered on uncertainty calibration, pack-level validation, electrochemical observability, version-controlled learning, and safety-case evidence.
authors: Feng Li; Yuan Li; Wenqi Wu; Huaying Qiao; Lihua Jiang

title: Future-Conditioned Representation and Active Sensing in Dynamical Systems
abstract: We show additional future-field predictability in an explicit quadratic expansion of known physical mode amplitudes,and localize forecasting errors by physical component in a controlled Brusselator ensemble. At the critical parameter andhorizon 10, a four-coordinate predictive autoencoder (PRED) gives mean relative L2 field error 0.039 versus 0.152 forthe tested predictive linear references. A quadratic expansion of six physical amplitudes gives lower field error, 0.0229.A nonorthogonal error decomposition resolves the forecasts into critical, fast, uniform and remaining-field components:the quadratic model has smaller uniform and remaining-field squared errors, while PRED predicts the critical amplitudemore accurately. The 27-feature physical expansion uses a larger output-rank allowance and analytical prior, in anexploratory reuse of the original held-out states. Field and linear-coordinate diagnostics support a fast-to-uniform-tocritical interpretation at the sampled horizons in this ensemble. An alanine-dipeptide comparison retains strong linearand torsion-feature references, with a smaller nonlinear margin and an unconfirmed prespecified target-specific crossranking. Separate sensing tests in the Brusselator and Kuramoto–Sivashinsky (KS) systems show favorable, unresolvedor adverse ambiguity-based measurement value, depending on system, horizon and loss.

title: Gallbladder Collapse: Has Its Incidence Increased?
abstract: Introduction: perforation of the gallbladder is infrequent due to prompt and expeditious diagnosis and treatment of biliary pathology. Objective: to report the experience of diagnosis and treatment in patients with gallbladder bladder in a second-level health care hospital. Method: a descriptive, retrospective, longitudinal and observational study was carried out, with a descriptive statistical analysis in patients with gallbladder and/or biliperitoneum after cholecystectomy, emergency or scheduled. Results: 101 patients who underwent cholecystectomy, of which 82 were women, representing 81.18 %, and only 18 men, representing 18.82 %, with a male/female ratio of 1:5. The mean age was 53 years. Gallbladder cholecyst occurred in 12 patients, 11.88 %, 7 more with biliperitoneum 6.93 %, 5 patients with residual choledocholithiasis 4.95 %, and two with persistent jaundice 1.98 %. Discussion: an incidence of gallbladder perforation of 2 to 11 % is reported. Patients with acute cholecystitis, especially elderly people with diabetes and vascular disease, are particularly vulnerable due to microangiopathy, compromised immune response, and delayed perception of symptoms. Emergency, robotic or conventional laparoscopic cholecystectomy is indicated, as opposed to only gallbladder drainage guided by endoscopic ultrasound or cholecystostomy. Conclusions: gallbladder cholecystectomy is such a complex complication that it is reflected in high morbidity with transcendental sequelae and with a high mortality increasing its incidence exponentially. Since the delay in diagnosis and treatment secondary to a lack of infrastructure, supplies, directed health policies and correct regulations.

title: Gastrointestinal obstruction secondary to Rapunzel syndrome: A case report and review of the literature
abstract: Rapunzel syndrome is an extremely rare and complex manifestation of a gastric trichobezoar, characterized by a hairball mass that extends from the stomach into the small intestine. This report details a unique case of a 30-year-old female with cerebral palsy who presented with a five-month history of vomiting, a progressive decrease in oral intake leading to an inability to feed by mouth, and significant weight loss. Physical examination revealed diffuse alopecia, clinical signs of malnutrition, and a firm, mobile epigastric mass. Diagnostic imaging through computed tomography (CT) identified a large intraluminal mass extending from the gastric lumen into the jejunum, resulting in mechanical obstruction. While endoscopy visualized the mass, its significant size precluded endoscopic retrieval. Consequently, the patient underwent an exploratory laparotomy and longitudinal gastrotomy for successful extraction. The postoperative recovery was uncomplicated, and a four month follow-up demonstrated a complete resolution of symptoms and significant weight gain. In conclusion, the early clinical suspicion of Rapunzel syndrome is vital in patients with underlying psychiatric conditions or neurological impairments, to prevent life-threatening complications and ensure timely surgical intervention. In addition to the case presentation, this paper provides a review of the literature.

title: Gate-Tunable Single Ag–rGO FET Platform for Room-Temperature Trigas Detection with a CMOS-Compatible PWM Readout Interface
abstract: Abstract Room-temperature gas sensing requires high sensitivity and selectivity, which FET-based architectures achieve through gate-controlled modulation of surface potential and carrier transport, enabling tunable and efficient chemical transduction. In this work, we introduce a smart trigas sensor capable of selectively detecting three target gases─acetone, formaldehyde, and ammonia at room temperature using a single FET by simply tuning the gate voltage. By leveraging gate-induced modulation, this study demonstrates dynamic control over the interaction between gas molecules and the silver-decorated Reduced Graphene Oxide (Ag-rGO) channel-based gas FET sensor, enabling the individual and selective detection of three distinct gases using the single device. Furthermore, the proposed platform demonstrates distinct cross-sensitivity characteristics, wherein gate-bias modulation enables selective discrimination between formaldehyde, acetone, and ammonia under mixed-gas environments. The device exhibits high detection capability with experimentally estimated limits of detection (LOD) of 158 ppb for acetone, 31 ppb for formaldehyde, and 36 ppb for ammonia, highlighting its potential for low-concentration, room-temperature multigas sensing applications. Beyond material and device-level innovation, a TSMC 180 nm 3.3 V CMOS readout circuit is designed and simulated in Cadence Virtuoso, featuring analogue front-end design for interfacing the proposed gas sensor with a low-power embedded system via PWM signals. The proposed multigas sensor platform and the designed and simulated readout circuit establish a compact and low-power sensing framework, providing a foundation for future studies on breath biomarker analysis and disease-detection applications.

title: Green space exposure predicts manic episodes in bipolar disorder: one year longitudinal analysis using smartphone-derived GPS data
abstract: Urban living is linked to increased psychiatric morbidity, while green spaces may protect mental health via stress-buffering effects. Yet, the role of green space exposure in the onset of affective episodes in bipolar disorder (BD) remains unclear. Using 12 months of GPS data from 29 participants with BD-I/II, we quantified daily exposure to green spaces (green area & NDVI; covariates: population density & imperviousness). Affective status (euthymia, depressive or (hypo)manic episode) was assessed via SCID-based biweekly clinician interviews (26 assessments per participant). Multilevel logistic regression examined moving averages and temporal variance of green space exposure during prodromal and episode weeks relative to euthymia. Reduced mean green space exposure and increased exposure variability were consistently associated with prodromal phases of (hypo)manic episodes, with variance effects persisting into acute (hypo)mania. In contrast, depressive episodes showed limited prodromal predictability. These findings suggest dynamic environmental signatures consistent with early-warning dynamics as modifiable contextual correlates in BD.

title: Gut microbiota-derived tryptophan metabolites in cardiovascular disease: mechanisms, biomarkers, and precision interventions
abstract: The gut microbiota plays a significant role in cardiovascular disease (CVD), through its metabolic products. Tryptophan is a key signaling molecule in the microbiota-host network; its gut microbial metabolites, including indole derivatives, kynurenine and serotonin, have dual effects on cardiovascular homeostasis. This review summarizes research progress on gut microbiota-derived tryptophan metabolites in atherosclerosis, hypertension, heart failure and other CVDs, focusing on metabolic flux in three pathways, the indole, kynurenine (KYN) and 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT) pathways, and their mechanisms via gut barrier maintenance, immune regulation through Th17/Treg and aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) axis, and neuroendocrine blood pressure control. It also evaluates clinical evidence for key metabolites, such as indoxyl sulfate (IS), indole-3-propionic acid (IPA) and indole-3-acetic acid (IAA), as novel biomarkers, and explores precision interventions including dietary regimens, probiotic or postbiotic supplementation, traditional Chinese medicine ingredients, and host genetic background-guided strategies. Current evidence shows these metabolites exert both protective and pathogenic effects, highly dependent on disease context, microenvironment and host genetics. However, most data are from animal models and small cohort studies; remaining challenges include detection standardization, causality establishment and clinical translation. Future research should employ large prospective cohorts, multi-omics integration and mechanism-driven intervention trials to systematically elucidate the regulatory network and advance precision prevention and treatment.
authors: Qian Ding; Siqi Li; Mu Guo; Jia Pu; Jun Wei; Wei Chen

title: Gut-liver axis in liver pre-metastatic niche formation: immune networks, microbial, and metabolic and emerging therapeutic opportunities
abstract: The liver is a leading target for distant metastasis across multiple cancer types, and liver metastasis invariably portends poor prognosis. The formation of pre-metastatic niches (PMNs) within the hepatic microenvironment creates a permissive “soil” for disseminated tumor cells. However, how the gut-liver axis integrates microbial and metabolic signals to remodel the hepatic PMN remains incompletely understood. In this review, we delineate the six hallmark features of PMN assembly, with an emphasis on the complex crosstalk among gut microbiota, their bioactive metabolites, and resident liver cells—including hepatocytes and hepatic immune populations. Notably, these elements engage in a dynamic, reciprocally regulated network characterized by bidirectional feedback loops, rather than a linear signaling cascade. We further survey the emerging landscape of diagnostic biomarkers, including exosomal microRNAs and neutrophil extracellular traps, alongside microbiota-targeted therapeutic interventions. This framework provides testable hypotheses for early interception of liver metastasis and highlights precision medicine opportunities targeting the gut-liver-immune axis.

title: Human-Computer Co-Regulation: A Review of Biofeedback for Meditative Practice
abstract: Biofeedback has been proposed to support meditation and mindfulness practices through wearables, mobile applications, VR/AR systems for decades, and other interactive devices. However, evidence of its effectiveness remains mixed and fragmented across existing research in psychophysiology and Human-Computer Interaction (HCI). This work analyzes 39 studies published between 2015 and 2025 on real-time, user-facing biofeedback for contemplative practice. We first outline a taxonomy of biofeedback interfaces based on sensing modality, feedback channel, interaction context and temporal feedback characteristics, then we synthesize the existing study results on modality-practice fit, showing that the performance of each biofeedback sensing modality in meditative practice is closely related to the meditation practice type: Respiration and heart rate variability (HRV) are the most suitable modalities for paced breathing and stress recovery, and EEG is more appropriate for attention-oriented and experiential targets. Electrodermal activity (EDA) mainly reflects arousal awareness rather than directly measuring meditation quality. In addition, a review-informed co-regulation framework consisting of within-session physiological regulation, experiential mediation, and transfer support is proposed in this work. Finally, we summarize the main gaps in the existing literature and propose design principles for future systems.

title: Hydrogel-based delivery of extracellular vesicles for skin wound healing: design strategies, therapeutic mechanisms, and translational perspectives
abstract: Skin wound healing remains a formidable clinical challenge. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) have attracted considerable attention as therapeutic candidates for wound repair, given their intrinsic capacities to modulate inflammation, promote angiogenesis, and stimulate tissue regeneration. Hydrogels, with favorable biocompatibility, tunable degradation, and sustained-release properties, serve as candidate EV delivery platforms. This review critically examines the landscape of hydrogel-mediated EV delivery for skin wound repair, progressing from EV sources and engineering strategies, through hydrogel design principles and crosslinking modalities, to the modes of EV-hydrogel integration and the multi-dimensional mechanisms including immunomodulation, angiogenesis, extracellular matrix remodeling, and cell proliferation that drive the healing process. Recent advances across acute, diabetic chronic, and burn wounds are evaluated, together with stimuli-responsive hydrogels capable of sensing wound microenvironmental cues such as reactive oxygen species, pH, and matrix metalloproteinase activity to enable microenvironment-responsive EV release, representing a transition from passive delivery toward more adaptive and controlled therapeutic strategies. Nevertheless, the current evidence is derived predominantly from in vitro and small-animal studies and is constrained by heterogeneous EV preparations, insufficient standardization of manufacturing and quality control, and limited clinical validation. Finally, critical challenges including production standardization, scalable manufacturing, and regulatory barriers to clinical translation are analyzed, and future directions for advancing hydrogel-EV systems toward clinical translation are discussed, aiming to provide insights and perspectives for further fundamental research and clinical translation of hydrogel-EV systems in skin wound healing.

title: INDIY ASOSIDAGI NANOZARRALAR: SINTEZ STRATEGIYALARI, TUZILISH VA XOSSALAR O‘RTASIDAGI BOG‘LIQLIK HAMDA BIOTIBBIYOT, SENSOR TEXNOLOGIYALARI VA KATALIZDA ISTIQBOLLI QO‘LLANILISH SOHALARI
abstract: Indium-based nanoparticles - metallic indium, indium oxide (In₂O₃), indium tin oxide (ITO), indium-doped oxides, indium chalcogenides and indium-containing quantum dots - combine tunable band gaps, oxygen-vacancy-controlled conductivity and luminescence, and plasmonic responses extending from the ultraviolet to the infrared. Although In₂O₃ nanoparticles have received far less attention than ZnO or TiO₂, they are emerging as promising materials for biomedicine, chemical sensing, photocatalysis and optoelectronics. This review compares physical (solvated metal atom dispersion, pulsed laser ablation, laser/electron irradiation), solution-chemical (thermolysis, hydrothermal, solvothermal, sol– gel auto-combustion, hot injection), electrochemical (ionic-liquid and aqueous electroreduction) and plant-mediated synthesis routes, with emphasis on green synthesis using Aloe vera, Aerva javanica, Artemisia vulgaris, Vitis vinifera and green tea extracts. The roles of oxygen vacancies, dopants and composition in determining optical and electronic properties are discussed. Applications are surveyed, including antibacterial and anticancer activity, photothermal and photoacoustic theragnostic, drug delivery with SPECT imaging, quantum- dot-based biomarker detection, ethanol and humidity sensing, ITO-based electrochemical sensing, dye photodegradation and heterogeneous organic catalysis.

title: Immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and immunotherapy resistance of esophageal carcinoma
abstract: Esophageal carcinoma (EC) remains one of the most lethal malignancies, with a five-year survival rate of only 15-25% in advanced stages. Although immunotherapy including immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and antibody-based therapies have improved clinical outcomes, durable responses are confined to a minority of patients because primary and acquired resistance affect the majority. The tumor microenvironment (TME)-composed of immune cells, stromal cells, and the extracellular matrix-has emerged as a central driver of the immune resistance, wherein infiltrating immune cells and stromal cells form suppressive networks that impair cytotoxic immunity and foster tumor progression. However, a coherent framework linking clinical practice, TME-mediated resistance mechanisms, and therapeutic strategies remains lacking. In this review, we dissect the cellular and molecular basis of TME-driven immune resistance in EC, summarize established and emerging immunotherapies, and evaluate strategies to overcome treatment failure, including TME-targeted therapy, metabolic modulation, photodynamic therapy, and mechanism-guided combination approaches. These insights reframe immunotherapy resistance as a TME-driven process rather than a purely tumor-intrinsic defect, underscoring the need to concurrently target malignant cells and their surrounding immunosuppressive niche. Ultimately, elucidating TME heterogeneity and its dynamic evolution is essential to convert resistant EC into an immunotherapy-responsive disease and to guide precision combination strategies.

title: Indocyanine green fluorescence-guided surgery in acute settings: state-of-the art
abstract: Background: Operating in acute surgical settings is significantly different from elective surgery. One aspect is the complexity of acutely ill or injured patients with abnormal physiology, unoptimized comorbidities, and unplanned interventions. Traditional visual and tactile assessments of the surgical field anatomy and tissue viability have documented limitations. The need for integrated technology to augment such assessments is described. Indocyanine green fluorescence-guided surgery (ICG-FGS) is a promising tool, given its history, safety, low cost, and accumulated experience in elective settings for many surgeries, to help transform precision surgery into acute settings (trauma and emergency surgery). An updated review is needed based on new evidence outlining the current landscape of ICG in acute settings. Methods: We performed a comprehensive review of literature update in the last two decades through June 2026, covering PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, and published societal guidelines, including, but not limited to, the World Society of Emergency Surgery (WSES) consensus position paper and the Society of American Gastrointestinal and Endoscopic Surgeons (SAGES) review. Results: ICG is applicable across the full spectrum of acute surgical care, classified under two principal functions: anatomical mapping (biliary, ureteric, thoracic duct, and vascular structures) and perfusion assessment (bowel and mesenteric ischemia, anastomotic perfusion, pancreatic necrosis, burns, soft tissue, extremity trauma, and organ injury). Emerging and less commonly reported applications include necrotizing fasciitis debridement guidance, traumatic brain injury monitoring, penetrating abdominal trauma, gonadal torsion, fistula detection, damage control surgery, and AI-augmented quantitative fluorescence. The WSES consensus and SAGES meta-analysis provided strong prospective validation to date regarding anastomotic leakage reduction. Current gaps include the absence of standardized dosing protocols in acute settings, limited randomized data, and the subjectivity inherent to qualitative fluorescence interpretation. Conclusions: ICG fluorescence-guided surgery is a safe, low-cost, and rapidly deployable adjunct for emergency surgery. Its breadth of applicability warrants wider consideration and integration into acute surgical workflows to inform surgical decision making based specific considerations including specific indications, evidence support, equipment availability, local expertise, workflow readiness and clinical judgement. Standardized protocols, prospective trials, objective and AI-powered quantification are the research priorities to further clarify its practical role.

title: Inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor of the psoas muscle presenting as a retroperitoneal mass: a case report.
abstract: Introduction: Inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor (IMT) is a rare mesenchymal neoplasm of intermediate biological potential characterized by myofibroblastic spindle-cell proliferation and a variable inflammatory infiltrate. Although IMT may arise in a wide range of anatomical locations, primary involvement of the psoas muscle is exceptionally uncommon and may present significant diagnostic challenges due to its nonspecific clinical and radiological features. Case presentation: A 29-year-old man presented with progressive left flank and left iliac fossa pain radiating to the back and left lower limb. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) revealed a 5.8 × 4.7 × 6.6 cm hypervascular intramuscular mass within the left psoas muscle, highly suspicious for a malignant retroperitoneal soft-tissue neoplasm. CT-guided core needle biopsy was inconclusive. Due to persistent symptoms and diagnostic uncertainty, the patient underwent complete surgical excision of the lesion. Histopathological examination demonstrated a spindle-cell proliferation with a prominent inflammatory infiltrate, while immunohistochemistry showed positivity for vimentin and smooth muscle actin with focal weak ALK-1 expression and a low Ki-67 proliferation index, confirming the diagnosis of IMT. Surgical margins were negative. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient remained free of recurrence at 5-month follow-up. Discussion: Primary IMT of the psoas muscle is extremely rare and may closely mimic malignant retroperitoneal tumors on clinical and radiological evaluation. Preoperative diagnosis is often difficult, and image-guided biopsy may be non-diagnostic. Definitive diagnosis relies on histopathological and immunohistochemical assessment, while complete surgical excision remains the treatment of choice for localized disease. Conclusion: IMT should be considered in the differential diagnosis of retroperitoneal and intramuscular soft-tissue masses, particularly in young adults. Complete surgical resection provides both definitive diagnosis and effective treatment, with favorable short-term outcomes when negative margins are achieved.
authors: Wail Alqatta; Shaima Alfaqeeh

title: Information asymmetry and the operational efficiency of the hospital emergency department: An analysis of complications associated with the use of anabolic-androgenic substances
abstract: Aim: Concealment of anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) use by patients may increase diagnostic uncertainty, prolong emergency department stay, and generate costs related to exclusionary testing. The aim of the study was to assess the impact of information asymmetry regarding AAS use on emergency department operational efficiency, including diagnostic time, resource utilization, and cost of care, and to identify organizational measures that may reduce this problem. Materials and methods: A qualitative-quantitative case study was combined with process observation and simplified value stream mapping. The analysis included an anonymized case of a 43-year-old male patient admitted to the emergency department with cardiological symptoms and observational material covering approximately 80 patients with suspected AAS-related complications from 2025-2026. Triage stages, diagnostic pathway, length of stay, and cost structure were assessed. Results: In the analyzed case, total emergency department stay was 18 hours and the cost of care was estimated at PLN 3150. Approximately 65% of the total cost resulted from diagnostic activities initiated before AAS use was disclosed. Observational material indicated that about half of the presentations concerned men aged 40-60 years. The greatest process losses were related to delayed history taking, waiting for results, and the use of high-cost resources. Conclusions: Information asymmetry significantly reduces emergency department operational efficiency, prolongs lead time, and increases diagnostic costs. Early screening questions on AAS use, standardized triage, and a fast-track consultation pathway may reduce unnecessary testing and improve departmental throughput.
authors: Bartosz Izydor Sieńkowski

title: Inguinal Hernia in a Woman: A Rare Clinical Entity – Case Report
abstract: Inguinal hernia in females is not common, and they are misdiagnosed due to atypical presentation and lower clinical suspicion as compared to males. Inguinal hernia usually presents as a groin swelling with or without pain and carries a higher risk of complications such as incarceration or strangulation. Diagnosis is primarily by clinical examination, but may need imaging support when uncertain. Surgical repair remains the definitive treatment, with both open and laparoscopic approaches. Early recognition is very important to prevent unwanted complications, which are more common in women with femoral hernias. This case report presents a patient with a right-sided inguinal hernia. A 44-year old female patient presented in outpatient surgery with a history of a lump in the right groin area for the last few months.
authors: Amir Yousaf; Raheel Ahmed

title: Inspect Robots: Evaluating the Capabilities and Safety of Embodied AI
abstract: General purpose language models are increasingly able to control robotic hardware. Understanding the capabilities and safety of these models when embodied is therefore increasingly important for understanding their societal impact and risks. To this end, we introduce Inspect Robots, a modular, open-source framework for developing and running evaluations of embodied agents. Inspect Robots pairs customizable, reusable abstractions for specifying physical evaluations and analyzing their results with infrastructure that automates evaluation setup, execution and termination. We demonstrate Inspect Robots by using it to evaluate the capabilities and safety of six policies based on frontier language models. Inspect Robots has seen significant early uptake, receiving nearly 100,000 downloads in the three months since its release.

title: Integrating Technology in Mathematics Classrooms: A Case Study of Scientific Calculator Use in Secondary Schools
abstract: The educational system in Malaysia needs to improve calculator implementation because schools must fulfill their responsibility of developing Higher Order Thinking Skills (HOTS) through national regulations. This research study examines the link between scientific calculator competencies and the Higher Order Thinking Skills (HOTS) performance of Form Four students who solve quadratic functions. A secondary school in Johor conducted a primarily quantitative research study with supplementary qualitative elements (open-ended questionnaire responses), involving 55 students who completed the Calculator Competency Test (α = 0.89), the HOTS Assessment (α = 0.91), and the student questionnaire (α = 0.85). The findings showed a strong positive association between calculator proficiency and HOTS performance (r = 0.949, p < 0.001). The regression results (R² = 0.901) are exploratory due to the small sample size (n = 55); this should be interpreted as a preliminary association rather than a predictive relationship. No multicollinearity was found (VIF = 1.48), but discriminant validity testing is needed (Fornell-Larcker, HTMT). Students showed a major confidence deficiency, with the majority reporting low confidence levels for difficult tasks, even though 56.36% of students demonstrated high performance on the competency test. The study revealed four illustrative themes from qualitative responses: technical obstacles, strategic uncertainty, restricted teaching time, and preference for traditional methods. As basic skills calculators function as scaffolding tools that help students, they do not address fundamental learning gaps. The study recommends professional development, curriculum alignment, and resource distribution through classroom sets, government funding, shared-device systems, and public-private partnerships.
authors: Leong Zi Jun; Norulhuda Binti Ismail

title: Intelligent Distributed Optical Fiber Pressure Sensing for Dental Bite-Force Analysis
abstract: Measuring bite force is essential for assessing the masticatory system and diagnosing oral disease. Existing measurement devices have low spatial resolution and susceptibility to electromagnetic interference. This paper presents a machine learning (ML)-assisted distributed fiber optic sensing system based on Scattering Level Multiplexing (SLMux) for high-resolution bite force analysis. Enhanced backscattered data were acquired through optical backscattered reflectometry from 88 sensing points along the dental arch. Measured data were reconstructed into a two-dimensional map of bite force and analyzed through an ML pipeline. Sector classification across 4 regions and weight prediction were processed by an end-to-end fine-tuned ResNet-18 Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and classical ML approaches. ResNet-18 is compared with Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest, XGBoost (Extreme Gradient Boosting), Extra Trees, and k-Nearest Neighbors (kNN) trained on handcrafted features. On sector classification, Logistic Regression achieved the best performance (98.71% accuracy). On the weight prediction task, formulated as a 12-class problem, the end-to-end ResNet-18 CNN substantially outperformed all classical models, reaching 51.28% accuracy and a mean absolute error of 78 g, versus 124 g for the best classical model. A regression-based ResNet-18 variant was also trained on the wavelength-shift and weight data, resulting in a mean absolute error of 62.6 g. The results indicate that integrating ML with distributed fiber-optic sensing has the potential to enhance dental diagnostics and treatment planning.

title: Knowing Long COVID: Epistemic Barriers to Recognition and Care
abstract: Objective This study explored the epistemic barriers affecting the recognition and care of Long COVID. It sought to understand how uncertainty is produced, distributed, and navigated among clinicians, researchers, and patients, and how these dynamics shape care pathways and patient experiences. Methods We conducted a qualitative analysis grounded in more than 400 accounts of clinical encounters, alongside more than 100 patient testimonies collected through the Long Covid Belgium organisation. Informed by interdisciplinary socio-medical scholarship, the analysis examined how Long COVID is narrated, negotiated, and recognised across healthcare and institutional pathways. Results Clinical uncertainty was unevenly distributed among clinicians, researchers, and patients. From the patient perspective, these asymmetries frequently manifested as symptom minimisation, psychosocial reframing, delayed investigation, and fragmented care. Persistent gaps in recognition and care were linked to epistemic injustice and gender bias, alongside limitations associated with positivist medical training models. In response, patients increasingly drew on biomedical evidence and collective forms of lay knowledge, fostering the emergence of “expert patients”. Conclusion Long COVID may be understood as a “total social fact,” revealing structural vulnerabilities within and beyond healthcare systems. More integrated, reflexive, and relational models of care are needed to improve recognition and management while reducing iatrogenic risk. The findings identify actionable pathways towards more epistemically responsible, coordinated, and patient-attuned care.

title: LAPAROSCOPIC REMOVAL OF MESH FOR PELVIC ORGAN PROLAPSE: A SURGICAL NIGHTMARE
abstract: Objective: To present a combined laparoscopic-endoscopic surgical approach for the treatment of a TVT bladder extrusion.Description: A 79-year-old woman with a history of TVT mesh placement for stress urinary incontinence.Five years later, she returned to the clinic with urgency urinary incontinence and pain.Ultrasound and cystoscopy revealed a mesh extrusion at the bladder dome of approximately 1 cm.Given the location of the extrusion, a combined laparoscopic-endoscopic approach was used.Clinically, after one year of follow-up, the pain has subsided, with mild residual urge and stress incontinence.This is an effective and reproducible approach for the management of TVT mesh bladder extrusions with difficult transvaginal access.

title: LAPAROSCOPIC UROLOGIC SURGERY: INITIAL EXPERIENCES IN PADANG
abstract: Introduction: Laparoscopic surgery is increasingly prevalent in urology due to improved surgical expertise. This minimally invasive procedure, popularized in the nineteenth century, offers advantages including reduced pain, less bleeding, shorter hospital stays, and improved cosmetic results compared to open surgery. Laparoscopy has expanded to various applications, including nephrectomies, pyeloplasty, ureteral stone removal, nonpalpable testes, and adrenal surgeries. Today, most urological procedures can be performed using laparoscopy, with oncological outcomes comparable to open surgery. Objective: In this retrospective study, we assess urological laparoscopic surgery results and complications in Padang, Indonesia. Material & Methods: A retrospective evaluation was conducted on patients who underwent laparoscopic surgery in Padang, Indonesia, between September 2017 and July 2023. The assessment encompassed preoperative diagnoses, laparoscopic procedure types, operation duration, hospital stays, blood loss, conversion to open surgery, and complications. Results: Of the 155 patients, 105 (67.7%) were male, with a median age of 37 years (range: 1-78). The common laparoscopic surgeries included simple nephrectomy (29%), laparoscopy undescended testis (UDT) (19.3%), renal cyst unroofing (13.5%), and radical nephrectomy (13.5%). Hospital stays ranged from 1 to 7 days, depending on the laparoscopic procedure type. Approximately 12.9% of patients required conversion to open surgery, and no major complications or fatalities were observed. Conclusion: The success and complication rates of laparoscopic surgeries in our city align with those reported in the literature. We firmly believe that technological advancements, increasing experience, and improved patient tolerance make laparoscopic surgery a secure and minimally invasive alternative to open procedures. Keywords: Laparoscopic surgery, minimally invasive surgery, urological surgery.

title: Legal Frameworks, Institutional Barriers and Unmet Needs of Young University Students With Cancer in Italy: A Call to Action
abstract: ABSTRACT University students with cancer in Italy face major barriers in maintaining their academic pathways despite existing disability legislation. This brief communication combines an overview of the Italian legal and institutional context with findings from a community‐led qualitative descriptive needs‐assessment. Following a national social media call, the analysis included semi‐structured interviews with 69 eligible participants. Interviews were documented through contemporaneous written notes and analyzed manually using descriptive content analysis, combining domains from the interview guide with recurrent categories identified in open‐ended responses. Participants described administrative burdens, inconsistent recognition of cancer‐related needs, limited access to remote learning and flexible examinations, marked variability in university support, emotional distress, and social isolation. These findings provide preliminary real‐world evidence of how existing arrangements are experienced by Italian university students affected by cancer. Although specific interventions were not evaluated, the findings may inform the development and prospective assessment of more consistent academic accommodations, accessible information, individualized support, and integrated psychosocial services.

title: Legal Protection for People with Mental Disorders Who Are Victims of Sexual Violence Through the Social Services Agency in Sorong City
abstract: This study aims to analyze the implementation of legal protections for people with mental disorders (ODGJ) who are victims of sexual violence in Sorong City and to identify institutional and coordination barriers to the fulfillment of victims’ rights, as well as their support, rehabilitation, and recovery. The method used in this study is empirical legal research with a socio-legal approach. Primary data were obtained through interviews with the Sorong City Social Services Agency and relevant parties, while secondary data were obtained from relevant laws and regulations and legal literature. The analysis was conducted qualitatively by comparing the normative framework for victim protection with the actual implementation of protection measures at the local level. The novelty of this study lies in its analysis of protection for people with mental health conditions who are victims of sexual violence through the lens of institutional integration, positioning the Social Services Agency as part of a protection ecosystem that must be connected to the police, the DP3A, health services, professionals, support organizations, families, and the community. The results of the study indicate that, normatively, legal protection for people with mental health conditions who are victims of sexual violence has an adequate legal basis; however, its implementation in Sorong City has not been optimal and remains unintegrated. The Social Services Agency has provided support, social worker interventions, family and community guidance, needs assessments, and service referrals; however, it does not yet have a specific program for people with mental health conditions who are victims of sexual violence. Other barriers include limited mental health and rehabilitation facilities, a shortage of professionals, a lack of social rehabilitation centers, as well as persistent stigma and weak family support. The study concludes that it is necessary to strengthen the integrated protection model and cross-sectoral coordination from the identification of victims, through support, legal proceedings, health and psychological services, rehabilitation, to social reintegration.
authors: Oriza Sativa Ningrum Ombaer; Wahab Aznul Hidaya; Sokhib Naim

title: Low-power wireless communication technologies empower wearable healthcare monitoring
abstract: Low-power wireless communication is critical for long-term wearable healthcare monitoring. This review presents a structured technical comparison of radio frequency identification (RFID), near field communication (NFC), backscatter communication (BackCom), and ultra-wideband (UWB) in terms of principles, energy mechanisms, architectures, and performance. We further examine their applications in body-fluid and vital-parameter monitoring, identify challenges in power, range, integration and security, and provide guidance for selecting communication technologies for next-generation wearable medical systems.
authors: Xiaodong Na; Lin Wu; Qingxiang Kong; Wei Cao; Xiao Fang; Yuanqing Wu; Tianzhe Bao; Shengquan Xie

title: Low‐Field MRI for Knee Imaging: Current Insights and Evidence From a Systematic Review
abstract: BACKGROUND: Low-field magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has regained interest for musculoskeletal imaging due to advances in magnet design, hardware optimization, and artificial intelligence (AI)-based reconstruction, offering improved accessibility, patient comfort, and sustainability. PURPOSE: This systematic review aimed to explore and summarize the current status of low-field MRI for knee investigations. STUDY TYPE: Systematic review on MEDLINE, Cinhal, EMBASE, Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar databases. PROSPERO protocol (CRD42024544354). POPULATION: Approximately 3400 participants (8-89 years) encompassing healthy volunteers, community-based cohorts, and patients with diverse knee pathologies were evaluated. Few studies incorporate phantom experiments. FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: This review covered a range of very-low-field (< 0.1 T), conventional low-field (0.1-< 0.29 T), and upper-range low-field (> 0.3 T-0.55 T) with standard, extremity, open, and weight-bearing/standing systems. SE/FSE and GRE sequences, 3D GRE quantitative protocols, and AI-based were used. ASSESSMENT: Two reviewers independently extracted data on knee protocols, technical parameters, diagnostic performance, and reported advantages and limitations. STATISTICAL TESTS: Study quality was assessed using appropriate JBI critical appraisal tools. A narrative synthesis and descriptive analysis of the findings from the included studies are provided due to the heterogeneity of the intervention and outcome. RESULTS: From 3726 records, 31 were included. Low-field MRI demonstrated high diagnostic performance for meniscal and ligamentous injuries but lower sensitivity for early cartilage degeneration. Weight-bearing MRI provided distinct functional information but not direct equivalence to standard MRI. AI-enhanced reconstruction was evaluated in a limited number of single-center, vendor-specific studies and was associated with improved image quality and diagnostic confidence. Important limitations included lower signal-to-noise ratio, reduced spatial resolution, protocol heterogeneity, and limited pathology-validated evidence. DATA CONCLUSION: Low-field MRI may provide a clinically useful complementary option for selected knee meniscal and ligamentous indications. However, heterogeneous evidence, influenced by field strength, scanner design, sequences, and reference standards, limits claims of equivalence with high-field MRI, particularly for subtle cartilage lesions. Advances in hardware and AI have improved image quality and efficiency; however, evidence is limited and larger standardized multicenter studies are required. EVIDENCE LEVEL: 5. TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 5.

title: Machine Learning Modelling of Mental Disorders in the People of South Sudan
abstract: The increase in mental health challenges among the population has raised serious concerns among educators, healthcare professionals, and lawmakers. Because of the substantial impact of mental diseases on emotions, cognition, and social relationships, creative preventative and intervention measures are required, particularly for those living in conflict-prone locations. Early detection is critical, and medical predictive analytics could change healthcare, especially given the severe impact of mental disorders on individuals. However, the conventional methods of mental illness prediction often suffer from the issue of either over-detection or under-detection and the time-consuming manual review process of patients' data during screening sessions. Therefore, the main objective of the study was to utilize machine learning approaches in the prediction of mental health problems that can complement the traditional clinical screening and diagnosis process. It developed five machine learning models namely logistic regression, Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, Decision Tree, and K-Nearest Neighbors that can be used to predict mental disorders outcomes among the people of South Sudan. They were trained and evaluated on the cross-sectional dataset collected from the South Sudan Demobilization, Disarmament and Re-integration Commission’s community surveys (DDRC, 2021). The study results show that the random forest model performs better than the other four models and the most important predictors of the target variable (mental health disorders) were, in order of influence, state, income and number of children. The study demonstrates that the use of machine learning models can help with mental health assessment, giving a patient-friendly and a solution that is scalable option for early detection. It is conceivable to integrate machine learning models into digital health platforms to help mental health providers make decisions that are informed and provide timely interventions. The research suggests that in order to enhance generalizability across diverse populations, it is necessary to incorporate multimodal information, enhance models, and utilize a variety of datasets in future investigations. AI-powered mental healthcare solutions have the potential to revolutionize the processes of diagnosing and arranging treatment for individuals with mental health issues in countries with limited resources.

title: Malignant Priapism as the Sole Initial Manifestation of Metastatic Carcinoma with Suspected Pulmonary Origin: A Case Report and Review of the Literature
abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Malignant priapism is a rare manifestation of advanced malignancy caused by malignant infiltration of the corpora cavernosa. We report a case of persistent and refractory priapism associated with penile carcinoma and extensive metastatic disease, with a suspected pulmonary primary. Case Presentation: An 81-year-old man with a history of prostate cancer treated by radical prostatectomy and persistently undetectable PSA levels developed persistent low-flow priapism. Despite aspiration and irrigation, followed by distal and proximal shunting procedures, the condition recurred with progressive corporal induration and severe pain. Cavernous biopsy was initially interpreted as moderately differentiated squamous carcinoma, while total penectomy performed for refractory pain showed poorly differentiated carcinoma with morphological adenosquamous features. CT and PET/CT demonstrated a pulmonary mass and widespread metastatic disease, although bronchoscopy was non-diagnostic and no histological confirmation of the pulmonary lesion was obtained. A focused review of the literature identified 32 published cases of malignant priapism; bladder cancer was the most frequently reported primary malignancy (37.5%), followed by prostate cancer (18.8%) and renal cell carcinoma (9.4%), while penectomy was performed in 34.4% of cases. Conclusions: Persistent or recurrent priapism associated with corporal induration, progressive or atypical pain, failure of conventional treatment, or discordant imaging findings should raise suspicion of malignant infiltration and prompt consideration of repeat imaging and tissue sampling. In the present case, carcinoma involving the penile structures was histologically confirmed, whereas pulmonary origin remained a clinicoradiological suspicion; penectomy provided immediate pain relief in the setting of extensive refractory local disease.
