title: SurgGraph: Quantitative Laparoscopic Video Understanding via Geometry-Grounded Scene Graphs
abstract: Surgical videos are a primary resource for teaching trainees anatomy, tool usage, and procedural skills. Yet learning from them at scale requires systems that understand surgical scenes. Existing approaches fall short: vision-language models lack fine-grained domain reasoning, task-specific models do not generalize, and prior scene graphs omit clinically meaningful detail. We present SurgGraph, a training-free pipeline that generates quantitative scene graphs from surgical videos. Operating on segmentation masks and depth maps, SurgGraph encodes each clinically meaningful relation (attachment, occlusion, separation, tool actions) as a tuple whose numeric value quantifies the relation's extent over time. Technical evaluations show more precise scene understanding than state-of-the-art surgical VLM baselines. We then build SurgGraphQA, a proof-of-concept learning application that retrieves meaningful and boundary-case exemplars and generates visual explanations and feedback. A study with 17 medical students and 2 resident surgeons shows significant learning gains, demonstrating its educational value.

title: Surgical Approaches and Prognostic Factors in Superior Sulcus Tumors
abstract: Objective: To evaluate surgical approaches, clinical characteristics, and prognostic factors in patients with superior sulcus tumors (SSTs) and to assess survival outcomes according to resection type.Materials and Methods: This study included 20 patients with histopathologically confirmed SSTs who underwent surgical treatment between 1997 and 2004. Eight patients were evaluated retrospectively and twelve prospectively. Demographic, clinical, radiological, histopathological, and treatment-related data were analyzed. Survival outcomes were assessed using the Kaplan–Meier method, and comparisons between groups were performed using the log-rank test.Results: All patients were male, with a mean age of 53 years. Pain was the most common presenting symptom (100%). Tumors were predominantly located in the right hemithorax (75%). Lobectomy was performed in 85% of patients, while 15% underwent wedge resection due to limited pulmonary reserve. Postoperative complications occurred in 45% of patients, with atelectasis being the most frequent. Squamous cell carcinoma was the most common histopathological subtype. Median survival was longer in the lobectomy group compared with the wedge resection group (38 vs. 14 months), although the difference did not reach statistical significance (p=0.075). Patients with nodal involvement and vertebral invasion had poorer survival.Conclusion: Extent of resection, nodal status, and local invasion remain key determinants of prognosis in SST. Lobectomy was associated with more favorable survival outcomes than limited resection, although these findings should be interpreted cautiously. Despite advances in multimodality treatment, prognostic factors continue to guide clinical decision-making in this complex disease.
authors: Hüseyin Eren; Tamer Altınok; Abdullah İrfan Taştepe

title: Surgical Tricks in Living Donor Organ Transplantation
abstract: This chapter explores advanced surgical techniques and strategies in living donor organ transplantation, emphasizing innovations that enhance graft function, minimize complications and rejection, and improve long-term outcomes. Divided into three major sections, it integrates practical experience with scientific evidence. The first part focuses on (LDKT) living donor kidney transplantation, detailing donor evaluation, imaging, laparoscopic and robotic donor nephrectomy, back-table vascular reconstruction, and recipient implantation. Surgical refinements – such as meticulous lymphatic control, ureteral preservation, and optimized ureteroneocystostomy – are discussed for preventing vascular, urinary, and lymphatic complications. The second part covers (LDLT) living donor liver transplantation, highlighting donor selection, preoperative volumetric planning, and complex vascular and biliary reconstructions. Technical maneuvers ensuring adequate graft perfusion and biliary integrity are presented, with emphasis on donor safety, precision surgery, and ethical principles guiding the procedure. The final part examines future directions, including robotic and minimally invasive donor surgery, 3D modeling, machine perfusion, regenerative medicine, and the integration of artificial intelligence in surgical planning and postoperative care. Ethical and policy considerations are reviewed to ensure sustainable and equitable practice. This comprehensive overview serves as both a technical reference and educational guide, aiming to enhance surgical excellence, promote innovation, and reinforce the humanitarian foundation of living donor transplantation.

title: Synergistic Li + -functionalized Mo 2 CT X MXene and polyaniline composite for rapid and stable moisture sensing in wearable wound monitoring application
abstract: Abstract Managing optimal moisture balance is essential for chronic wound healing, yet current clinical assessments are often subjective and intermittent. This study reports the development of a high-performance, flexible resistive moisture sensor designed for real-time, quantitative wound monitoring. The active sensing layer consists of a lithium-ion (Li + ) functionalized Mo 2 CT X MXene and polyaniline (PANI) composite. Li + intercalation was utilized to expand the MXene interlayer spacing, enhancing water adsorption and ion transport. Simultaneously, in situ polymerized PANI was introduced to provide stable proton-conductive pathways. Current–voltage characterization verified that the Li + –Mo 2 CT X /PANI composite forms robust Ohmic contacts with the electrodes, exhibiting over a 40-fold enhancement in baseline electrical conductance compared to pristine Mo 2 CT X . The composite was integrated onto screen-printed circular interdigitated electrodes on a flexible PET substrate and encapsulated with poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) (PDAC). This protective PDAC layer acts as a semi-permeable moisture-diffusion barrier that regulates water molecule transport, prevents surface fouling and uncontrolled hydration saturation, and ensures environmental stability without compromising response speed. The sensor demonstrates a linear response across a wide relative humidity (RH) range of 20%–80%, featuring sensitivity of approximately 2.0 Δ R /%ΔRH, with a rapid response time of ∼1 s and a recovery time of ∼11 s. The device demonstrates high mechanical flexibility, and stable operation over a 15 d period. Real-time assessments using finger-touch tests and PVA-hydrogel wound models successfully distinguished between dry, normal, and wet clinical states. The superior performance is attributed to the synergistic effects of Li + -assisted interlayer hydration, Grotthuss-type proton hopping, and moisture-induced PANI protonation. These findings position the Li + –Mo 2 CT X /PANI composite as a promising candidate for next-generation smart dressings in digital wound management.

title: TRACE: Learning to Self-Calibrate Wireless Digital Twins from ISAC Measurements
abstract: Wireless digital twins (DTs) rely on 3D environment models to predict radio propagation and support wireless-network decisions, yet these models are often initialized from imperfect 3D maps. Errors in building position, height, footprint, and orientation can therefore cause a high-fidelity propagation engine to simulate the wrong physical environment. In this paper, we study how a deployed wireless network can repair an existing DT using its own radio frequency (RF) measurements. In particular, we introduce Twin Residual Alignment and Calibration Engine (TRACE), a physics-grounded learning-based self-calibration framework that treats twin maintenance as residual alignment between the physical world and the current DT. Using the same sensing configuration as the physical measurements, TRACE ray-traces the current DT, coherently backprojects the measured and simulated RF onto a common world grid, and extracts the same local region around each building's current DT position. A multi-view corrector then fuses evidence across sensing nodes and neighboring buildings to predict a gated six-parameter correction per building, without relying on absolute layout or sensor ordering, and supports iterative correction through re-rendering. On 5,400 held-out samples from unseen simulated scenes at 28 GHz, TRACE reduces 3D position RMSE from 2.202 m to 0.302 m and yaw RMSE from 4.978° to 0.894°, outperforming ViT and U-Net baselines under changes in layout, building count, sensing-node count, and SNR. On measured 28 GHz RF data from the NIST outdoor courtyard, a model trained only on synthetic RF reduces mean planar wall-position error from 1.00 m to 7.8 cm, without measured-data fine-tuning or geometric labels. These results show that the discrepancy between measured and twin-rendered RF can serve as a learning signal for repairing a wireless DT.

title: TVT MESH BLADDER EXTRUSION: REPAIR BY COMBINED LAPAROSCOPIC-ENDOSCOPIC APPROACH
abstract: Objective: To present a combined laparoscopic-endoscopic surgical approach for the treatment of a TVT bladder extrusion.Description: A 79-year-old woman with a history of TVT mesh placement for stress urinary incontinence.Five years later, she returned to the clinic with urgency urinary incontinence and pain.Ultrasound and cystoscopy revealed a mesh extrusion at the bladder dome of approximately 1 cm.Given the location of the extrusion, a combined laparoscopic-endoscopic approach was used.Clinically, after one year of follow-up, the pain has subsided, with mild residual urge and stress incontinence.This is an effective and reproducible approach for the management of TVT mesh bladder extrusions with difficult transvaginal access.

title: Tail-Risk-Aware Information Guidance for Angles-Only Spacecraft Rendezvous Under Markovian Measurement Outages
abstract: Angles-only spacecraft rendezvous couples guidance and navigation because trajectory geometry changes both observability and measurement availability. This paper develops tail-risk-aware guidance for geometry-dependent, burst-correlated optical outages. A planar benchmark uses explicit Markov measurement-arrival scenarios and conditional value at risk to shape terminal navigation uncertainty, followed by independent 10,000-run validation. Relative to expected availability guidance, the selected trajectory reduces 95% conditional value at risk by 39.2% and 99% conditional value at risk by 15.7%, at 35.8% higher maneuver expenditure. A separate 200-run nonlinear three-dimensional holdout uses two-body-plus-oblateness truth dynamics, azimuth/elevation sensing, maneuver errors, unscented Kalman filtering, and covariance-weighted terminal feedback. The risk-aware trajectory increases realized measurement availability from 20.7% to 56.1%, reduces mean longest outage from 14.39 to 6.80 epochs, and reduces median and 95th-percentile terminal estimation error from 49.64m to 0.89m and 223.24m to 21.93m, respectively, while mission success remains statistically comparable. This demonstrates that the operational payoff is navigation robustness rather than consistent superior terminal accuracy. Because approach-corridor constraints are monitored but not enforced, the study does not establish safety-compliant proximity operations.
authors: Archit Das

title: Temporal signatures of prediction error reveal external forces on an embodied robot
abstract: Embodied robots must distinguish self-generated sensory consequences from externally caused perturbations. In predictive processing, such deviation is accounted for as prediction error, but it is commonly treated primarily as a signal to be minimised. Here, we test whether the temporal profile of load-related prediction error provides diagnostic information about the type of physical interaction a robot experiences. We trained and evaluated windowed multilayer perceptrons to predict servo current, used as a proxy for joint load, from proprioceptive, inertial, and servo current history. The training data were recorded during random movements of tilt and pan servo motors of a robotic head. The best model was deployed in the robot in real time and evaluated across free movements and external perturbations, including brief pushes, sustained forces, and obstacle interactions. Prediction error and raw current time series were summarised using features capturing magnitude statistics, temporal structure, and signal shape. A random forest classifier was then used to classify the conditions based on the features. Different interaction conditions produced distinct profiles that supported robust perturbation classification with high cross-validated accuracy. Classification performance for prediction error was equal to the classification of raw current. The results suggest that load-related prediction error is not only a residual of imperfect prediction. Its temporal structure can act as an embodied self-monitoring signal for classifying physical interactions.
authors: Pierre Klintefors; Birger Johansson; Christian Balkenius

title: Testicular Necrosis Following Inguinal Herniorrhaphy: A Case Report
abstract: Testicular necrosis is a rare complication associated with inguinal herniorrhaphy.The main blood supply to the testicles comes from the testicular artery (internal spermatic artery), which branches off from the abdominal aorta; the external spermatic artery, which branches off from the inferior epigastric artery; and the arteries supplying the vas deferens.The testicles are extremely resistant to necrosis.Although early surgical intervention may reverse testicular ischemia, delayed diagnosis can necessitate orchiectomy.We report a case of testicular necrosis shortly after radical inguinal herniorrhaphy requiring orchiectomy following emergency exploration.A 73-year-old man presented to our hospital 18 months after undergoing robot-assisted radical prostatectomy.He developed a left inguinal hernia following radical prostatectomy and subsequently underwent inguinal herniorrhaphy.On the fifth postoperative day, the patient presented to the hospital complaining of pain and swelling in the left testicle.Physical examination revealed swelling of the left scrotum, and scrotal ultrasonography showed no blood flow in the left testicle.Emergency scrotal exploration for suspected testicular necrosis revealed scrotal skin thickening and black discoloration of the testis and epididymis without evidence of strangulation.Owing to absent testicular blood flow on intraoperative ultrasonography, left orchiectomy was performed.Histopathological examination revealed hemorrhage and ischemic necrosis.When scrotal pain, erythema, or swelling develops after inguinal surgery, prompt evaluation with scrotal ultrasonography is warranted, and the potential need for emergency surgical exploration should be considered.
authors: Takuya Yashima; Yoshihiro Nakagami; Kazuhiko Oshinomi; Masakazu Nagata; Takashi Fukagai

title: The Lived Experience of Chinese Patients With Somatic Symptom Disorder: An Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis
abstract: Aim To deeply explore the subjective illness experience of patients with Somatic Symptom Disorder (SSD) throughout the entire course from the initial onset of symptoms and repeated medical consultations to receiving psychological interventions. Methods Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA) was adopted. Purposive sampling was used to recruit 8 patients meeting the diagnostic criteria for somatic symptom disorder in DSM-5 from the clinical psychology department of a tertiary general hospital between June 2025 and December 2025. Semi-structured in-depth interviews were conducted with these patients. After verbatim transcription of interview recordings, data analysis was carried out in accordance with the six-step coding procedure of IPA. Results Four main superordinate themes emerged from data analysis: (a) Embodied processing of distress and enduring somatic imprinting; (b) An unsafe living world co-existing with Symptoms; (c) Tracing symptom origins and the journey of help‑seeking; (d) Self‑growth within the lived experience of symptom co‑existence Conclusion The underlying driving force for patients with SSD is fear of death. These individuals frequently endure intense feelings of helplessness and insecurity, yet they consistently attribute their symptoms to physical pathology. Healthcare providers may obtain medical histories from patients with SSD to assess their emotional difficulties, family-related factors, personality traits, and illness-related beliefs. Furthermore, clinicians ought to provide feedback on physical-examination findings, refrain from redundant investigations, and validate patients’ distress through empathic responding. It is essential to reframe the meaning of symptoms: draw connections between symptoms and stress- or lifestyle-related triggers; illustrate the anxiety-to-illness transition pathway, alongside the vicious cycle that sustains somatic symptom responses.
authors: Xue Y, Chen F.

title: The Role of Laparoscopic Surgery in Abdominal Trauma: A Case Report and Review
abstract: Background: Abdominal trauma accounts for approximately 15 % of trauma admissions and remains a leading cause of preventable mortality.Traditionally managed by exploratory laparotomy of which up to 40 % are non-therapeutic the paradigm has shifted toward minimally invasive approaches.Laparoscopy now demonstrates diagnostic accuracy rates of 96-98 % and enables therapeutic repair in hemodynamically stable patients, resulting in reduced morbidity, infection rates, and length of stay.Case Presentation: A 23-year-old male sustained blunt abdominal trauma following a motorbike accident.He was hemodynamically stable with a positive FAST scan and CT evidence of hemoperitoneum and mesenteric contusion without solid-organ injury.Diagnostic laparoscopy revealed 6.3 L of hemoperitoneum and a through-and-through mesenteric tear 20 cm proximal to the ileocecal junction.Hemostasis was achieved using V-Loc 2.0 sutures with peritoneal lavage and drain placement.One unit of PRBC was transfused.Postoperatively, hemoglobin rose from 7.6 to 12.0 g/dL and CRP fell from 64 to 21 mg/L.The patient tolerated oral intake within 24 h and was discharged on day 4 without complications.Discussion/Review: Nontherapeutic laparotomies decreased by 58%, postoperative complication rates decreased by four times, and hospital stays decreased from 10.8 to 3.9 days, according to a targeted literature review (2020-2025; 24 studies).Conclusion: Laparoscopy should be a mainstay of contemporary trauma therapy since it provides therapeutic benefit and diagnostic accuracy in stable trauma patients, lowering hospitalization and morbidity.
venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: The intersection of Pediatric dentistry and Obstructive sleep apnea – An overview
abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) in children also referred as “Pediatric obstructive sleep apnea” (POSA) is the most commonly observable clinical condition, characterized by adeno-tonsillar hypertrophy and found frequently associated with obesity and craniofacial malformations. It is constituted by different pathophysiological mechanisms, clinical features, and treatment modalities. If not treated, POSA leads to significant morbidity, including neurocognitive complications, cardiovascular problems and growth impairment. Epigenetics is a novel concept and can be defined as heritable alterations in gene expression patterns that are not directly encoded by modifications in the nucleotide genome sequence but by post-translational modifications in DNA and histone proteins and by the regulation of non-coding RNA. Although the domain epigenetics is considered as an exciting arena in realm of biology, its relation with POSA is still in budding stage. Therefore, aim of the present article is to enlighten the literature pertaining to current evidence regarding the prevalence, pathophysiology, diagnostic methods, multidisciplinary management and brief note the role of epigenetics in POSA.
authors: Tuhin A Gupta; Nagaveni NB; Sumedha Kundu Chaudhary; Kanishka Gautam; Isha Goel

title: The relationship between alienation appraisals and trauma
abstract: Systematic Review Research suggests that alienation appraisals, defined as feeling disconnected from the self and others, mediate the relationship between traumatic events and subsequent PTSD symptoms. A systematic search of 6 databases found 463 studies, 9 met full inclusion criteria. Studies were quality assessed using the QATSDD. A random effects meta-analysis for the relationship between alienation appraisals and PTSD symptoms showed a total effect size of r = .57, with 95% confidence intervals between .46 and .66 (Z = 8.41, p < .001). The effect size was large, suggesting that as alienation appraisals increase, PTSD symptoms increase. Although a strong, positive relationship was found between alienation and PTSD symptoms, the mechanism of this relationship remains unclear. Limitations included significant heterogeneity and correlational data. Large-scale Cognitive models highlight the importance of negative trauma appraisals in maintaining symptoms of PTSD. The current study explored the role of alienation appraisals across student and clinical samples, assessing if alienation appraisals significantly mediated the relationship between cumulative trauma and trauma-related distress. Secondly, this study explored if alexithymia, social support and loneliness could also mediate the relationship between cumulative trauma and distress, clarifying the role of alienation. Mediation and hierarchical regression models were tested with questionnaire data from student (N = 100) and clinical samples (N = 93). In the student sample, alienation (B = 1.27) fully mediated the relationship between cumulative trauma and posttraumatic stress, but not depression. When alexithymia, social support and loneliness were entered as parallel mediators, only alienation appraisals (B = 1.03) were significant. For the clinical sample, alienation appraisals (β = .53) were the only significant predictor of posttraumatic stress symptoms whilst alienation appraisals (β = .75), and to a lesser extent, social support (β = .19) and loneliness (β = .30), significantly predicted depression. Clinical implications and limitations are discussed.
authors: Rachel McIlveen

title: Thriving at work, decent work, and motivation as pathways to employee well-being and work fulfilment: Study among healthcare workers
abstract: Healthcare workers play a critical role in sustaining the quality, accessibility, and continuity of healthcare services, yet their own well-being and work fulfilment remain important concerns. This study examined the associations between thriving at work and decent work with employee well-being and work fulfilment, and tested motivational orientations as potential explanatory mechanisms among healthcare workers in Indonesia. A cross-sectional survey was conducted with 330 healthcare workers, using validated measures of decent work, thriving at work, motivation strategy, employee well-being, and work fulfilment, analyzed through confirmatory factor analysis and mediation analysis. In Model 1, decent work was significantly and positively associated with employee well-being, while thriving at work did not demonstrate a significant direct association. Indirect associations through instrumental motivation were non-significant for both predictors. In Model 2, thriving at work was significantly and positively associated with work fulfilment, while decent work did not produce a significant direct association. Internal self-concept motivation showed a significant positive indirect association between thriving at work and work fulfilment, while external self-concept motivation showed a significant negative indirect association between decent work and work fulfilment. Instrumental motivation did not show significant indirect associations in either model. These findings suggest that employee well-being and work fulfilment are distinct outcomes shaped by different combinations of structural and psychological factors. Healthcare organizations should prioritize structural decency as the foundation for workforce well-being, while cultivating conditions that foster thriving and autonomous motivation as the pathway to work fulfilment.
authors: Endang Parahyanti; Kristiana Dewayani; Alice Salendu; Billah Ahsanul Karima; Aliyah Salsabila; Bernadete Irene

title: Total-field atomic magnetometry using an elliptically-polarized frequency-modulated light beam for geomagnetic-field applications
abstract: We investigate an all-optical scheme for high-sensitivity measurements of the Earth's scale magnetic field ($B$). The scheme is based on the Bell-Bloom technique with frequency-modulated light. A single elliptically polarized light beam is used both for pumping the alkali-metal atoms and probing Larmor precession of their spins under the external magnetic field. In contrast to many other high-sensitivity magnetometry schemes based on nonlinear polarization rotation of the light, the proposed approach enables the observation of magnetic resonance via changes in the light-beam ellipticity parameter. The approach has been validated in experiments with a vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser, irradiating a $0.125$ cm$^3$ cesium vapor cell filled with a buffer gas. In the current experimental conditions, the achieved sensitivity is estimated at $220$ fT/$\surd$Hz under $B$$\,\approx\,$$50$ $μ$T, while the shot-noise floor corresponds to $\approx\,$$20$ fT/$\surd$Hz. The bandwidth is estimated at $\approx\,$$1$ kHz. The proposed simple and robust single-beam scheme is well suited for miniaturization and is therefore particularly promising for the development of compact, highly sensitive, low-power-consumption atomic magnetometers for a wide range of applications in the geomagnetic field.

title: Towards clinical communication training with LLM-based conversational virtual patients and automatic evaluation systems
abstract: Clinical communication is a fundamental skill that impacts patient satisfaction, treatment adherence, and clinical outcomes. Traditional training methods, such as standardized patients (SPs) or virtual standardized patients (VSPs), face barriers including high costs, logistical complexity, and lack of spontaneous interaction. This study addresses these challenges by developing a scalable alternative based on Large Language Models (LLMs) to train medical students in the anamnesis phase. We developed an interactive Conversational Virtual Patient (CVP) system, understood here as a text- and voice-based simulated patient without graphical embodiment. The conversational logic is orchestrated as an explicit state machine over the interview, implemented with LangGraph, a graph-based framework in which each node performs one processing stage and a shared state persists across turns. Clinical consistency across the interview is maintained by a semantic memory layer implemented with LangMem, a library that stores clinical facts as vector embeddings and retrieves them by similarity. Performance is measured by an automatic evaluation module assessing 24 communication criteria derived from validated instruments such as the Communication Assessment Tool (CAT) and the Communication Skills Scale (CSS). The platform was validated with 21 participants, comprising 9 eighth-semester medical students, 11 practising physicians, and 1 expert in healthcare technology. All sessions were conducted in Spanish. Considering the student cohort, which addresses the educational utility of the tool, the system obtained a Chatbot Usability Questionnaire (CUQ) score of 82.3/100 and an average acceptance of the automated feedback of 4.50/5. The physician and expert cohort, which provides expert clinical validation, obtained 96.5/100 and 4.21/5 respectively, yielding a pooled usability score of 90.4/100 and a pooled feedback acceptance of 4.33/5. In an exploratory comparison against eleven physician ratings of the same interviews, rank agreement was highest for “Interest” ( $$\rho = 0.64$$ ) and lowest for “Completeness” ( $$\rho = 0.09$$ ), and the automated scores fell below the physician scores in every dimension. No dimension attained significance after correction for six comparisons, and the confidence intervals were wide, so these coefficients describe the observed sample rather than the agreement attainable in general. The results support the feasibility of the system as a complement to traditional medical training, providing immediate and standardized feedback. Given the sample size and the single-institution design, these findings should be read as an initial validation of feasibility and acceptability rather than as evidence of pedagogical efficacy.
authors: Andrea Bayona; Rubén Manrique; Christian Grévisse

title: Training the Next Generation of Future Surgical Residents: A Scoping Review and Proposal for an Undergraduate Curriculum From the Italian Polispecialistic Society of Young Surgeons
abstract: AIM: The transition from medical school to surgical residency is marked by a persistent gap between theoretical instruction and clinical readiness. In Italy, variability in training programs across centers creates persistent gaps in residents' medical education. Scientific societies are asked to identify current training gaps and define the core competencies required for effective surgical training. We propose an undergraduate curriculum to support last-year medical students in Italy. METHODS: A scoping review of the literature focusing on structured surgical curricula for undergraduate medical students was conducted. A suggested "curriculum" was introduced at the 2025 Congress of the Italian Polispecialistic Society of Young Surgeons (SPIGC) in Bari, Italy. RESULTS: The SPIGC curriculum includes seven domains: (1) soft skills: communication, informed consent, and interdisciplinary collaboration; (2) clinical and diagnostic skills: outpatient clinic management and perioperative care; (3) hygiene, prevention, healthcare systems; (4) technical skills; (5) emergency and trauma surgery; (6) perioperative management, integrating Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) protocols, nutritional assessment, and infections; (7) evidence-based medicine and recommendations. The SPIGC curriculum highlights the importance of simulation labs, hands-on workshops, and online learning, while providing clear pathways for fellowships or masters. It also introduces artificial intelligence (AI) systems as a modern learning tool, while highlighting the importance of their safe and responsible use. CONCLUSIONS: The SPIGC curriculum may provide a structured plan to improve surgical education for medical students in Italy and to align it with international standards. Its acceptability and impact on training quality and patient outcomes remain to be evaluated through future consensus and prospective studies.

title: Twelve tips on engaging effectively with emotion in Health Professions Education
abstract: Emotion is a ubiquitous component of the clinical environment that profoundly influences cognition, academic achievement, and professional identity. This Twelve Tips article highlights the importance of dismantling outdated models of emotions in health professions education and recognizing affect as a fundamental driver of clinical performance and learning. The article provides a practical guide to establishing relational trust, normalizing affective responses, cultivating emotional granularity, and developing adaptive emotion regulation skills for both learners and faculty, with consideration of the essential boundaries of the educator role and the value of shared meaning-making.
authors: Lynnea M. Mills; Jerusalem Merkebu

title: Type I Choledochal Cyst in a Three-Year-Old with Recurrent Vomiting and Pancreatitis: A Case Report
abstract: Introduction: Choledochal cysts are rare congenital dilatations of the biliary tree that may present with nonspecific gastrointestinal symptoms in children, posing diagnostic challenges. Case Report: We report a 3-year-old girl who presented with recurrent vomiting and abdominal pain. Initial laboratory testing revealed a mildly elevated lipase. An abdominal ultrasound demonstrated a pancreatic cyst; the patient was discharged with outpatient follow-up. She returned with worsening symptoms and a markedly elevated lipase of 2,247 U/L (reference range, < 160 U/L). Computed tomography subsequently revealed a type I choledochal cyst. She underwent operative resection with an uncomplicated postoperative course. Conclusion: Persistent gastrointestinal symptoms with uptrending lipase in children should prompt consideration of hepatobiliary etiologies. Choledochal cysts may be missed on initial presentation as the classic triad of jaundice, palpable abdominal mass, and right upper quadrant pain is present in a minority of cases.
authors: Dominic Diprinzio; Rance Del Mar

title: Unraveling uterine carcinosarcoma:From population data to precision oncology in the pursuit of improving prognosis
abstract: Accordingly, the primary aim of this thesis is to analyze dedicated, largescale studies focusing exclusively on UCS, with specific attention to its incidence, treatment patterns, and prognosis. Secondary aims involve evaluating diagnostic accuracy, identifying prognostic determinants, assessing QoL outcomes, and exploring molecular targets. Collectively, such research is needed to thoroughly characterize the clinical and molecular profile of UCS, determine the benefits of available treatments, and understand the impact of therapeutic interventions on patients’ quality of life To address these aims, the outline of this thesis is as follows: Chapter 2 analyzes a nationwide cohort of patients diagnosed with UCS in the Netherlands between 2001 and 2021 by using data from the Dutch Cancer Registry (IKNL) and Dutch Pathology Registry (PALGA). The study aims to describe survival across two decades and to identify clinical and histopathological factors associated with these outcomes. The long-term, population‑based dataset also enables comparison between earlier and later cohorts and assesses the impact of the transition from FIGO 2009 to FIGO 2023 staging and evolving treatment strategies on prognosis. Chapter 3 aims to analyze the diagnostic accuracy of preoperative sampling methods in diagnosing UCS. The chapter evaluates the performance of aspiration biopsy, hysteroscopic biopsy, and dilation and curettage in identifying UCS, and examines cases with discrepant preoperative and postoperative diagnoses using the nationwide data from PALGA. Chapters 4 and 5 report findings from the prospective Carcinosarcoma of the Uterus Study (CUS), a registry initiated in 2016 at Erasmus MC, a tertiary referral center in the South-West Netherlands. The study collects detailed clinical, surgical, and histopathological data, and includes longitudinal QoL assessments at baseline, posttreatment, and one, two, and five years after therapy. In Chapter 4 the effect of the UCS and treatment on QoL is assessed patients treated at Erasmus MC. It evaluates QoL with standardized questionnaires focusing on (endometrial) cancer patients. The follow up is up to five years after end of treatment. 17 Introduction Chapter 5 explores the molecular landscape of UCS, with particular attention to its biphasic architecture. Genomic analyses with Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) were performed on both the carcinoma and sarcoma components when available. Beyond confirming the heterogeneity within the TP53mutant subgroup, the study aims to identify additional molecular patterns with prognostic or therapeutic relevance. Analyses include recurrent gene alterations, tumor mutational burden, microsatellite instability (MMRD), homologous recombination deficiency, and dysregulated oncogenic pathways, with the goal of highlighting potential targets for existing or future therapies. By addressing these key points, this thesis critically evaluates current treatment strategies in terms of both survival outcomes and QoL, providing insight into their actual benefit for patients with UCS. Moreover, it highlights the significant gaps in existing research and understanding of UCS, thereby identifying priorities for future studies aimed at improving prognosis.
authors: Eveline Ngoc Bao Pham

title: Variability of Head Motion Reveals Development of Spatial Attention
abstract: Abstract Selective attention, the ability to focus on relevant information while ignoring task-irrelevant information, is crucial for learning. Selective attention has largely been studied in motionless individuals. However, body movements are intrinsic to cognition and particularly frequent in children. To test whether movements explain successful attention control throughout childhood, we tracked head rotations while younger children (6–8 years, n = 25), older children (9–10 years, n = 20) and adults (18–30 years; n = 21) identified a spatial target sound under distraction. Distractor reports decreased with age, confirming a developmental increase in attention control. Importantly, a dissociation of two distinct types of movement emerged: Task-dependent head rotation to lateral targets was similar across age groups. Contrary, task-independent movements before and early during a trial decreased with age and predicted attention accuracy. Thus, movements unrelated to the attention goal do not reflect noise but signify attentional control across development.
authors: Malte Wöstmann; Dunja Kunke; Nicole Wetzel

title: VibraGlot: Contactless Vocal Disorder Screening via mmWave Neck-Surface Vibration Sensing
abstract: Vocal disorders often begin as subtle mechanical irregularities in vocal-fold vibration before speech quality noticeably degrades. Early identification of such abnormalities is valuable because timely intervention may prevent progression to more advanced stages. However, detecting these weak early cues outside clinical settings remains challenging: microphone-based analysis observes an acoustically shaped signal that may only weakly express source-level irregularity, while contact-based vibration sensors suffer from low user compliance. We present VibraGlot, a contactless screening system that leverages millimeter-wave radar to sense neck-surface micro-vibrations during a short, non-linguistic sustained phonation (3-5 s). Rather than adopting generic end-to-end learning, VibraGlot uses a kinematics-first design. It first isolates the laryngeal region through observability-aware locking to suppress static clutter, then performs cycle-synchronous reconstruction in a canonical phase domain. Crucially, this pipeline explicitly preserves template-violating motion as structured residuals, transforming irregular mechanical behavior into diagnostic features rather than smoothing it away as noise. We evaluate VibraGlot on a clinical cohort of 74 subjects spanning five common vocal pathologies and healthy controls, collected in both hospital and home environments. Under a strict minimal-input protocol, the system achieves a macro-F1 score exceeding 0.91. These results demonstrate that radar-based neck-surface kinematics provide a robust, interpretable, and contactless pathway for scalable early vocal disorder screening, particularly when pathology is still expressed as subtle mechanical irregularity.

title: Virulence Mechanisms of Streptococcus pneumoniae During Co-Infection
abstract: Streptococcus pneumoniae (pneumococcus) represents a key clinical challenge, being a major global cause of morbidity and mortality. Typically existing as a nasopharyngeal commensal, pneumococcus undergoes significant metabolic changes during its switch to a virulent pathogen, when it can cause severe pneumoniae, bacteriemia and meningitis. This switch is poorly understood but is thought to be influenced by environmental signals arising from co-infections between pneumococcus and other bacteria as well as viruses in the nasopharynx. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the multi-stage progression of pneumococcal invasive disease, from initial colonisation to host barrier migration. We examine environmental triggers that drive the lifestyle switch from commensal to virulent, highlighting the role of other organisms in this stimulation. In particular, we focus on influenza A and respiratory syncytial virus, as well as other bacteria including Staphylococcus aureus, Moraxella catarrhalis and Haemophilus influenzae. Overall, we bring the current understanding of the field into the context of the growing antimicrobial resistance global threat, demonstrating that understanding these complex cross-species interactions is vital for developing clinical interventions against secondary pneumococcal infections.
authors: Nicholas S Briggs; Stefano Camaione; Jack Goodall; Kevin E. Bruce; Thushan de Silva; Malcolm E. Winkler; David I. Roper

title: Wearable sweat sensors for arthritis monitoring
abstract: Arthritis, including rheumatoid arthritis and gout, imposes increasing clinical and economic burdens. Current diagnostic tools such as serology, imaging, and clinical assessments are episodic, resource-intensive, and insufficient for capturing the daily dynamics of disease activity. Epidermal sweat sensing has emerged as a promising non-invasive technique for at-home physiological tracking. This review presents a comprehensive analysis and proof-of-concept for the application of wearable sweat sensors in arthritis management. The current state of detecting arthritis-related biomarkers in sweat, including specific metabolites, proteins, and markers of oxidative stress, is examined. The review surveys critical components of existing sensor architectures, ranging from substrates to transduction modalities. Methodologies for establishing sweat-blood correlations are discussed, emphasizing the physiological partitioning of biomarkers from blood to sweat. Finally, current challenges and the potential of integrated sweat-sensing systems to transform early detection are addressed.
authors: Appurva Tiwari; Ben Bin Xu; Xuehua Zhang

title: What’s New in Hand and Wrist Arthroscopy: Indications, Techniques, and Emerging Applications
abstract: Wrist arthroscopy has undergone substantial evolution over the past 2 decades, transitioning from a primarily diagnostic procedure to a versatile therapeutic platform with applications across trauma, instability, degenerative disease, and reconstructive surgery. Advances in instrumentation, visualization, and surgical technique have expanded indications while facilitating less invasive management of complex wrist pathology. In acute fracture care, arthroscopy provides direct assessment of articular reduction and associated soft tissue injuries in scaphoid and distal radius fractures, with emerging applications in distal radius malunion correction. Arthroscopic techniques for scaphoid nonunion management have demonstrated high union rates while preserving vascularity and permitting treatment of concomitant intraarticular pathology. Management of ulnar-sided wrist pain continues to expand through arthroscopic triangular fibrocartilage complex repair and reconstruction, distal radioulnar joint assessment, extensor carpi ulnaris tenoscopy, and treatment of pisotriquetral disorders. Arthroscopy also plays an increasing role in the diagnosis and treatment of Kienböck disease, offering minimally invasive options ranging from core decompression and debridement to arthroscopic assisted intercarpal fusion procedures. In the setting of carpal instability, advances in arthroscopic capsulodesis, ligament reconstruction, and treatment algorithms for scapholunate and dorsal intercarpal ligament injuries have broadened therapeutic possibilities. Arthroscopic and arthroscopic assisted procedures for wrist arthritis, including partial wrist arthrodesis, continue to gain acceptance, whereas small joint arthroscopy has expanded indications for fracture management and treatment of select degenerative and inflammatory conditions. Emerging technologies, including dry arthroscopy, needle arthroscopy, augmented reality navigation, robotics, and artificial intelligence-assisted image recognition may further enhance precision and accessibility. This review summarizes contemporary evidence, evolving indications, technical innovations, and future directions in wrist arthroscopy, highlighting its growing role as a central component of modern hand and wrist surgery.
authors: Parker Johnsen; A. Bobby Chhabra; Brent R. DeGeorge

title: Whole-Blood Boundary Analysis of BioFET-Based ctDNA Detection for Intravascular Sensing in Intrabody Nanonetworks
abstract: Liquid biopsy can detect tumor-derived biomarkers such as circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), but ultra-low-fraction assays remain costly, slow, and difficult to scale. This motivates interest in intravascular in vivo sensing in the context of intrabody nanonetworks, where nanosensors could support local biomarker monitoring. BioFET-based nanosensors are relevant here because they are label-free, highly miniaturizable, and have shown strong ctDNA sensitivity in controlled media. We examine whether this sensitivity still yields reliable ctDNA detection in whole blood using a reduced-order stochastic simulation model that links operating-point selection, Debye-screened charge transduction, stochastic finite-capacity binding, nonspecific adsorption, background fluctuations, and intrinsic electronic noise to blank-threshold detection. Monte Carlo evaluation under the stated physiological screening and lumped interface assumptions shows that short Debye length and interface attenuation reduce the current shift, while low-frequency noise and background fluctuations reduce the margin between target-present and blank responses. Across the tested quasi-static charge-gating regimes, sensitivity ranges from low values under short Debye length and thicker interfaces to near 100% for higher target concentrations under stronger coupling conditions. Specificity ranges from approximately 85% to 91% across the evaluated oxide thicknesses. The model therefore provides an exploratory whole-blood boundary analysis that identifies how screening, interface geometry, target concentration, and electronic noise shape BioFET-based intravascular ctDNA detection.

title: Whose business is autism? Exploring the intersecting roles of developmental paediatrics and child and adolescent mental health services
abstract: This opinion article looks at how autism services for children and young people are organised within child development and child and adolescent mental health services. Although both play vital roles, their responsibilities often overlap, which can lead to delays and uncertainty for families. Rising demand, limited resources and differing pathways have added further pressure, especially since the COVID-19 pandemic. The article highlights key challenges, including age cut-offs, gaps in continuity, the need for a collaborative integrated model, the impact of stigma and the difficulties faced by children whose main needs relate to developmental delay. It argues for clearer pathways and more coordinated care.
authors: Yasser Saeed Khan; Mohamed Adil Shah Khoodoruth; Nazim Abdel Aati

title: Wireless Brain‐Computer Interface With MagnetoElectric NanoParticles: Recording of Neural Activity
abstract: ABSTRACT Non‐invasive recording of neural activity from deep brain regions with high spatial and temporal resolution remains an unsolved challenge. Here we investigate the feasibility of exploiting the converse magnetoelectric effect of magnetoelectric nanoparticles (MENPs) to enable wireless non‐invasive recording of electric fields due to local neural activity deep in the brain. To validate the proposed mechanism, we developed a physics‐based simulation of MENP‐assisted neural recordings. The model incorporates nonlinear magnetization dynamics, multistage filtering, and realistic noise sources to stimulate MENPs‐assisted neural recording. The results demonstrate extractable neural activity with positive signal‐to‐noise ratios (SNRs), confirming the theoretical feasibility of wireless MENP‐based brain recording, with a simulated peak‐based SNR of 24.4 dB. These findings validate the physics of the approach. Importantly, the mechanism favors membrane‐local electric fields, suggesting sensitivity to highly localized neuronal activity, while the detectable bandwidth overlaps with canonical neural oscillations. The system further enables dynamic control of nanoparticle behavior through frequency‐dependent switching of the superparamagnetic state, allowing separation between stable delivery and active sensing. Together, these results establish a physically grounded pathway toward non‐invasive, real‐time mapping of neural activity in deep brain regions.

title: 24-Hour Radar-Based Activity Monitoring Dataset for a Simulated Nursing Home Environment
abstract: This dataset contains multi-session radar recordings collected during two pilot studies in which each participant simulated a patient, a nurse, or visitors with the aim of replicating a real nursing home environment. The experiments took place in a Living Lab environment at the Health Lab of VSB – Technical University of Ostrava (more information about the laboratory is available at https://healthlab.vsb.cz/en/). The data collection aimed to study whether a privacy-preserving, contactless mmWave radar sensor can recognize daily-care activities (sleeping, relaxing, eating, caregiver visits, etc.) of an older adult over long, realistic time periods, 24 hours, without cameras or wearable devices. In addition to radar, the dataset includes environmental air-quality/context information used for room-dynamics analysis: CO₂ concentration, temperature, relative humidity, and door opening information. Sensor and data format. Radar data are acquired using InvisiAngel (https://invisiangel.vsb.cz/en/), a 60 GHz radar device, for privacy preserving monitoring of movement, activity and falls. The device is based on Texas Instruments (TI) IWR6843 60 GHz FMCW mmWave sensor (IWR6843ISK-ODS/AOP module). The device is mounted on the ceiling at approximately 2.8–3 m and runs TI's “Overhead 3D People Tracking” demo firmware. Instead of storing raw radar signals, the sensor performs on-board detection and tracking and provides two processed outputs: TLV type 1020: a 3D point cloud of detections in spherical coordinates (elevation, azimuth, Doppler velocity, range, SNR); TLV types 1010/1021: a list of tracked people with 3D position, velocity, acceleration, tracking-error covariance and a binary presence indicator. Environmental data are collected with wireless CO₂ monitoring based on the IQRF indoor air-quality system documented by Velička, Pies and Hájovský (2018), with data collected every 5 minutes. In this dataset, the exported environmental streams include CO₂ concentration, relative humidity, and temperature. The exported CSV file is structured in the following way: Timestamp (Time) CO₂ values (ppm) Temperature (°C) Humidity (RH). Door opening and closing are recorded using a Tuya Wi-Fi/Zigbee magnetic contact sensor. For both pilots, the door-contact stream was processed into a three-column event table (Date, Time, Door Status), with the Open/Closed states already harmonized from the raw Boolean values. No magnetic sensor was installed on the window in either pilot: window opening and closing were instead inferred from the time-stamped "Room ventilation" and "Window closed" events recorded in the activity log. Ground truth. Each recording session is paired with an activity log (CSV/XLSX file) automatically generated by a custom Python application we developed. The log file is organized as: Date Start and end time Type of activity performed Number of people present in the room Who performed it (patient, nurse, visitor) The application also allows users to write notes and, for example, to annotate changes in the activity. It was used to log activities in real time during each session, allowing radar timestamps to be precisely aligned with the corresponding activity and occupancy. The activities performed are: Patient relaxing: the patient is on the bed relaxing or doing light activity Patient sleeping: the patient is sleeping on the bed Patient hygiene: the nurse is assisting the patient with personal hygiene Meal service: the nurse is serving the meal to the patient Eating: the patient is eating his meal while sitting on the bed or sometimes at the table. The nurse stays there to assist the patient Meal collection: the dishes are collected Patient checks: the nurse checks the patient to see if he needs something, trying to measure vital signs or simply assess his health status Nurse cleaning: the nurse is cleaning the room or making the bed Visiting hours: relatives or friends of the patient come to visit Patient out of the room: the patient is not in the room Room ventilation: the nurse is opening the window Window closed: the nurse is closing the window. Known data-quality note. A small number of rows in radar_data_1021_1010_Pilot1.xlsx contain a corrupted posY value (a logging artifact), which should be filtered or clipped by downstream users. title: 55th Child Neurology Society Annual Meeting
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Pediatric concussion care is rapidly evolving, leading to significant shifts in clinical recommendations.We updated clinical recommendations, tools, and algorithms within the Living Guideline for Pediatric Concussion using peer-reviewed evidence, while integrating patient engagement and expanding scope to priority populations and emerging areas.METHODS: 4041 papers published through 2025 were critically assessed, aligned with current clinical recommendations, and coded with EppiReviewer.An interactive living evidence gap map generated using EPPI-vis was shared with 45 expert panel members and consensus voting informed updates.This was repeated every six months and includes ongoing input from individuals with lived experience.RESULTS: Recommendation updates include aerobic exercise to treat concussion, guidance on screen time, return to school, mental health, and early interventions to facilitate recovery and reduce the risk of persisting symptoms after concussion.The strength of evidence varies, with more high quality (level 1-2) studies supporting initial medical management (131) and prolonged symptoms (57), while telemedicine (3) and interpersonal violence (0) remain limited, reflecting emerging areas of research.The Living Guideline Evidence Map includes 1511 publicly accessible records published from 2013 -2025.Guideline recommendations, tools, evidence maps, and details of the consensus process are freely shared on pedsconcussion.com,with over 989,000 total engagements.CONCLUSIONS: Evaluation and synthesis of evidence coupled with commitment and collaboration from leaders in the field is essential for developing and sustaining evidencebased clinical guidelines.The creation and regular updating of the Living Guideline for Pediatric Concussion provide a mechanism for continually advancing pediatric postconcussion knowledge and care.

title: A Conceptual Framework for Intelligent IoT and AI-Driven Neurocognitive Healthcare Assistive Systems
abstract: Intelligent Internet of Things (IoT) and assistive technologies are revolutionizing neurocognitive healthcare, with the ability to continuously monitor, use early diagnostics, assess disease progression and deliver personalized interventions. In this chapter, a conceptual framework concerning the integration of wearable sensing technologies, ambient intelligence, edge–cloud computing, multimodal artificial intelligence, explainable deep learning, and assistive technologies for rehabilitation to support proactive personalized care is introduced. The framework covers the neurocognitive disorders such as Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, dementia, autism spectrum disorders, attention-related disorders and post-stroke cognitive rehabilitation. Future directions for precision neurocognitive healthcare are presented for emerging technologies including federated learning, digital twins and brain–computer interfaces. The chapter serves as a handy guide for researchers, clinicians, and health care technology developers.
authors: Berlin Magthalin R; Mizpah Queeny R

title: A Curved Bimodal Hair Sensor for Airflow and Electrostatic Perception in Robotic Control
abstract: ABSTRACT Noncontact environmental perception is crucial for autonomous alerting and behavior control in mobile robots, yet existing artificial sensory systems still fall short in integrating weak‐stimulus detection, interaction‐direction discrimination, and multimodal sensing within a single device. Drawing inspiration from the electroreceptive hair‐like sensilla of treehoppers and the high‐curvature proboscis of butterflies, we report a Curved Bimodal Hair Sensor (CBHS) that achieves dual‐mode noncontact perception of electrostatic and airflow stimuli. The high‐curvature hair architecture enhances mechanical coupling, and a sliding‐rheostat‐based length‐encoded resistance mechanism enables stable detection of compressive and tensile loads down to 10 −4 N. Electrostatic and airflow stimuli are inherently discriminated by their contrasting time scales and signal profiles. Under airflow, hair oscillation induces interfacial contact electrification, dynamically modulating the electrical state to enable wind‐speed detection as low as 0.9 m·s −1 , with a random forest model classifying six speed levels at 98.89% accuracy. When integrated into a robotic platform, CBHS directly maps electrostatic polarity to approach and escape behaviors, while a four‐sensor array enables airflow‐direction‐guided vigilance and closed‐loop directional motion. This work presents a structure‐driven bioinspired strategy for low‐complexity multimodal artificial sensory systems directly coupled to robotic behavior.

title: A Knowledge Management System for University Public Music Education Based on Ambient Intelligence and Data Steganography
abstract: Digital transformation brings new challenges to cultural knowledge management in higher music education. This paper develops an integrated system combining ambient computing and steganography technology to manage explicit and implicit music knowledge. The system protects knowledge assets, tracks resource sources, and facilitates the fusion of different types of music culture. Comparative experiments prove its reliability and practicality. The findings expand the application of intelligent technologies in educational knowledge management and contribute to the digital inheritance and innovative development of traditional music culture.
authors: ShiChu Qin

title: A Lag-1 Autocorrelation Statistic for Early Warning of Illness and Heat Stress in Older Adults From Everyday Wearables, With a Graded Shunt
abstract: Older people often become seriously ill quietly. An infection may build for two or three days before anyone notices that something is wrong, and by then it may already need a hospital. In a heatwave, an older person may not feel thirsty or hot until it is dangerous. Many older people already wear a smartwatch or a fitness band that measures the heart rate and movement every minute. This paper describes an early warning that works on those readings. The body is always making small corrections to the heart rate; in a healthy body, each small wobble settles back quickly. When illness or heat stress begins, the wobbles settle back more slowly. We measure this slowing with one simple number, and when it rises, the person, their family, or a care-home nurse is alerted in three steps, through the link the wearable already has. It is the same general method as in our companion paper on animals; only a small table of numbers, the "profile", changes. In a computer simulation of 30 people of each kind in each situation, for an infection, compared with the moment the person looked ill: our method gave its first notice about 14 to 15 hours before; today's wearables, which watch the day's activity, alerted about 30 hours after. For frail older people, today's high heart-rate alarm never fired at all. In a heatwave, compared with the moment heatstroke signs appeared: our method's first notice came 88 to 103 minutes before, and even earlier with the heat watch rule on forecast-hot days; today's high heart-rate alarm came 41 to 63 minutes before. Healthy people rarely received a false alarm. All results come from simulated data; testing on real wearable data is the necessary next step.
