title: Advancing Occupational Safety with AI-Powered Monitoring Systems: A Conceptual Framework for Hazard Detection and Exposure Control
abstract: Occupational safety remains a critical concern across industries, necessitating innovative solutions to mitigate hazards and control worker exposure to harmful environments. This paper presents a conceptual framework for leveraging Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered monitoring systems to enhance occupational safety. The framework integrates advanced data analytics, machine learning algorithms, and Internet of Things (IoT) devices to enable realtime hazard detection and exposure control. By utilizing AI's predictive capabilities, the system identifies potential risks and triggers preemptive measures to prevent accidents and long-term health impacts. Key components of the framework include wearable IoT sensors for monitoring workers' vital signs and environmental parameters, AI-driven analysis to process large datasets, and adaptive feedback mechanisms to inform decision-making. The system also incorporates computer vision for identifying physical hazards and proximity detection for alerting workers in high-risk zones. These technologies collectively facilitate a proactive approach to workplace safety, shifting the paradigm from reactive to preventive measures. The framework emphasizes scalability and flexibility, making it adaptable to various industrial sectors, including construction, manufacturing, and healthcare. The integration of AI-powered systems aligns with Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) regulations and supports compliance with safety standards. Furthermore, the proposed framework addresses challenges such as false positives, data privacy concerns, and user adoption through robust algorithm design, secure data management practices, and user-centric interfaces. Preliminary simulations demonstrate the system's potential to significantly reduce workplace injuries and improve hazard response times. Case studies from the construction and oil and gas industries underscore the value of real-time hazard monitoring in high-risk environments. The paper concludes by highlighting future research directions, including advancements in AI algorithms, enhanced sensor technologies, and cross-industry implementation strategies. This conceptual framework positions AI-powered monitoring systems as a transformative solution for advancing occupational safety, offering a pathway to safer, more resilient workplaces through data-driven innovation.
authors: Cynthia Obianuju Ozobu
venue: WORLD JOURNAL OF INNOVATION AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY

title: Aerial Magnetic Anomaly Target Detection Method Based on Multi-Scale Orthonormal Basis Function Convolution and Convolution-Augmented Gated Attention
abstract: Magnetic anomaly detection from aerial platforms enables passive, non-contact detection of underwater ferromagnetic targets. To address the issues of traditional Orthonormal Basis Function (OBF) detection relying on prior knowledge of the closest contact distance and susceptibility to mismatch with single-scale templates, this paper proposes an aerial magnetic anomaly target detection method that integrates multi-scale OBF with a convolution-augmented gated attention unit (CGAU). Six sets of fixed OBF convolution kernels each output three matching responses, which are concatenated with the original sequence to form 19-channel features. Four layers of one-dimensional (1-D) convolution and two stages of CGAU extract local waveform features and capture long-range dependencies. The precision (PC), detection rate (DR), and F1-score of the proposed network on the simulated test set are 94.70%, 95.11%, and 94.90%, respectively (best-performing seed = 42). On the measured dataset, it detected 11 of 12 overpass events, achieving an event detection rate of 91.67%. The proposed network has approximately 0.43 M trainable parameters and achieves a higher mean F1 across three random seeds than the seven selected baselines, demonstrating its potential for aerial magnetic anomaly target detection.
authors: Haozhe Chen; Ke Zhang; Wanhua Zhu

title: Air-Coupled Acoustic Emission Detection Using a Multifrequency MEMS Sensor
abstract: Acoustic emission (AE) monitoring is widely used for structural health monitoring (SHM) and nondestructive evaluation (NDE), yet most conventional sensors require direct mechanical contact with the monitored structure. Air-coupled sensing offers a non-contact alternative, but only a small fraction of elastic wave energy radiates from solids into air due to severe acoustic impedance mismatch, producing extremely weak airborne signals. This work presents an experimental demonstration of air-coupled acoustic emission detection using a compact multifrequency microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) sensor. The sensor consists of an array of sixteen diaphragm-type resonators with resonance frequencies distributed between 100 kHz and 700 kHz and microfabricated using the PiezoMUMPs process. Airborne acoustic signals generated by pencil lead break excitation on an aluminum plate were recorded with the MEMS sensor positioned in air without mechanical contact. The sensor successfully detected leaky acoustic emission signals, exhibiting clear transient responses and distinct spectral peaks aligned with its designed resonance frequencies while also capturing low-frequency components. The results demonstrate that multifrequency MEMS sensors provide sufficient sensitivity and frequency-selective response for detecting weak airborne AE signals, highlighting their potential for compact and scalable non-contact acoustic emission monitoring in structural health monitoring applications.
authors: Talha Masood Khan; Didem Ozevin

title: Ambient intelligence platforms and new frontiers in surgical safety.
abstract: The operating room is a high-risk, high-entropy environment, prone to human error and preventable adverse events. Drawing on lessons from high-reliability organizations such as the aviation industry, Aimbient (formerly Operating Room Black Box by Surgical Safety Technologies, New York, NY) collects continuous, multimodal audiovisual and physiologic data capture to deepen our understanding of surgical safety. This platform has demonstrated improvements in patient safety domains across several metrics, including ground-truth benchmarking of checklist adherence, video-based multidisciplinary review conferences, and automated physiologic event tagging. Recent integration of key postoperative morbidity and mortality metrics into the data streams collected by Aimbient monitoring platforms allows for us to achieve a holistic understanding of the perioperative record. As artificial intelligence capabilities rapidly expand and begin to integrate into our health care systems, ambient data capture is uniquely poised to generate real-time insights and open new frontiers in surgical patient safety.
authors: Chloe K Nobuhara; Mary T Hawn; Teodor P Grantcharov

title: Ambient intelligence-based framework for quantitative evaluation of cell culture operations to support standardization and training
abstract: Introduction: The widespread implementation of cell therapy has increased the demand for stable and reproducible cell manufacturing methods. However, many cell manufacturing processes rely heavily on manual cell culture operations, and operator training remains largely dependent on subjective assessment and tacit knowledge. This limits the establishment of training targets and hinders operational standardization. Recent advances in ambient intelligence have created new opportunities for digitizing human work processes and supporting their quantitative evaluation. In this study, we developed an ambient intelligence-based framework for digitizing, visualizing, and quantitatively comparing manual cell culture operations. Methods: A defined mock seeding operation was performed by one expert with 10 years of cell culture experience and three trainees with approximately two years of experience. Videos of the operation were recorded inside a biosafety cabinet, and the dominant-hand motion was extracted using an artificial intelligence (AI)-based skeleton estimation. The resulting time-series data were converted into quantitative speed-based temporal profiles for each operation, termed Operation Profiles. To compare operations with different execution times, the similarity between each Operation Profile and the target Operation Profile derived from the expert was evaluated using fast derivative dynamic time warping (fastDDTW). Distance and gap index were used as complementary metrics to assess the waveform deviation and temporal misalignment, respectively. Results: Skeleton estimation AI, combined with visual quality control, interpolation, and manual correction, extracted the dominant-hand motion from the operation videos and enabled the construction of interpretable Operation Profiles that reflect the internal temporal structure of the defined cell culture operation. Although all operators performed the same operation, their Operation Profiles differed, indicating operator-dependent variations in the operation patterns. Iterative feedback based on phase-specific differences from the target expert operation was associated with progressive improvement in the trainees' similarity to the target Operation Profile. Conclusions: This study established a framework for recording, digitizing, and quantitatively evaluating cell culture operations using ambient intelligence. These findings demonstrate that the alignment of cell culture operations toward a target expert operation can be quantitatively evaluated through an Operation Profile analysis. By enabling objective comparison of operator behavior and quantitative evaluation of alignment toward a facility-defined target operation, this approach may provide a basis for operational standardization and training support in cell manufacturing.
authors: Kengo Momose; Takeru Shiina; Yuto Takemoto; Mai Okada; Kakeru Koide; Tomohiro Yokoi; Ayako Sugimoto; Kei Kanie; Kenjiro Tanaka; Ryuji Kato

title: An Enhancing Lung Disease Detection with Scalable UNet-Mamba Segmentation
abstract: Lung diseases are conditions that damage the lung tissues, airways or blood vessels of the lungs, causing breathing difficulties and decreased oxygen supply to the body. Computed Tomography (CT) plays a crucial role in lung disease prediction because it provides detailed cross-sectional images for detecting tumors at initial stages. However, CT scans have drawbacks such as radiation exposure, high cost, large data size, and the possibility of false positives. Recently, many Deep Learning (DL) techniques have been used to automatically analyze CT images for early and accurate detection of lung diseases, improving diagnostic efficiency. However, existing models may struggle to capture fine spatial details, leading to inaccurate boundary delineation and poor segmentation of small or low-contrast regions. Some models are also sensitive to imaging artifacts, which can reduce performance in real-world conditions. In this paper, a lung disease prediction model is developed using ResNet and Mamba Network (LRMNet) to solve the aforementioned issues for lung disease prediction. The first step is improving the model's ability to conduct pre-processing and enrich the data using a Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Network (DCGAN). Then, the Scalable Vision UNet-Mamba (SVU-M) model is developed to efficiently capture fine spatial details along with long-range contextual information. SVU-M leverages Scalable Vision State Space (SVSS) blocks to efficiently model the global dependencies while maintaining linear computational complexity. The integration of SVSS within a U-shaped framework enhances the boundary delineation and improves segmentation of small or low-contrast regions, which increases the efficiency against imaging artifacts for more reliable performance. The decoder feature maps of SVU-M are further processed using Global Average Pooling (GAP) to determine image-level feature representations for classification. Simultaneously, the input image is directly fed into ResNet-50 for capturing the whole image's semantic features. A Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) classifier is trained with the extracted features to forecast lung diseases. A total accuracy of 94.15% on the customized dataset and 93.29% on the SARS-CoV-2 CT dataset was achieved by the suggested model, according to the experimental results, exceeding the performance of other models.
authors: Sivasakthi S; Radha V
venue: International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology

title: An Indoor Object Detection and Navigation System
abstract: “Indoor Object Detection for Blind” is a dedicated assistive technology project designed to enhance indoor navigation for visually impaired individuals. Utilizing advanced computer vision techniques, the system detects and identifies objects in real-time using wearable devices like smart glasses or smartphones. It integrates YOLO-based deep learning models, fine-tuned with a custom indoor dataset, to ensure high accuracy in recognizing objects such as furniture, doors, and appliances. Additionally, natural language processing (NLP) enables context-aware descriptions, providing adaptive feedback. The project is designed to be flexible and seamlessly integrate with wearable technology, ensuring a smooth and efficient user experience. The system evaluates various aspects of objects, including their spatial positioning and contextual information, to assist users in real-time. By concentrating solely on object detection within indoor environments, this system significantly improves spatial awareness and navigation for visually impaired individuals. Extensive testing demonstrates the system's performance in detecting and identifying objects while minimizing false positives.
authors: Kukkadapu Natarajan
venue: Journal of Research in Science Computing and Engineering

title: An Integrated Visual–Textual Approach for Accurate Phishing Detection on Social Media Platforms
abstract: The rapid rise of phishing attacks on social media platforms highlights an urgent and growing cybersecurity challenge in today’s digitally connected world. As millions of users rely on these platforms for communication, business, and information sharing, cybercriminals increasingly exploit them to distribute deceptive links, fake advertisements, and fraudulent messages designed to steal sensitive data such as login credentials, financial information, and personal identities. The sophistication of these attacks—often leveraging social engineering techniques, impersonation of trusted entities, and AI-generated content—makes them difficult for users to recognize and avoid. Consequently, there is a critical need for robust and intelligent detection systems capable of reliably identifying malicious content in real time. Such systems should incorporate advanced machine learning models, behavioral analysis, and continuous adaptation to emerging attack patterns in order to effectively mitigate risks, protect users, and maintain trust in social media ecosystems. This paper proposes a multimodal phishing detection framework that integrates visual indicators (e.g., logos and page imagery) with textual signals (e.g., URL structure and phishing-related keywords). Our contributions are threefold: (i) a feature fusion strategy that combines visual and textual cues, (ii) the construction of a comprehensive dataset using feature extraction and natural language processing (NLP), and (iii) a comparative evaluation of multiple machine learning models. We extract 27 discriminative URL features and evaluate Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and Naı̈ve Bayes. Random Forest achieves the best performance, reaching 98.6% accuracy with a false positive rate of 0.01, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed multimodal approach for phishing detection on social media.
authors: Ala’ S Mughaid; Andaleep Shdeifat; Abedalmuhdi Almomany; Mohammad Kharabsheh; Shadi Mahmoud Faleh AlZu’bi

title: Antecedents of Adoption Intention for AI-Driven Wearable Technology in Malaysian Healthcare
abstract: This study reports the pilot phase of a larger doctoral investigation into the adoption of AI-driven wearable technology in Malaysian healthcare. Guided by an integration of Diffusion of Innovations theory and the Technology Acceptance Model, the pilot tested seven direct effect hypotheses linking compatibility, relative advantage, trialability, complexity, observability, perceived ease of use, and perceived usefulness to adoption intention. Data were collected from healthcare sector respondents at a professional conference in Kuala Lumpur in August 2026 (N = 93, after removing two duplicates from 95 raw responses). Partial least squares structural equation modeling was used for its suitability to prediction oriented research. The structural model explained 60.0 percent of the variance in adoption intention. Perceived usefulness (beta = 0.261), perceived ease of use (beta = 0.201), observability (beta = 0.174), compatibility (beta = 0.162), and complexity (beta = -0.152) significantly predicted adoption intention (all p < .05); relative advantage and trialability did not. Composite reliability exceeded 0.78 for all nine constructs, and heterotrait monotrait ratios for all 36 construct pairs fell below the conservative 0.85 threshold as point estimates, but bootstrap confidence intervals crossed 0.85 for six of the eight adoption intention pairs, so discriminant validity for that construct remains provisional. Perceived regulatory support was retained for reliability assessment but not tested as a moderator here, a test reserved for the full study. Findings offer preliminary support for the framework and considerations for the full scale study.
authors: Syeda Hafsa Rizwan; Anusuyah Subbarao; Shereen Khan
venue: The Journal of Applied Technology and Innovation

title: Application and prospects of veterinary diagnostic techniques in laboratory monkeys
abstract: -threaten animal welfare and colony security, while also elevating zoonotic transmission risks and compromising the reliability of research data. The diversity, complexity, and clinically insidious nature of diseases in laboratory monkeys impose stringent demands on veterinary diagnostic capabilities. This review summarizes the current status and recent advances in mainstream veterinary diagnostic techniques applied to laboratory monkey disease surveillance. We analyze the specific applications, strengths, and limitations of molecular, immunological, imaging, and conventional microbiological methods for detecting major viral, bacterial, and parasitic pathogens of laboratory monkeys, covering quantitative PCR (qPCR), CRISPR-based assays, ELISA, IFA/IHC, and other established platforms. By comparing these techniques across sensitivity, specificity, cost-effectiveness, and operational feasibility, we delineate their suitability for distinct use cases: high-precision laboratory testing, large-scale colony screening, and point-of-care clinical diagnosis. Current veterinary diagnostic assays for laboratory monkeys achieve robust analytical performance. In several studies, qPCR delivers 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity for B virus detection, digital PCR (dPCR) attains a limit of detection as low as 45 copies/ml for monkeypox virus; and CRISPR/Cas-based assays have demonstrated 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity in clinical validation cohorts. Building on these advances, we further identify practical bottlenecks in diagnostic deployment and propose targeted countermeasures. Finally, we explore emerging trends and application prospects for point-of-care testing, multiplex pathogen detection, and artificial intelligence-assisted diagnosis, which collectively support the development of accurate, efficient, and intelligent disease diagnostics for laboratory monkeys. This work aims to provide a theoretical and practical reference for clinical practice and scientific research focused on laboratory monkey disease prevention and control.
authors: Zhengjia Zhang; Diangang Han; Qiujiang Wei; Xuewei Fu; Yongqing Yan; Dandan Li; JIGE XIN

title: Applying artificial intelligence to the hypertension care cascade: Opportunities and challenges
abstract: In the United States, hypertension control curves have plateaued below what is achievable and acceptable. The persistence of suboptimal disease control—despite a robust clinical armamentarium—suggests failure points between guideline-directed and real-world care. This manuscript examines the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) to address the public health challenges undermining hypertension control. Using the hypertension care cascade (which comprises diagnosis, awareness, treatment, and control) as a guiding framework, we synthesize current evidence and identify promising applications of AI-enabled tools and technologies at each stage of the cascade. AI, indeed, offers a plausible pathway for addressing some of the most pernicious forces undermining sustained, scalable hypertension control; however, it is not without risks and limitations. Its deployment must, therefore, be paired with a comprehensive governance structure that safeguards patients and prioritizes safety, equity, and accountability. With these safeguards in place, AI holds promise for bridging hypertension's operational gaps and improving population health.
authors: Matthew E. Berman; Mateen H. Abbasi; Roman Pati; Thomas Wyskowski; Divij Satapathy; Jay Tamirisa; Faraan O. Rahim; Jared W. Magnani
venue: American Heart Journal Plus Cardiology Research and Practice

title: Artificial Intelligence in Sports Analytics for Performance Enhancement and Injury Prevention: A Study of Perceptions and Adoption
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) are becoming increasingly relevant to sports analytics, where data-driven techniques are being considered for athlete performance assessment, training management, recovery monitoring, and injury-risk estimation. The growing use of wearable technologies, tracking systems, video-based analysis, physiological measurements, and training data has increased the amount of information available to support sporting decisions. However, the practical adoption of AI is influenced not only by its analytical capabilities but also by how users perceive its usefulness, reliability, transparency, privacy implications, and appropriate level of human involvement. This study examines perceptions and factors associated with the acceptance of AI in sports analytics, focusing specifically on performance enhancement and injury prevention. A quantitative cross-sectional survey involving 50 participants was conducted to assess awareness of AI in sports, perceived usefulness of AI-assisted performance analysis, responses to AI-generated injury-risk warnings, trust, explainability, privacy concerns, and preferences for human oversight. Descriptive analysis showed an overall favourable attitude toward AI applications in sports. Recovery and fatigue monitoring and improvement in physical performance were among the benefits most frequently identified by participants. A substantial proportion of respondents were also willing to give serious consideration to AI-generated injury-risk warnings, although human judgement remained an important part of the decision process. Concerns related to privacy, data quality, prediction errors, and potential bias were identified as factors that could weaken trust in AI systems. Overall, the findings suggest that participants are more supportive of AI when it functions alongside human expertise rather than replacing human decision-makers. The study consequently highlights a human-centred approach to AI adoption in sports analytics, emphasising explainability, dependable data, privacy safeguards, professional involvement, and appropriate human oversight.
authors: Maitrayee Mahesh Gawde
venue: International Journal for Research Trends and Innovation

title: Artificial Intelligence in Supporting Early Intervention for Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder: Opportunities and Challenges
abstract: Early identification and intervention are central to improving developmental trajectories for children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), yet access to specialist assessment and therapy remains uneven. Artificial intelligence (AI) has been proposed as a way to extend the reach and precision of early support. This article reviews the opportunities and challenges of AI in early intervention for children with ASD, using a conceptual-analytical narrative review. It synthesizes peer-reviewed studies and authoritative guidance across three stages of the care pathway: screening, diagnostic decision support, and intervention delivery, and examines the limitations that accompany each. The findings indicate that machine learning applied to parent reports, home videos, eye-gaze and attention measures, and neuroimaging shows promising accuracy for early detection; that social robots and wearable aids can elicit social behavior in structured settings; and that these gains are constrained by small and unrepresentative samples, limited external validation, algorithmic bias, opacity, privacy risks, and uncertain transfer to everyday life. The discussion argues that AI is best positioned as an augmentation of, and not a substitute for, clinical judgment and family-centered care, and it outlines implications for practitioners and research priorities, including validation in culturally and linguistically diverse populations.
authors: Dr. Bourkache Sabiha

title: Artificial Intelligence in Wearable ECG and PPG Devices for Arrhythmia Detection: A Narrative Review
abstract: Cardiovascular disease is the world’s top cause of death. Short recording times and a dependence on clinical settings are two practical drawbacks of traditional methods like Holter monitoring and standard 12-lead ECG. Two significant trends have come together in recent years: the broad availability of consumer-grade wearable technology, including smartwatches and adhesive ambulatory ECG patches, and the quick advancement of deep learning and artificial intelligence. Four main themes currently dominate research in this field: diagnostic accuracy under controlled conditions, algorithmic innovation for real-time and on-device analysis, real-world implementation and performance in large prospective studies, and the persistent technical, clinical, and regulatory challenges that limit widespread deployment.AI-based systems have shown consistently high performance in controlled environments and curated datasets, with reported sensitivities and specificities commonly ranging between 92% and 99%.However, performance, especially specificity and generalizability, frequently declines significantly if these algorithms are exposed to the messiness of daily movement, a variety of patient demographics, fluctuating skin contact, and hardware limitations outside of the lab. More advanced transformer architectures and multimodal techniques that combine ECG signals with photoplethysmography (PPG) waveforms, as well as lightweight convolutional neural networks that can operate directly on the device itself and provide true real-time detection, have been the focus of recent algorithmic work. The present status of wearable ECG and PPG technology for AI-enabled arrhythmia detection is examined in this review. It critically evaluates diagnostic performance, translational gaps that still exist and paying attention to the prospective studies that have shaped the field. All things considered, the data indicates that wearables driven by AI have real potential for screening for arrhythmias at the population level and have already shown promising signs of clinical utility. The field will require larger, longer, and more diversified prospective trials that are sufficiently powered to identify significant differences in hard clinical outcomes.
authors: Farid Taghavi; Shirin Alord; Alireza Ghaffari; Somayyeh Mehanfar; Kamran Mohammadi

title: Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning–Enabled Precision Nutrition Modestly Improves Anthropometric Outcomes and Systolic Blood Pressure: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
abstract: Precision nutrition tailors dietary guidance to individual biological, genetic, metabolic, and behavioral characteristics. Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), wearables, sensors, mobile apps, and multi-omics tools increasingly support this approach, but evidence on their effectiveness, feasibility, implementation, and equity remains fragmented. This review evaluated the effectiveness of AI/ML-enabled analytical approaches and technologies in precision nutrition across dietary, metabolic, behavioral, implementation, and equity outcomes. We conducted a PRISMA-guided systematic review and meta-analysis of studies published from January 2015 to December 2025 across six databases. Eligible studies examined AI/ML, digital tools, wearables, mobile platforms, or multi-omics approaches for personalized nutrition across the lifespan. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed bias. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted where outcomes were comparable; remaining studies underwent qualitative and thematic synthesis. Overall, 262 studies met the inclusion criteria. Meta-analyses indicated modest pooled reductions in body weight (−1.97 kg), BMI (−0.57 kg/m 2 ), waist circumference (−2.41 cm), and systolic blood pressure (−4.05 mmHg), whereas no significant pooled effects were observed for lipid outcomes or glycemic markers. Corresponding 95% confidence intervals and 95% prediction intervals were −3.02 to −0.92 and −6.69 to 2.75 kg for body weight, −0.99 to −0.15 and −2.43 to 1.29 kg/m 2 for BMI, −4.75 to −0.07 and −11.30 to 6.49 cm for waist circumference, and −6.90 to −1.19 and −13.24 to 5.15 mmHg for systolic blood pressure. Dietary intake outcomes were generally small and inconsistent, although vegetable intake showed a modest improvement. Certainty of evidence was generally low to very low because of risk-of-bias concerns, imprecision, and substantial heterogeneity; prediction intervals for several statistically significant pooled effects crossed the null. Subgroup findings were exploratory and underpowered. Technology-enabled precision nutrition may modestly improve anthropometric outcomes and systolic blood pressure, but longer, well-reported studies are needed to clarify the clinical impact of precision nutrition technologies. Systematic review registration This review was registered with PROSPERO under registration number CRD420251241063.
authors: Janet Antwi; Obed Akwaa Harrison; Niki Hayatbini

title: Artificial intelligence for sleep-disordered breathing: a taxonomy of methods, data modalities, and clinical applications
abstract: Sleep-disordered breathing (SDB), particularly obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), is a highly prevalent group of disorders associated with disrupted sleep, intermittent hypoxemia, excessive daytime sleepiness, neurocognitive impairment, and cardiometabolic morbidity. Although laboratory polysomnography remains central to diagnosis, conventional sleep testing can be costly, labor-intensive, and difficult to scale. Recent advances in data mining, machine learning, deep learning, wearable sensing, mobile health, multimodal analytics, and large language models are creating new opportunities for more accessible, personalized, and efficient SDB care. This review examines recent advances in artificial intelligence for SDB diagnosis and management, with emphasis on polysomnography and home sleep apnea testing, wearable and contactless screening, audio and physiological-signal analysis, imaging and anatomical risk prediction, phenotyping and endotyping, treatment monitoring, continuous positive airway pressure adherence, and clinically deployable explainable AI. We also discuss the emerging role of large language models in patient education, sleep-report summarization, clinical documentation, and decision-support workflows. Finally, we identify major challenges related to data heterogeneity, external validation, interpretability, privacy, fairness, reproducibility, regulation, and real-world integration into sleep medicine. This review aims to provide an evidence-based framework for researchers and clinicians to understand current AI applications and identify future directions for precision diagnosis and management of SDB.
authors: Tai Dinh; Daniil Lisik; Prof. Philippe Fournier-Viger; Dat Tran; Philip S. Yu; Huynh Van Hong; Ding Zou

title: Assistive Input Device for Users with Limb Impairments
abstract: Individuals with severe limb impairments encounter substantial barriers during human‑computer interaction, while commercially available assistive input devices are often prohibitively expensive. This paper presents a low‑cost wearable assistive input device (bill‑of‑materials cost < ¥130) built around the nRF52832 Bluetooth‑Low‑Energy (BLE) system‑on‑chip and an MPU‑6050 inertial measurement unit. A real‑time‑clock‑based asynchronous event‑driven architecture reduces power consumption, and the sensor's on‑chip 5 Hz digital low‑pass filter suppresses involuntary muscle tremor at the signal source. A multi‑threaded PC‑side client maps real‑time posture data to discrete keyboard commands. A user study with three participants exhibiting distinct physiological profiles was carried out under two interaction modes. In discrete click‑trigger mode, the system achieved a peak directional‑selection throughput of 12 WPM, while continuous dwell‑hold control yielded an average throughput of 4.2 WPM. The participant with a full, unrestricted range‑of‑motion (ROM) reached a trigger accuracy of 98.2 %, whereas the participant with severely‑restricted head movement obtained only 64.0 % accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that fixed‑cutoff on‑chip filtering carries inherent performance limitations for users with extremely limited motion range. Directions for future work include adaptive filtering algorithms and multi‑modal interaction schemes.
authors: Xuanting Chen

title: Atrial Fibrillation in Athletes: Evaluation, Management and Prognostic Considerations
abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is increasingly recognized among competitive athletes, posing unique challenges in management and prognostication. While regular physical activity is known to reduce overall cardiovascular risk, sustained high-intensity endurance exercise is associated with atrial remodeling, enhanced vagal tone, and a higher lifetime incidence of AF. Athletes with AF frequently differ from typical patients in that they often present at a younger age and have fewer traditional risk factors, which complicates risk assessment and medical decision-making. Knowledge gaps remain regarding thromboembolic risk estimation with traditional risk scores, optimal rhythm-control strategies, and return to play. This chapter will review current evidence regarding epidemiology, proposed mechanisms, clinical evaluation, and management approaches specific to athletes with AF, including lifestyle modification, pharmacologic therapy, catheter ablation, anticoagulation considerations, emerging roles for advanced imaging, and wearable-guided AF detection strategies. Areas of prognostic uncertainty and individualized risk assessment in athletic populations will receive particular emphasis.
authors: Nicholas Tyndall; John Henry Dean; Adam J. Kisling

title: Autonomic Function in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Narrative Review of Objective Assessment and Physiological Monitoring
abstract: Introduction and purpose: Autonomic alterations may contribute to the physiological heterogeneity of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). This review examines objective autonomic assessment in Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis, focusing on physiological phenotyping and longitudinal monitoring. Methods: This focused narrative review synthesizes 25 included studies. Evidence on heart rate variability (HRV), Holter monitoring, cardiovascular reflexes, orthostatic responses, baroreflex function, sudomotor testing, and wearable-derived signals was organized by modality and relationship with disease activity. Brief description of the state of knowledge: HRV was the most studied modality and was associated with clinical, biochemical, and endoscopic activity in selected cohorts. Autonomic alterations may persist during remission and do not consistently correspond to symptoms or inflammatory markers. Reduced HRV alone does not establish autonomic neuropathy. Multimodal testing assesses complementary physiological domains and may yield discordant findings. Wearables offer opportunities for repeated assessment alongside sleep and physical activity, while neuromodulation remains investigational. Heterogeneous protocols, small cohorts, and limited external validation constrain clinical interpretation. Conclusions: Objective autonomic assessment may complement established IBD evaluation in selected patients. The proposed Clinical Algorithm and Physiological Framework are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation. Standardized multimodal protocols and longitudinal studies are needed. Current evidence does not support autonomic biomarkers as stand-alone tools for disease monitoring or exercise prescription.
authors: Jakub Marcel Korowicki; Julia Beata Woźniak; Helena Strzelka; Milena Dziedzina; Bartosz Seroczyński; Marta Labon; Anna Zyskowska

title: Ball milling of avocado seed residues: Defining an operational space for preserving bioactive molecules and antioxidant functionality
abstract: Avocado seeds are phenolic-rich by-products, but dry comminution may alter powder structure and extractable phenolics. This study evaluated avocado seed flour after 120 min of ball milling at 30–90 rpm and ball-to-powder ratios (BPR) of 1.0–2.0, with milling time and grinding-media mass fixed. Particle size and morphology were assessed by laser diffraction and scanning electron microscopy; total phenolics, ortho-diphenols, flavonoids, ABTS, DPPH, FRAP, and targeted high-performance liquid chromatography with diode-array detection (HPLC-DAD) markers were measured. An operational low-degree-proanthocyanidin index (ΣPAC) was calculated. Process-level replication was available only at the center point (60 rpm, BPR 1.5; three independent runs). Samples 1–4 were single milling runs, so their statistical lettering reflects extraction and analytical variability and treatment comparisons are exploratory. Milling reduced D50 from 17.10 μm to 9.80–12.15 μm. Among the tested single-run factorial batches, Sample 1 (30 rpm, BPR 2.0) had the highest ΣPAC retention (0.975); the other tested batches showed retention of 0.323–0.532 and lower antioxidant responses. The algebraic retention analysis indicated that assay decline was not described by ΣPAC retention alone and may also reflect extractability, matrix interactions, assay responsiveness, and unmeasured transformations. The results identify Sample 1 as a candidate for confirmatory testing, not an optimized operating window, and support direct measurement of internal temperature, oxygen exposure, enzyme activity, and media wear in future replicated studies.
authors: Leonardo Batista; Rogério Andrade; Janaina Lima; Amanda Nascimento; Ana Barros; Hugo Miguel Lisboa

title: Bedside data to clinical foresight: the emerging role of nurses in AI-enabled predictive care and early patient deterioration detection
abstract: Early recognition of patient deterioration remains a cornerstone of high-quality nursing care and is essential for preventing avoidable morbidity, mortality, and unplanned intensive care admissions. Despite advances in physiological monitoring, delays in recognizing subtle clinical changes continue to contribute to adverse patient outcomes. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative technology capable of integrating large volumes of clinical, physiological, laboratory, and electronic health record (EHR) data to generate predictive insights that support timely clinical decision-making. AI-enabled predictive care systems, including machine learning algorithms, deep learning models, wearable sensor analytics, and early warning systems, provide nurses with opportunities to identify high-risk patients before overt clinical deterioration occurs. Rather than replacing nurses, these technologies augment clinical judgment by facilitating continuous risk assessment, prioritization of care, and proactive intervention. This narrative review explores the evolving role of nurses in AI-enabled predictive care and early patient deterioration detection. It examines the integration of bedside clinical observations with AI-driven predictive analytics, highlights current applications across acute and critical care settings, and discusses implications for nursing education, leadership, ethical practice, and interdisciplinary collaboration. The review also addresses challenges related to algorithmic bias, explainability, data quality, digital literacy, and governance while identifying future opportunities for human-centered AI implementation. Strengthening nurses' competencies in digital health and AI is essential for maximizing patient safety and ensuring equitable, evidence-based care in increasingly technology-enabled healthcare environments.
authors: R. Sheeba; N. Murugananandan; Tamilselvan; Tanusri Mandal; Israel Jeba Prab D.; Jamunarani P.; N Ilakkiya; N Padmapriya; Nithin Manly S.; Golda Sahaya Rani R.; J. Sathya Shenbega Priya; Mohammed Umar
venue: International Journal of Research in Medical Sciences

title: Bench Testing of an 8 N Slip-Resistance Specification for the Handle–Shaft Locking Interface of an Articulated Laparoscopic Instrument
abstract: Abstract Background Articulated laparoscopic instruments require a reliable mechanical connection between the handle and shaft to maintain the intended instrument configuration during surgical manipulation. The handle–shaft locking interface should resist unintended relative displacement under external loading. However, the appropriateness of a specific slip-resistance threshold must be evaluated in relation to the instrument design and intended conditions of use. Objective To evaluate the mechanical performance associated with an 8 N slip-resistance specification for the locked handle–shaft interface of an articulated laparoscopic instrument using a controlled bench model. Methods A bench-based mechanical evaluation method was designed using the instrument under test, mechanical fixtures, a calibrated force-measurement device, and displacement-measurement equipment. After engagement of the handle–shaft locking mechanism, external forces were applied to evaluate resistance to relative displacement. Testing included axial loading, loading in relevant transverse directions, and repeated locking–unlocking cycles. The primary outcome was the force corresponding to the onset of relative slippage at the locked interface. Secondary outcomes included displacement under load, complete locking failure, and changes in mechanical performance after repeated operation. Acceptance criteria should be established before confirmatory testing. Results All 30 instruments from three production batches met the 8 N axial requirement (30/30). The axial slip-onset force was 12.40 ± 0.97 N (range, 10.80–14.00 N). Under a sustained load of 8 N for 60 s, mean relative displacement increased from 0.06 mm to 0.10 mm, and mean residual displacement was 0.02 mm. After 1,000 cycles, the axial slip-onset force was 12.00 ± 0.97 N (range, 10.40–13.60 N). Conclusions This study provides a bench-testing framework for evaluating an 8 N slip-resistance specification for the handle–shaft locking interface of an articulated laparoscopic instrument. Whether this specification provides adequate mechanical stability can be determined only by comparing the measured performance with engineering acceptance criteria established in advance on the basis of the instrument’s intended use and foreseeable loading conditions.
authors: Hongchang Ma

title: Between algorithmic alerts and bodily sensations: a qualitative study of post-PCI patients' experiences with wrist-worn heart health information
abstract: Background Smart wrist-worn devices are increasingly used by patients after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) to monitor heart rate, rhythm-related alerts, sleep, activity, and other health-related data. However, limited qualitative evidence exists on how post-PCI patients interpret and respond to such information in daily life. Objective This study aimed to explore how patients with coronary heart disease after PCI understand, evaluate, and respond to heart rate, heart rhythm, and health-related information generated by smart wrist-worn devices. Methods A qualitative descriptive design was adopted. From January to May 2026, purposive sampling was used to recruit 23 post-PCI patients who had used smartwatches or smart bands in daily life. Semi-structured interviews were conducted, audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using thematic analysis. Data collection and analysis were conducted concurrently until data saturation was achieved. Results Four themes were developed: (1) cardiac status became continuously datafied; (2) calibrating risk between alerts and sensations; (3) device information awaited medical interpretation; and (4) from self-management to disease burden. Patients did not simply accept or reject device-generated data. Instead, they interpreted alerts by comparing them with bodily sensations, previous cardiac events, stent implantation experiences, follow-up results, and healthcare professionals' explanations. Device information could enhance awareness of medication use, follow-up, and lifestyle management. However, when alerts lacked medical interpretation or follow-up response, they also increased uncertainty, worry, repeated self-monitoring, and perceived disease burden. Conclusions Smart wrist-worn devices may support daily observation and clinician–patient communication in post-PCI management, but they should not be regarded as substitutes for clinical examinations or professional judgment. Clearer interpretive boundaries, stratified guidance, and follow-up response pathways are needed to help patients appropriately understand and act on device-generated information.
authors: Angang Tong; Ruiqi Luo; Pan Jin; Cuihuan Wu

title: Beyond Atrial Fibrillation: Emerging Clinical Applications of Photoplethysmography in Consumer Wearables
abstract: Introduction: Photoplethysmography (PPG) is an optical sensing technology embedded in many current consumer smartwatches and smart rings. Long used for heart-rate monitoring and pulse oximetry, PPG has more recently become the foundation for population-scale screening for atrial fibrillation. The clinical applications of PPG now extend well beyond rhythm monitoring. Method: A narrative literature review of English-language publications indexed in PubMed, Europe PMC, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar between January 2020 and May 2026 was conducted, using combinations of the search term photoplethysmography with application-specific search terms. Earlier foundational publications were included selectively where necessary. Discussion: Current evidence most strongly supports consumer-wearable PPG for resting heart-rate estimation and for atrial-fibrillation notification pathways with adjudicated electrocardiographic confirmation. SpO2 trending is conditionally supported in healthy, normoxaemic adults but is insufficient for clinical decision-making during desaturation, motion, low perfusion, or in populations under-represented in validation datasets. Cuffless blood-pressure estimation, heart-rate variability, sleep staging, and obstructive sleep apnoea screening show device-, context-, and reference-standard-dependent reliability. Non-invasive blood-glucose monitoring through smartwatches or smart rings should not be used for diabetes management and is the subject of an explicit FDA safety communication. Conclusion: Consumer-wearable PPG is a multifunctional clinical sensing platform whose evidence maturity differs sharply by application. Responsible deployment requires awareness of signal quality, motion artefact, skin-tone bias, regulatory authorisation status, and local validation, particularly in the Indonesian primary-care context.
authors: Muhammad Rifqi Haikal
venue: JIMKI Jurnal Ilmiah Mahasiswa Kedokteran Indonesia

title: Beyond responsiveness: Differentiated associations among product features, psychological needs, perceived enjoyment, and continuance intention toward AI learning devices
abstract: As large language models are increasingly embedded in dedicated learning tablets, educational robots, and other physical AI learning devices (AILDs), sustaining learners' engagement beyond initial adoption has become a broader challenge for educational technology research and design. Although the technical capabilities of such devices continue to advance, the factors associated with continued use remain poorly understood. Drawing on the Stimulus-Organism-Response framework and Self-Determination Theory, this study examines associations among perceived personalization, interactivity, response timeliness, friendliness, autonomy, competence, relatedness, perceived enjoyment, and continuance intention. Cross-sectional survey data were collected from 726 first-year senior high school students with experience using AILDs and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Effect sizes varied substantially across the estimated associations. The association between relatedness and perceived enjoyment had the largest effect size (f2 = 0.266), whereas the remaining effect sizes were small or negligible. Two theoretically informative expected associations were not supported: perceived personalization with autonomy and response timeliness with relatedness. The model explained 47.0% of the variance in continuance intention and 50.7% in perceived enjoyment. Perceived friendliness showed the largest feature-need association with relatedness, whereas response timeliness was associated with autonomy and competence but not with relatedness. Autonomy and competence showed statistically significant direct and indirect associations with continuance intention, whereas relatedness showed a statistically significant indirect association involving perceived enjoyment but no significant direct association with continuance intention. Perceived enjoyment was positively associated with continuance intention and was involved in statistically significant indirect associations for all three psychological needs. These findings reveal differentiated feature-need and need-intention association patterns in physical AI educational hardware and suggest that design attention may usefully extend beyond responsiveness to relational and enjoyable interaction. Because the data are cross-sectional, these association patterns should not be interpreted as evidence of temporal or causal relationships.
authors: Gang Ren; Xuezhen Wu; Gang Wang; Yinuo Ye; Zhihuang Huang; Tianyang Huang

title: Beyond symptoms: wearable digital biomarkers for subclinical detection of chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy.
abstract:
Background

Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) is the most prevalent dose-limiting toxicity of taxane-, platinum-, and proteasome inhibitor-based regimens, yet clinical management has a structural flaw: assessment depends on CTCAE clinician grading that registers symptoms only after axonal degeneration has reached an irreversible stage.

Main body

Quantitative sensory testing studies demonstrate that vibration perception, thermal detection, and sudomotor function deteriorate before patients report numbness or pain, suggesting a subclinical window of one to two chemotherapy cycles. Whether detection within this window can prevent permanent nerve injury remains biologically plausible but prospectively unestablished. Wearable sensors-inertial measurement units for gait, plantar pressure insoles, electrochemical skin conductance devices, and vibration sensors-have demonstrated proof-of-concept capacity to capture subclinical CIPN signals, but evidence remains largely cross-sectional with limited longitudinal validation. This Perspective distinguishes the conceptual framework for subclinical CIPN surveillance from the currently available clinical validation evidence. I systematically categorize four sensing modalities by neuropathological substrate, provide a cross-modality readiness comparison, and identify translational barriers including absent alert thresholds and confounding factors such as age, diabetes, anemia, and fatigue. I propose a phased prospective validation framework; specific monitoring recommendations should be regarded as hypotheses for testing rather than current clinical guidance.

Conclusion

Wearable sensors should not replace patient-reported outcomes but may add an objective neurotoxicity monitoring layer whose capacity to improve clinical outcomes requires prospective validation.
authors: Xu D.

title: Bioinspired Selective Perception Through On‐Chip Te/Ag Integration and Interface Interference
abstract: ABSTRACT Infrared sensing in the 1–4 µm band is of great significance in fields such as thermal detection and flame identification. However, in practical applications, this band is often disturbed by strong visible solar background radiation, leading to a reduction in signal‐to‐noise ratio. Here, inspired by jewel beetles, which use specialized thoracic pit organs to block visible light and transmit infrared radiation for forest fire detection, we present an on‐chip recognition strategy based on tellurium/silver hybrid films. The optimized films exhibit high infrared transmittance (91.5% at 2400 nm) while strongly suppressing visible light (20.6% at 400 nm) based on the interface interference effect. Leveraging this bio‐inspired spectral selectivity, we demonstrate a highly compact sensing platform integrated with a low‐cost integrated microcontroller unit running a lightweight multilayer perceptron network (0.6 kB, 149 parameters) for real‐time gesture recognition. Under the interference of visible light at 405 nm, this device achieves an on‐chip recognition accuracy up to 98.8%, significantly outperforming the pristine device (50.9%). This low‐cost and transferable bio‐inspired integration provides a practical pathway toward robust non‐contact sensing for human‐machine interaction applications.
authors: Tao Zheng; Junyi Li; Guangjie Zhou; Jie Zhang; Xiang Lin; Yupeng Guo; Xinyue Niu; Chengyi Zhu; Wenxiao Wang; Jiewei Chen

title: Biometric Data Acquisition and Monitoring via Light Signal Processing Technologies
abstract: Wearable devices enable continuous monitoring of physiological parameters through non-invasive sensors. This paper presents a biometric data acquisition and monitoring system implemented on the open-source PineTime smartwatch. The system is designed for heart-rate estimation and stress assessment based on photoplethysmography (PPG) signal processing.The proposed system consists of two applications, HRX and Zenify. HRX provides real-time heart-rate monitoring by displaying the photoplethysmographic waveform, the current heart-rate estimate, and the minimum recorded heart rate. Zenify assesses stress through heart-rate variability (HRV) analysis and classifies stress levels as low, moderate, or high.The system architecture relies on the PineTime smartwatch’s built-in optical heart-rate sensor and accelerometer, which are combined with light-signal processing algorithms. The original InfiniTime firmware was replaced with Wasp-OS, an open-source MicroPython-based watch operating system that supports rapid development and testing of biometric applications.The proposed system may be applied in preventive medicine to support early detection of physiological abnormalities, stress monitoring, and personalized health management.
authors: Anna Hovakimyan; Areg Oseyan; Siranush A. Sargsyan
venue: International Journal of Data Processing & Networking

title: Broadband wearable acoustic sensing for continuous cardiopulmonary monitoring
abstract: The human body continuously generates weak, broadband acoustic-mechanical signals that encode rich cardiopulmonary information, yet their reliable capture in real-world settings remains constrained by motion artifacts, limited bandwidth, and suboptimal mechanical coupling. Here, we present a wearable, wireless stethoscope that enables high-fidelity acquisition of heart and respiratory sounds through a mechanically compliant, broadband sensing interface. The system is built on a piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducer (PMUT) engineered to achieve ultrahigh sensitivity (-167.5 dB), a wide operating bandwidth (10 Hz-10 kHz), and a flat frequency response (±0.5 dB), enabling accurate reconstruction of subtle physiological signals across a broad spectral range. Integration with soft, skin-conformal packaging and a robust wireless readout minimizes motion-induced noise and supports stable, long-term monitoring during daily activities. Validation across multiple participants demonstrates strong agreement with clinical-grade systems, including consistent auscultation at standard cardiac sites and accurate heart-rate tracking during dynamic exercise. Furthermore, coupling the sensing platform with a residual neural network enables automated classification of five respiratory states (awake, asleep, apnea, rhonchi, and wheeze) with an accuracy of 98.7%. This work establishes a scalable, low-cost framework for continuous, high-fidelity cardiopulmonary monitoring in real-world environments.

title: CONTEXT-AWARE, GRAPH-CENTRIC AND ROBUSTNESS-GOVERNED INTRUSION DETECTION FRAMEWORK FOR VEHICULAR NETWORKS
abstract: An abundance of cyber-physical communication ecosystems can be found in modern automobiles. The interactions between CAN, ECU, and V2X create attack paths that flat intrusion labels or accuracy-only IDS evaluation can't safely handle in the process. The purpose of this research is to provide a five-stage intrusion detection approach for automotive networks that is aware of the context, centered on graphs, and regulated by robustness. Threat-Graph Entropy Mining (TGEM) is the initial component of the framework that has been developed. Attack surfaces, protocol artifacts, ECUs, and observable symptoms are all connected to one another through a multi-layer threat interaction graph in this procedure. Then, entropycentrality scoring finds the main attack families and unsolved defense gaps. The payload, temporal, and topological views are then aligned into a threat-priority-guided latent model via CMV-DD. This is accomplished by having the instructor and students distill the data. The Graph-TCN Transformer with Reliability-Gated Fusion (GTT-RGF) finds threats by combining ECU relationships, short-term temporal deviations, and long-range planned attack patterns. In order to accomplish this, it dynamically reduces the impact of views that are either fraudulent or highly noisy. When a minimum attack is utilized in a manner that is consistent with the graph, Counterfactual Attack-Path Verification (CAPV) monitors the situation to determine whether or not the alarms continue to be reliable. Under the Risk Calibration and Continuous Drift Governance (RCC-DG) system, detection data are converted into practical risk scores that are more precise. Additionally, the technology enables regulated updates to be made after drift has occurred. The findings of tests that were conducted with settings that were influenced by CAN and V2X revealed that F1- scores ranged from 93.9 to 96.2% in highway, urban, intersection, and mixed driving scenarios. Depending on the amount of traffic on the network, this indicates that the percentage of false positives decreases to between 1.9 and 3.1%. The model also has an average detection latency of 18–27 ms, a throughput of nearly 940 windows per second, a robust detection range of 88.9–90.6% under minor coordinated perturbations, an expected calibration error of 0.03 ms, and 95.6% performance retention after drift. Findings such as these demonstrate that the proposed paradigm not only improves the accuracy of detection, but also improves causal robustness, contextual generalization, risk interpretability, and implementation reliability for the next generation of intelligent transportation systems.

title: CRAFT: Exploring Wearable Creative AI on Smart Glasses for Fiction Writing in Real-World Contexts
abstract: Creative writing increasingly integrates AI assistance, yet current tools miss in-situ moments when writers draw inspiration from real-world experiences. We envision Context-aware Reality-Fiction Transformation ( CRAFT ), an approach for AI glasses that translates daily experiences into fiction narratives. We explored its desirability, feasibility, and potential viability through three studies. Interviews with nine writers yielded desires and three design goals: 1) augmenting in-situ perception to bridge reality-fiction gaps, 2) promoting authenticity grounded in real-world experiences while maintaining fictionalization, and 3) preserving creative agency, enjoyment, and life-art boundaries. Co-design workshops with 16 writers and researchers operationalized these goals into concrete interaction mechanisms using a technology probe. We then conducted supported field trials with eight writers across 24 sessions using a refined probe, revealing writer-perceived benefits (e.g., enriched fictional ideas from serendipitous encounters), emergent practices (e.g., micro-creation), and design considerations for future sustained use. We contribute design explorations for the CRAFT approach, offering design implications and empirical insights on ubiquitous human-AI creative collaboration in everyday life.

title: Can Technology Support Healthy Ageing? Feasibility Study of a Wellbeing Management Platform for Self-care and Early Intervention in Older Adults
abstract: Background: Digital tools may support people to develop and maintain lifestyle changes and make “better-informed decisions about their health”.[1] The use of wearable and smart devices may further enable the identification of subclinical fluctuations in health, facilitating early intervention and preventative care at the population level.[1],[2] This study aims to assess the usability, adherence and feasibility of the Tinteán™ wellbeing management platform in supporting self-care and early intervention in community-dwelling adults over 55.[3] Approach:A total of 100 participants with at least one chronic health condition have been recruited on a voluntary basis from volunteer, community and social enterprises including ALONE (Ireland’s national elder support charity), Friends of the Elderly, disease-specific support groups (COPD Support Ireland, Diabetes Ireland, Asthma Society) and retired professionals associations (Garda Retired Members, Retired Teachers’ Association).[4] Inclusion criteria include: being aged 55 years or older, living independently with a fixed address, owning a suitable smartphone, being independently mobile and living in or willing to travel to Dublin for in-person testing days. Prospective clients were contacted by wellbeing team members to complete a screening questionnaire (adapted from the Tilburg Frailty Indicator) to establish suitability, with those scoring five or above excluded from the study.[5] All participants have received a smart watch and scales, and 10% have been supplied with a smart home blood pressure monitor. Devices are linked with the Tinteán mobile app and readings are uploaded to a user dashboard daily. Results are flagged according to a threshold-based system derived from the HSE’s National Early Warning System and made available to healthcare providers via a unique QR code on participants’ apps.[6] At onboarding and subsequent 3-monthly intervals, participants undergo hearing, vision and cognitive assessments, as well as strength, mobility and balance testing under the supervision of a clinical physiotherapist. Participants also complete regular mental health questionnaires and record relevant life events (e.g., falls, GP visits). These measures of physical, mental, and social health are tracked, and participants are connected with local health and/or social support services based on concerning scores or trends in these metrics. Results: Preliminary results (study to end in March 2026) indicate high levels of acceptance and adherence among participants, despite the reportedly low acceptability of digital devices in this age group.[7] Participants have reported increased awareness of their health status, motivation to improve measures e.g., step count, and a sense of confidence in knowing that someone is looking out for them. Some participants have described feeling better able to advocate for themselves in interactions with healthcare professionals. The main alert categories to date are cardiovascular (55%), strength and mobility (15%), pain (9%), and mental health (8%). Preliminary limitations and issues include the deliberate selection of participants, the high numbers of alerts generated in free-living conditions, the corresponding requirement for healthcare professionals to follow-up the alerts and the complexity of refining the model to generate individualised thresholds for clients. Implications: Pending finalisation of results, though likely applicable across different health system contexts and settings.

title: Can a Ring Measure, Predict or Heal Stress? A Critical Appraisal of the Oura Ring's Stress, Resilience and Cumulative Stress Claims
abstract: Background. Since 2023 the Oura Ring has offered three stress-related outputs. Daytime Stress labels minutes as stressed, engaged, relaxed or restored. Resilience grades the 14-day balance of stress and recovery on five levels from “limited” to “exceptional.” Cumulative Stress claims to reveal the “hidden toll” of chronic stress “before it manifests as fatigue, burnout, or illness.” Oura’s marketing invites users to “take charge of your stress” and “avoid burnout.” Its Chief Executive, in an interview the company filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), describes a device that can say “something’s really wrong” and prompt behaviour change. Objective. To define what stress and resilience are and how they are measured, to establish what a finger-worn photoplethysmography (PPG), temperature and motion sensor can physiologically detect, and to appraise Oura’s claims to measure, predict and help remediate stress against the published evidence. Findings. The ring’s inputs (heart rate, heart-rate variability, skin temperature and motion) index autonomic arousal, not stress. Arousal rises with psychological threat but equally with caffeine, alcohol, digestion, heat, posture, fever, dehydration, the luteal phase, many drugs and excitement. Oura itself acknowledges that the ring “can’t detect psychological stress.” Its own member data show that users who logged alcohol recorded about 50% more “stress” minutes, illustrating the non-specificity. No peer-reviewed validation of Daytime Stress or Resilience against a laboratory stressor, a cortisol reference or a validated resilience scale has been published. Cumulative Stress is supported by company-reported agreement with the Perceived Stress Scale or Copenhagen Burnout Inventory: 76% concordance in high scorers, 86% in low scorers and 82% overall. The development cohort, however, was recruited from people at the extremes of perceived stress, a design known to inflate diagnostic accuracy. The figures are not peer-reviewed and report no kappa, no calibration and no prediction of any clinical outcome. Resilience, a psychological capacity to adapt to adversity, is operationalised as a 14-day ratio of physiological load to recovery, partly built from a sleep score whose staging is itself weakly validated. On remediation, Oura does not claim to heal. We found no controlled trial showing that using the ring or its stress features reduces stress, prevents burnout or improves health. The study Oura cites tested a meditation app, had no control group and used the ring only as a measurement tool. Conclusions. The Oura Ring measures arousal, not stress. It labels resilience without measuring it, and it cannot predict burnout or illness on any published evidence. Nor has it been shown to heal stress. Interventions with evidence, such as mindfulness-based programmes and structured heart-rate-variability biofeedback, exist independently of the ring. Clinicians should treat ring stress outputs as unvalidated wellness indicators. They should neither dismiss distress because the ring is reassuring nor attribute medical arousal to “stress” because the ring says so. Keywords: stress; resilience; burnout; allostatic load; heart rate variability; autonomic nervous system; wearable devices; photoplethysmography; device validation; Oura Ring

title: Changes in modifiable dementia risk factors and subjective cognitive decline in mid and later life
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Exposure to modifiable dementia risk factors (MDRFs) contributes substantially to dementia risk across the life course. Less is known about persistence and changes in these factors during mid- and later life and how they relate to early neurophysiological changes associated with dementia. This study examined rates and changes in MDRFs over two years and their associations with subjective cognitive decline (SCD) among older adults. DESIGN: Cohort study. SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: Participants were 2370 adults aged 55-92 years (M = 68.54, SD = 7.15; 56.5% female) who completed the 2018 and 2020 waves of a longitudinal survey of ageing in New Zealand. MEASUREMENTS: Self-reported hypertension, diabetes, hearing impairment, vision impairment, current smoking, hazardous alcohol use, physical inactivity, depression, and loneliness were classified into four categories across waves: stable absence, reduction, onset, and stable presence. SCD was assessed in 2020. Logistic regression models were used to examine associations between MDRF categories and SCD. RESULTS: Survey-weighted responses indicated 8.6% of older adults experienced SCD. Diabetes, hearing impairment, current vision impairment, stable presence of physical inactivity, depression, and current loneliness were associated with increased odds of SCD. CONCLUSIONS: Both the onset and reduction of psychosocial and sensory MDRFs in mid- and later life have measurable implications for subjective cognitive outcomes in a general population sample. Prevention and reduction of diabetes, sensory loss, physical inactivity, depression, and social isolation represent meaningful targets for supporting cognitive well-being among older adults.

title: Comparative Efficacy of eHealth ‐Based Interventions for Weight Loss in Adults With Overweight or Obesity: A Systematic Review and Network Meta‐Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Aims This systematic review and network meta‐analysis aimed to compare the efficacy of eHealth‐based interventions on body weight reduction in adults who are overweight or obesity. Design This study was designed as a systematic review and network meta‐analysis (NMA) following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Data Sources Five electronic databases (i.e., PubMed, EMBASE, CINAHL, Cochrane Library and Scopus), were systematically searched from inception to May 4, 2026. Review Methods Studies were assessed for eligibility using predefined criteria. Two authors independently assessed the methodological quality using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. Confidence in the NMA findings was evaluated using the CINeMA. Data were synthesized using a frequentist random‐effects NMA with restricted maximum‐likelihood estimation in R. Results A total of 182 trials evaluating 21 single‐ and multi‐component eHealth interventions were included. Overall, 36.3% of studies were at low risk of bias, 34.1% had some concerns, and 29.7% were at high risk. Confidence in the NMA estimates ranged from very low to high, with 72.5% of comparisons rated as high or moderate confidence. The combination of a mobile application, wearable device and health education demonstrated the greatest efficacy, resulting in significantly greater weight loss than all comparators, with mean differences ranging from −9.14 to −3.86 kg (all p < 0.05). Among single‐component interventions, phone call‐based interventions ranked highest for weight loss ( p ‐score = 0.52). Conclusions Combining a mobile application, wearable device and health education appeared to be an effective strategy for reducing body weight in adults with overweight or obesity. Impact These findings may support evidence‐based selection of eHealth weight management interventions for implementation in individual, community and healthcare settings. No Patient or Public Contribution Neither patients nor the public were involved in the design, conduct or reporting of this study. Trial Registration PROSPERO (CRD no: 420251119776)

title: Comparative study of zero degree and ambient plate temperature of submerged arc welded IS 2062 grade B steel for application in cold region
abstract: Submerged Arc Welding (SAW) is widely used in the fabrication of structural steel components; however, its performance under cold-region conditions remains insufficiently explored. This study presents a comparative investigation of SAW performed on IS 2062 Grade B steel plates maintained at ambient temperature and 0 °C, with the objective of assessing the feasibility of welding without preheating for cold-region applications. Welding trials were conducted in a bead-on-plate configuration, and the influence of arc voltage, travel speed, wire feed rate, and electrode stick-out was systematically evaluated using a Taguchi L16 orthogonal array. A total of 32 welded specimens, comprising 16 welds at ambient temperature and 16 welds at 0 °C, were produced and characterized through weld bead geometry measurements, microhardness testing, and optical microscopy. The results demonstrated that sound and defect-free welds could be successfully produced at both plate temperatures without the need for preheating. Comparative analysis revealed that welding at 0 °C increased heat dissipation from the weld zone, resulting in reduced weld penetration and reinforcement height compared with ambient-temperature welding. However, bead width showed only minor variations between the two temperature conditions. Microhardness measurements indicated that the 0 °C plate temperature significantly enhanced hardness, particularly within the heat-affected zone (HAZ), where an average increase of approximately 36% was observed relative to ambient-temperature welds. The reinforcement region exhibited a hardness increase of about 7.7%, while the weld metal hardness remained largely unaffected. Microstructural evaluation showed that ferrite and pearlite were the dominant phases in both welding conditions. Nevertheless, the higher cooling rate associated with the 0 °C plate temperature promoted grain refinement and reduced grain coarsening in the HAZ compared with ambient-temperature welding. Finally, the comparative study confirms that SAW of IS 2062 Grade B steel at 0 °C can achieve weld quality comparable to that obtained under ambient conditions while offering improved hardness and refined microstructural characteristics. These findings highlight the potential of SAW without preheating for structural steel fabrication and repair operations in cold-region environments.

title: Comprehensive Review on Artificial Intelligence-Based Smart Healthcare Monitoring Using IoT and HCI
abstract: The convergence of the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), and human–computer interaction (HCI) is reshaping healthcare monitoring from episodic clinical observation toward continuous, context-aware, and increasingly personalized health management. IoT-enabled medical sensors, wearable devices, ambient intelligence systems, mobile platforms, and connected clinical equipment generate heterogeneous physiological, behavioural, environmental, and contextual data at unprecedented temporal resolution. AI techniques transform these data into predictions, classifications, anomaly detection, risk scores, and decision-support information, while HCI provides the mechanisms through which patients, caregivers, and clinicians perceive, interpret, validate, and act upon algorithmic outputs. Recent reviews indicate that AI-enabled remote monitoring has expanded from conventional cloud-based architectures toward edge intelligence, federated learning, explainable AI, and human-centred Healthcare 5.0 architectures [1]–[5]. This review critically examines the integration of AI, IoT, and HCI in smart healthcare monitoring. A layered taxonomy is developed covering sensing and acquisition, communication, edge/cloud intelligence, clinical analytics, interaction, and governance. Machine-learning, deep-learning, multimodal fusion, time-series modeling, explainable AI, reinforcement learning, and federated-learning methodologies are examined with respect to their suitability for continuous monitoring. Particular attention is given to latency, energy consumption, model generalization, data heterogeneity, interpretability, interoperability, privacy, cybersecurity, usability, and clinical validation. The review also compares centralized, edge, cloud, and federated architectures and examines their implications for real-time healthcare applications. Representative applications involving cardiovascular monitoring, diabetes management, respiratory disease, neurological disorders, elderly care, rehabilitation, mental-health monitoring, and emergency detection are discussed. A reference case study is presented for an AI-assisted remote patient-monitoring system integrating wearable sensors, edge analytics, a clinical dashboard, and human-centred alert mechanisms. Finally, the review identifies unresolved challenges involving dataset bias, sensor reliability, model drift, human over-reliance, alarm fatigue, interoperability, regulatory compliance, and equitable access. Future research directions include multimodal foundation models, adaptive edge intelligence, digital twins, privacy-preserving learning, standardized evaluation protocols, explainable multimodal AI, and human-AI collaborative decision-making.
