title: Contactless Upper-Limb Bradykinesia Monitoring for Parkinson's Disease via Semantic-Aware mmWave Sensing in Daily Life
abstract: Upper-limb bradykinesia, a cardinal symptom of Parkinson's disease (PD), significantly disrupts daily activities with slowness and reduced amplitude of voluntary movement. Current clinical assessments are episodic and subjective, and fail to capture real-world symptom fluctuations, while wearable systems suffer from low long-term adherence and vision-based solutions raise privacy concerns. We introduce mmBrady, the first contactless system that enables continuous, privacy-preserving estimation of upper-limb bradykinesia in daily environments using mmWave radar. To address core challenges including coarse clinical supervision, noisy superimposed signals, and heterogeneous daily activities, we propose three key modules: (1) a decoupled strategy using cross-modal dense supervision for kinematic extractors; (2) a hierarchical framework modeling spatial joint synergy to disentangle overlapping reflections; and (3) a semantic-aware multi-instance regressor that aggregates motion-stage-specific observations to distinguish pathological slowness from normal pauses. Evaluated on 42 PD patients across 8 real-world environments (clinic, nursing home, and homes), mmBrady achieves a high correlation of 0.73 and a low MAE of 1.59 with clinician-anchored MDS-UPDRS bradykinesia scores, which is even better than state-of-the-art single-wearable solutions but with no user burden. We will release the first contactless bradykinesia dataset to advance in-home neurological healthcare. We envision that mmBrady paves the way for longitudinal, low-burden PD monitoring to support timely medication adjustments and improve patient quality of life.

title: CropAI-SOS: AI-Powered Crop Health Monitoring, Weather Alert, Geo-Mapping, and Emergency Support System for Farmers
abstract: Early detection of crop diseases and nutrient deficiencies is important for improving crop yield, reducing losses, and helping farmers take timely action.While AI can aid in accurate crop diagnostics, there is a lack of available, easy-to-use mobile tools that allow farmers to not only make an accurate diagnosis, but receive support in real time.The proposed system, called CropAI-SOS, is a smart agriculture support system which assists farmers in problem identification via mobile application and further environmental and emergency support.In this system, a farmer takes or uploads the image of the crop leaf onto his/her cell phone, and the image is fed into an AI-based prediction module in order to detect the presence of a disease or nutrient deficiency.The application shows the problem that has been detected, how certain the application is about the problem, and a basic treatment recommendation.To make the system more practical it also incorporates weather data and geo-location mapping to enable farmers to see not only weather conditions but the location of their crops and the crop context.A special SOS module is included to enable farmers to generate instant requests for support of their crops to the admin side, if the detected problem is serious.All scan records, SOS requests and user information is kept in a cloud-based database for monitoring and future reference.An admin dashboard is also included that provides an overview of users, scan reports, emergency cases and updates case status.The proposed system is simple, scalable and easy to use and showcases the potential of integrating AI, mobile computing, weather data and cloud services to provide a practical farmer support solution.

title: Cross-sectional stratification of fall-related vulnerability in Parkinson’s disease through multimodal fusion of speech, gait, facial expression, and upper-limb movement
abstract: Falls constitute a significant cause of morbidity in Parkinson's disease (PD), but current approaches to cross-sectional assessment of fall-related vulnerability frequently depend on unimodal mobility metrics with limited ability to characterize its multidimensional manifestations. This study presents a multimodal deep learning (DL) architecture that incorporates facial expressions, voice, gait dynamics, and upper-limb movements to classify cross-sectional fall-related vulnerability in PD using current postural-instability status and fall history. Data were gathered from 147 patients, and modality-specific models were systematically pruned to reduce model size, inference latency, and computational requirements while maintaining classification performance, providing an initial assessment of computational efficiency within the experimental environment. Various fusion strategies, including late, intermediate, attention-based, transformer-based, and large-language-model-assisted methods, were assessed using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. The large-language-model-assisted analysis was exploratory and was based on a single recorded API run per participant-modality configuration. Pruning resulted in considerable efficiency improvements without a notable decrease in accuracy, with gait demonstrating the highest robustness. Fusion performance varied across methods and modality combinations. Attention-based fusion with face and gait achieved an observed macro-f1 of 91.67%. An exploratory large-language-model-assisted face-upper-limb configuration produced an observed macro-f1 of 93.75% in a single recorded run; because repeated-run stability and exact model-version reproducibility were not established, this result should not be interpreted as evidence of reproducible superiority. Transformer fusion produced an observed macro-f1 of 85.02% when all four modalities were included. Significantly, speech and particularly face expressivity provided supplementary signals to conventional gait and upper-limb assessments, underscoring the potential of underexplored axial characteristics as complementary digital markers associated with fall-related vulnerability. These findings support further study of multimodal AI for cross-sectional classification of fall-related vulnerability in PD. Prospective fall prediction, external generalizability, and performance on intended devices remain to be evaluated in independent future studies.

title: DARE to wear: digital health promotion and disease prevention using wearable devices
abstract: Abstract Global healthcare systems are under increasing strain to ensure long-term sustainability, necessitating a fundamental transition towards proactive, preventive healthcare strategies. Wearable sensor technologies are uniquely positioned to facilitate this paradigm shift by enabling continuous physiological and behavioral monitoring, facilitating early risk stratification, and enabling timely interventions. DigitAl lifelong pREvention (DARE) is a nationwide initiative conceived in Italy to develop and evaluate novel digital tools and services aimed at fostering innovative health promotion and disease prevention pathways, with wearable devices identified as a critical enabling technology. Herein, we present a comprehensive overview of 16 pilot investigations designed in DARE to rigorously assess the utility of wearable devices in the continuous monitoring of physical activity, joint mobility, sleep architecture, heart rate variability, nutrition, and glucose homeostasis across diverse health domains, including healthy aging, chronic disease prevention, and lifestyle modification programs targeting over 20000 participants. We meticulously detail the methodological characteristics of these study protocols, explicitly outlining the technical specifications, functional capabilities, and inherent limitations of the 18 distinct wearable devices (sourced from 12 different manufacturers) employed across these clinical trials. The breadth of applications and the heterogeneity of the target populations underscore the significant potential of wearable devices as an integral component of future digital health prevention strategies.

title: DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION OF AN INTELLIGENT HYBRID INTRUSION DETECTION SYSTEM USING SIGNATURE-BASED DETECTION, LIGHTGBM, AND ISOLATION FOREST
abstract: Network intrusion detection systems must identify known attacks while remaining sensitive to previously unseen or behaviorally unusual traffic. Single detection paradigms are limited because signature-based methods depend on known attack patterns, supervised classifiers may miss behavior outside their training distribution, and anomaly detectors may generate false alarms when legitimate traffic changes. This study presents an intelligent hybrid network intrusion detection system that combines signature-based detection, LightGBM supervised classification, and Isolation Forest anomaly detection in a sequential pipeline. The system was implemented as a Python/Flask application with passive packet monitoring and manual analysis of JSON/CSV traffic records. HIKARI-2021 was used for supervised training. The dataset contained 555,278 records; after preprocessing, 81 features were retained. A stratified 80:20 train-test split was used for LightGBM, while Isolation Forest was trained on 414,065 benign training records. LightGBM was configured with 250 estimators, a learning rate of 0.05, 48 leaves, class weighting, and a tuned decision threshold of 0.7987. On the test set, the classifier achieved 90.60% accuracy, 94.63% weighted precision, 90.60% weighted recall, and 92.01% weighted F1-score. The suspicious-class recall was 81.89%, while suspicious-class precision was 40.50%. The ROC curve produced an AUC of 0.9522. The results demonstrate that the supervised component provides useful discrimination, while the hybrid architecture supplies complementary signature and anomaly-detection mechanisms. Because the available experiment did not produce a separate end-to-end quantitative evaluation of the complete hybrid pipeline, the reported numerical metrics are explicitly attributed to the LightGBM component.

title: DRW-CNN: A Dilated Residual Wavelet CNN for ECG-based Severe Heart Failure Screening
abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG)-based heart-failure screening requires clinically valid labels, record-independent evaluation, and uncertainty analysis at the level of independent records. This study evaluates a Dilated Residual Wavelet Convolutional Neural Network (DRW-CNN) for discrimination of clinically confirmed severe Congestive Heart Failure (CHF) from normal sinus rhythm. The primary cohort comprises all 15 available BIDMC CHF records and 18 MIT-BIH Normal Sinus Rhythm Database records. Records are partitioned before segmentation, yielding 528 training, 96 validation, and 168 held-out test segments from mutually exclusive records. The network applies level-4 Daubechies-4 wavelet denoising, z-score normalization, residual blocks with dilation factors 1, 2, and 4, global average pooling, and sigmoid classification. Class-weighted binary cross-entropy addresses imbalance without deleting independent records. At the prespecified threshold of 0.5, held-out predictions achieve 95.238% accuracy, 95.833% sensitivity, 94.792% specificity, 93.243% precision, 94.521% F1-score, MCC 0.903, ROC-AUC 0.988, and average precision 0.989. Record-cluster bootstrap intervals, calibration, threshold sensitivity, record-level aggregation, leave-one-record-out stability, and auxiliary non-HF domain-shift stress analyses are also reported. The study provides a leakage-resistant severe-CHF screening evaluation that separates disease-specific evidence from auxiliary abnormality testing and quantifies uncertainty at record level.

title: Decentralized Epidemic Tracking using Federated Learning and Edge AI on Consumer Wearables
abstract: Early detection of infectious-disease outbreaks depends on how quickly weak, distributed signals can be turned into a public-health decision, yet conventional surveillance relies on clinic visits, laboratory confirmation, and syndromic reporting that lag infection by days. Consumer wearables such as smartwatches, fitness bands, and smart rings continuously record resting heart rate, heart-rate variability, skin temperature, blood-oxygen saturation, respiration, sleep, and activity, and prior studies show that deviations from a person's own baseline can appear before symptoms. Centralizing this data, however, creates serious privacy, security, and regulatory exposure. This paper proposes a decentralized epidemic-tracking framework that combines Federated Learning (FL) and Edge AI on consumer wearables. Personalized anomaly detectors run on the device; only privacy-protected model updates and coarse, thresholded anomaly flags leave the user's phone; and a hierarchical wearable, smartphone, regional-edge, and health-authority architecture converts local signals into population-level outbreak indicators. Building on a recent wearable-centric review of federated AI, the framework adds eight design innovations: personalized baseline-deviation modelling, hierarchical hybrid aggregation, outbreak-risk-adaptive differential privacy, energy-aware client participation, federated analytics with secure aggregation and k-anonymous geo-cells, a permissioned-ledger audit trail kept off the critical path, federated unlearning for erasure rights, and a pathogen-agnostic cold-start strategy. Six learning approaches are compared conceptually, and detection, timeliness, communication, energy, and privacy metrics are defined. As no field deployment or labelled dataset was collected for this study, the work is presented as a proposed framework and illustrative experimental design rather than a report of empirical results, and all performance figures shown are clearly marked as illustrative placeholders. The discussion covers practical significance for public-health agencies, limitations such as sensor noise, non-IID data, client dropout, dataset shift, and regulatory classification, and the future directions needed to move from prototype to field-ready deployment.

title: Decision-centered wearable biosensors for personalized rehabilitation: integrating multimodal monitoring, artificial intelligence, and closed-loop intervention
abstract: Personalized rehabilitation requires repeated assessment of movement, physiological tolerance, fatigue, and adherence, yet conventional clinic-based measurements provide only intermittent snapshots. The convergence of wearable biosensors with artificial intelligence, edge-cloud computing, and connected data infrastructures creates an opportunity to convert continuous multimodal signals into timely rehabilitation decisions. This critical narrative review synthesizes physiological, biochemical, electrophysiological, biomechanical, and behavioral sensing within a monitoring-interpretation-feedback-adaptation-outcome framework. We first evaluate analytical validity, real-world robustness, biocompatibility, wearability, calibration drift, and power continuity. We then examine signal-quality control, multimodal fusion, digital biomarkers, federated learning, digital twins, and predictive models according to latency, uncertainty, generalizability, privacy, and decision utility. The review follows biosensor-derived information across a graded spectrum of action, from clinician-reviewed monitoring and real-time biofeedback to assist-as-needed adaptation, functional electrical stimulation, and state-responsive neuromodulation. Applications include motor and physiological assessment, fatigue-aware dose adjustment, musculoskeletal and neurological rehabilitation, posture correction, sensor-rich prosthetics, and Internet of Things-enabled home rehabilitation. Across these settings, greater autonomy increases the evidence and safety requirements: models should expose confidence, systems should degrade safely when signal quality falls, and digital infrastructures should preserve interoperability, version traceability, privacy, and accountable clinician oversight. The central translational gap is not sensor sensitivity alone but whether an integrated biosensor system produces a reliable metric, supports an explicit and proportionate decision, and improves an outcome important to the patient. Decision-centered evaluation can help move wearable biosensing from fragmented technology demonstrations toward secure, personalized, continuous, and clinically accountable rehabilitation.
authors: Fujin Jia; Xinzhu Li; Hui Song; Xinyue Liu; Yuli Tang; Qingping Wen; Ping Wu

title: Demo: Surface Material and Roughness Sensing via mmWave Vibrometry
abstract: mmWave sensing has emerged as a promising contactless solution for object detection and material sensing. While existing material-sensing approaches exploit differences in mmWave signal reflectivity, their performance in understanding fine-grained surface characteristics, such as texture and roughness, is limited by sensing wavelength and spatial resolution. We propose mmTexora, a novel system that extends mmWave material sensing to surface roughness sensing for robotic grasping and manipulation. mmTexora adapts vibrometry principles to mmWave radar by leveraging ambient vibrations from sources such as air conditioning or machinery, which subtly modulate surface scattering and embed roughness-related information in the received radar signals. By extracting these vibration-induced features, mm-Texora enables texture and roughness sensing in quasi-static scenes. In this demonstration, we show that a simplified mmTexora prototype using a single TI AWR1843 mmWave radar can identify surfaces made of different materials and distinguish surfaces with different textures and roughness levels, even when they are made of the same material.

title: Developing an AI-Powered Occupational Health Surveillance System for Real-Time Detection and Management of Workplace Health Hazards
abstract: The increasing complexity of workplace environments necessitates advanced solutions for monitoring and managing occupational health risks. Traditional occupational health surveillance systems often struggle with inefficiencies, delayed hazard detection, and limited adaptability to dynamic workplace conditions. This study proposes the development of an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered occupational health surveillance system designed to enable real-time detection, assessment, and management of workplace health hazards. The system leverages machine learning (ML) algorithms, predictive analytics, and Internet of Things (IoT) devices to enhance workplace safety and improve health outcomes for employees. Central to the proposed system is the integration of wearable devices and IoT sensors to collect real-time data on environmental conditions, such as air quality, noise levels, and temperature, as well as employee health metrics, including heart rate, stress levels, and fatigue. These data streams are processed using AI algorithms capable of identifying patterns, detecting anomalies, and predicting potential risks. Predictive analytics further support proactive interventions, enabling organizations to mitigate hazards before they escalate into critical incidents. The system incorporates a user-friendly dashboard for visualizing insights, generating automated reports, and delivering actionable recommendations to managers and employees. Additionally, the framework supports compliance with occupational safety regulations by providing detailed documentation and audit trails. By combining real-time monitoring with AI-driven insights, the system promotes a culture of safety, minimizes workplace injuries, and enhances employee well-being. Moreover, the scalability of the framework allows it to be adapted across industries, addressing sector-specific challenges and operational requirements. This innovative approach bridges the gap between emerging technologies and occupational health, providing a comprehensive solution for organizations aiming to foster safe and healthy work environments. title: Development of a Model for Health Monitoring Using Machine Learning and Data Mining System
abstract: Mobile Health is an emerging field that allows for real-time monitoring of individuals between routine clinical visits. It also makes it possible to remotely gather health signals, track disease progression and provide just-in-time interventions. Data Mining is the process of extracting valid, previously unknown, comprehensible and actionable information from large databases and using it to make crucial, critical business and logical decisions. The motivation is to improve on the existing by designing a medical bio-card, where the patient’s medical history can be accessed by any readily available medical personnel, other than the registered one (probably due to network issues or remote location), to proscribe drugs and commence treatment when the patient is in critical condition. The Objective of this research is to improve on the current system that focused on key risk factors such as High/ low Blood Pressure (H/LBP), Sugar level, Blood level, High Body Temperature (Fever), Tobacco use, Alcohol use, Inadequate Physical Inactivity, Unhealthy Diets, Abnormal Sleep Patterns etc which plays key roles in many chronic diseases. Hence, there is a need to continuously monitor at risk individuals for their health status and activities over extended periods of time in their natural settings with the goal of improving their health and well being using wearable sensors. Wearable devices are devices worn on, in or around the body, and it has highly reduced form factors, longer battery life and enhanced network capabilities to continuously and remotely monitor individuals in their natural settings over extended period of time. The Methodology employed for the study of the existing system and adopted for the design of the new system is Object-Oriented Analysis and Design Method (OOADM) since it is object-oriented in nature. The improved system implemented with an accelerometer, gyroscope and/or magnetometer will detect motion, orientation and direction. The mobile App developed using Python programming language, MySQLite and a Cloud Infrastructure (AWS). The result is in form of coupling these wearable devices with smart phones and cloud computing, where large volume of data can be remotely analyzed to find interesting patterns, detect abnormalities and detect target activities from continuous stream of data.

title: Diabetes Mellitus Detection System Using Machine Learning with the Support Vector Machine (SVM) Method
abstract: Background: Diabetes Mellitus (DM) remains a major non-communicable disease with a continuously rising prevalence, and delayed diagnosis increases the risk of severe complications such as kidney failure, cardiovascular disease, and neuropathy. Objective: This study aims to design and build a web-based Diabetes Mellitus detection system using the Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithm and to measure the classification performance of the resulting model. Methods: The dataset consisted of 170 medical records from Rumah Sakit Cut Meutia collected over the 2023-2025 period, comprising eight predictor variables (gender, blood pressure, glucose level, insulin, skin thickness, Body Mass Index, diabetes family-history score, and age). The data were preprocessed through label encoding, median-based missing-value imputation, Interquartile Range (IQR) outlier clipping, and Min-Max normalization, then split into 80% training data (132 records) and 20% testing data (34 records). The SVM model, comparing Linear and Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernels, was optimized using GridSearchCV with Stratified 5-Fold Cross Validation. Results: The optimal model used an RBF kernel with C = 1 and gamma = 0.01, achieving a cross-validation ROC-AUC of 96.43%. On the test set, the model achieved an accuracy of 88.24%, precision of 94.12%, recall of 84.21%, and an F1-score of 88.89%, with a test-set AUC of 96.1%. Usability testing using the System Usability Scale (SUS) on 10 respondents produced an average score of 71.75, placed in the "Good" category. Conclusion: The SVM-based web system was able to classify Diabetes Mellitus status accurately and was assessed by users as easy to operate, indicating its feasibility as a decision-support tool for the early detection of Diabetes Mellitus.
authors: Syahira Ratu Fadilla; Sayed Fachrurrazi; Desvina Yulisda

title: Diabetic retinopathy detection models: Transition from conventional to deep learning approaches and a hybrid model
abstract: Diabetes is a chronic and common disease all over the world that has many side effects. One of the main side effects of this disease is diabetic retinopathy (DR), which if not diagnosed and treated in time, causes low vision and eventually blindness. Early diagnosis of this disease prevents the occurrence of complications of it. As artificial intelligence and deep learning technologies progress, various models for diagnosing medical images like fundus images in diabetic retinopathy became available. Due to the increase in the prevalence of DR, we propose a hybrid method with VGG-16 deep learning model and a hand-crafted feature extraction technique, namely Principal Component Analysis, for the classification of DR. To achieve this goal, two well-known datasets, namely APTOS 2019 and Messidor-2, are considered. On each of the datasets, two hand-crafted models, namely Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Local Binary Patterns (LBP), and various deep learning models are implemented. In order to evaluate the models and compare them with each other and the state-of-the-art in this field, standard metrics such as accuracy are calculated. The results show that deep learning models are significantly superior to manual models regarding performance in diagnosing DR and its degrees. Moreover, the proposed hybrid method shows notable improvement in classification performance. Furthermore, the results obtained in this study have shown better performance than some other recent studies in the literature.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of wearable technologies for atrial fibrillation detection: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia and a major cause of ischemic stroke. Because AF is frequently paroxysmal and asymptomatic, conventional short-term monitoring often fails to detect it. Wearable technologies have emerged as promising tools for AF screening, but their diagnostic performance requires comprehensive evaluation. We conducted a systematic review and diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis following PRISMA-DTA guidelines. PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to 25 February 2026 for prospective and retrospective studies using electrocardiographic reference standards. Bivariate random-effects and Bayesian hierarchical models were used to pool diagnostic accuracy estimates. Fifty-one studies involving 33,374 participants from 15 countries were included. PPG-based smartwatches demonstrated the highest sensitivity (96.3%) with specificity of 93.6%. ECG-based smartwatches achieved sensitivity of 89.0% and specificity of 92.8% (DOR 103.9). Smartphone-based ECG devices showed the strongest overall diagnostic performance, with sensitivity of 94.5%, specificity of 95.8%, DOR of 396.4, LR+ of 22.6, and LR− of 0.057. Smartphone-based PPG applications achieved sensitivity of 92.0% and specificity of 91.9%. Apple Watch demonstrated sensitivity of 94.1% and specificity of 94.6%. Meta-regression revealed no statistically significant differences in diagnostic accuracy between device categories despite slightly higher point estimates for PPG-based smartwatches. No significant publication bias was detected (Deeks' test, p=0.18). Wearable devices demonstrate excellent diagnostic accuracy for AF detection, particularly smartphone-based ECG applications. These technologies support scalable AF screening and monitoring, although heterogeneity in study populations and diagnostic thresholds should be considered when applying these findings to routine clinical practice.
authors: Alina Abbas; Gauhar Hamid; Beesham Kumar; Sajida Moiz Hussain Qamari; Hira Riaz

title: Digital Health Among Educators: A Scoping Review
abstract: Background: Digital health technologies are increasingly used to support health management, monitoring, and health-related practices. Educators face a range of physical and mental health challenges, yet research on educators’ digital health remains fragmented across educational settings, geographical contexts, and forms of digital health management. This scoping review aimed to map and synthesize the literature on educators’ digital health by examining (1) digital health literacy and related competencies; (2) experiences with digital health technologies, and (3) factors influencing educators’ capacity to navigate the digital health ecosystem. Methods: The scoping review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. A systematic search was conducted for English written empirical peer-reviewed articles related to educators’ digital health on 8 June 2026. Results: A total of 31 studies were included. Three themes were identified. First, educators’ digital health literacy varied across demographic groups and educational settings in different geographical contexts and was associated with health behaviors and well-being. Second, educators engaged with mobile applications, wearable devices, AI-driven technologies, telehealth, and online programs. Third, educators’ engagement with these technologies was shaped by individual, technological, organizational, and contextual factors, including leadership support, privacy concerns, time pressure, and workplace culture. Conclusions: This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of educators’ digital health, covering digital health literacy, experiences with digital health technologies, and factors influencing engagement. The findings highlight uneven digital health literacy, varied experiences with digital technologies, and the importance of institutional support. They also underscore the need for targeted capacity-building initiatives, context-sensitive interventions, and further research to strengthen educators’ digital health.
authors: Weiyan Liao; Min Qiu; Dandan Wu; Xianhan Huang; Junjun Chen; Minjuan Wang; Hui Li

title: Digital transformation of clinical trials with remote patient monitoring solutions
abstract: Remote patient monitoring (RPM) is becoming increasingly feasible to implement in clinical trials. A framework is presented for developing RPM digital solutions incorporating the needs and perspectives of patients and healthcare professionals, and regulatory requirements/guidance. This framework is illustrated with recent examples of RPM deployments in the context of skin toxicities and stomatitis. Strategies to overcome challenges in the adoption of RPM solutions in clinical trials are discussed.
authors: Elisabeth Piault; Ramya Sita Palacholla; SIMON PULMAN‐JONES; Emmett Alton Sartor; Sergio Simön; Jill Bell

title: Disease progression shapes circadian and locomotor disruption in a model of multiple sclerosis
abstract: ABSTRACT Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune demyelinating disease of the central nervous system featuring a wide range of debilitating symptoms. Wearable activity recording devices have recently been adopted to improve symptom monitoring in MS, capturing symptoms related to sleep/wake cycles, circadian disruption, and fatigue. However, comparable measures of activity have yet been established in pre-clinical models of MS, the most widely used being experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE). We therefore sought to characterize changes in continual home-cage activity over the course of EAE, and establish whether home-cage monitoring can be used as an observer-independent measure of disease progression. Our results showed that locomotor activity in the mid-active/dark phase was most severely affected by EAE. Disrupted circadian (24-hour) activity was observed during the peak and onset stages of disease. Bout activity analysis revealed >40-minute long activity bouts as a sensitive indicator of non-motor symptoms independent of clinical score-based motor deficits. Current assessment of disease progression in EAE relies on clinical scores, which primarily assess motor deficits through visual observation prone to observer bias. Various computed activity parameters were found to be altered during key disease stages, suggesting that a combination of activity measures can serve as objective indicators of disease progression. Overall, our results show that home-cage activity effectively captures signs of non-motor symptoms in the EAE model of MS and can serve as an observer-independent measure of EAE disease progression.
authors: Vina Wenyu Li; Julia P. Segal; Nader Ghasemlou

title: DuBCG: Unlocking In-Home, Clinically Comparable mmWave Cardiac Monitoring for Co-Sleepers via Physics-Informed Spatial Sensing
abstract: Continuous, fine-grained cardiac monitoring during sleep is vital for cardiovascular health. Emerging as a promising alternative to cumbersome wearables, mmWave radar offers a contactless, privacy-preserving modality capable of capturing minute skin vibrations. However, transitioning mmWave radar from labs to real-world bedrooms remains challenging. Our rigorous empirical evaluation of state-of-the-art systems reveals a severe reliability gap: valid Inter-Beat Intervals (IBI) are captured for only 24%-42% of the night within an error threshold of 50 ms. Since clinical HRV analysis requires millisecond-level precision (e.g., RMSSD changes), such coarse and intermittent tracking renders existing methods medically insufficient. We attribute this failure to two fundamental hurdles: (i) instability driven by overwhelming respiratory interference and postural diversity, and (ii) signal entanglement in co-sleeping scenarios where angular separation defies hardware resolution. To bridge this gap, we present DuBCG. First, to tackle instability, we introduce a Head-Facing configuration to capture the Radar Ballistocardiogram (R-BCG). By leveraging the body's longitudinal recoil, this approach achieves orthogonal respiratory suppression and posture-invariant robustness. Second, to resolve entanglement, we propose the Multi-point Scattering Spatial Selectivity Model, theoretically proving that signal separability is achievable beyond physical resolution limits. Extensive real-world benchmarks demonstrate that DuBCG achieves a median IBI error of 8.4 ms—an 8× improvement over existing methods. This precision bridges the gap from existing intermittent monitoring to long-term, clinically comparable continuous HRV assessment.
authors: Xusheng Zhang; Duo Zhang; Jingfu Dong; Ruiqi Yu; Hongliu Yang; Junzhe Wang; Zizhou Fan; Z X Yin; Daqing Zhang

title: EETANet: A Human-Centered Intelligent Framework for Exercise Posture Quality Assessment
abstract: As physical rehabilitation and fitness monitoring increasingly shift toward autonomous and home-based healthcare, accurate and intelligent posture assessment systems have become essential for supporting personalized rehabilitation and clinical decision making. This study proposes the Edge-Enhanced Temporal Attention Network (EETANet), a human-centered ambient intelligence framework for automated exercise posture assessment and quality evaluation. The proposed framework is designed as an end-to-end computational pipeline that transforms raw multivariate motion signals into posture quality predictions using a compact set of core biomechanical posture features. The pipeline integrates data preprocessing, signal enhancement, multi-domain feature representation, and deep neural classification to capture the relevant spatial and temporal characteristics of human movement. Signal preprocessing incorporates data cleaning, z-score normalization, and Savitzky–Golay smoothing to improve signal quality while preserving temporal dynamics. Subsequently, informative posture representations are extracted through complementary temporal, spectral, and morphological descriptors, enabling the model to characterize motion variations associated with posture quality. These representations are learned using a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) classifier within the proposed EETANet framework to model nonlinear relationships between posture features and quality levels. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that the compact five-feature configuration achieves an accuracy of 90.83%, precision of 90.99%, recall of 90.83%, and F1-score of 90.84%. Notably, this compact configuration outperforms the corresponding 24-feature MLP configuration, which achieves 88.83% accuracy, indicating that a reduced set of core posture features can provide effective discriminative information while avoiding unnecessary feature redundancy. These findings demonstrate the potential of EETANet as an efficient framework for automated posture quality assessment in rehabilitation, fitness monitoring, and ambient healthcare applications.
authors: Esraa Hassan; Amira Samy Talaat; Aliya Aleryani; Rana Albelaihi; M. A. Elsabagh

title: EMERGING BLOOD-BASED BIOMARKERS IN ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE: FOCUS ON TAU, NFL, AND GFAP
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterised by progressive neurological disorder marked by the gradual decline of memory and cognitive abilities, affecting daily functioning and quality of life, imposing a leading socioeconomic disruption and healthcare burden.For the effective interventions, treatment and management, early diagnosis is important though conventional techniques like imaging and cerebrospinal fluid tests are invasive and costly.The inclusion of blood-based biomarkers provides a transformative approach for the early detection and disease monitoring.The purpose of this review is to critically evaluate the emerging evidence on Tau181, Tau217, NfL, and GFAP, aiming to delineate their role in reshaping future strategies for detection, monitoring, and intervention.Tau 217, among the tau isoforms biomarkers, demonstrated as a superior candidate with regards to diagnostic accuracy and stronger co-relation with Amyloid Positron Emission Tomography and disease progression, while compared to Tau 181.As the frontrunner biomarker, Tau 217 has emerged for AD with NfL and GFAP that provide precious complementary insights.Axonal degeneration is reflected by NfL while astrocytic activation is indicated by GFAP.Both serve as complementary markers.Combined multi-marker panels integrating these biomarkers enhanced sensitivity and specificity for AD detection.Therefore, these blood-based biomarkers provide a potential and revolutionary AD diagnosis and management by enabling non-invasive, early, and precise disease characterization.
authors: Sakina Turabi
venue: Indian Journal of Health Care Medical & Pharmacy Practice

title: EXTENT OF AWARENESS OF WEARABLE TECHNOLOGY DEVICES AND HEALTH BENEFITS AMONG LECTURERS OF EBONYI STATE UNIVERSITY, ABAKALIKI
abstract: The study investigated the extent of awareness of wearable fashion technology devices and their health benefits among lecturers of Ebonyi State University Abakaliki. Specifically, the study determined the extent of awareness of fashion clothing technology devices among lecturers at Ebonyi State University Abakaliki and the extent of health benefits of fashion clothing technology devices in the area of the study. Using a descriptive survey research design, the population of the study comprised nine hundred and sixty lecturers (960) in Ebonyi State University. A cluster sampling technique was adopted to select a sample of 100 lecturers. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire administered by hand to the study respondents. The data collected was analyzed using mean statistics. Findings revealed that the respondents were unaware of seven out of the ten identified fashion clothing devices; these include smart clothing, smart jewellery, smart rings, smart watches, and others. In the same vein, the respondents were unaware of seven out of the ten identified health benefits; these include control of hypertension, monitoring heart health, control of sleep, and reduction of anxiety, among others. Based on the findings, the study recommends that the university management and relevant public health organizations should initiate targeted digital health literacy programmes focused on clearly demonstrating the health benefits of these devices to lecturers. This is essential for converting low awareness into an active intention to utilize and eventual adoption.
authors: OKORO Victoria Ifeyinwa; Tessy EDE-AUGUSTINE; FRED Chidinma Vivian

title: Edge AI for Real-Time Facial Emotion Detection: A Raspberry Pi-Based Approach with CNN
abstract: Forecasts and analysis of human behavior and emotions have received a lot of development in the area of artificial intelligence. There are some potentials that edge computing in the field of human behavior and emotion forecasting and analysis. In this research, an autonomous edge computing system utilizing Raspberry Pi for real-time emotion detection, which can detect seven basic emotions, namely, happiness, anger, sadness, surprise, neutral, fear, and disgust, has been developed. The system extracts several feature sets such as edges, shapes, and textures, as well as landmarks of the face and upper body. A convolutional neural network classifier is applied to these feature sets to classify emotions in real time. A classification model has been trained using a manually developed dataset through the Data Collector class. Real-time testing of the system and evaluation of the system based on several criteria such as F-measure, accuracy, precision, and sensitivity have been performed. It has been found that the proposed system has up to 98% accuracy in real-time emotion detection. title: Edge AI on Constrained Devices for Binary Sleep-Wake Classification in Dynamic Environments
abstract: This paper presents an Edge AI-based system for detecting sleep and wake states in non-stationary mobile environments using resource-constrained embedded hardware. Conventional approaches relying on accelerometer-based activity metrics are highly susceptible to motion and vibration artifacts and are limited by strict compute and energy budgets of wearable and IoT devices. To address these challenges, a multimodal pipeline is designed and implemented on an ESP32-S3 microcontroller. The system combines inertial sensing for head movement analysis and visual pose classification. A dual-core architecture with FreeRTOS enables parallel execution of real-time data acquisition and on-device inference. Sleep detection follows a two-stage strategy: low-movement detection over a temporal window, followed by visual validation of poses. Experimental results show accuracies of 96.5% for motion-based detection and 89% for pose classification, yielding robust binary sleep-wake classification. Field tests confirmed feasibility in representative mobile scenarios. The results demonstrate that privacy-preserving, local sleep detection is achievable on edge hardware through careful co-design, while highlighting limitations in sensing intrusiveness, dataset scale, and system integration.
authors: Stefan Reitmann; Lena Oden

title: Effect of a wearable-based individualised multidomain lifestyle intervention on cognitive and physical function in older adults at risk of decline (INSPIOR): a single-centre, open-label, randomised controlled trial
abstract: Background Multidomain lifestyle programmes are the leading preventive approach to cognitive decline, but they rely on intensive face-to-face delivery that is hard to scale. We assessed whether an automated, wearable-based multidomain programme of activity, sleep, and optional nutrition prompts changed cognitive and physical function in at-risk older adults. Methods INSPIOR was a 6-month, single-centre, open-label, randomised controlled trial in Kashiwa, Japan. Adults aged 65–92 years with low body-mass index, pre-frailty, frailty, or sarcopenia-related decline were randomly assigned 1:1, in permuted blocks of four and without stratification, to the Fitbit-based intervention or an assessment-only control; allocation was not concealed and outcome assessors were not masked. Co-primary outcomes were the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), Trail Making Test (TMT), and skeletal muscle mass index (SMI), with no pre-specified hierarchy or multiplicity adjustment; analyses used intention-to-treat analysis of covariance with multiple imputation. This trial was registered with UMIN-CTR, UMIN000052707, and ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06135740. Findings Between Nov 8, 2023, and Jul 31, 2024, 355 participants were randomly assigned to the intervention group (n = 178) or control group (n = 177); all were analysed. Adjusted between-group differences were 0·58 MoCA points (95% CI 0·03–1·13; p=0·039; Holm-adjusted p=0·12), 0·16 s (−5·07 to 5·40; p=0·95) for TMT-A, 5·59 s (−3·88 to 15·05; p=0·25) for TMT-B, and −0·01 kg/m 2 (−0·09 to 0·07; p=0·88) for SMI. Mild skin irritation and dietary-recording stress occurred; no serious adverse event was intervention-related. Interpretation The intervention was associated with a small difference in a global cognitive screening score that did not survive multiplicity adjustment and is of uncertain clinical significance; the other two showed none. Larger, longer, masked trials are needed. Funding University of Tokyo–NH Foods Collaborative Research Programme, Google, Mitsui Fudosan.

title: Effect of neurodegenerative comorbidities on the risk of revision of knee joint replacements
abstract: Background: As populations age, both joint arthroplasty procedures and neurodegenerative diseases like Parkinson's disease (PD) are increasingly common. While general risk factors for knee prosthesis failure are well known, the specific impact of PD on implant survival is less clear. Motor symptoms of PD—rigidity, bradykinesia, postural instability—could impair joint function and raise complication risks. Understanding this relationship is crucial for optimizing care in these patients. Aim: This study investigated whether patients with preoperative PD have a greater risk of revision after total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Secondary aims included determining causes of failure, comparing outcomes with total hip arthroplasty (THA), and assessing biomechanical factors through computer modeling. Materials and Methods: A retrospective cohort analysis was conducted using the Emilia-Romagna Joint Replacement Registry (RIPO) and administrative databases. Patients with PD who underwent TKA from 2003–2018 were compared to matched controls without neurodegenerative diseases. The primary endpoint was revision for any reason. Kaplan–Meier survival analysis and multivariate Cox regression were applied. THA outcomes were analyzed in parallel, and biomechanical modeling was performed to simulate joint forces in PD. Results: Of 52,573 TKAs, 551 were in PD patients. The revision rate was significantly higher in the PD group (8.4% vs. 3.5%), with a 2.7-fold increased risk (HR 2.7; 95% CI 2.1–3.7). Septic loosening and implant dislocation were more common in PD patients, while aseptic loosening rates were similar. For THA, long-term revision rates did not differ, but PD patients had more early complications, notably periprosthetic fractures. Biomechanical modeling showed no significant differences in joint loading. Conclusions: Parkinson’s disease independently increases the risk of TKA failure, primarily due to systemic frailty, infection, trauma and not mechanical overload. Tailored perioperative and multidisciplinary approaches are needed to improve outcomes in this population.

title: Effects of eyelash extensions on the ocular surface: a systematic review of clinical outcomes and adverse events
abstract: Topic To synthesise evidence on ocular surface outcomes, symptoms and adverse events associated with semi-permanent eyelash extensions. Clinical relevance Eyelash extensions are applied beside the ocular surface; their clinical effects and associated complications warrant assessment. Methods PubMed, Ovid, CINAHL and Scopus were searched to 3 September 2026 without date or language restrictions for primary human studies reporting extension-specific ocular or periocular outcomes. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data and appraised studies using adapted Newcastle-Ottawa and Joanna Briggs Institute tools. Findings were synthesised narratively owing to heterogeneity. The review followed PRISMA 2020 and a prospectively registered protocol (PROSPERO CRD420261383757). Results Nineteen studies were included: two prospective studies, five cross-sectional studies, four case series and eight case reports. In one prospective study, corneal staining peaked at one hour and tear-film stability was lowest at one week after application. A matched comparator study found between-group differences in tear break-up time and clinical signs. One removal study showed improvement in symptomatic users. Four self-report studies included 845 users; symptom prevalence ranged from 26.8% to 97.5%, reflecting different samples and methods. Reported adverse events included keratoconjunctivitis, contact dermatitis, bacterial keratitis and eyelid leukoderma. Conclusion Eyelash extensions are associated with ocular surface disturbance and diverse adverse events, involving exposures beyond the adhesive. Small uncontrolled studies, self-reported surveys and case-level evidence limit certainty and prevent population-risk estimation. The findings support clinical enquiry about extension use in patients with unexplained ocular surface or perioperative symptoms.
authors: Minnan Al-Khafaji; Hussain Al-Hilali; Stephen Ong

title: ElectroCalm: Investigating User Experience and Physiological Responses to Multi-Node Transcutaneous Electrical Stimulation for Stress Modulation
abstract: Transcutaneous Electrical Stimulation (TES) for stress modulation has largely focused on vagus nerve stimulation at the neck, yet two questions remain underexplored: how users experience electrotactile sensations at this sensitive site, and whether electrotactile feedback itself can function as a haptic stress intervention. To investigate this gap, we applied an 8-node TES array to two body sites during a cognitively demanding 2-back task: the neck, a site used in prior vagal TES research for its anatomical proximity to the cervical vagus nerve, and the arm, the most common haptic wearable site, which primarily provides cutaneous electrotactile sensation without vagal access. In a usability study, both sites were rated as comparably comfortable without disrupting task performance, though the same stimulation was interpreted differently across sites. A second study assessing the physiological effects of active versus inactive stimulation under identical electrode attachment revealed that only neck TES produced cortical and autonomic changes consistent with stress modulation, while arm TES did not differ from inactive conditions. These findings suggest that neck TES can be acceptable despite the site's sensitivity, and that both the physiological effects and the sensory experience of TES depend on placement.
authors: Yoon Kyung Shon; Pablo Enrique Paredes

title: Electronic Devices and Digital Therapeutics in Neuromuscular Diseases: Narrative Review on Current Applications in Patients' Management and Pharmacovigilance
abstract: Digital health technologies have revolutionized the management of neuromuscular diseases (NMDs), offering novel opportunities for disease monitoring, rehabilitation, telemedicine, pharmacological research, and pharmacovigilance. This narrative review aims to provide an integrated overview of the current applications of digital health technologies in NMDs, highlighting their role in diagnosis, disease monitoring, rehabilitation, telemedicine, pharmacological research, and pharmacovigilance. Relevant articles were identified by interrogating PubMed using combinations of keywords including "neuromuscular diseases," "digital health," "digital therapeutics," "telemedicine," "wearable devices," "remote monitoring," "telerehabilitation," and "pharmacovigilance." This review describes how wearable devices, digital biomarkers, telemedicine platforms, and digital therapeutics can facilitate continuous and real-time monitoring of clinically relevant parameters, including muscle strength, mobility, physical activity, and disease progression. In addition, digital technologies support remote patient management, rehabilitation programs, early detection of clinical changes, and the development of personalized therapeutic interventions. Emerging evidence also suggests that digital health tools may improve the design and conduct of clinical trials, enhance the collection and analysis of real-world data and patient-reported outcomes, and contribute to more effective pharmacovigilance strategies. Despite challenges on data privacy, digital literacy, integration into healthcare system and the need for large-scale or long-term clinical trials, the integration of digital therapeutics, digital biomarkers, and pharmacovigilance frameworks represents a promising and still underexplored area of research that may substantially contribute to the development of precision medicine approaches in NMDs.

title: Emergent blink rate in early childhood is associated with neural origins of executive function
abstract: Abstract Executive function develops rapidly in early childhood and predicts later success in life, yet its neurobiological correlates during this period remain poorly understood. In adults, executive function is supported by prefrontal–striatal circuits under neuromodulatory control, including dopamine. Here, we show that spontaneous eye-blink rate (sEBR), a physiological output influenced by neuromodulatory systems, is associated with the developmental trajectory of executive function and prefrontal functional differentiation. We used fNIRS to monitor prefrontal cortex (PFC) activation in 113 children (35–80 months) during a cognitive flexibility task. With increasing age, the children’s task performance improved, and their PFC activation showed greater right-hemisphere and dorsal bias, reflecting functional differentiation. Importantly, higher sEBR was also associated with this right-dorsal PFC activation and with better task performance. The current findings demonstrate that emergent sEBR is associated with the neural origins of executive function development in young children. This highlights the potential of sEBR to serve as a unique and previously unrecognised indicator of this critical developmental neural mechanism.
authors: Ryuta Kuwamizu; Nozomi Yamamoto; Kota Otani; Yusuke Moriguchi

title: Enhancing Maternal and Child Health in Rural Areas Through AI and Mobile Health Solutions
abstract: Enhancing maternal and child health in rural areas presents significant challenges due to geographic isolation, limited healthcare infrastructure, and a shortage of medical professionals. This abstract explores the transformative potential of artificial intelligence (AI) and mobile health (mHealth) solutions in addressing these challenges and improving health outcomes for mothers and children in underserved regions. AI technologies offer robust tools for predictive analytics, decision support, and personalized care. In rural healthcare settings, AI can enhance maternal and child health by providing real-time insights into patient data, predicting potential complications, and supporting personalized treatment plans. For instance, AI algorithms can analyze data from electronic health records to identify high-risk pregnancies, enable early intervention, and optimize resource allocation. Furthermore, AI-driven chatbots and virtual health assistants can offer remote consultations and health education, reducing the need for travel and making healthcare more accessible. Mobile health solutions, including smartphones and wearable devices, play a critical role in bridging gaps in rural healthcare. mHealth applications facilitate remote monitoring of maternal and child health metrics, such as blood pressure, glucose levels, and fetal heart rates. These applications can alert healthcare providers to potential issues, enabling timely interventions. Mobile platforms also support health education, offering resources on prenatal care, nutrition, and childhood vaccinations, thus empowering individuals with knowledge and tools to manage their health proactively. By integrating AI and mHealth technologies, rural healthcare systems can achieve significant improvements in maternal and child health outcomes. These technologies provide essential support in areas with limited medical resources, enhance access to quality care, and enable more effective management of health conditions. However, successful implementation requires addressing barriers such as technology adoption, data privacy concerns, and infrastructure limitations. In conclusion, leveraging AI and mHealth solutions holds promise for transforming maternal and child health care in rural areas, offering innovative approaches to overcoming existing challenges and enhancing overall health outcomes

title: Enhancing breast cancer detection: A CycleGAN-enhanced approach with enhancing sparrow search optimization
abstract: Breast cancer remains one of the leading causes of mortality among women worldwide, necessitating the development of highly accurate and computationally efficient diagnostic methods. Recent advancements in artificial intelligence and deep learning have provide the way for more reliable automated systems to assist in tumor classification. In this study, a novel hybrid classification framework called Cycle-consistent Adversarial Adaptation Network with Enhancing Sparrow Search Optimization (Cy2AN-ESSO) is proposed to improve the diagnostic performance for breast cancer detection using two benchmark datasets: BreakHis and TCGA-BRCA. The proposed approach begins with pre-processing using Robust Double-Weighted Guided Image Filtering (RD-WGIF) to enhance image quality and remove noise, ensuring that relevant features are preserved for subsequent stages. For segmentation, the Memory Efficient Vision Transformer (MEVis-Tr) is employed to accurately identify and isolate tumor regions, providing a reliable foundation for feature extraction. Feature extraction and classification uses the Multimodal Cycle-Triplet Adaptation Attention Network (MCT2AN), which integrates Triplet Attention Network (TAN) for feature extraction and the Cycle-consistent Adversarial Adaptation Network (C-2AN) for robust classification. The process is optimized using Enhancing Sparrow Search Optimization (ESSO) to refine decision boundaries and improve learning accuracy. The experimental results demonstrate that Cy2AN-ESSO demonstrated improved classification performance than current techniques for measuring accuracy and precision as well as recall and sensitivity and specificity and F1-score. Both accuracies and precisions and recalls reach 98.4%, 98.6% and 98.8% respectively for BreakHis data as well as TCGA-BRCA subtypes IDC, ILC, DCIS and LCIS. The proposed framework provided better classification accuracy and computational efficiency over the test datasets. More validation is needed on independent clinical cohorts before clinical use. Using Cy2AN-ESSO enables robust breast cancer classification that shows strong potential for accurate early disease diagnosis.
authors: Megha Sinha; M.SivaramKrishnan; B. Veeramalini; Nivethitha Thangavelsamy; D. Kavitha; M. Siva Ramkumar; Khayala Mammadova; Kasim Sakran Abass; Mekhrbonu Rakhimova; Mohammad Khishe

title: Environmental Scan of Public Health Directives During COVID-19: A View Through the Lens of Children With Complex Care Needs and Their Families
abstract: Background: The COVID-19 pandemic shaped childhood globally. The experiences of vulnerable children in Canada’s Maritime provinces reveal important lessons about equity, resilience, and the unintended consequences of public health directives. Public health restrictions were enacted in the early days of COVID-19. At-risk populations such as children with complex care needs (CCN) were among those most impacted by health system changes due to COVID-19. To better understand how COVID-19 public health measures impacted children with CCN who were highly susceptible to the virus and associated disruptions, we conducted an environmental scan to map changes in COVID-19 public health directives and services impacting children with CCN. Methods: We systematically retrieved government news releases communicating new or changing COVID-19 public health directives published March 1, 2020-March 31, 2022. All directives and service changes in the health and education sectors were included. Directives were divided into 13 categories co-developed with parent and decision-maker partners, and we identified whether directives included support measures relevant to children with CCN. Results: The environmental scan revealed that children with CCN were largely overlooked in COVID-19 directives across the Maritime provinces. We identified 699 public health directives and services changes. Fewer than 2.2% of COVID-19 directives explicitly referenced children with CCN, with most guidance focusing on general social restrictions, vaccinations, and education/daycare. Mental health and well-being were also rarely addressed (13 directives). Conclusion: The Maritimes’ predominately rural and geographically dispersed population exacerbates the inequities experienced by children with CCN, offering insights relevant to other regions about the unintended consequences of broad public health policies delivered to heterogeneous populations. Examining this data through the lens of children with CCN and their families can inform recommendations to better support this vulnerable population in future public health emergencies.
authors: Janet Curran; Holly McCulloch; Catie Johnson; Jennifer Lane; Leah Boulos; Lisa Keeping‐Burke; Mary-Ann Standing; Julie Clegg; Robyn M. Kydd; Helen W. L. Wong; Kristy Hancock; Margie Lamb

title: Establishment of Standardized Normative Reference Values for Pressure-Based Gait Analysis in the Healthy Korean Population: A Nationwide Multi-Center Registry Study
abstract: Objective Normative gait data for Asian populations remain scarce, and Western reference values may not apply to Koreans.We aimed to establish nationwide reference values for pressure-based gait analysis in healthy Korean adults.Methods Healthy community-dwelling adults (N = 612, aged 20 to 80s) were enrolled at 11 randomly selected centers using quota-based recruitment across 18 sex-and age-stratified cohorts.Spatiotemporal gait parameters, classified into five domains, were recorded on a pressure-based electronic walkway.Gait speed cutoffs were defined at -1.0 and -1.5 standard deviations (SD) below age-and sex-specific means.Age-group differences were evaluated using ANOVA and linear mixed-effects models adjusted for height and study site. ResultsGait velocity followed a normal distribution in all strata.In both sexes, older age groups showed lower Pace domain values and higher step length variability, which remained significant after adjustment for height and study site.In contrast, Rhythm domain parameters and asymmetry indices were preserved across age groups.Cutoffs were provided at -1.5 SD for normally distributed parameters and the 7th percentile for non-normally distributed parameters.Conclusions This is the first nationwide multicenter reference dataset for spatiotemporal gait parameters in healthy Korean adults across the full adult age range.These population-specific values provide a practical baseline for interpreting pressure-based gait analysis and for applying gait-based clinical criteria in Korea.

title: Estimating Heart Failure Health Status From Multimodal Wearables: Implementation of a Feature-Engineering Framework for KCCQ-12 Prediction
abstract: Routine monitoring of symptom burden and quality of life in heart failure (HF) patients is limited by intermittent sampling of validated instruments, such as the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ-12). As more wearable devices track physiological measures in real-world settings than ever before, we propose an exploratory implementation of a feature-engineering framework to bridge this sampling gap, approximating KCCQ-12 scores and patient health status from wearable features. In this narrative, we processed data from the 8-week multicenter observational study of HF patients (NYHA class I-III) wearing Everion® multisensor smartwatches: "Evaluating Mobile Health Tool Use for Capturing Patient-centered Outcomes Measures in HF Patients" (NCT04191356). Then, LASSO logistic regression was applied for feature selection, followed by binary classification and linear mixed-effects modeling to predict KCCQ-12 scores. Among patients generating sufficient data (n = 59), there were 173 unique KCCQ-12 observations. From 7,235 candidate features, LASSO retained 88 predictors (Supplementary Table 1), including the top predictors: p6MWD (positive), daily steps/walking time (positive), nocturnal respiratory variability (negative), and patient-reported dyspnea (negative). Binary classification models achieved test AUC=0.77 (sensitivity 91%, specificity 63%) and linear mixed-effects models produced a RMSE of 14.7 (R 2 = 0.58) for predicting patient health status and continuous KCCQ-12 scores, respectively. A patient-level split analysis revealed decreased model performance (RMSE = 18.9; R 2 =0.33), suggesting limited generalizability to new individuals. This exploratory implementation with small sample size outlines wearable features that warrant future investigation for KCCQ-12 score monitoring and offers early-stage lessons for assessing such features as proxies of KCCQ-12 scores in real-world settings.
authors: Christopher John McLeod; Charles J. Bruce; Kuldeep Singh Rajput; Joseph S. Ross; Sy Jackie Lou Velarde; Felis Dwiyasa; Chen Hao; Yan He; Pyae Phyo Tun; Stephanie J. Zawada; Maulik D. Majmudar

title: Evaluating CNN Architectures for Optimal Deployment in Plant Disease Detection Systems
abstract: This paper presents a web-based plant disease detection system presented in this study which classifies plant diseases from uploaded photos using deep learning techniques. Users can upload photos of their plants to the portal, and those photos are evaluated to find diseases. For picture categorization, the system uses Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), more especially the VGG-16 and VGG-19 models. The effectiveness of these two models in detecting plant illnesses was the main subject of a comparison study. VGG-19's superior disease detection accuracy led to its selection as the best model for this application. For farmers and agricultural specialists, the system offers a complete answer by not only identifying the ailment but also suggesting treatments. The potential of AI-based methods to enhance plant health monitoring and support precision agriculture is demonstrated by this study.
authors: V. Nivethitha; S. Rohith; S. K. Miruthula; J. Sanjay

title: Evaluation of the Perimouse Online Suprathreshold Visual Field Test for Glaucoma Screening in a Chinese Population: A Comparison with the Humphrey Field Analyzer
abstract: Purpose: To evaluate the diagnostic performance and spatial agreement of an online suprathreshold perimeter (Perimouse) compared with the Humphrey Field Analyzer (HFA) for detecting glaucomatous visual field defects. Patients and Methods: In this prospective comparative study, 174 participants (283 eyes with open-angle glaucoma or healthy controls) underwent Perimouse suprathreshold program and HFA. Abnormal points (missed stimuli in Perimouse; points with P< 0.5% on HFA total deviation map) were compared. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Point-wise performance used neural network–derived area under the curve (AUC) and Cohen’s κ. Results: Perimouse abnormal-point counts were correlated with HFA abnormal-point counts ( r = 0.88, P < 0.001) and negatively correlated with HFA mean deviation ( r = − 0.80, P < 0.001). The intraclass correlation coefficient for abnormal-point counts between Perimouse and HFA was 0.93, and Bland–Altman analysis showed a mean bias of 0.73 abnormal points, with 95% limits of agreement ranging from − 10.70 to 12.17. A cutoff of five abnormal points achieved 85.9% sensitivity and 97.9% specificity (AUC = 0.97), with performance improving with disease severity. Point-wise κ values ranged from 0.32 to 0.78 (AUC, 0.67– 0.96). The test duration for Perimouse was 2.64 ± 1.83 minutes. Conclusion: Perimouse demonstrated reasonable overall diagnostic accuracy for detecting HFA-defined visual field defects. Diagnostic performance was higher for moderate and advanced glaucomatous defects than for early defects, with variable point-wise agreement with HFA. Perimouse may serve as a rapid, adjunctive tool for preliminary functional screening of glaucomatous visual field loss. Keywords: glaucoma, visual field tests, screening, telemedicine
authors: Xiaoyuan Shen; Zidong Chen; Kaixin Tan; Yanmei Fan; Pingping Liu; Haorui Wang; Jing Samantha Pan; Yangfan Yang; Minbin Yu

title: Evolution of evidence-based medicine: toward digital evidence ecosystems and artificial intelligence
abstract: Evidence-based medicine (EBM) has transformed clinical decision-making by integrating the best available research evidence with clinical expertise and patients’ values and preferences. Over the past three decades, EBM has evolved from the critical appraisal of individual studies into a broader framework encompassing evidence synthesis, clinical practice guidelines, assessment of evidence certainty, research transparency, and shared decision-making. Despite these advances, contemporary EBM faces important challenges, including the rapidly increasing volume of research, delays in evidence synthesis and implementation, limited applicability of randomized controlled trials to heterogeneous real-world populations, and difficulties in individualizing population-level evidence. Emerging approaches—including real-world evidence, living evidence, learning health systems, precision medicine, and artificial intelligence (AI)—offer opportunities to address these limitations. Together, these approaches may enable a transition from static to continuously updated evidence, from population-average to more personalized evidence, and from a linear evidence pipeline to a learning evidence ecosystem in which clinical practice both uses and generates evidence. AI may further accelerate evidence retrieval, synthesis, updating, and individualized decision support, while introducing challenges related to reliability, bias, transparency, reproducibility, and accountability. Next-generation EBM should therefore be conceptualized not as a replacement for traditional EBM but as its evolution into a digitally connected, continuously learning evidence ecosystem. In the AI era, the foundational principles of EBM—source verification, critical appraisal, uncertainty assessment, integration of patient preferences, and accountable human judgment—will become increasingly important.
