title: Long-term quality of life, rehospitalization risks, and economic viability of remote cardiac rehabilitation: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background Although remote cardiac rehabilitation (RCR) is a promising alternative to traditional center-based care, evidence regarding its exact impact on health-related quality of life (HRQoL), cardiovascular safety, and economic viability remains fragmented, necessitating a comprehensive synthesis to guide clinical implementation. Objectives This systematic review and meta-analysis aim to evaluate the HRQoL, cardiovascular safety, and economic viability of RCR versus standard center-based care in cardiovascular disease, with subgroup analyses based on follow-up duration and high-risk patient cohorts. Methods Literature searches were conducted across multiple databases, including PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library, supplemented by manual screening of relevant references to identify clinical studies on RCR up to July 2026. Two independent review teams performed data extraction and risk of bias assessment using the RevMan software. Meta-analyses were conducted employing random-effects models to calculate pooled effect sizes with corresponding 95% confidence intervals. Heterogeneity was assessed using the Cochrane Q test and I 2 statistic, and potential publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots and Egger's test. To evaluate the robustness of the pooled results and explore potential heterogeneity, subgroup and fixed-effects sensitivity analyses were conducted, supplemented by trial sequential analysis (TSA). Results A total of 45 randomized controlled trials were included in this meta-analysis. RCR significantly improved HRQoL across multiple scales (MacNew: MD = 0.17; MLHFQ: MD = −5.38; P < 0.05), while maintaining SF-36 and HADS outcomes comparable to standard care. Exploratory analyses indicated statistically significant improvements in mental health at 6 months (MD = 1.73, P = 0.03) and physical functioning at 12 months (MD = 1.48, P = 0.0002). Regarding cardiovascular safety, RCR was not associated with a statistically significant increase in the risk of MACEs, all-cause mortality, or adverse events ( P > 0.05) compared to conventional care. RCR significantly reduced the risk of cardiac rehospitalization (RR = 0.70, P = 0.01), with exploratory stratified analyses indicating that this favorable association was evident in the hardware-integrated interventions subgroup (RR = 0.59, P = 0.02) and 6-month observation subgroup (RR = 0.38, P < 0.00001), alongside a non-significant numerical protective trend among high-risk patients (RR: 0.59 vs. 0.74, P = 0.15). The economic viability of RCR remains uncertain, critically depending on initial setup outlays, patient scaling, and subsequent healthcare utilization. Conclusions RCR may serve as an effective and safe alternative to conventional care that improves physical and psychological well-being, was associated with a lower risk of cardiac rehospitalization, and may provide economic value in certain healthcare systems. Systematic Review Registration: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261374977 , PROSPERO CRD420261374977.
authors: Hui Pei; Hengrui Li; Miaomiao Hu; Boyan Liu; Dali Hu; Yuanmin Li; Qiang Feng Xiao

title: LukeNet: A lightweight CNN integrated with an XAI model for Smart acute lymphoblastic leukemia detection and management
abstract: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) patients require early, accurate detection to enable timely treatment and effective patient management. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is well-suited for creating an end-to-end enabling environment for ALL detection and classification. However, most CNN-based ALL detection systems are theoretical and unsuitable for deployment on edge devices due to high computational demands. The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT)-enabled devices offer an opportunity to monitor ALL patients in real time. Wearables that track temperature, heart rate, oxygen saturation, and activity can deliver critical data to support timely clinical intervention and improve patient outcomes. In smart IoMT environments, a lightweight CNN is essential because connected devices often operate under limited computational power, memory, and latency constraints. To address this need, this study proposes LukeNet, a lightweight CNN integrated with explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) for an IoMT-based SMART Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia Detection and Management System. Trained on three (3) ALL datasets and five-fold cross-validation, LukeNet achieved an impressive 99% model accuracy as well as 99% unseen test accuracy, which is higher than six state-of-the-art (SOTA) CNNs, such as DenseNet121, MobileNet, ResNet50, InceptionV3, Xception, and VGG16, as well as transfer learning models. Furthermore, LukeNet was compared with two ensemble models. In addition, explainable AI methods are integrated to highlight relevant regions in microscopic images. The novelty of this study lies in the architecture of LukeNet, which balances model depth and computational efficiency by using depthwise separable convolutions, mitigates the risk of gradient loss in deeper layers, and provides strong global and local feature extraction capabilities.
authors: Md Taimur Ahad

title: Lung Disease Detection and Classification Based on AI, Deep Learning and Machine Learning: A Comprehensive Survey
abstract: Background: Lung diseases significantly contribute to substantial global morbidity and mortality, which pose considerable diagnostic challenges. Manual analysis of medical images like chest X-rays and CT scans is often subject to human error, requires specialized expertise, and is time-consuming. To build fully automated systems that analyze the information contained in medical images, robust and efficient algorithms are required. In response, artificial intelligence (AI), especially deep learning (DL), has become an innovative approach that shows excellent results for the automation of lung disease detection and classification. Objective: Following a strict systematic literature review methodology, this study aims to provide an extensive survey of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and deep learning approaches for the detection and classification of lung diseases. Methods: The survey discusses over 30 reported approaches in the field. These approaches have been categorized and evaluated based on the methodology and reported results. We also discuss relevant datasets and benchmarking that have been used in state-of-the-art models and have undergone peer review. Results: The survey reveals a strong trend towards powerful ensemble and hybrid architectures like ResNet, VGG, RVCNet, Vision Transformers (ViTs), etc., and their variations. These models have achieved high accuracy for detecting and classifying various diseases. Conclusions: This work highlights the advancement and recent progress in using AI and deep learning to detect and classify lung diseases while addressing identified gaps and the limitations related to dataset availability, standardization, and imbalance, in addition to model transparency and the computational cost, providing a prospective roadmap for further research or implementation.
authors: Harith S. Hassan; Sinan A. Naji; Abdullah Ghanim Jaber

title: MSAFE: A Monitoring, Modeling and Prediction Framework for Smart Manufacturing Systems
abstract: Capturing a consistent global state is a significant challenge when it comes to cyber-physical systems (CPS) and, in particular, smart manufacturing systems. Three critical challenges stand in the way of obtaining such a global view: (i) multiple controllers in one system, (ii) modeling of programmable logic controllers (PLCs), especially multiple ones and (iii) multiple products being manufactured at the same time, say on different parts of the plant. In this paper, we introduce the Manufacturing State Auto-Transformation Framework (MSAFE) to not just overcome the above issues but also predict the future states of a manufacturing system. MSAFE uses a combination of the code from PLCs, system topology models and pilot runtime data to generate a “State Progress Table” (SPT) that is then used to: (i) reconstruct the existing state of the system and (ii) extrapolate future behavior. By associating runtime (sensor, actuator) data from real plants with static information (code, topology models), our framework can reconstruct current and future states for the plant (as well as individual components). The states predicted by MSAFE can be used to compute additional information, e.g., throughput, end-to-end latencies, number of live widgets, etc. Using two realistic testbeds and thirteen third-party PLC code samples, we demonstrate the effectiveness of MSAFE at (a) recreating current states of manufacturing systems and (b) predicting future states of — both for entire plants and individual components
authors: Bin-Chou Kao
venue: Illinois Digital Environment for Access to Learning and Scholarship (University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign)

title: Machine Learning Algorithms for Predicting Psychostimulant Intoxication in Emergency Department Patients: A Multicenter Study
abstract: Introduction: Psychostimulant detection rates among emergency department (ED) patients presenting with suspected substance intoxication are low and are influenced by limited access to confirmatory testing, insufficient clinical information, and variability in physician experience. These challenges often result in high false-positive rates and unnecessary resource use. We hypothesized that machine learning (ML) algorithms could maintain reliable diagnostic performance across a temporal validation cohort and perform comparably to physicians with varying experience levels. Methods: This multicenter study prospectively enrolled ED patients with suspected substance intoxication between March 2019 and January 2020. We chronologically partitioned data into a training set (March–October 2019) and a temporal validation cohort (November 2019–January 2020) to assess model generalizability. After determining psychostimulant intoxication via liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry from urine samples, we trained the ML algorithms using the confirmed positive cases. The primary outcome was the diagnostic discrimination of the models, measured by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) in the temporal validation cohort. Secondary outcomes included model accuracy, the Youden index, and a comparative assessment of sensitivity and specificity relative to five physicians of varying experience levels. Results: Among 1,382 patients (mean age 43.8 [standard deviation 19.2] years; 55.3% male), 302 patients (21.9%) had confirmed psychostimulant intoxication, primarily involving (meth)amphetamines (134 [44.4%]), cathinones (107 [35.4%]), and ketamine (97 [32.1%]). In the temporal validation cohort (n = 382), the ML models demonstrated consistent performance, with AUCs ranging from 0.786 to 0.836. The primary outcome was met by the top-performing extreme gradient boosting (XGB) model (AUC, 0.836, 95% CI, 0.785-0.882; accuracy, 0.866 (95% CI, 0.838-0.895); and Youden index, 0.590 (95% CI, 0.480-0.694). To evaluate secondary outcomes, the XGB model’s predictive accuracy was evaluated against 5 emergency physicians. The model surpassed the junior emergency physicians in both specificity (0.910 vs 0.633-0.867) and sensitivity (0.681 vs 0.500-0.633); its specificity was comparable to that of the senior emergency physicians (0.900-0.933). Conclusion: Machine learning models provide reliable diagnostic utility for identifying psychostimulant intoxication, achieving performance comparable to senior emergency physicians. While moderate sensitivity (0.389–0.708) limits their role as standalone rule-out tools, their high specificity provides a standardized tool to assist clinical decision-making and reduce diagnostic uncertainty in the fast-paced ED setting.
authors: Jiun‐Hao Yu; Yueh-Peng Chen; Chih-Huang Hsieh; Yu-Jang Su; Hsien-Yi Chen; Chih-Chuan Lin; Te-I Weng; Cheng-Chung Fang; Sung-Wei Liu; Yen-Chia Chen; Yu-Cheng Pei; Kuan-Fu Chen

title: Machine Learning Augmented Detection of Trace Explosives on Surfaces Using Active Longwave Infrared Imaging
abstract: There is a need for rapid non-contact detection of trace explosives on arbitrary surfaces for applications such as checkpoint screening and post-blast forensics. In this work, active longwave infrared imaging, using a tunable quantum cascade laser light source, is shown to be able to detect three common explosives on typical luggage material substrates at surface concentrations as low as 230 ng/cm 2 . Use of a random forest machine learning algorithm, trained using synthetically produced spectra, allows performance beyond predicted limitations of speckle noise. The random forest algorithm further allows discrimination against ambient dust without specific training. Use of high collection angles reduces the dynamic range requirement of the system without impairing performance. Potential system improvements are discussed to meet the area coverage rate needs of several applications.
authors: William M. Barney; Mitesh Amin; William D. Herzog; Jason M. Jong; Max Kenngott; Keegan Quigley; Patrick Wen; Roderick Russell Kunz

title: Machine Learning Detection of Revenue Leakage From Clinical Coding, Claims, and Reimbursement Discrepancies
abstract: Healthcare revenue cycles increasingly depend on accurate clinical documentation, coding, claims processing, and reimbursement, yet their complexity creates substantial opportunities for revenue leakage. Coding inaccuracies, incomplete documentation, claim denials, underpayments, contractual inconsistencies, and reimbursement discrepancies can reduce healthcare organizations’ financial performance while increasing administrative burden. Conventional audit approaches are often retrospective, rule-based, and resource-intensive, limiting their ability to identify complex or evolving patterns across large volumes of clinical and financial data. This study examines a machine learning framework for detecting revenue leakage by integrating clinical coding, claims, payment, denial, and reimbursement information. The framework applies supervised and anomaly-detection techniques to identify discrepancies between expected and received reimbursement, coding irregularities, recurrent denial patterns, and financially significant claim anomalies. Predictive features incorporate diagnosis and procedure codes, billed charges, payer characteristics, reimbursement amounts, denial reasons, and historical payment behavior. Model performance can be evaluated using precision, recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC, and financial recovery indicators. The proposed approach supports risk-based claim prioritization, earlier identification of revenue loss, targeted auditing, and data-driven revenue-cycle management across healthcare reimbursement systems.
authors: Jine Laner
venue: International Journal of Research Publication and Reviews

title: Machine Learning and Deep Learning for Early Disease Detection Across Modalities: A Comprehensive Review of Methods, Applications, and Clinical Translation.
abstract: Early disease detection is not a single classification problem. It includes population screening, presymptomatic risk estimation, identification of early pathological change, and detection of disease before conventional clinical recognition. Machine learning and deep learning systems approach these targets through medical images, physiological signals, longitudinal health records, molecular measurements, wearable sensors, and multimodal combinations. This survey organizes the evidence around the complete decision pathway linking the clinical target, data generation process, preprocessing, representation, model, validation design, reported performance, methodological limitation, and level of clinical translation. The analysis distinguishes early detection from ordinary diagnosis, prognosis, and progression prediction, as merging these tasks can make apparently strong results clinically misleading. Across modalities, deep learning is most useful when spatial, temporal, or cross-modal representations must be learned from sufficiently large and representative data. Traditional machine learning remains competitive when cohorts are modest, clinically meaningful variables are available, or transparent feature-level reasoning is required. The evidence also shows that performance is strongly influenced by patient-level separation, cohort construction, prevalence, label definition, missingness, external validation, calibration, and the handling of uncertain cases; therefore, high discrimination on an internal split cannot establish clinical utility. The survey further examines the gap between retrospective model development and deployment, emphasizing temporal and external validation, prospective workflow evaluation, decision thresholds, false negative consequences, demographic robustness, interpretability, and post-deployment monitoring. The resulting synthesis provides a modality-aware and clinically grounded framework for deciding not only which algorithms perform well but also what their results mean and what evidence remains necessary before they can support early clinical action.
authors: Ahlem Aziz; Seydi Kacmaz; Azam Isam Abdulkareem Aladwani

title: Machine Learning for Noninvasive Diagnosis of Neurodegenerative Diseases Using Retinal and Optic Nerve Imaging: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: Neurodegenerative disorders, including Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and multiple sclerosis, encompass a wide range of chronic conditions with irreversible damage to the central nervous system. Current diagnostic workups of these disorders rely on invasive, time-consuming, and costly tests, such as magnetic resonance imaging and cerebrospinal fluid analysis, preventing accurate decision-making and timely therapeutic interventions. The retina is an extension of the central nervous system; thus, retinal imaging, which is a noninvasive and easily accessible tool, provides a unique window to study brain pathologies. There is a great body of evidence suggesting that neurodegenerative disorders are associated with various structural and vascular problems within the retina. Notably, training machine learning models with retinal images has yielded high levels of accuracy in classifying neurodegenerative diseases, encouraging a new era for early and automated diagnosis of these disorders. This article reviews studies that use such models for classifying these disorders.
authors: Ali Aghababaei; Masoud Etemadifar; Amir Atapour-Abarghouei; William Innes; Masoud Aghsaei Fard; Friedemann Paul; Hossein Rabbani; Rahele Kafieh

title: Mapping Conventional and Emerging Sensors for Neonatal Physiological Monitoring: A Scoping Review of the Technological Transition and Validation Gaps
abstract: Continuous physiological monitoring is a cornerstone of neonatal intensive care. Yet, current NICU sensing technologies- adhesive electrodes, contact pulse oximeters, and wired thermistors- carry well-documented clinical limitations, including adhesive-related skin injury, restricted mobility, and interference with family-centered developmental care protocols. Although the past decade has witnessed a proliferation of alternative sensing proposals spanning flexible electronics, wireless wearable platforms, and fully contactless approaches, this body of research remains fragmented across distinct technical communities, and no comprehensive mapping of the conventional and emerging sensor ecosystem has been published to date. To address this gap, this scoping review followed the PRISMA-ScR guidelines and was structured around a Population, Concept, and Context (PCC) framework: Population, neonates admitted to the NICU; Concept, sensors used in physiological monitoring equipment; Context, the hospital neonatal intensive care setting. Searches in PubMed, Scopus, and IEEE Xplore retrieved 197 records, reduced to 166 unique records after deduplication; 40 studies published between 2016 and 2026 were included following a two-stage screening process. The synthesized evidence reveals that emerging technologies predominate (26 of 40, 65%), with optical transduction as the leading physical principle (15 of 40) and flexible or wearable form factors already outnumbering rigid designs (23 of 40 versus 9 of 40). Research activity concentrates heavily on respiratory rate (20 of 40) and heart rate (18 of 40), while electroencephalography and transcutaneous bilirubin each appear in only 1 of 40 studies and blood pressure exclusively as a secondary channel in multiparameter platforms (3 of 40), gaps independently corroborated by contemporaneous systematic reviews of the same domain. Regulatory transparency is markedly absent, with 85% of included studies making no mention of regulatory status, reflecting the field's predominantly proof-of-concept readiness. These findings delineate the current technological frontier of neonatal sensing, identify priority targets for future complementary searches, and underscore the urgent need for standardized validation frameworks to enable direct cross-technology comparisons in subsequent reviews.
authors: Gabriela Cianciarullo; Salvador Pinillos Gimenes; Carlos Eduardo Thomaz

title: Measurement-Error-Aware Causal Distributed-Lag Quantile Modeling of Indoor Air Pollution and Short-Term Lung-Function Deterioration
abstract: Low-cost indoor air-quality sensors could support personalized asthma prevention, but their nonlinear measurement error, delayed exposure effects, time-varying confounding, and heterogeneous lower-tail responses limit risk estimation. We present CAUSALQUANT-ASTHMA, a measurement-error-aware causal quantile distributed-lag framework for short-horizon peak expiratory flow analysis. Sparse reference measurements train a nonlinear calibration model; stabilized sequential generalized-propensity weights address measured exposure assignment; and a susceptibility-modulated, smooth, noncrossing quantile model estimates lag-specific and sustained-exposure contrasts. Because no authorized cohort simultaneously provided dense indoor sensing, reference co-location, and outcome-compatible longitudinal data, evaluation used five semi-synthetic panels with known counterfactual truth, 150 patients and 12,600 patient-days per realization. Across eight methods, CAUSALQUANT achieved a dose-response integrated absolute error of 0.304 plus or minus 0.094, improving 24.2 percent over the strongest measurement-error and propensity-weighted baseline. It also obtained the lowest overall pinball loss, 1.065, while maintaining zero quantile crossings and 78.1 percent coverage for the nominal 80 percent interval. Sensor calibration reduced held-out exposure RMSE by 33.7 percent. Stress tests quantified degradation under sensor noise, missing personal measurements, and hidden confounding. These findings establish methodological feasibility and reproducibility, not clinical effectiveness; prospective, governance-approved external validation is required before patient-level interpretation or deployment.
authors: Shayma Alkobaisi; Anas Ali

title: Mechanically Robust and Self‐Healing Sustainable Solid‐State Ion‐Conductive Elastomer for Near‐Infrared‐Driven Noncontact Sensing
abstract: ABSTRACT Stretchable solid‐state ionic conductive elastomers (SICEs), serving as essential materials for ionotronic devices, exhibit great promise in emerging applications in electronic skin, soft robotics, especially in wearable sensors. Nevertheless, the development of such materials with high strength, self‐healing, and ionic conductivity remains highly desirable yet challenging, as simultaneously integrating these properties is often hindered by intrinsic trade‐offs among molecular chain dynamics and desired functions. Herein, we develop a SICE featuring a natural rubber‐based segregated network, in which latex particles are encapsulated by carboxylated cellulose nanofibers, polydopamine, and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide. The formation of integrated dense interfacial hydrogen and lithium bonds among the components leads to a robust interface and superior integral architecture, delivering an unprecedented combination of properties: a tensile strength of 6.23 MPa, a room‐temperature self‐healing efficiency of 98%, and an ionic conductivity of 4.15 × 10 − 3 S·m −1 . Such performance substantially outperforms the most state‐of‐the‐art bio‐based counterparts, noting that all main components are derived from bio‐based resources. Furthermore, the polydopamine imparts photothermal conversion capability, enabling not only remote‐triggered rapid self‐healing but also non‐contact sensing via near‐infrared light‐mediated thermal stimulation. This study advances a sustainable and remotely controllable platform based on bio‐based SICEs, opening new avenues for next‐generation intelligent flexible electronics.
authors: Mingliang Wu; Quanyong Cheng; Yi‐Dong Li; Caili Huang; Jian‐Bing Zeng

title: Mechatronic Platform Driven by Thoracic Impedance Signals for the Experimental Evaluation of a Radar-Based Respiratory Monitoring System
abstract: Short-range FMCW radar has emerged as a promising contactless technology for respiratory monitoring. However, the experimental evaluation of radar-based respiratory monitoring systems using human subjects is often affected by inter-subject variability, involuntary body movements, and the limited repeatability of respiratory patterns. This work presents a mechatronic platform that reproduces respiratory motion using thoracic impedance signals from the publicly available BIDMC dataset to enable controlled evaluation of the Acconeer XM132 radar. The respiratory signals were resampled, normalized, and converted into motion commands for MG90S servo motors, reproducing physiological breathing patterns through a movable PLA and acrylic structure. A total of 12 recordings, each lasting 240 s, were analyzed. The filtered radar signal was used as the primary source for respiratory rate (RR) estimation, while an MPU6050 inertial sensor provided an auxiliary measurement of the platform motion. Different analysis window lengths and RR estimation methods were investigated. FFT-based estimation using 60 s windows achieved a mean error of 1.94 breathing per minute (bpm) and a median error of 0.09 bpm, whereas analysis of the complete 240 s recordings yielded a median error of 0.03 bpm. The proposed platform contributes to the development of biomedical instrumentation for radar-based respiratory monitoring by providing a controlled and repeatable environment for evaluating radar acquisition parameters, signal filtering techniques, and RR estimation algorithms, representing an intermediate step between laboratory characterization and clinical validation.
authors: Júlio Cardoso Scorpion; João Lucas Pereira dos Santos de Paula; Feres A. Salem; Elço João dos Santos; Flávio Gabriel Oliveira Barbosa; Paulo Alberto Macedo Vieira Violada

title: Metaheuristic and Nonlinear Optimization for Intelligent Energy and Environmental Systems: A Review of Renewable Generation, Smart Metering, Networks and Environmental Monitoring
abstract: Energy and environmental systems are full of decisions that must be tuned under uncertainty: how much power to draw from a solar panel, how to bill and balance consumption on a smart grid, how to share spectrum in a wireless network and how to read a biosensor in the field. Computing itself is part of the problem, since data centres, web services and smartphones draw a growing share of electricity. Many of these decisions have no closed-form solution because the underlying models are nonlinear, noisy or only partly known. Metaheuristic search, fuzzy reasoning, nonlinear analysis and data-driven forecasting are now used to find good settings, but studies are spread across power engineering, networking and environmental science. This chapter reviews optimization and learning methods for five groups of problems: renewable generation and grid interfacing, smart metering and energy forecasting, resource allocation and energy-aware computing in communication and IoT systems, environmental and agricultural monitoring, and the approximation of nonlinear physical models. The review finds that hybrid metaheuristics, such as grey wolf optimization with opposition-based learning, improve tracking and control in renewable systems, that tree ensembles and regression models are standard for consumption forecasting, that fuzzy optimization handles uncertainty in network resource allocation, that signal-aware transfer scheduling and green design guidelines reduce the energy used by smartphones and web services, and that neural approximation can stand in for expensive solvers of nonlinear equations. Few studies, however, compare methods on shared benchmarks or report computation cost. Future work should use common test systems, report run time next to solution quality and link optimization with forecasting in one loop.
authors: Kennedy R; Santhalakshmi M; Balamurali S
venue: International Journal Of Recent Trends In Multidisciplinary Research

title: Metal Hypersensitivity Reactions Following Spinal Implants
abstract: BACKGROUND: Metal hypersensitivity reactions are infrequently reported but clinically significant after spinal implant surgery. Clinical presentation can mimic infection or mechanical failure, making diagnosis difficult. Evidence to guide diagnosis and management is largely limited to short case series and case reports. The purpose of this study was to systematically review the clinical presentation, diagnostic methods, and outcomes of metal hypersensitivity associated with spinal implants. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted of PubMed, Embase, and Scopus from inception through June 22, 2026, in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Title and abstract screening, full-text review, and data extraction were performed independently by 2 reviewers with conflicts resolved by a third reviewer. Eligible studies included adult patients with suspected or confirmed metal hypersensitivity following spinal implant surgery that reported patient-level clinical outcomes. RESULTS: Fifteen studies with a total of 19 patients met inclusion criteria (53% female, 42% male, and 5% not reported). The median patient age was 47 years (range, 19-69). Twelve procedures (63%) were fusion-based, while 7 (37%) were motion preserving, including disk arthroplasty and artificial facet replacement systems. Common clinical presentations included persistent pain, with 8 patients (42%) exhibiting dermatologic manifestations. Metal hypersensitivity was immunologically confirmed by positive patch testing and/or lymphocyte transformation testing in 11 patients (58%), while 8 (42%) were diagnosed clinically. Onset of symptoms ranged from immediately postoperatively to 15 years after implantation. Eighteen patients underwent removal or revision with clinical improvement in 14 of 16 with a reported outcome (88%). CONCLUSION: Metal hypersensitivity reactions following spinal implants are infrequently reported but may present either immediately or in a delayed manner with symptoms that mimic more common postoperative complications, such as infection or pseudarthrosis, or may present with dermatologic manifestations. In cases where other etiologies are ruled out, hardware removal was frequently, though not invariably, associated with clinical improvement, which was reported narratively rather than by validated outcome measures. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Therapeutic Level V. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.
authors: Joseph Abbo; Jacob Thomas; Christian Stipho; Erik Nakken; Rakesh Patel; Joshua David Piche; IIyas Aleem

title: Millimetre-Wave Radar for Sports Engineering Applications: A Scoping Review of Current Evidence, Validation, and Future Directions
abstract: Millimetre-wave (mmWave) radar has emerged as a promising non-contact sensing technology capable of capturing human movement and physiological information without requiring wearable devices or continuous visual recording. Although mmWave radar has been extensively investigated in general human sensing applications, its current role and potential translation in sports engineering remain unclear. This scoping review aims to systematically map current evidence regarding mmWave radar applications relevant to sports engineering, including localisation and tracking, movement recognition, pose estimation, and physiological monitoring. The review will summarise sensing configurations, experimental designs, validation approaches, performance metrics, and engineering limitations reported in existing studies. The review will follow the methodological framework for scoping reviews and will be reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines. The findings will identify current capabilities, evidence gaps, and future directions for translating mmWave radar technologies into practical sports engineering applications.
authors: Rouli Ye; Xu Wen

title: Mobile Health Technologies for Long COVID Management: A Scoping Review
abstract: Background: Long COVID affects an estimated 400 million worldwide. Individuals with long COVID face a range of fluctuating and often debilitating symptoms including myalgia, fatigue, and cognitive difficulties. Psychological effects such as anxiety, depression, and reduced quality of life are also commonly reported. Together, these symptoms present barriers to accessing traditional healthcare services. Furthermore, a lack of satisfaction in traditional healthcare services is often reported. Mobile health has been proposed as a solution to improve long COVID symptom management whilst overcoming some barriers and improving patient experience of healthcare services. This scoping review aimed to identify mobile health technologies to support long COVID symptom management or tracking and to synthesise their reported outcomes. Methods: Following JBI guidelines and the PRISMA-ScR checklist, five databases (CINAHL ultimate, MEDLINE, ScienceDirect, Cochrane, and Scopus) were searched. Articles were eligible for the review if they examined the use of mobile health technologies for long COVID symptom management or tracking. Articles which involved individuals under 18 years or non-human samples or focussed on conditions alongside long COVID where results could not be separated were not eligible for inclusion. Risk of bias was assessed using JBI, ROB 2, and ROBINS-1 V2, and is presented using both visual summaries and narrative descriptions. Results: Of 737 articles screened, 38 met the eligibility criteria and were included in the current review. These articles totalled 3541 participants across 14 countries. Technology modality varied, with the current review synthesising findings from mobile apps, web pages, video-calling platforms, wearables, and virtual reality headsets. Findings showed that mobile health technologies were acceptable and feasible, although a one-size-fits-all approach cannot be adopted due to individual differences in symptomatology and support needs. Conclusions: Promising improvements in symptom-based outcome measures and fitness tests were reported, although intervention and methodological heterogeneity limits our conclusions regarding comparative effectiveness.
authors: Gabrielle Humphreys; Lawrence D. Hayes; Ethan C J Berry; Eleanor Daniels; Abby Pritchard; Ramna A. Bukhari; Barbara Budai; Siyra Sabah; Nilihan E. M. Sanal‐Hayes

title: Mobility Enhancement of Patients Body Monitoring based on WBAN with Multipath Routing
abstract: One of the promising applications of wireless sensor networks (WSNs) is monitoring of the human body for health concerns. For this purpose, a large number of small sensors are implanted in the human body. These sensors altogether provide a network of wireless sensors (WBANs) and monitor the vital signs and signals of the human body; these sensors will then send this information to the doctor. The most important application of the WBAN is the implementation of the monitoring network for patient safety in the hospital environment. In this case, supporting patients’ mobility is one of the basic needs, which has been underestimated in recent studies. The problem that involves providing the required energy for the units used in this type of network is challenging; for this reason, sent/ received units with very low power consumption and with a very small radius are used in order to save energy. The resulting small sending range, leads to the lack of support for patients' mobility. In this paper, the AD HOC mode is suggested for use to establish a network and a multi-path routing algorithm, for the purpose of importing patients’ mobility in hospital setting. The results of the simulation show that in addition to supporting patients' mobility, the use of the proposed idea instead of previously presented protocols, reduces delays in data transmission and energy consumption; and it also increases the delivery rate depending on the destination and the lifetime of the network, while on the other hand, it increases routing overhead.
authors: Nastooh Javan

title: Molecular Mechanisms and Biochemical Alterations in Huntington’s Disease: Current Perspectives and Emerging Insights
abstract: Huntington disease (HD) is a progressive, inherited neurodegenerative disorder with motor, cognitive, and psychiatric manifestations.This review aims to synthesize current knowledge on the epidemiology, pathogenesis, and management of HD, and critically evaluate advances in emerging therapeutic strategies.Key findings reveal that HD is frequently underdiagnosed in non-European populations due to limited data and awareness, and that significant disparities exist in access to care and genetic testing worldwide.Although current therapies are limited to symptomatic management, recent research has clarified the molecular mechanisms of neuronal degeneration, including excitotoxicity, mitochondrial dysfunction, and oxidative stress.The review highlights promising developments in RNA-targeted therapies, gene-editing technologies such as CRISPR-Cas9, stem cell approaches, and antioxidant interventions, though none have yet to demonstrate disease-modifying effects in clinical trials.Overall, continued research and improved global surveillance are essential for advancing early diagnosis, expanding access to care, and ultimately developing effective, disease-modifying treatments for HD.
authors: Moses Adondua Abah; Micheal Oladosu Abimbola; Nathan Rimamsanati Yohanna; Abdulkabir Abdulquadri Ola; Ahmed Olajide Akinlabi; Yunusa Rahima

title: Multi-Method Explainable Deep Learning for Acute Stress Analysis using Physiological Signals
abstract: Wearable devices measure body signals such as skin conductance, pulse, skin temperature and movement, and machine-learning models can use these signals to detect acute stress. Recent work has added explainability so that a user can see which signal influenced a decision. However, most studies use only a single explanation method, judge that explanation visually, and rarely report how confident the model is. This raises a practical question: can these explanations be trusted? This paper studies that question on the WESAD dataset under strict subject-independent (Leave-One-Subject-Out) evaluation. Five deep models (LSTM, BiLSTM, GRU, CNN-LSTM, Transformer) and five classical models are trained on identical folds. Explanations are generated with three methods (Integrated Gradients, SHAP, LIME) and their agreement is measured across six held-out participants; explanations are further examined with faithfulness tests, cross-architecture comparison, counterfactual and temporal analysis; and predictive uncertainty is estimated with deep ensembles and assessed for calibration. Three findings are reported. First, the five deep architectures perform almost identically (0.846–0.863 accuracy) and are statistically indistinguishable (all Holm-corrected p = 1.00, small effect sizes), while a classical Random Forest is more accurate (0.911); after Holm–Bonferroni correction no individual classical-vs-deep pair is significant at 15 subjects, but the direction is consistent across every comparison, with medium-to-large effect sizes for nine of the ten comparisons (rank-biserial 0.50–0.68) and a smaller effect for the tenth (Logistic Regression vs Transformer, +0.25), so at this data scale increasing architectural complexity is not the productive direction. Second, across six subjects the three explanation methods agree only partially, heart rate is the single most important channel in two to four of six subjects depending on the method, and pairwise method agreement is low-to-moderate and highly variable (Spearman ρ from 0.10 ± 0.45 to 0.70 ± 0.20), which shows that a single explanation method is insufficient on its own and that reliability must be measured rather than assumed; faithfulness is in the expected direction (mean insertion AUC 0.794 > deletion AUC 0.756) but modest and subject-dependent. Third, the ensemble is well calibrated (Expected Calibration Error 0.065) and, under a coverage–risk (deferral) analysis, answering only the most-confident 50% of cases raises selective accuracy from 0.884 to 0.960. The study concludes that trustworthiness, measured explanation reliability together with calibration, rather than accuracy alone, is the appropriate objective for wearable stress detection.
authors: Nanda Yasaswini; Setti Sarika
venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: Multimodal approaches in hazard detection and risk assessment: current methods and future trends
abstract: Hazard detection and risk assessment are important across transportation, healthcare, mining, industry, and environmental monitoring. Advances in sensor technology and deep learning have increased the use of multimodal approaches that combine complementary sensing and data sources. This structured narrative review examines 89 publications and classifies hazard detection methods as visual-based, environmental sensor-based, wearable device-based, or multimodal fusion methods. Risk assessment methods are organized as deterministic and rule-based, probabilistic, statistical and data-driven, or methods under non-statistical uncertainty. Among the 39 original hazard detection studies, 27 (69.2%) used single-modal or non-fusion approaches, whereas 12 (30.8%) used explicit multimodal fusion. Representative within-study comparisons showed that camera–LiDAR fusion increased detection accuracy from 58.3% to 74.7%, while radar- camera fusion reduced the average false-negative rate from 6.46% for the camera and 6.59% for the radar to 0.61% for the fused tracker. These findings indicate that multimodal fusion can improve detection robustness within the same evaluation setting, although the magnitude of improvement depends on the task, dataset, sensors, and fusion architecture. The review also finds that risk assessment method selection depends mainly on data availability, uncertainty type, explainability, computational resources, and response-time requirements. Sensor alignment, data quality, real-time processing, maintenance cost, and limited common evaluation procedures remain major challenges.
authors: Naji Alhusaini; Amar N. Alsheavi; Abdulqawi Alarefi; Shenghui Zhao; Jing Li; Haibao Chen; Pan Lei; Ibrahim Abdulrab Ahmed; Jamil A. M. Saif; Ali Abdo Mohammed Al-kubati; Peng Gao
venue: Journal of King Saud University - Computer and Information Sciences

title: Multimodal deep learning with particle swarm guided feature refinement for automated pain detection
abstract: Pain assessment remains a significant challenge in clinical practice because conventional self-reporting methods are subjective and unreliable for non-verbal, cognitively impaired, and critically ill patients. Existing automated pain detection approaches primarily rely on single-modality data or limited multimodal integration, resulting in inadequate feature representation, feature redundancy, and reduced classification performance. To address these limitations, this study proposes a multimodal deep learning framework that integrates physiological signals, facial images, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and clinical text for objective pain detection. The physiological branch employs a hybrid architecture comprising a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network, Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU), and Deep Neural Network (DNN) to learn hierarchical spatial-temporal representations. The facial branch combines EfficientNet and Residual Network (ResNet) to extract discriminative facial features, while a CNN-based architecture processes MRI images. Clinical narratives are encoded using Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) and BioBERT to capture contextual semantic information. An Adaptive Feature Refinement Layer (AFRL) enhances modality-specific feature learning, followed by Particle Swarm Optimisation (PSO) for feature selection and a novel PSO-Guided Feature Refinement Layer (PFRL) for adaptive feature weighting prior to multimodal fusion. We implement the framework in TensorFlow and PyTorch and evaluate it on the BioVid, UNBC-McMaster, and Trigeminal Neuralgia MRI datasets. Experimental results achieve 96.2% accuracy, outperforming Support Vector Machine (82.4%), K-Nearest Neighbors (79.6%), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (88.9%), and AdaBoost (90.7%). The proposed framework provides a robust, scalable, and clinically applicable solution for automated multimodal pain detection and improved clinical decision support.
authors: Karim Gasmi; Sarah Almaghrabi; Ibrahim Rizqallah Alzahrani; Adil Mahmoud Mohamed Mahmoud; Alameen Abdalrahman Eltoum; Abdullah Sawdi Alenzi; Osama R. Shahin; Ahmed I. Taloba; Fatma Al Zahraa Hamed Abdel Hameed

title: Multiobjective Optimization of Performance and Emission Profiles in a WCO–Butanol‐Fueled RCCI Engine: An RSM‐Based Investigation of EGR and Injection Duration Interactions
abstract: ABSTRACT This investigation develops a multiobjective optimization framework for Reactivity Controlled Compression Ignition (RCCI) engines utilizing a butanol, waste cooking oils–biodiesel, and diesel ternary blend. Moving beyond traditional parametric sweeps, the study employs Response Surface Methodology in conjunction with a Face‐Centered Central Composite Design to systematically decode the coupled influences of Injection Duration (ID), exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) rates, and engine load on combustion dynamics. Statistical validation via analysis of variance ensures high predictive fidelity, offering a robust mapping of the dual‐fuel reactivity landscape. Experimental results initially identified a peak brake thermal efficiency (BTE) of 32.0% at high‐load conditions (16 kg); however, this point exhibited significant NO x penalties. To reconcile the performance‐emission trade‐off, a multiobjective optimization was executed using desirability functions. The global optimum was identified at 5.68°CA ID, 13.58% EGR, and 6.66 kg load, yielding a predicted BTE of 23.73% and NO x emissions of 809.2 ppm. At this Pareto‐optimal point, NO x was reduced by 35% compared with baseline diesel through thermal dilution and reactivity stratification. The model was validated through confirmatory experiments, with a maximum error of 1.89%, confirming that the RCCI strategy offers superior environmental‐performance trade‐offs at midload conditions for sustainable, low‐carbon propulsion.
authors: Naresh Ajmeera; Ravi Kumar Puli

title: Navigating human-robot interaction challenges in private and residential aged care homes
abstract: This chapter explores how robotic systems and ambient intelligence can enhance care for older adults in residential aged care (RAC) homes and private homes. Although these settings differ, we frame both as extreme and challenging environments for human-robot interaction (HRI), characterised by cluttered and dynamic layouts, diverse resident needs, and limited on-site technical support. We review embodied and non-embodied systems that assist with daily living, safety monitoring, and social engagement, highlighting hybrid deployments where robots complement fixed and wearable sensors. To ensure these technologies are usable and effective, design considerations consider the cognitive, physical, and social needs of older adults. Interaction design prioritises accessibility for older adults with low digital literacy, using robust but simple voice interfaces, small sets of non-verbal cues, accessible screen-based companions, and safe object handovers. Privacy, trust, and acceptability are addressed via practical strategies such as on-device inference, data minimisation, visible consent controls, and transparent data handling aligned with emerging artificial intelligence (AI) and privacy regulation. Evaluation emphasises real-world metrics including false alarms per day, time to recover from faults, staff workload, and long-term system reliability. We close by outlining open research challenges and future directions for scalable, regulation-ready deployments that support aging with dignity, safety, and independence.
authors: David Ahmedt-Aristizabal; Mohammad Ali Armin; Akila Pemasiri; Harshala Gammulle; Tharindu Fernando; David Silvera-Tawil; Simon Denman

title: Neural encoding of auditory processing in schizophrenia
abstract: Introduction: Auditory processing abnormalities are a core feature of schizophrenia and are linked to deficits in speech perception, cognitive function, and everyday communication. It remains unclear which stages of auditory processing are most disrupted and how these disruptions relate to symptoms at the level of population-wide neural representations. Methods: We used fMRI recordings acquired while individuals with schizophrenia and matched healthy controls completed a controlled block-design speech-perception task. Voxel-wise encoding models mapped self-supervised speech-model representations, together with complementary acoustic and linguistic features, to neural responses. Results: Across cross-validated evaluations, individuals with schizophrenia showed numerically higher encoding alignment than matched controls across all evaluated regions of interest, although no effect survived false discovery rate correction in this small sample. The largest numerical group differences occurred in frontal language regions, including the middle frontal gyrus and dorsomedial prefrontal cortex, and in early auditory cortex. Subgroup analyses suggested that patients without auditory verbal hallucinations drove much of this numerical separation. Discussion: These descriptive, hypothesis-generating findings suggest that model-based encoding can reveal a frontal-auditory signature in schizophrenia, but they do not establish a clinically actionable biomarker or preserved or enhanced speech encoding. Larger, adequately powered studies with richer feature spaces are needed for confirmatory inference and to test whether encoding-based measures can serve as clinically meaningful biomarkers.
authors: Lakshma Reddy Vuyyuru; Anitha Raju

title: NeuroCareIoT for reliable multimodal edge based Alzheimer’s home monitoring using NeuroFuseNet
abstract: Continuous, reliable assessment of falls and night-time wandering, routine deviations and physiological instability must be provided for people with Alzheimer’s disease at home. Current methods, however, typically address only a single modality of sensing, are grounded in fixed decision thresholds, and fail to appropriately consider probability calibration and predictive uncertainty, resulting in too many false alarms at night, delayed detection of subtle changes, and diminished trust by caregivers. To fill these gaps, we present NeuroCareIoT, an edge-first IoT framework that integrates motion, location, routines, and vitals while accounting for reliability and uncertainty. It consists of four task-specific backbones (IMU micro-dynamics: SafeFallNet; room-level localisation with path entropy: WanderSenseNet; temporal deviation modelling: DailyRoutineNet; motion-aware HR/HRV: VitalRhythmNet), coupled by NeuroFuseNet, a reliability-aware fusion layer that weighs modalities based on quality scores ( $$qi$$ ) and outputs a calibrated risk. On top of this, NeuroFuseNet applies Platt scaling at the internal node level for calibration and includes an entropy-based gate to suppress low-confidence windows and drive tiered escalation. NeuroCareIoT was shown to provide better performance in terms of precision (86.9%) and recall (90.3%) across five random seed data sets than both the heuristic baseline, the best-performing single-modality model and naïve average fusion. It also achieved better probability calibration (Brier score = 0.061), lower expected calibration error (2.6%), and more stable performance across decision thresholds. Ablation analysis revealed that reliability weighting and uncertainty gating had the greatest effect on precision, and SafeFallNet had the greatest effect on sensitivity, while maintaining a 95th-percentile decision latency under 200 ms on both the Raspberry Pi 4B and Jetson Nano platforms. Personalisation reduced the number of false alarms by 0.54 per night and shortened the time to detect routine deviations by 1.7 minutes. Quiet-hours alert burden was further lowered, and the precision of night-time alerts was further improved by tuning the policy for caregivers. In addition, case studies of SHAP-based care notes were given to facilitate transparent decision-making, along with risk and entropy trajectories. All results show that NeuroCareIoT is a viable prototype for implementing a multimodal monitoring framework that can be realised through an edge-first approach and tested in controlled, synchronised replay experiments built on publicly available datasets. The suggested framework serves as a basis for future validation through longitudinal real-home studies with Alzheimer’s patients, caregivers, and clinician-adjudicated incident records. Not applicable.

title: New Oxygen Sensor with Polyaniline Spin Probe and Low Frequency EPR (L-Band) Detection System
abstract: Our research demonstrates the potential of certain PANI samples to serve as sensitive and reliable spin probes for oxygen detection, while also highlighting the advantages of the low-frequency EPR technique. Compared to other methods of measuring oxygen concentration, the new sensor—based on a PANI spin probe and a low-frequency EPR detector—offers unique benefits: it ensures high sensitivity to changes in oxygen concentration and does not require direct contact between the EPR detector and the sensor itself (the polyaniline probe). This sensor can be placed in isolated environments, including biological samples (tissues), and - thanks to the use of nanodispersed polyaniline - even inside living cells.

title: Non-contact Cardiorespiratory Monitoring in a Smart Triage Chair using Laser Speckle Pattern Dynamics
abstract: Emergency triage requires rapid, simultaneous vital-sign acquisition, yet contact-based sensors create throughput bottlenecks during surge events. We present a triage chair that measures heart rate (HR) and respiration rate (RR) simultaneously without patient contact, using time-varying laser speckle patterns projected onto the posterior thorax. We conducted our experiments in a cohort of 34 volunteers (19 males, 15 females, age 39.6 ± 11.4 years). RR estimation showed good agreement with an MAE of 1.9 br/min and an RMSE of 3.4 br/min (95% CI: [0.9, 2.9] br/min). For HR estimation, an MAE of 10.68 BPM and an RMSE of 19.0 BPM were obtained (95% CI: [5.2, 16.2] BPM).

title: Non-invasive monitoring of human vital signs under dynamic conditions: A review of acoustic, optical and ballistocardiographic methods
abstract: Introduction: Modern healthcare systems face a critical shortage of personnel, which in the traditional model leads to dangerous “time windows” (reaching up to 22 h per day) during which the patient remains unsupervised. The response to this challenge is the dynamic development of contactless monitoring technologies, enabling continuous assessment of vital parameters without the discomfort associated with cabling. However, the implementation of these solutions in real-world environments encounters a fundamental barrier in the form of motion artifacts, variable environmental conditions, and demographic heterogeneity. Aim: This article provides a review of non-invasive monitoring methods under dynamic conditions, with a particular emphasis on interference compensation techniques. The aim of the work is a comparative analysis of three leading modalities: optical and guided-wave photonic (rPPG, thermography, LiDAR, FBG, FPI), vibrational-mechanical (BCG, SCG), and acoustic (passive and active), in the context of their clinical reliability, privacy protection, and motion robustness. Methodology: The review includes a literature analysis from the years 1947–2025, with a special emphasis on the “digital era” after 2010. The effectiveness of modern signal processing algorithms was analyzed, including bounded Kalman filters, Tile and Aggregation (T&A) methods for diverse skin pigmentation, and deep learning architectures (UNet, Bi-LSTM) used for the reconstruction of biomedical signals, alongside targeted strategies evaluated for specific vulnerable demographics (high BMI, preterm infants, and elderly populations). Results: The analysis shows a clear specialization of individual technologies. Optical methods (rPPG) offer the highest precision in measuring heart rate and saturation, particularly in neonatology (SIDS prevention), but are limited by lighting conditions and privacy issues, whereas guided-wave photonics offer complete electromagnetic immunity. Vibrational methods (BCG/SCG) provide discrete “zero-effort” measurement and unique hemodynamic data (PEP, LVET), yet they exhibit critical sensitivity to patient motor activity. Acoustic technologies, especially active ultrasonic sonars, represent a compromise that allows for respiratory monitoring in the dark and through obstacles. Conclusions: There is currently no single, universal measurement method robust to all environmental interferences. The future of non-invasive monitoring lies in hybrid systems (sensor fusion), combining the advantages of different modalities (e.g., optics and vibration), and in edge processing (Edge AI). Addressing the strict trade-offs between computational overhead in matrix-inversion algorithms and hardware power constraints will be key. Only the integration of multi-source data will allow for the effective elimination of motion artifacts and the implementation of medical safety-critical systems in home and mobile conditions.

title: Noninvasive assessment of the anaerobic threshold in endurance athletes: an evidence-based narrative review of methods, validity, and field feasibility
abstract: INTRODUCTION OR BACKGROUND: The anaerobic threshold (AnT) marks the transition between heavy and severe exercise intensity domains and guides training prescription and performance monitoring. Criterion methods (blood lactate and gas exchange) are accurate but invasive, costly, or impractical outside laboratories, prompting the search for noninvasive surrogates. This review evaluates the validity of these estimation procedures rather than the underlying physiology. SOURCES OF DATA: MEDLINE (via PubMed) was searched from inception without language restrictions, supplemented by reference-list and citation searching. Eligible studies compared noninvasive AnT indices, including heart rate variability (HRV; including detrended fluctuation analysis [DFA] α1), cardiac repolarization instability, heart rate deflection/field slope-variation methods, critical power (CP)/ critical speed (CS), near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS), the talk test, and machine-learning (ML) models, with criterion standards. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2. Eighty-eight reports were synthesized narratively; no meta-analysis was performed. AREAS OF AGREEMENT: DFA α1, NIRS breakpoints, and CP/CS show strong associations with laboratory criteria and increasing field applicability through wearables. Accuracy and feasibility trade-offs require method selection according to the threshold, sport, and required precision. AREAS OF CONTROVERSY: Correlation indicates group-level association rather than individual agreement; Bland-Altman and reliability analyses are more informative for substitution. Criterion standards are not interchangeable, and heart rate deflection is not consistently identifiable. Evidence in female athletes remains limited. GROWING POINTS: Multimodal wearables integrating HRV, muscle oxygenation, and running power with ML may improve field-based threshold estimation. AREAS FOR DEVELOPING RESEARCH: Priorities include standardized reporting, transparent bias assessment, female-athlete validation, and broader systematic and meta-analytic synthesis.
authors: Nicola Maffulli; Johnny Padulo; Francesco Oliva

title: Noninvasive diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease: a review of emerging biomarkers and multimodal approaches
abstract: Noninvasive biomarkers are expanding access to biological assessment of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). This review evaluates blood-based, neuroimaging, retinal, electrophysiological, digital, and behavioral measures alongside structured cognitive and functional assessment, and examines multimodal and machine-learning approaches for detection, differential diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment monitoring. Plasma phosphorylated tau, particularly p-tau217, currently offers the strongest scalable evidence for identifying amyloid and advanced tau pathology, whereas PET and MRI retain complementary roles in pathological confirmation, regional staging, exclusion of alternative causes, and characterization of atypical phenotypes. Retinal, electrophysiological, speech, sleep, and eye-tracking measures remain promising but require greater standardization and external validation. Across modalities, biomarker trajectories are temporally staggered, assay and platform differences affect interpretation, and pathology–phenotype mapping is modified by disease stage, cognitive reserve, copathology, vascular factors, and population characteristics. We therefore propose a phenotype-anchored, stepped pathway that begins with patient and informant history, objective cognitive and functional assessment, structural imaging, and routine laboratory evaluation; adds validated blood biomarkers when they resolve a defined uncertainty; and reserves CSF or PET for unresolved, atypical, or treatment-relevant cases. Discordant findings should prompt reassessment rather than automatic reclassification. We describe the literature-search and descriptive evidence-categorization approach used to select and categorize the evidence reviewed, and we place the findings within the emerging regulatory context of blood-based testing. Clinical translation will depend on harmonized thresholds, representative prospective cohorts, calibration, independent validation, and evidence that multimodal systems improve decisions and patient outcomes rather than benchmark accuracy alone.

title: Nurse-led mobile health interventions for heart failure self-care: A systematic review
abstract: Heart failure places a heavy and growing demand on health systems, and much of its everyday management depends on what patients do at home: taking medicines as prescribed, weighing themselves, limiting salt and fluid, and noticing the early signs of decompensation. Nurses have traditionally led the education and follow-up that sustain these behaviours, and mobile health tools now allow that support to continue well beyond the clinic. This systematic review examined whether nurse-led mobile health interventions improve self-care and related outcomes in adults living with heart failure. Guided by PRISMA 2020, we searched PubMed/MEDLINE for studies published between January 2010 and October 2026 and supplemented this with citation and targeted keyword searching. Sixteen studies from fourteen countries were included, fifteen of them randomised. Interventions ranged from structured telephone support and messaging to smartphone applications, wireless telemonitoring and wearable-guided coaching. Most trials that used validated instruments reported better self-care, especially daily weighing, self-care maintenance and medication adherence, although some gains faded once active support ended. Effects on rehospitalisation were inconsistent; reductions appeared mainly where nurses acted promptly on transmitted data. Quality of life improved in several, but not all, trials. Small samples, short follow-up and the impossibility of blinding limit certainty. Nurse-led mobile health appears to strengthen heart failure self-care when technology is paired with timely clinical response, and it warrants rigorous testing in low- and middle-income settings, including India.

title: Oculomics using artificial intelligence derived retinal biomarkers for cardiovascular health
abstract: This narrative review synthesizes evidence from retinal vascular morphology, structural and perfusion imaging, retinal aging, metabolomics, and artificial intelligence models linking retinal biomarkers with cardiovascular risk factors, subclinical disease, clinical events, and cardiorenal and metabolic outcomes. These biomarkers may complement conventional risk assessment, but clinical utility is unproven and integration into cardiovascular digital twins remains conceptual. Prospective validation, standardized acquisition, interoperability, interpretability, and equitable evaluation are required before implementation.

title: On‐Skin Wireless Vibratory Interfaces by Stretchable Multilayer Circuits
abstract: ABSTRACT Emerging technologies in soft electronics are facilitating seamless interactions with the human body's neural network. Among various sensory modalities, vibratory stimulation offers distinct advantages as a feedback strategy in wearable and implantable systems. However, existing devices face challenges of limited battery life, noncompliant device architecture, and complicated circuit designs, particularly for devices requiring adaptive fitting to various curved surfaces of the human body. In this study, we present a wireless and stretchable electronic device with multilayer circuits using elastic and printable metallic inks. The wireless vibratory interfaces were designed with a compact and soft circuit, which directly converts electromagnetic power to produce vibrotactile stimulation. Patterns of the mechanical vibration were highly programmable by frequency‐shift keying (FSK) modulation of the input signals. The wireless and soft vibratory interfaces have excellent mechanical compliance, maintaining their functionalities under large deformations. Together with a fabric signal transmitter fabricated from elastic conductive fibers, we demonstrate a smart and interactive on‐skin device, which translates spatial information into perceptible tactile cues to navigate visually impaired users through unstructured environments. The developed device holds significant promise for applications in sensory substitution, human‐machine interfaces, and biomedical treatments.

title: OptimalStop: Predictability–complexity trade-off for optimising stop detection in human mobility data
abstract: Human mobility analysis increasingly relies on large-scale trajectory data, yet results remain highly sensitive to preprocessing choices that are rarely applied in a consistent or well-documented manner. Stop detection, which transforms raw location traces into sequences of visited places, is a particularly critical and bias-prone step, with parameter choices often guided by dataset-specific conventions. The absence of systematic and transparent parameter-selection practices risks introducing methodological bias and limits the comparability and reproducibility of mobility studies. Here, we introduce OptimalStop , a model-agnostic optimisation framework for stop detection that exploits a predictability–complexity trade-off in human mobility trajectories to guide preprocessing. OptimalStop operates as a higher-level tuning layer applicable to any method that produces symbolic mobility sequences. By framing stop detection as a multi-objective optimisation problem, the framework identifies compact Pareto-optimal sets of parameter configurations that balance predictability and structural complexity, avoiding over-fragmented or over-aggregated representations. We evaluate OptimalStop on both real-world and synthetic mobility datasets using multiple stop detection algorithms, and confirm through controlled synthetic experiments that the predictability–complexity trade-off is structurally grounded in recurrent return-to-place behaviour rather than being a mathematical artefact of discretisation. The results show that OptimalStop consistently retains near-optimal solutions while substantially reducing the effective parameter search space within a reasonable computational time. An optional automatic selection strategy further demonstrates that high-quality stop detection can be obtained without ground truth, outperforming or matching commonly used sensitivity-based tuning approaches. We release OptimalStop under an open licence, providing a transparent and reproducible framework for parameter selection that supports more structured mobility data preprocessing. While demonstrated here for stop detection, the underlying predictability–complexity balance offers a general perspective for mitigating methodological bias in mobility analytics.

title: Optimasi Parameter Pemesinan CNC Turning untuk Meminimalkan Deviasi Dimensi dan Kekasaran Permukaan
abstract: Deviasi diameter pada komponen collar roda depan sepeda motor berbahan Aluminium 6061 merupakan indikator kualitas kritis karena penyimpangan yang melewati batas toleransi ±0,02 mm dapat menyebabkan sambungan longgar dan getaran saat kendaraan beroperasi. Penelitian ini bertujuan menentukan kombinasi optimal parameter CNC turning untuk meminimalkan deviasi diameter menggunakan metode Taguchi. Tiga parameter yang dikaji meliputi putaran spindel (1300, 1900, 2500 rpm), laju pemakanan (0,10; 0,20; 0,30 mm/rev), dan kedalaman potong (1,50; 2,00; 2,50 mm) yang disusun dalam matriks ortogonal L9 dengan tiga kali replikasi menggunakan mesin CNC Turning SL-25 Mori Seiki dan pahat insert carbide CNMG 120402-HA. Karakteristik kualitas Smaller-the-Better diterapkan pada analisis rasio signal-to-noise dan analisis varians (ANOVA). Hasil penelitian menunjukkan kedalaman potong sebagai faktor paling dominan dengan kontribusi 60,09%, diikuti putaran spindel 28,08% dan laju pemakanan 10,71%, dengan galat 1,12%. Kondisi optimal diperoleh pada putaran spinoh anova di abstrak gasdel 2500 rpm, laju pemakanan 0,10 mm/rev, dan kedalaman potong 2,00 mm, menghasilkan prediksi deviasi diameter 0,031 mm pada interval keyakinan 95% antara 0,020 mm hingga 0,049 mm. Uji konfirmasi menghasilkan deviasi rata-rata 0,044 mm yang masih berada dalam rentang prediksi, sehingga memvalidasi model yang dibangun. Metode Taguchi terbukti efektif mengidentifikasi parameter pemesinan optimal untuk menghasilkan dimensi collar Aluminium 6061 yang presisi dan konsisten. Kata kunci: Aluminium 6061; ANOVA; CNC turning; deviasi diameter; metode Taguchi.

title: Optimization of Wear Behavior Analysis in MWCNT-Reinforced GFRP Composites Using RSM and ETLBO
abstract: The present study aims to optimize the fabrication processing of Multi-Walled Carbon Nanotube (MWCNT)-filled glass fiber-reinforced polymer (GFRP) composites to enhance their tribological performance during the hand layup process. A structured experimental approach based on the Box-Behnken design within the Response Surface Methodology (RSM) framework was used to evaluate the influence of wt% MWCNT loading, applied load, and sliding velocity. The fabrication was performed, ensuring a uniform MWCNT dispersion via mechanical stirring and probe sonication. The performance of the composites was assessed in terms of their specific wear rate (SWR) and wear coefficients (WC). Statistical analysis, including ANOVA and Pareto charts, revealed that the load and sliding velocity significantly affected both the SWR and WC, whereas interactions such as the MWCNT content and sliding velocity also played a crucial role. Mathematical models were developed for SWR and WC and optimized using Elitist Teaching-Learning-Based Optimization (ETLBO). The optimal fabrication settings were found to be 1wt% MWCNT loading, 30 N load, and 2 m/s sliding velocity, yielding improved wear characteristics. Confirmatory tests validated the model predictions and showed minimal errors. Scanning electron microscopy further confirmed that optimal nanotube dispersion led to a more uniform and durable composite structure, supporting its potential for high-performance engineering applications. The proposed integrated approach demonstrates the effectiveness of combining RSM and ETLBO to develop high-performance MWCNT-GFRP composites with superior wear resistance. The findings of this study provide practical guidelines for fabricating durable, wear-resistant composite structures for automotive brake systems, aerospace joints, and industrial machinery parts, where reliability under continuous sliding conditions is essential.
authors: Ch. Rajeswari; Namala Kiran Kumar; P. Saritha

title: PREDICTIVE CHRONIC DISEASE SURVEILLANCE FRAMEWORK: INTEGRATING MACHINE LEARNING, REAL-TIME DATA, AND PUBLIC HEALTH RESPONSE
abstract: Chronic disease surveillance is an essential part of public health because it helps governments and health organizations understand the burden of disease, identify risk factors, recognize disparities, and track changes in health outcomes. Most existing surveillance systems, however, are mainly concerned with describing what has already happened. The growing use of electronic health records, wearable devices, environmental sensors, administrative databases, and other continuously generated sources of information creates an opportunity to move surveillance toward a more forward-looking approach. This article presents the Predictive Chronic Disease Surveillance Framework (PCDSF), a framework for using multiple data sources and machine learning to estimate changing population-level risk and to connect those estimates to public health action. The framework treats predictive surveillance as a continuous cycle: data are collected and combined, population risk is estimated, emerging patterns are identified, decisions are made, interventions are implemented, and the resulting outcomes are fed back into the system. This makes surveillance an ongoing learning process rather than a one-way reporting exercise. The framework also makes an important distinction between predicting disease in an individual patient and predicting changes in risk across populations. Its purpose is not simply to identify who is likely to become ill, but to help public health organizations understand where risk is increasing, which groups may be most affected, and where preventive resources could have the greatest impact. Six propositions are developed around multimodal data integration, timely updating, predictive performance, intervention, equity, and continuous learning. The article also discusses privacy, interoperability, data quality, algorithmic bias, transparency, and organizational capacity as conditions that can determine whether predictive surveillance works in practice.

title: PS2-15. Multimodal Video and Audio Signal Processing for Estimating Cattle Forage Intake.
abstract: Abstract Accurate quantification of forage intake and rumen digesta during grazing is important for nutrition research but remains difficult to measure at scale. This pilot study evaluated whether contactless video and audio recordings collected during grazing contain kinematic and acoustic signatures that can be related to forage disappearance and rumen digesta dry matter measured via cannulation. Two Angus cattle were recorded across three days during controlled feeding trials in which cereal rye was presented in ground-level pots (three pots per animal per day) and consumed while a fixed-position action camera captured video with onboard audio. Jaw and head keypoints were tracked from video using SLEAP, and grazing-associated audio features were extracted from the video soundtrack using standard digital signal processing implemented in librosa. Features linked to biting events were used as inputs to a linear regression model to estimate forage dry matter disappearance and rumen digesta dry matter recovered after each trial. In this pilot dataset, recovered rumen digesta dry matter was highly correlated with forage disappearance (R² = 0.99), supporting the use of disappearance as a closely aligned intake-related endpoint under these controlled conditions. The results motivate expanded validation across more animals, forage types, and grazing conditions to assess model generalizability and the potential for contactless intake-related monitoring using invasive ground truth for calibration.
