title: Development, validation and clinical implementation of cellular swab materials for quality assurance of pharmacogenomic point-of-care testing
abstract: Abstract Background Pharmacogenomic point-of-care testing (PGx POCT) enables genotype-informed prescribing at the bedside, but implementation is limited by the lack of suitable reference materials for clinical verification and standardised external quality assessment (EQA). Methods Fixed lymphoblastoid cell lines were formulated as swab-based materials at defined cellular inputs for MT-RNR1 POCT. Materials were evaluated using Genedrive® assays, quantitative PCR, acceptance quality limit batch release, workflow-perturbation testing and stability studies, then deployed for clinical verification and in an international EQA programme. Results Materials were homogeneous, workflow compatible and reproducible, with 100% correct genotype calls at the lowest intended manufacturing cell load. Clinical verification of 11 Genedrive® systems across five neonatal units demonstrated 99% concordance with expected genotype classifications (232/234 results). Seven EQA surveys yielded 253 participant results, with full-mark rates of 87.5–100%, and six test failures. Most failures occurred with low cell-input materials near the assay limit of detection. The materials supported genotype concordance, performance monitoring and identification of workflow and sample-related variability. Conclusions Workflow-compatible cell-based reference materials combined with EQA provide a scalable framework for quality-assured PGx POCT beyond specialist laboratories. Clinical verification of Genedrive® systems within neonatal units using the cell-based swab materials, together with deployment of an International MT-RNR1 PGx POCT EQA programme, demonstrated their suitability for supporting both pre-implementation testing and ongoing quality assurance in decentralised healthcare settings. The framework may provide a model for the implementation, clinical verification and ongoing quality assessment of PGx POCT services. Further evaluation across platforms, analytes, settings and participant groups is required to establish broader applicability.

title: Diagnostic Performance and Safety Profile of Shape-sensing Robotic-assisted Bronchoscopy in Peripheral Pulmonary Lesions: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract:
Introduction

Shape-sensing robotic-assisted bronchoscopy (ssRAB) has emerged as a promising modality for diagnosing peripheral pulmonary lesions (PPLs). This meta-analysis evaluated its diagnostic performance and safety profile.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception to December 2025. Study quality was assessed using the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-3. Random-effects model was used to estimate the pooled diagnostic yield, sensitivity for malignancy, and complication, with rates (%) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) when the I2 index exceeded 50%. Cumulative meta-analysis was performed to assess the temporal stability and evidence saturation of the pooled diagnostic yield. Publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots and Egger's test.

Results

A total of 3678 lesions from 18 studies were included. Notably, diagnostic yield varied significantly by outcome definition, with pooled diagnostic yield of 82.5% (95% CI: 78.3%-86.0%) under strict definition versus 88.1% (95% CI: 82.8%-92.0%) under intermediate definition (P=0.036). The pooled sensitivity for malignancy of 90.0% (95% CI: 86.4%-92.8%). Cumulative meta-analysis showed stabilized diagnostic performance after approximately 1,500 lesions for the strict definition and 500 lesions for intermediate definition. Moreover, safety profile was favorable, with pooled rates of pneumothorax 1.8% (95% CI:1.3%-2.3%), chest tube placement 1.1% (95% CI: 0.7%-1.5%), and severe bleeding 0.0% (95% CI: 0.0%-0.3%). Subgroup analyses showed consistent performance across study designs, region, and nodule characteristics. Diagnostic yield was significantly influenced by publication year, and lesion size (P<0.05).

Conclusion

ssRAB was associated with favorable, definition-dependent diagnostic yield (82.5%-88.1%) with exceptional safety, supporting ssRAB as an attractive first-line minimally invasive diagnostic option in appropriately selected patients, especially for small nodules (<2cm) and patients at elevated procedural risk.

title: Diagnostic Yield and Molecular Testing Adequacy of Transbronchial Cryoprobe Biopsy Versus Needle Aspiration in Robotic Bronchoscopy.
abstract: In the AQuIRE trial, most cases (83.6%) did not involve transbronchial needle aspiration (TBNA), often underutilized due to challenges in accessing peripheral pulmonary lesions (PPLs). Advances in robotic bronchoscopy with shape-sensing technology (ssRAB) have mitigated these challenges, but the optimal number of needle and cryoprobe passes for reliable diagnosis remains undefined. This retrospective study compares the diagnostic yield (DY) of TBNA and transbronchial cryoprobe biopsy (TBCB) and their adequacy for molecular testing in PPLs. We performed a retrospective analysis of 166 patients who underwent ssRAB with both TBNA and TBCB from May to August 2024. Fisher exact tests and McNemar χ2 tests were used to compare prevalence differences in DY and molecular testing adequacy between discordant cases. Odds ratios (OR) and 95% CIs of associations between the number of passes and diagnostic yield and rates of obtaining adequate samples for molecular testing were obtained using generalized linear mixed models (GLMMs) with a logit link. TBCB demonstrated a higher diagnostic rate than TBNA (89% vs. 80%, OR=2.04, 95% CI=1.06-4.03; P=0.032), as well as better rates of obtaining samples adequate for molecular testing (60% vs. 20%, OR=5.94, 95% CI=2.31-16.38, P<0.001). TBCB provided diagnostic yields in 55% (χ2=9.33, P=0.002) of cases where TBNA failed to provide a diagnosis and was able to obtain adequate samples for molecular testing in 42% (χ2=15.06, P<0.001) of cases where TBNA was unable to. TBCB suggests a higher diagnostic yield and higher cellular adequacy for molecular testing compared with TBNA, underscoring its potential value as a reliable and versatile diagnostic tool in PPLs.
authors: Tariq Odeh; Vishwajit Hegde; Maggie Chen; Steven Haworth; Maykol Postigo

title: Diagnostic testing for pulmonary tuberculosis in low and middle-income countries: innovations to achieve universal access—a narrative review
abstract: Though rapid molecular diagnostics for tuberculosis (TB) have substantially improved diagnostic accuracy and turnaround times, implementation and impact has been constrained by cost, infrastructure requirements, and continued reliance on sputum. This review examines advances in diagnostic technologies and sampling strategies that could overcome these barriers and accelerate universal access to TB diagnostics. We conducted a narrative review of studies published between Jan 1, 2020, and April 30, 2026, focusing on near-point-of-care molecular (NPOC) platforms, next-generation lipoarabinomannan (LAM) assays, and non-sputum sampling approaches. Emerging NPOC molecular platforms, demonstrate high sensitivity using both sputum and tongue-swab specimens while substantially reducing equipment and testing costs compared with existing nucleic acid amplification test platforms. Next-generation urine LAM assays offer improved sensitivity and potential for use beyond people living with HIV. In addition, parallel testing approaches with multiple sample types, including sputum, tongue swab, stool for children, and urine testing, can substantially increase diagnostic yield in specific populations. Integrating low-cost technologies with non-sputum sampling strategies could provide a scalable pathway towards universal access to TB diagnostics. Realizing this potential will require streamlined regulatory pathways, sustainable financing, and integration of these tools into primary healthcare systems. Funding: None.

title: Diagnostic yield and predictors of complications in CT-guided percutaneous lung biopsy: an analysis based on ATS/ACCP criteria.
abstract:
Background

CT-guided percutaneous lung biopsy (CT-PLB) remains a cornerstone for the diagnosis of pulmonary nodules (PNs), although several alternative techniques, including robotic-assisted bronchoscopy, are increasingly adopted. This study aimed to evaluate CT-PLB in a real-world cohort, focusing on predictors of diagnostic yield and complications.

Methods

We retrospectively evaluated patients who underwent CT-PLB between 2020 and 2024. The diagnostic yield was defined according to the recently published ATS/ACCP criteria. Clinical, radiological, and periprocedural variables were assessed as predictors of diagnostic outcome and complication [pneumothorax (PNX) and pulmonary hemorrhage].

Results

Six hundred fifty-seven patients were included (mean age 69 ± 11 years; 54% male). The diagnostic yield was 84% with higher yield observed for nodule size (diameter ≥ 10 mm), density (solid), and location (peripheral). Increasing subcutaneous fat thickness was independently associated with a modest but significant reduction in diagnostic yield. PNX was radiologically present in 44.4% of cases; however, only 5.9% required hospitalization, and 4.7% required chest-tube placement. Greater parenchymal depth, trans-fissural needle passages, pleural tags and supine and left-lateral decubitus positions were associated with increased PNX extent, while intraparenchymal lesion and greater chest-wall thickness showed a protective effect. Radiological pulmonary hemorrhage >2 cm occurred in 38% of patients, whereas only 1.5% experienced major bleeding requiring intervention. Greater parenchymal depth and non-solid density were associated with increased hemorrhage severity.

Conclusions

In a contemporary diagnostic landscape, CT-PLNB still demonstrates high diagnostic yield and an acceptable safety profile when strict diagnostic criteria are applied. These findings support its continued role as a primary diagnostic approach for PNs.

title: Differences in microbiota profiles of simple and complicated pediatric appendicitis cases
abstract: This study aimed to identify the differences in microbial composition between simple appendicitis (SA) and complicated appendicitis (CA) in a limited sample size using culture and microbiota analysis. Appendix tissues and rectal swabs for microbiota analysis and conventional cultures were collected from patients. 16S rRNA regions were amplified using a DNA preparation kit with primers designed to target the V3-V4 region. Sixteen (41%) of the patients were classified as CA based on the histopathological analysis, and the rest as SA. The effect size was slightly greater in rectal swab samples than in appendiceal tissue samples. Based on the conventional culture, the most common aerobic bacteria were Escherichia , Klebsiella spp., and Enterococcus spp. A decrease in both Pseudomonadota and Bacteriodota phyla was observed in tissue samples, while a decrease in Bacteriodota and an increase in Pseudomonadota were observed in rectal samples. Differences in the relative abundance of Coprobacter and Hungatella were observed between CAT and SAT samples; however, no genus-level difference remained significant after ANCOM-BC2 multiple-testing correction. The most notable feature of the CAT group was the relatively higher presence of potential pathobionts. Bacteriodes and Roseburia showed higher relative abundance in the SA rectal (SAR) group. The genera Eubacterium and Clostridioides showed a significant increase in both the SAR and CA rectal (CAR) groups. Lower relative abundances of Parvimonas, Prevotella , and Dialister and a higher relative abundance of Tyzzerella were observed in CAR compared with controls, although these differences did not remain significant after multiple-testing correction. In the ANCOM-BC2 pairwise analysis, an unclassified genus within Enterobacteriaceae was significantly enriched in CAR compared with healthy controls (LFC = 3.56, q = 0.003). No statistically significant distinction was shown at the alpha and beta diversity levels between SA and CA cases. Our findings support previous studies on increased density and diversity at the phylum level in the CA group. The main limitations were the limited sample size and the use of pre-operative antibiotics. Microbiota profiling of appendiceal tissue and rectal swab samples may provide complementary information for understanding microbiota-associated patterns in appendicitis; however, the diagnostic or predictive utility of these microbial profiles requires validation in larger, independent cohorts using dedicated predictive modeling and diagnostic performance analyses.

title: Distribution and Age Dynamics of Respiratory Mycoplasmosis in Birds on Farms of the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic
abstract: Experiments revealed that 1- to 60-day-old chickens are more susceptible to respiratory mycoplasmosis. Those chickens that contracted the disease experienced developmental delays. Serological studies revealed that the serum droplet agglutination test (SDR) in chickens testing positive for mycoplasmosis resulted in high infection rates in 1- and 20-day-old chickens, amounting to 57.5% and 62.5%, respectively. Respiratory mycoplasmosis infection was recorded in 35.5% of 40-day-old chickens and 6.6% of 60-day-old chickens. Thus, during the study, the percentage of infected chickens did not fall below 50.0% in the RSPN, with the infection peaking at 7 and 10 months of age, amounting to 91.6% and 80.0%, respectively. According to the hemagglutination test, 100% antibodies to mycoplasma were detected at all age periods. At the same time, the maximum average titer (5286±932) was also recorded during the period of intensive egg production. With age, a decrease in the average titer to 3171±428 was recorded. Bacteriological examination of throat swabs taken from healthy laying hens revealed M. gallisepticum cultures in 26.6%–53.3% of all age groups. Detection of the causative agent of respiratory mycoplasmosis in embryos and one-day-old chicks indicates that the infection is transmitted transovarially. The highest mycoplasma carriage rate (53.3%) was detected in 10-month-old hens. Among 12-month-old roosters, the mycoplasma carriage rate was 64.0%.

title: Distribution of Ocular Pathogens and Antimicrobial Resistance Patterns in a Tertiary Care Center: A Retrospective Analysis from 2023 to 2026
abstract: Objective: Ocular infections are important causes of ocular morbidity and may result in permanent visual impairment if not diagnosed and treated promptly. Knowledge of local pathogen distribution and antimicrobial resistance patterns is essential for guiding empirical therapy. This study aimed to evaluate the distribution of bacterial pathogens isolated from ocular specimens and their antimicrobial resistance profiles in a tertiary care center.Methods: This retrospective study included ocular specimens submitted to the microbiology laboratory of a tertiary care center between January 2023 and May 2026. Conjunctival swabs, ocular fluid samples (vitreous, aqueous, and anterior chamber fluids), contact lenses, and corneal tissue specimens were evaluated. Bacterial identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing results obtained during routine laboratory practice were reviewed. Antimicrobial susceptibility results were interpreted according to the European Committee on Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing (EUCAST) criteria. Isolates categorized as “susceptible, increased exposure (I)” were considered susceptible.Results: A total of 1,347 ocular specimens were analyzed, of which 156 (11.6%) yielded bacterial growth, resulting in 184 bacterial isolates. Polymicrobial growth was observed in 24 (15.4%) culture-positive specimens. Conjunctival swabs accounted for the majority of bacterial isolates (63.6%), followed by ocular fluid samples (30.4%). Coagulase-negative staphylococci (CoNS) were the most frequently isolated microorganisms (28.8%), followed by Staphylococcus aureus (11.4%), Enterobacterales (11.4%), Pseudomonas aeruginosa (9.2%), and Haemophilus influenzae (7.6%). Methicillin resistance rates, determined by cefoxitin susceptibility testing, were 56.6% among CoNS isolates and 33.3% among S. aureus isolates. Among Gram-negative bacteria, resistance rates in P. aeruginosa ranged from 11.8% to 20.0% for commonly tested antimicrobials, whereas Enterobacterales demonstrated the highest resistance to ceftazidime (22.2%) and ceftriaxone (21.1%). No resistance to linezolid or vancomycin was detected among Gram-positive isolates.Conclusion: CoNS, S. aureus, and Gram-negative bacteria, particularly Enterobacterales and P. aeruginosa, were the predominant pathogens in ocular infections. High methicillin resistance rates among staphylococci emphasize the importance of local surveillance data for empirical treatment decisions. Continuous monitoring of antimicrobial resistance patterns may contribute to optimizing antimicrobial stewardship and improving patient outcomes in ocular infections.
authors: Barış Can; Işıl Akdemir; Furkan Çam; Gamze Özkan; Arzu İlki

title: Drill with Confidence: Real-Time Automated Drilling Fluid Testing and Dynamic Hydraulic Modeling for Drilling Optimization
abstract: Abstract Manual drilling fluid measurements typically conducted 2–4 times per day, lack the resolution required for precise hydraulic calculations and management in high-performance wells. This paper details the implementation of a closed-loop workflow involving an inline automated fluid testing device and real-time hydraulics simulation and monitoring across two wells in the field. The primary objective was to replace intermittent manual sampling with high-frequency data integrated into a live hydraulic and hole-cleaning simulator to monitor and optimize drilling performance parameters such as Rate of Penetration (ROP), tripping speeds, and circulation times. The technology utilized an inline dual-sampling drilling fluid characterization device to continuously analyze mud properties in the circulating system. The automated system achieved a significant increase in data density, providing 46 rheology tests and 1,920 density readings per day, a massive improvement over the conventional 2–4 rheology tests and 48 density readings. These real-time parameters (Density, PV, YP, and 6-speed readings) and drilling parameters were streamed to a Real-Time Center where a hydraulics modelling software was used for real-time monitoring and optimization. This allowed for the continuous monitoring of the Hole-Cleaning Index (HCI), Cuttings Bed Height (CBH), and Equivalent Circulating Density (ECD) against planned pressure and fracture gradients and identify opportunities for drilling parameter optimization. The integration of real-time data into predictive simulations yielded substantial operational efficiencies as follows: Drilling Performance: The system enabled a maximum ROP of 400 ft/hr while maintaining good hole cleaning. A field-best 24-hour footage of 3,945.68 feet was achieved in the 6-inch section at this time.Circulation Optimization: While the original plan was six bottom-up cycles, predictive simulations suggested optimizing this sequence to just two (a potential saving in circulation time of 67% whilst ensuring a clean wellbore)Tripping Efficiency: Real-time surge/swab monitoring enabled potential tripping speed increases of nearly 100% over previous rig KPIs, offering 15–25% time savings compared to the best-performing rigs in the region.Data Accuracy: Comparative analysis showed a high correlation between simulated ECD and actual annular pressure while drilling (APWD) data, confirming the reliability of automated fluid inputs for pressure management. This work demonstrates that automating the fluid-data-to-simulation loop moves the industry from reactive monitoring to proactive drilling management. It quantifies the specific "time-savings" value of high-frequency rheology data, proving that automated testing is a critical precursor to fully autonomous drilling systems.

title: E-Tactile Flow: Exploring A Novel Path of Pain Relief through Interactive Electrotactile Stimulation
abstract: Chronic or recurrent pain significantly impairs quality of life, and conventional pharmacological treatments often produce side effects, motivating the search for non-pharmacological alternatives. This study introduces a novel paradigm — E-Tactile Tactile Flow (E-Tactile Flow)—which integrates electrotactile stimulation with attentional engagement and flow-related task design. Inspired by a bidirectional attention mechanism, the paradigm designed goal-directed task mode and stimulus-driven task mode to examine the role of cognitive engagement in pain modulation. A preliminary study validated the feasibility and safety parameters of an 8×8 electrotactile system. In Experiment 1 (n = 42), both attention modes effectively reduced pain perception, with the goal-directed task mode showing significantly stronger modulation of several physiological measures and a marginal trend toward lower subjective pain ratings than the stimulus-driven task mode. Building on this, Experiment 2 introduced adaptive difficulty modulation to better align task challenge with participant performance. Results showed that dynamic task adjustment significantly enhanced attentional engagement and reduced pain ratings. Overall, this study provides initial empirical support for an electrotactile interaction paradigm for non-pharmacological pain modulation.

title: Early applications of apple vision pro in clinical medicine and medical education: a scoping review
abstract: The Apple Vision Pro (AVP), a next-generation spatial computing device, has demonstrated potential applications in multidisciplinary clinical diagnosis, treatment, and medical education, by leveraging its unique technical architecture and performance advantages. In clinical practice, its fundamental advantages of three-dimensional (3D) visualization, real-time image integration, and immersive interaction have been preliminarily employed in disease diagnosis and treatment, surgical planning, precise operations, and postoperative rehabilitation across multiple disciplines. In medical education, AVP surpasses the limitations of conventional models, offering a novel methodology for anatomy education, clinical skills development, specialized practical training, and collaboration of distance learning, thereby alleviating persistent challenges such as unequal distribution of teaching resources, low efficiency in skills and specialized training, and the high cost of distance education. However, AVP faces some limitations, including limited hardware portability, insufficient system compatibility, a lack of specialized medical applications, high costs, and incomplete medical certification. Currently, most evidence derives from feasibility studies, case reports, and opinion pieces. Only two Stage 2b confirmatory studies were identified. Thus, high-level evidence for clinical benefit remains scarce. Readers should interpret all reported benefits as preliminary technical demonstrations rather than established clinical outcomes. Future advancements necessitate iterative development of lightweight hardware design, development of specialized medical software, cross-system optimization, and establishment of standardization protocols. Moreover, more randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and multicenter studies are urgently needed to fully explore and validate its intrinsic value in precision medicine and the equitable allocation of medical resources.

title: Effects of a low dose of 3-nitrooxypropanol and a combination of direct-fed microbials on methane emission, oral swab bacterial community, and performance in dairy cows
abstract: Abstract Background 3-Nitrooxypropanol (3-NOP) can inhibit ruminal methane production by inactivating the key enzyme during methanogenesis. Combining 3-NOP and direct-fed microbials (DFM) can potentially provide a dual-action approach to reduce ruminal methane production. The objective of this study was to investigate the effects of supplementation of a low dose of 3-NOP and a mixture of DFM, on methane emissions, performance, and rumen microbial community of dairy cows. Results Forty-eight Danish Holstein dairy cows were used in a 14-week randomized complete block design. Due to a mixing error, 3-NOP was included at an unexpected low dose (6.0 mg/kg DM). Cows were fed with one of four experimental diets: (1) control diet, and other treatment diets were control diet supplemented with (2) 3-NOP, or with (3) DFM (12 mg/kg P. acidipropionici strain P169 and 120 mg/kg Bacillus subtilis and B. licheniformis mixture), or with (4) a combination of 3-NOP and DFM. 3-NOP inclusion did not affect DMI, feed efficiency, or milk yield and composition. DFM supplementation reduced partial mixed ration intake and total DMI. 3-NOP supplementation significantly reduced CH 4 production (g/d) (8%) and CH 4 intensity (g/kg ECM) (9%) but did not affect CH 4 yield (g/kg DMI). Furthermore, 3-NOP supplementation increased H 2 production, yield, and intensity. DFM supplementation reduced milk yield from weeks 3 to 8 and ECM yield from weeks 3 to 7, but these effects diminished over time. 3-NOP alone or in combination with DFM resulted in higher abundance of Megasphaera and Prevotella genera in oral swab samples. DFM supplementation had no effect on gas emissions, and it only tended to improve feed efficiency (ECM/DMI, kg/kg) during the later stage of the experiment. DFM supplementation led to higher abundance of certain species within the Lactobacillaceae family particularly at later stages of the experiment. Conclusions An unforeseen reduced dose of 3-NOP supplementation still can effectively mitigate methane emissions (both production and intensity) and increase H 2 emissions without affecting DMI or performance. DFM supplementation reduced DMI and milk yield at the onset of the experiment, but the effects subsided over time, resulting in an increased feed efficiency by the end of the experiment.

title: Electrochemical Detection of PFAS Contaminants Across Environmental and Pharmaceutical Matrices:Sensing Mechanisms, Nanomaterial Platforms, Biological Monitoring, and Regulatory Convergence
abstract: PFAS are a class of over 14,000 synthetic compounds characterized by a stable carbon-fluorine bond that confers resistance to thermal and biological degradation, resulting in common contamination of various aquatic matrices at concentrations ranging from sub-parts per trillion to parts per billion.Demand for directly deployable sensitive quantification methods has been spurred by increasingly stringent regulatory responses such as the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) proposed maximum contaminant levels of 4 ppt for PFOA and PFOS in 2024 under its third Fourth Unregulated Contaminant Monitoring Rule and sub-parametric values recommended by the EU Drinking Water Directive.Conventional liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry provides the required sensitivity but is still limited by centralized infrastructure and slow sample preparation that prevents point-of-care or real-time surveillance.Another critically understudied dimension includes pharmaceutical matrices, where PFAS can act as formulation excipients or derive from the synthesis of fluorinated active pharmaceutical ingredients and pharmacokinetically interfere with albumin binding and hepatic CYP450 activity in exposed populations.The current review summarized the existing electrochemical sensing strategies, including molecularly imprinted polymers, aptasensors, and CRISPR-Cas12a biosensors, and state-of-the-art electrode structures, including metal-organic frameworks, MXenes, and covalent triazine frameworks, for targeting PFAS in environmental and biological matrices.While some of these can be implemented analytically with detection below 1 ppt, critical benchmarking using regulatory thresholds reveals that 10% of sensor studies validate their performance in non-spiked field or clinical matrices.This highlights the need for multi-analyte array development to allow standardized sensor validation frameworks across environmental and pharmaceutical quality monitoring.
venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: Evaluation of the Hologic Aptima® Vaginitis and Seegene Allplex™ assays for microbiological diagnosis of bacterial vaginosis and Candida vaginitis in women in France, relative to Nugent score and culture
abstract: Introduction. Molecular assays such as the Hologic Aptima ® Vaginitis Panel and Seegene Allplex ™ Vaginitis assay offer improved sensitivity and multiplex detection for the diagnosis of vaginitis compared with the non-molecular standard of care. Gap Statement. Evidence comparing the relative performance of Aptima versus Seegene is limited, as is knowledge of Aptima’s compatibility with non-proprietary swabs. Aim. This prospective study assessed the diagnostic performance of the Aptima BV (bacterial vaginosis) and Aptima CV/TV assays ( Candida vaginitis/ Trichomonas vaginitis) alongside the Seegene Allplex assay in symptomatic women (≥18 years) presenting for vaginitis testing in primary care in France. Methodology. Two vaginal swabs were taken per patient: one Aptima Multitest Swab and one non-proprietary Σ-TRANSWAB liquid Amies collection swab. Aptima swab data were used solely to confirm performance of the Aptima assays under current test conditions, while all primary assay comparisons were performed using Σ-TRANSWAB samples. These comparisons were performed for each assay relative to Nugent score (for BV) or culture (for CV), as well as Aptima relative to Seegene. Results. In total, 500 women underwent vaginitis testing between July and August 2024. When using non-proprietary Σ-TRANSWAB collection methods, sensitivity and specificity values for the Aptima BV assay were 96.7 and 89.7% relative to Nugent score, and 89.9 and 90.6% for Seegene Allplex relative to Nugent score. Among ‘intermediate BV’ samples ( n =66), agreement between Seegene Allplex and Nugent score was 1.5%. Sensitivity and specificity values for the detection of CV were 88.6 and 90.8% for the Aptima CV/TV assay, and 90.2 and 93.7% for Seegene Allplex. Assay detection of TV could not be validated due to an insufficient number of TV-positive samples ( n =1). These findings were consistent with Aptima’s performance when using proprietary collection methods. Conclusion. Overall, the Aptima Vaginitis Panel demonstrated comparably high diagnostic performance to Seegene Allplex for the detection of BV and CV when using a non-proprietary sample collection method. TV prevalence was too low in this cohort to permit meaningful assay evaluation for this pathogen.
authors: Cécile Martaresche; Florian Scherrer

title: Evaluation of whole genome sequencing protocols and target-capture panels for detection of respiratory viruses in clinical specimens
abstract: Respiratory viruses are major contributors to global morbidity and mortality. When viral mutations compromise detection by conventional diagnostic assays, identifying cases and tracing transmission becomes challenging. Whole genome sequencing (WGS) improves on conventional diagnostics as it can detect viruses with novel mutations. This study evaluated the performance of the ePlex, a rapid multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assay (RMPA), an in-house real-time reverse transcription PCR assay (RT-qPCR) and WGS for detecting respiratory virus infections in clinical specimens. Sixty-one sequence libraries were prepared, and bait enriched from nasopharyngeal swabs, collected in 2021, which were negative for SARS-CoV-2 but positive for co-infections of respiratory viruses detected by the ePlex. An in-house bioinformatics pipeline enabled a metagenomic analysis approach to be compared with the ePlex and RT-qPCR. In most swabs, respiratory viruses were detected by WGS (average genome recovery: 85.9%) or RT-qPCR which concurred with the ePlex result, but as single viruses rather than co-infections. WGS recovered respiratory syncytial viruses (80%) and metapneumoviruses (70%) most often. This study demonstrates the power of WGS and bait capture in resolving the genomes of respiratory pathogens from limited clinical material. Detection of a single virus, rather than co-infections, in this instance could highlight the targeted nature of bait capture technology or competition between viruses during bait hybridization. The number of respiratory syncytial viruses detected (16/20) could be due to a spike in activity detected after the alleviation of non-pharmaceutical interventions in the COVID-19 pandemic.
authors: Daniel Kelly; Ketharani Yogananthan; Priya Subramaniam; Tiina Talts; Carmen F. Manso; Beatrix Kele; David Bibby; Mark A. Zuckerman; Jean Lutamyo Mbisa

title: Examining Post-Operative Antigen Specific CD8⁺ T Cell Dysfunction
abstract: Surgery remains the most effective approach to cure patients with solid malignancies. However, surgical trauma results in significant cellular immunosuppression. CD8⁺ T cell dysfunction post-operatively has been characterized, however the effects of surgery on antigen specific CD8⁺ T cell suppression has not been fully explored. Here, we established that surgery-induces antigen specific CD8⁺ T cell dysfunction, including impaired pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion and cytotoxicity in patients and mice. We developed a model to investigate surgical stress and cancer recurrence in C57Bl/6 mice, based on transfer of CD8⁺ OT-I T cells, reactive to ovalbumin (OVA), followed by challenge with B16-OVA melanoma cells. This model demonstrates 100% protection against cancer in control animals but 0% protection following surgery. Using a COVID-19 immunological tool kit to characterize post-operative function, we observed a significant suppression in T cells from vaccinated cancer patients. The OT-I model was used to evaluate the mechanisms of post-operative T cell dysfunction. We first established that a population of surgery induce Myeloid Derived Suppressor Cells (sxMDSCs) also known as GR-1⁺ cells in mice which expand after surgery in mice and cancer patients on post-operative day 1 (POD1), are suppressive of CD8⁺ T cells. We then performed single cell RNA sequencing, which identified the intracellular checkpoint CISH (Cytokine-inducible SH2-containing protein) as upregulated in antigen-stimulated human and murine CD8⁺ T cells following surgical stress. Overall, this work highlights antigen specific CD8⁺ T dysfunction post-operatively and uncovers a possible mechanism of dysfunction characterized by the expression of an intracellular checkpoint CISH.
authors: Oladunni Olanubi

title: Extracellular vesicle lipidomics liquid biopsy reveals systemic and tumor microenvironment metabolic reprogramming in ovarian cancer
abstract: Ovarian cancer is the most lethal gynecological malignancy, due to late-stage diagnosis, tumor heterogeneity, and lack of biomarkers for early detection. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) in plasma and ascites offer a minimally invasive source of tumor-derived information, yet their lipid composition and relationship to tumor heterogeneity remain poorly defined. We performed lipidomic profiling of EVs from plasma and ascites of high-grade serous ovarian cancer patients and from ovarian cancer and control cell lines to identify signatures of tumor progression and microenvironmental interactions. A lipid panel enriched in ovarian cancer EVs was evaluated in EVs and plasma across two independent cohorts (n = 146). Combined with CA125, this panel improved detection, particularly against benign adnexal masses, achieving an AUROC of 0.99 in the verification cohort in both formats. Ovarian cancer EVs preferentially accumulated triglycerides, including ether-linked species, whereas parental cells were enriched in phospholipids and ceramides. EV lipid signatures reflected tumor-associated metabolic reprogramming and captured tumor heterogeneity across cell models. These findings show that EV lipidomics from accessible biofluids offers a non-invasive window into ovarian cancer metabolism and candidate biomarkers for patient stratification and monitoring.
authors: Shikha Rani; Dominic Guanzon; Andrew Lai; Katherin Scholz‐Romero; Sarah Reed; Edita Ritmejerytė; Rohan Lourie; Naven Chetty; Kaltin Ferguson; Carlos Salomón

title: FORENSIC CLASSIFICATION OF GUNSHOT RESIDUE PARTICLES USING SEM-EDX AND MACHINE LEARNING
abstract: Machine learning (ML) is increasingly shaping forensic science by enabling more accurate and objective evidence analysis. This study applies ML algorithms to classify gunshot residue (GSR) particles using spectral data obtained through scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDX). Conventional GSR identification relies on detecting characteristic inorganic particles containing lead (Pb), barium (Ba), and antimony (Sb), which point to firearm discharge residue. Twelve spectra were collected from four hand swabs taken during a simulated shooting scenario, alongside control samples that yielded no residue signal. The particles were analysed for elemental distribution and subjected to ML-assisted classification. A statistical framework combining probabilistic modelling with likelihood ratios (LRs) was then used to weigh the evidential strength of competing hypotheses. Results revealed marked differences in elemental composition across samples, underscoring the importance of rigorous statistical treatment rather than relying solely on visual or qualitative assessment. Three of the four swab classes offered strong support for GSR presence, yielding high LRs favouring the prosecution hypothesis. One sample, however, deviated from the model's underlying assumptions, illustrating how elemental signatures alone can be misleading if interpreted without appropriate methodological safeguards. Overall, integrating ML with probabilistic modelling offers a robust framework for forensic GSR analysis. Nonetheless, the findings highlight that methodological rigor cannot be sacrificed for computational convenience, and analysts should remain attentive to cases where statistical assumptions break down.
authors: Tolulope Bayode Abejide; Graham Souch; David Olayemi Alebiosu

title: Factors Associated With Moderate‐to‐Severe Pain After Paediatric Laparoscopic Pyeloplasty: Implications for Nursing Care
abstract: BACKGROUND: Moderate-to-severe pain remains a clinically relevant concern after paediatric laparoscopic pyeloplasty and may interfere with early recovery. Identifying children at increased risk may support more timely and individualized perioperative pain management. AIMS: To investigate factors associated with moderate-to-severe pain after laparoscopic pyeloplasty in children and to inform targeted nursing and perioperative management strategies. METHODS: This single-centre retrospective observational study included children undergoing laparoscopic pyeloplasty. Postoperative pain was assessed at 2, 6, 12 and 24 h using either a Faces Pain Scale or the Face, Legs, Activity, Cry and Consolability (FLACC) scale according to age and communication ability. Moderate-to-severe pain was defined as a score ≥ 4 at any assessment within 24 h. Demographic, disease-related, surgical and perioperative variables were analysed. Multivariable binary logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with moderate-to-severe pain, and repeated-measures analysis of variance was used to assess changes in pain scores over time. This study was reported in accordance with the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) guidelines. RESULTS: Among 258 children, 65 developed moderate-to-severe postoperative pain, corresponding to an incidence of 25.2%. Multivariable analysis showed that age < 3 years, significant preoperative anxiety, operative time ≥ 120 min and the absence of a regional block were independently associated with moderate-to-severe pain. Sex, severe hydronephrosis and postoperative drainage tube placement were not independently associated with the outcome. Pain scores were highest at approximately 6 h after surgery, with significant group, time and group-by-time interaction effects. CONCLUSION: Moderate-to-severe pain is relatively common during the early postoperative period after paediatric laparoscopic pyeloplasty. Early risk identification, preoperative psychological support, appropriate regional analgesia and intensified pain assessment during the first 6-12 h may improve perioperative pain management. Prospective multicentre studies are warranted to validate these findings and develop clinically applicable risk-stratification strategies.
authors: Yueqin Xiang; Ruxia Min; Lianlian Ge; Lanzheng Bian

title: Feasibility Of a Multi-Modal Sensing Guidewire for Tissue Interaction Awareness in Bronchoscopic Lung Cancer Intervention: A Conceptual Architecture and Validation Roadmap
abstract: Bronchoscopicaccess to peripheral pulmonary lesions has been transformed by navigation, robotic, and imaging-assisted platforms, yet the physical interaction between an instrument tip and airway tissue remains difficult to quantify directly.Conventional guidewires provide push ability, torque transmission, and mechanical steering, but generally do not return a direct quantitative signal describing tissue interaction.This paper presents a literature-grounded feasibility framework that reimagines the guidewire as a multimodal sensing platform rather than a purely mechanical component.Four complementary sensing channelsforce, localized pressure, electrical impedance, and temperature-are proposed within a guidewire-centred architecture.The methodology comprises channel calibration and signal conditioning, temporal synchronization, feature extraction, lightweight edgeassisted sensor fusion, confidence estimation, and human-in-the-loop clinician feedback.Artificial intelligence is deliberately positioned as a supporting interpretation layer for procedural interaction states rather than as an autonomous cancer-diagnosis mechanism.The study analyses the principal mechanical, electrical, miniaturization, packaging, safety, and manufacturing constraints and defines a staged validation pathway from component calibration and bench testing through tissue-mimicking phantom evaluation, AI validation, preclinical feasibility, and eventual clinical feasibility.No prototype measurements or clinical diagnostic performance are claimed in the present work.The principal outcome is a coherent, experimentally testable architecture and validation roadmap that identifies how quantitative instrumenttissue information could complement existing bronchoscopic navigation while preserving clinician control.Advanced technologies are retained as future extensions outside the present scope. title: Frameless VarioGuide biopsy for pediatric brainstem lesions in the molecular era: diagnostic performance and workflow characteristics in a comparative single-center series
abstract: BACKGROUND: Molecular characterization has become essential for the diagnosis and treatment of pediatric brainstem lesions. While frame-based stereotactic and robotic-assisted biopsies are well established, comparative data on frameless VarioGuide biopsy for pediatric brainstem lesions remain scarce. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance, safety, and workflow characteristics of frameless VarioGuide biopsy compared with frame-based stereotactic and ROSA-assisted techniques. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed all pediatric patients (≤ 18 years) who underwent stereotactic biopsy of a brainstem lesion at a single tertiary neurosurgical center between 2016 and 2026. Patients were grouped according to biopsy technique (frameless VarioGuide, frame-based stereotaxy, or ROSA-assisted biopsy). Diagnostic yield, molecular diagnostic yield, complications, operative times, and workflow parameters were analyzed. RESULTS: Twenty-two pediatric patients met inclusion criteria. Six underwent frameless VarioGuide biopsy, nine frame-based stereotactic biopsy, and seven ROSA-assisted biopsy. Overall diagnostic and molecular diagnostic yields were 95%. Diagnostic and molecular diagnostic yields were 100% with VarioGuide, 89% with frame-based stereotactic biopsy, and 100% with ROSA-assisted biopsy, without statistically significant differences between groups (p = 0.62). Median operative times were similar among groups (32, 36, and 25 min, respectively; p = 0.28). However, preoperative setup time differed significantly, with the shortest duration observed in the VarioGuide cohort (40.5 min) compared with ROSA-assisted biopsy (64 min) and frame-based stereotaxy (112 min; p = 0.002). Despite the absence of intraoperative neuropathological assessment, all VarioGuide procedures yielded diagnostically and molecular-pathologically informative tissue. No procedure-related hemorrhage, infection, permanent neurological deficit, or procedure-related mortality were observed. CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory single-center cohort, frameless VarioGuide biopsy achieved high diagnostic and molecular diagnostic yields without permanent procedure-related morbidity and was associated with shorter preoperative setup time. These findings support further evaluation of frameless VarioGuide biopsy as a workflow-efficient approach for tissue acquisition in pediatric brainstem lesions.
authors: Sepide Kashefiolasl; Karsten Lachner; Christian Joerg Braun; Katharina Johanna Weber; Luciana Porto; Marcus Czabanka; Tobias Finger

title: From imaging enhancement to surgical autonomy: the evolutionary role of nanotechnology in AI-driven robotic surgery
abstract: Robot-assisted minimally invasive surgery provides stable visualisation and manipulation, but direct access to local tissue state remains limited. Lesion boundaries, mechanics, molecular activity and microenvironmental changes are often inferred from conventional feedback. This review evaluates how nano-enabled imaging, flexible and local sensing, and micro/nanorobotic intervention may extend signals and localised actions in robot-assisted procedures. We organise the evidence along an information-flow framework: signal acquisition, processing or computational interpretation, task-relevant state estimation, conversion into a decision variable or control-relevant input, and feedback-guided robotic action. Processing may involve calibration, signal processing, computational modelling, conventional machine learning, deep learning or artificial intelligence (AI)-based methods. The evidence reviewed is strongest for localised signal acquisition and supervised intervention. Selected forms of computational interpretation have been demonstrated, and localisation- or motion-derived geometric states enter feedback controllers in some systems. By contrast, biochemical, spectral, tactile and physiological states are usually displayed, analysed offline or returned through human-facing feedback; they rarely modify an online surgical controller. Closed-loop navigation in phantoms, surrogate-device studies and constrained navigation autonomy therefore represent partial control capabilities, not clinically relevant surgical autonomy. The principal missing transitions are robust validation of task-relevant tissue states, uncertainty-aware conversion of those states into control inputs, and safe action within realistic surgical workflows. Near-term clinical use is more likely to centre on bounded nano-enabled sensing or intervention modules embedded within supervised procedures. Progress towards bounded task autonomy will require reproducibility, material safety, workflow compatibility, explicit human supervision and prospective evidence of patient and task benefits.
authors: Jiahao Zhu; Shengcheng Tai; Zhihang Zhang; Ruicheng Wu; Dengxiong Li; Xiaodong Jin

title: Fully automatic airway segmentation in CT images via dual-stage neural network with topology-constrained centerline completion
abstract: Background: Precise segmentation of airways from computed tomography (CT) images is critical for pre-procedural planning in navigational bronchoscopy; however, existing methods often suffer from distal branch fractures and morphological losses due to slender diameters, low contrast, and noise. To address these limitations and achieve accurate, topologically complete airway segmentation, this study proposed a novel dual-stage neural network with topology-constrained centerline completion. Methods: A two-stage centerline-guided network (TSC-Net) was developed that innovatively combines centerline structural similarity (CSS) loss and centerline overlap rate (COR) loss. CSS loss maintains the continuity of airway tree structures by strengthening centerline morphological constraints, while COR loss enhances global centerline overlap to ensure branch integrity. Additionally, a topology-difference-driven fracture-region completion mechanism was adopted to adaptively repair the fracturedand misclassified areas. The model employs a residual UNet (ResUNet) backbone integrated with an atrous spatial pyramid pooling (ASPP) module to capture multi-scale contextual features and adopts a two-stage training strategy in which the encoder is frozen during stage 2 while the decoder is fine-tuned using dynamically adjusted loss weights. This strategy enables targeted optimization of discontinuous regions without compromising globally well-predicted areas. Results: Experiments on the Airway Tree Modeling Challenge 2022 (ATM'22), Lung Image Database Consortium and Image Database Resource Initiative (LIDC-IDRI), Extraction of Airways from CT (EXACT'09), and private datasets showed that TSC-Net achieved a Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 93.2%±2.1%, significantly outperforming SwinUNETR (92.9%±3.6%, P<0.05), nnUNet (91.2%±1.2%, P<0.05), and UNet (75.6%±4.3%, P<0.05). The tree-length detection (TD) rate reached 95.5%±4.2%, and the branch detection (BD) rate reached 92.6%±3.6%, both of which were significantly higher than those of all baseline methods (P<0.01). Moreover, the segmented distal branches exhibited continuous and smooth morphology. Conclusions: Overall, our method significantly enhanced both segmentation accuracy and distal branch integrity in automated CT-based airway segmentation through multi-dimensional feature enhancement, topological constraint optimization, and a dynamic completion mechanism. This method holds great promise for pre-procedural planning in robotic-assisted bronchoscopy by enabling accurate visualization of peripheral airways and facilitating navigation to distant pulmonary targets.
authors: Harmony Yuan; Yuan Cheng; Chengxi Yan; Jiangang Chen; Qian Ding; Ying Zhou; Minglei Yang
venue: Quantitative Imaging in Medicine and Surgery

title: GPU-resident Execution for Timing-predictable Sensor Processing Systems
abstract: Real-time embedded systems increasingly place GPU-accelerated processing of high-bandwidth sensor streams inside closed-loop systems, but the CPU (the host) remains the primary orchestrator of each iteration. The host observes sensor inputs, submits CUDA work, waits for completion, and commits actuation. This host-mediated path exposes the closed-loop end-to-end latency to I/O interrupts, host scheduler decisions, and CUDA API overheads even after common host-side mitigations such as GPU-memory RDMA or CPU core isolation. This paper presents GPU-resident Execution, a new execution model for real-time sensor processing pipelines that keeps I/O and GPU execution in a long-lived device-resident loop. Sensor inputs arrive in GPU memory, trigger GPU-side processing, and reach GPU-visible output endpoints without any host wakeups. We implement the model in the NVIDIA Holoscan C++ framework and provide reference components for building GPU-resident applications. We evaluate our system on NVIDIA GPUs and SoCs with inference, host-contention, multi-loop, and streaming camera workloads. On an industry-grade 1080p, 60 Hz real-time camera-to-display application, GPU-resident Execution reduces photon-to-display jitter from 4.83 ms to 0.66 ms (7.3x) relative to a CPU-driven GPU-memory RDMA baseline and reduces software-processing jitter from 1.70 ms to 0.01 ms (170x).
authors: Soham Sinha; Rahul Choudhury; Shekhar Dwivedi; Gregory Lee; Gigon Bae; Anisha Goel; Elena Agostini; Patrick O'Grady; Yosi Levi; Mahdi Azizian

title: Genomic tracking of Campylobacter jejuni along poultry and pig value chains in Northeast India: Implications for food safety
abstract: Campylobacter jejuni is the predominant causative agent of human campylobacteriosis. A total of 864 samples (poultry cloacal swabs, chicken intestine, chicken meat, pig rectal swab, pig intestine, pork) were screened for the presence of C. jejuni using standard methods. A total of 27 isolates were confirmed with PCR with an overall occurrence rate of 3.13%. Highest isolation rates were from chicken intestine samples (9.72%), followed by pork (7.64%) and chicken meat (1.39%). Resistance levels were high towards nalidixic acid, tetracycline, ampicillin and ciprofloxacin. Multidrug-resistance and biofilm formation featured in 30.77% and 53.84% isolates, respectively. Genomic characterization identified the highest presence of T86I mutation in gyrA and cmeABC system. The isolates were abundant with important virulence genes such as cdtABC, wlan, neuABC and cstIII . The isolates belonged to diverse Penner serotypes and MLST types with ST 353 complex being the predominant clonal complex. Phylogenetic analysis indicated tendency of the genomes with similar ST/CC to cluster together and indicated wide genetic diversity . To the best of our knowledge, this serves as the first genome submission of C. jejuni from porcine sources of India. Further, this study underscores the need for exploiting modern technologies, including genomics, to study various food-borne pathogens.
authors: Arockiasamy Arun Prince Milton; Kandhan Srinivas; Heiborkie Shilla; Balusamy Dhayananth; Samir Das; G Bhuvana Priya; Sandeep Ghatak

title: Haematological alterations in dogs with canine distemper virus-associated respiratory tract infection in Guwahati, Assam
abstract: Canine distemper is a multisystemic viral disease of dogs in which the blood picture changes with the stage of infection and with secondary complications. This study evaluated the haematological alterations in dogs with respiratory tract infection associated with canine distemper virus (CDV) under field conditions in Guwahati, Assam, India. Twelve dogs formed two groups of six: dogs with respiratory signs that were positive for CDV antigen in a rapid immunochromatographic test of nasal and conjunctival swabs (CDV group) and apparently healthy dogs (control group). Haemoglobin (Hb), total erythrocyte count (TEC), packed cell volume (PCV), thrombocyte count, total leukocyte count (TLC), and differential leukocyte percentages were measured with an automated haematology analyser. Groups were compared by the independent samples t-test, with P < 0.05 considered significant. Dogs in the CDV group had significantly (P < 0.01) lower Hb (42.3%), TEC (32.3%), PCV (25.5%), and thrombocyte count (40.3%) than the control group, and all four values were below the canine reference limits. The TLC was significantly (P < 0.01) higher (46.2%), with higher percentages of granulocytes and monocytes and a lower percentage of lymphocytes. The absolute granulocyte (14.45 × 103/µL) and monocyte (1.68 × 103/µL) counts estimated from the group means exceeded the upper reference limits, whereas the estimated lymphocyte count (1.77 × 103/µL) remained within the reference interval. The results indicate anaemia, thrombocytopenia, and granulocytic leukocytosis with monocytosis in CDV-infected dogs and suggest that the fall in lymphocytes was relative and not absolute.
authors: Shveta Singh; Deepa Lahkar; Arabinda Phukan; Ditul Barman; Durlav Prasad Bora; Lukumoni Buragohain; Archana Hazarika

title: Health Care Teams Under Pressure: The Impact of Complexity on Team Cognition and Team Performance
abstract: Healthcare teams play a central role in delivering care to patients and their families. Teamwork has been shown to be directly related to clinical performance and patient outcomes, making it essential that these teams receive appropriate training, feedback, and assessment. These teams work in complex, dynamic environments characterized by changing team membership, time pressures, and large amounts of information that may be ambiguous, missing, or unknown. These characteristics make it difficult to fully capture team-level performance. Despite the critical role of healthcare teams, most approaches to measuring team performance are static, capturing what teams do rather than how or why performance emerges. This study investigated the dynamics of team cognition in complex, dynamic environments. Using a concurrent mixed methods design with a qualitative strand nested within the quantitative strand, this observational study addressed three questions: 1) What patterns exist in team communication and coordination behaviours, and how do these vary with team experience and case complexity 2) How does the rate of team cognition mediate the relationship between case complexity and team performance, 3) What insights do teams’ reflections and reflexive practices provide into the cognitive processes that shape their performance. Data were collected from video recordings of flight paramedic teams performing simulated scenarios, demographic surveys, reflective interviews, and performance scores. Lag sequential analysis (LSA) was used to identify significant patterns of behaviour, and mediation analysis was used to determine whether the rate of team cognition mediated the relationship between case complexity and team performance. Thematic analysis of the post-simulation interviews provided additional insight into the cognitive processes underlying team performance. Findings showed that communication is central to developing shared understanding. Teams relied on adaptive coordination to respond to the changing environment. Empirical evidence shows that behavioural sequences were observable, forming a part of paramedic clinical practice, and varying by team experience. These findings provide a preliminary perspective on team cognition and team performance in dynamic environments.
authors: de Vries, Ingrid

title: How exposed is work to robotics? Occupational, industry, and geographic measures
abstract: Exposure indices that map technical capabilities onto occupational abilities have become a standard tool for anticipating how AI may reshape work, but existing measures either cover software AI or proxy robotics through patents and installation data that reflect the industrial robots of past decades. We construct the first abilities-based exposure measures for robotics and physical AI, and the first to span occupations, industries, and geographies. Following the framework of Felten et al. (2018, 2021), we build a robotics capability taxonomy of 16 capabilities in eight domains from 78 academic, industry, and standards sources, use a large language model to score the relatedness of each capability to the 52 ONET work abilities, and aggregate to Robotics Occupational Exposure (ROE) for 774 occupations, Robotics Industry Exposure (RIE) for 250 NAICS industries, and county-level Robotics Geographic Exposure (RGE). We find that robotics exposure concentrates in physically intensive work such as construction, farming, transportation, and production, and in industries such as logging, mining, trucking, and warehousing. Unlike generative-AI exposure, ROE is higher in occupations with lower wages, lower education requirements, and less creative-ability content. Physical collaboration and assistance, terrain-based locomotion, grasping and handling, and task and functional reasoning move the exposure ranking most, yet no single capability carries the index. Because the measures capture technical relatedness rather than readiness, cost, or adoption, they should be read as an upper bound on where physical automation could affect work.
authors: Sebastian Sartor; Robert Seamans; Neil Thompson

title: Humoral Immunity and Variant Cross-Reactivity Following Asymptomatic and Symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 Infection and Vaccination in Young Adults (The ACE Cohort)
abstract: Abstract Purpose Asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection was a driving force of the COVID-19 pandemic, acting as a silent transmitter of the virus. The question of whether asymptomatic immunity differs from symptomatic immunity remains, as existing studies fail to recruit ‘well-defined’ asymptomatic individuals. Here, we conducted a longitudinal cohort study to evaluate humoral responses to infection and vaccination in asymptomatic predominantly young adults identified as part of the Asymptomatic COVID-19 in Education [ACE] cohort. Methods Asymptomatic testing services, located at three UK universities, identified asymptomatic adults who were subsequently recruited with age- and sex-matched symptomatic and uninfected controls. Blood and saliva samples were collected after SARS-CoV-2 Wuhan infection, and again after vaccination. Over 500 participants were recruited, and their IgG and IgA titres were measured in response to 5 Variants of Concern. Results Pre-vaccination, asymptomatic individuals exhibit significantly lower IgG responses to four of the tested variants; Wuhan, Alpha, Beta, and Delta, compared to symptomatic individuals; these differences diminished post-vaccination. In addition, there were key differences in terms of IgG cross-reactivity, where symptomatic individuals displayed stronger IgG cross-reactivity than asymptomatic and uninfected individuals, alluding to better protection from emerging variants. Individuals without prior natural infection displayed reduced IgG responses compared to symptomatic individuals, to all variants, post-vaccination. Despite their low IgG, salivary IgA levels in uninfected individuals were high, pre-vaccination. Conclusion This work demonstrates the requirement of vaccinations to enhance weaker IgG responses but also highlights that vaccines need to be constantly adapted to overcome viral evolution, particularly with more done to improve mucosal delivery options for respiratory viruses to enhance IgA responses.

title: Impact of Nasopharyngeal Swab Freezing Storage on the De-tection of Common Respiratory Viral Molecular Targets
abstract: Archived respiratory specimens are valuable for retrospective diagnostic studies, although long-term storage may affect viral RNA detection. This study evaluated nasopharyngeal swabs (NPS) stored at −80 °C for at least one year and retested using automated molecular assays with different multiplexing formats. Qualitative agreement with initial results and changes in cycle threshold (Ct) values were assessed, with discordant results investigated using an independent assay. SARS-CoV-2 showed the highest stability (positive percent agreement, PPA: 97.1–98.6%; mean Ct increase: 2.8–3.4), followed by respiratory syncytial virus (RSV; PPA: 88.4–97.1%; mean Ct increase: 1.75–4.50) and influenza virus (PPA: 80.0–92.9%; mean Ct increase: 5.48–7.92). Ct increases were significant for all viral targets. Differences across assay configurations suggested that assay formulation and target characteristics may influence post-storage detection. NPS aliquots stored at −80 °C remain useful for retrospective molecular testing, although target- and assay-dependent signal loss should be considered when interpreting results from archived specimens. title: Improved metabolic profiles, body condition score and body weight as positive modulators of conception rate of nondescript pre-partum does fed concentrates
abstract: Does fed with roughage and concentrate had higher average body weight (p<0.01) and body condition score (p<0.05) from the second month until the end of the feeding period. Mean serum cholesterol concentrations were higher (p<0.05) in does fed roughage and concentrate compared to those fed roughage alone except during the first blood collection, while no significant differences (p>0.05) were found in mean serum triglyceride and glucose levels. Does fed with roughage and concentrate showed 100% estrus, 80% conception rate, shorter estrus cycle length (29.4 days vs. 32.6 days), and higher conception rate (80% compared to 37.5%) than does fed with roughage only.

title: Integrated Microfluidic CRISPR-Based Diagnostic Device for Rapid Testing of HPVs
abstract: Screening for high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) is a pivotal strategy for the prevention of invasive cervical cancer, particularly in resource-constrained settings. In this study, we developed a CRISPR-based compact automated real-time detection system, termed Ccard, for rapid testing of HPV16, HPV18, and the internal reference gene GAPDH through a streamlined workflow. A simple room-temperature treatment efficiently releases nucleic acids directly from swab samples, bypassing the need for extraction. The mixture was driven through the channels and loaded into the reaction chambers on the microfluidic chip by a vacuum pump. The lyophilized reagents in the reaction zone of the microfluidic chip were redissolved. The system subsequently performs a single-step RPA-CRISPR/Cas13a reaction, with real-time detection enabled by an Internet of Things device. The assay achieved detection within 30 min, with a limit of detection (LOD) of 5 copies/µL for both HPV16 and HPV18. Validation with clinical samples demonstrated high sensitivity (96.8% for HPV16 and 100% for HPV18) and 100% specificity. These results highlight the reliability, precision, and strong potential of the Ccard system for rapid testing of HR-HPVs.
authors: Tianci Wang; Lingyun Li; Yunxiang Wang; Yongjun Han; Teng Li; Chaoran Yu; Yufeng Lou; Zhen Rong; Kai Lin; Shengqi Wang

title: Integrity Detection and Characterization of Malicious Injections in RAVEN II
abstract: The increasing adoption of robotic systems in surgery, together with the expanding range of procedures they can support and the growing level of autonomy they provide, has substantially increased the complexity of surgical robots. As these systems integrate more sensors, controllers, communication interfaces, and model-driven control components, their attack surface continues to expand. A compromise of the integrity of a surgical robot can therefore cause unintended robot behavior and potentially threaten patient safety. In this paper, we characterize the detection boundary of malicious injections on RAVEN II using a public dataset that pairs the platform's telemetry with external high-resolution encoder ground truth. We identify three injection points spanning the command and observation paths and evaluate three injection patterns with increasing temporal dispersion. To capture different detection behaviors, we perform detection at two timescales: the window scale and the session scale. Rather than reporting detection rates at an arbitrarily chosen threshold, we quantify, for each injection point and injection pattern, the smallest end-effector deviation that can be resolved while maintaining an alarm rate acceptable for surgical operation. Our results show that detectability is strongly influenced by how the injected deviation is distributed over time. An abrupt step can be detected at deviations well below the 1 mm clinical tolerance, whereas the same overall deviation spread across a window or a session can remain hidden from single-window statistics. The open source code can be found at http://github.com/RAVENIIROS/RAVENIIIntegrity.

title: Intracardiac echocardiography during invasive electrophysiological procedures
abstract: Intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) is an imaging technique that provides real-time, detailed visualization of intracardiac structures during various interventional procedures performed in the electrophysiology laboratory. Over the past decades, ICE has evolved beyond simply assisting with transseptal puncture, becoming an auxiliary tool in numerous aspects of cardiac interventions. This scientific statement offers a comprehensive, systematic overview of current applications of ICE across different clinical scenarios. The existing evidence regarding the benefits of ICE is primarily derived from observational studies, which complicates the formulation of definitive advice for its clinical use. Thus, this document aims to serve as a practical roadmap, emphasizing the key benefits of the technique. The document covers fundamental principles of ICE imaging, standardized views, its role in transseptal puncture, ablation of supraventricular and ventricular arrhythmias, reduction of procedural radiation, early detection and management of periprocedural complications, identification of infective endocarditis, and the role of ICE for endomyocardial biopsy and left atrial appendage occlusion procedures.

title: Investigating the antigenicity of the lyssavirus glycoprotein
abstract: Rabies, the archetypal lyssavirus, is one of the most feared viruses known to man and globally, is the cause of more than 55,000 deaths per year. Alongside rabies virus, numerous related lyssaviruses exist that are also capable of causing fatal disease, clinically indistinguishable from rabies. Whilst the human burden of these non-rabies lyssaviruses remains unknown, fatalities have been reported. The lyssavirus glycoprotein is the sole target for virus neutralising antibodies and several amino acid epitopes have been linked to virus neutralisation. Lyssaviruses are genetically and antigenically categorised into phylogroups that indicate the level of protection afforded by current vaccines. It is generally accepted that an antibody response to the currently available rabies vaccines affords protection against all viruses that are categorised into phylogroup I. However, this antibody response does not protect against lyssavirus species within phylogroups II and III. Indeed, experimental data has shown that the antibody repertoire induced by rabies virus vaccines is unable to neutralise viruses in these phylogroups. In this study we have generated lentivirus pseudotypes representing all currently defined lyssaviruses as well as including chimeric lyssavirus glycoproteins that have had their antigenic sites swapped between phylogroup I and II viruses. Using the wildtype lyssavirus pseudotypes we have confirmed a strong level of intra-phylogroup neutralisation in addition to very limited inter-phylogroup neutralisation. The antigenic site swap constructs have shown an alteration in both glycoprotein functionality alongside altered neutralisation profiles using a variety of vaccine induced and divergent lyssavirus specific sera. Promising cross protective candidates have been cloned into a vaccine strain full length backbone and reverse genetics has enabled rescue of these viruses. The growth kinetics of recombinant viruses have been studied in vitro and an investigation into the pathogenicity and degree of vaccine induced protection against these viruses in vivo has been conducted.

title: Isolation and Identification of Microorganisms Associated with Automated Teller Machines in Calabar Metropolis
abstract: The metallic keyboards of automated teller machines situated within Calabar metropolis were investigated for microbial contamination due to their vast dermal contact by multiple users. Swab sticks soaked with normal sterile saline were used to collect specimens from the keypads. Isolation was done on nutrient agar and eosine methylene blue (EMB) for bacteria and Sabouraud dextrose agar for fungi using standard microbiological procedures. Identification of microorganisms was done using colonial, microscopic and biochemical characteristics. The results reveal that these machines that serve as cash dispensing device can be a potential disease dispensing machines as samples analyzed revealed bacterial isolates such as Staphylococcus spp (32%)), Bacillus spp (24%), Escherichia spp (20%), Pseudomonas spp (18%) and Salmonella spp (6%) while fungal isolates of the samples analyzed include microorganisms such as Rhizopus spp (56%), Aspergillus spp, (25%) and Penicillium spp (19%). These findings necessitate the need for adequate personal hygiene by users and frequent routine cleaning of these machines by the bank’s authorities is highly recommended.

title: LC−MS-Based Chlorine-Signature Query Engine Strategy for Automated Discovery of Phosphate-Containing Metabolites
abstract: Abstract Comprehensive profiling of phosphate-containing compounds (PCCs) in untargeted metabolomics remains challenging due to their high hydrophilicity, poor separation, and low stability, which hampers high-throughput screening from large-scale liquid chromatography−mass spectrometry (LC−MS) datasets. Herein, an LC-MS-based chlorine-tagging strategy integrated with a Chlorine Signature Query Engine (Cl-SQE) was established for the rapid identification of potential PCCs in complex matrices. The novel derivatization reagent, [5-(2-chlorophenyl)isoxazol-3-yl]methyl amine (ClXIMA), can react with phosphate groups on PCCs, such as nucleotides, sugar phosphates, glycerophosphates, and nucleotide sugars under mild conditions, thereby markedly enhancing reversed-phase retention and separation resolution. More importantly, the incorporation of chlorine, identifiable by its characteristic isotopic peak pattern, provides a unique digital signature in the mass spectra. Leveraging these features, Cl-SQE, a data mining program, was developed to systematically and automatically extract candidate PCCs from large-scale datasets. By applying this strategy to liver tissues from a mouse model of cholestasis, 318 potential ClXIMA derivatives were screened out, and 189 metabolites were identified or tentatively assigned. Statistical analysis revealed significant disturbances in nucleotide metabolism, addressing a critical gap in phospho-metabolomic profiling for cholestatic disease and revealing dysregulated nucleotide homeostasis as a potential feature of cholestasis-associated metabolic remodeling. Overall, this platform facilitates the discovery of PCCs in complex matrices and provides new insights into the pathogenesis of cholestasis and other clinical diseases.

title: Large-scale characterization of the bovine virome reveals viral diversity and community patterns in Northwest China
abstract: Cattle play a critical role in global agriculture and food security while serving as hosts for diverse viruses with potential implications for animal and public health. To comprehensively characterize the bovine virome and its community patterns, we conducted a large-scale characterization of the beef cattle-associated virome in Northwest China using viral metagenomic sequencing. A total of 2,353 specimens, including nasal swabs, anal swabs, and serum, were collected from 794 cattle across 28 sites in Shaanxi, Gansu, and Ningxia, with nasal and anal swab specimens used for the metagenomic analyses. High-throughput sequencing identified viruses belonging to 14 phyla, 32 classes, 39 orders, 71 families, and 397 genera, revealing substantial viral diversity. Descriptive comparisons of the pooled libraries revealed differences in virome composition across geographic regions, farming systems, and sampling seasons, with the summer pool showing greater viral richness and contig abundance than the winter pool. Phylogenetic analyses revealed genetic relationships between several viral sequences detected in this study and viral lineages previously reported from humans and other animal hosts, raising hypotheses regarding broader host associations and potential cross-species transmission that require further investigation. Targeted PCR/RT-PCR screening and cell-culture-based virus characterization provided complementary validation of representative metagenomic findings and revealed frequent co-detection of multiple viral targets among the sampled cattle. Collectively, this study provides a large-scale characterization of the beef cattle-associated virome in Northwest China, expands current knowledge of viral diversity associated with beef cattle populations, and establishes a valuable resource for future virome surveillance, studies of viral evolution, and disease prevention.
authors: Lingling Jiang; Yunyi Kong; Gang Zhang; Pu Wang; Min Fang; Qiang Liu; Sinong Zhang; Yong Li

title: Limited efficacy of enrofloxacin against Mesomycoplasma ovipneumoniae infection in domestic lambs
abstract: Mesomycoplasma ovipneumoniae is an important respiratory pathogen in sheep that leads to pneumonia and reduced productivity, commonly upon co-infection with other opportunistic microbes. Whether M. ovipneumoniae infection can be successfully treated with antibiotics is unclear. Our pilot study evaluated the efficacy of enrofloxacin (Baytril ® ) for treating experimental M. ovipneumoniae infection in domestic lambs. Ten 3-month-old specific-pathogen-free lambs were randomly assigned to a treatment and an untreated control group. Lambs were inoculated with fresh nasal wash fluids from M. ovipneumoniae- positive sheep. After 4 weeks, the treatment group received enrofloxacin at 0.5 mg/kg in 200 mL of saline intranasally and 5 mg/kg subcutaneously on five consecutive days. Lambs were observed for an additional 4 weeks, with daily health scoring, weekly assessment of weight gain, and weekly nasal swab quantitative (q)PCR analysis for M. ovipneumoniae and Mannheimia haemolytica . Successful M. ovipneumoniae infection of all lambs was confirmed by qPCR 1 week after inoculation. While overall health scores and average daily weight gains were statistically similar between groups, enrofloxacin administration significantly accelerated the rate of body temperature decline over the post-treatment period ( P = 0.007). Interestingly, all treated lambs tested negative for M. ovipneumoniae by qPCR 1 week after treatment. However, there was a re-emergence of M. ovipneumoniae infection 2 weeks after treatment with 1/5 lambs testing positive, and 3/5 lambs tested positive 4 weeks after treatment. Co-infection with Mannheimia haemolytica was detected in all lambs, with a similar temporary suppression after enrofloxacin treatment. Endpoint tissue swab samples revealed variable qPCR detection of M. ovipneumoniae , with a trend for reduced infection of the lower respiratory tract in the treated lambs. However, middle ear swabs from all lambs tested qPCR-positive for M. ovipneumoniae , suggesting that the middle ear is a potential reservoir of this pathogen. Tissues collected after euthanasia showed reduced histopathological lung lesions in the enrofloxacin-treated group (Mann–Whitney U test, P = 0.032 ). Amongst four M. ovipneumoniae isolates recovered from the lung of one enrofloxacin-treated lamb, one isolate showed reduced susceptibility to enrofloxacin in vitro . Overall, our study showed that enrofloxacin treatment was only partially successful in reducing M. ovipneumoniae infection in domestic lambs.
