title: Robotic-assisted bronchoscopic biopsy and EBUS-TBNA in lung cancer: An outcome comparison between clinical and pathological staging.
abstract: Accurate mediastinal staging of suspected lung cancer is critical for guiding treatment and determining prognosis. While computed tomography (CT) and positron emission tomography (PET) are integral to initial staging, both modalities have limitations for detecting nodal metastases. Endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration (EBUS-TBNA) provides a minimally invasive option for obtaining tissue confirmation. This study evaluates the impact of adding EBUS-TBNA at the time of lung tumor biopsy on mediastinal staging accuracy. We conducted a retrospective study of patients who underwent shape-sensing robotic-assisted bronchoscopy (ssRAB) with concurrent EBUS-TBNA between June 2020 and December 2025. Preprocedural CT and PET findings were compared with EBUS-TBNA cytopathology to assess their diagnostic performance and to evaluate stage migration in patients with primary pulmonary malignancies. A total of 1,234 patients underwent ssRAB with EBUS-TBNA, of whom 123 (10.0 %) had malignant lymph nodes on cytopathology. Among these, 23 patients (18.7 %) had no suspicious lymphadenopathy on preprocedural CT and/or PET imaging. The sensitivity of CT and PET for detecting malignancy at specific lymph node stations was 44.5 % and 68.5 %, respectively. In the clinical-to-EBUS staging analysis, 66 (74.2 %) demonstrated no major stage change, while 23 (25.9 %) experienced stage migration. Concurrent EBUS-TBNA identified occult nodal involvement and resulted in stage migration. These findings underscore the critical role of EBUS-TBNA in identifying clinically occult nodal disease and optimizing lung cancer treatment.
authors: Sebastian Fernandez-Bussy; Regina M Murillo-Torres; Tatiana A Rojas-Zapata; Alejandra Yu Lee-Mateus; Paola Gutierrez-Gallegos; David Abia-Trujillo; Linh H Vu; Ryan M Chadha; Kelly S Robertson; Bryan C Husta

title: Robotics in neurosurgery: past, present, and future
abstract: Background Robotics has progressed from stereotactic positioning and instrument guidance toward integrated platforms combining navigation, intraoperative imaging, immersive visualization, and computer-assisted control. However, technical accuracy and clinical benefit are not interchangeable, and the maturity of evidence differs markedly across neurosurgical indications. Objective To critically synthesize the historical development, contemporary applications, supporting evidence, implementation constraints, and research priorities of robotic and complementary augmented-reality (AR)/virtual-reality (VR) technologies in neurosurgery. Methods This is a critical narrative review and technology-focused synthesis, informed by the literature and reference set of the original manuscript (which described searching PubMed, Google Scholar, and ScienceDirect through January 2021), supplemented by selected contemporary publications and the two VOSTARS studies suggested during peer review. No new reproducible systematic search, dual-reviewer screening, formal risk-of-bias assessment, or quantitative synthesis was performed; therefore, PRISMA study counts are not reported. Synthesis Cranial robotic systems facilitate trajectory planning and reproducible positioning for stereotactic biopsy, stereoelectroencephalography, deep brain stimulation, and related interventions. Spine robotics can support pedicle screw placement, although comparative estimates depend on platform, comparator, experience, and outcome definition. Endovascular and microsurgical robotics remain heterogeneous, with many applications at feasibility or early clinical stages. Wearable AR systems such as VOSTARS illustrate the convergence of visualization and navigation but require validation under real operative conditions. Acquisition and maintenance costs, registration error, line-of-sight constraints, human factors, training, and cybersecurity are distinct adoption barriers. Conclusions The most defensible current contribution of robotics is task-specific assistance within surgeon-led workflows, not universal superiority or autonomy. Future studies should prioritize patient-important outcomes, transparent technical reporting, prospective comparisons, and context-sensitive economic evaluation.
authors: Hosam Maher Al-Jehani; Ahmed Hafez Mousa

title: SWINE VIRAL INFECTIONS IN KAZAKHSTAN
abstract: The article presents the results of molecular diagnostics of 156 biological samples (105 nasopharyngeal swabs and 51 blood serum samples) collected from small and large pig farms in Central, Eastern, and Northern Kazakhstan. PCR results determined the presence of genetic material of type 2 circovirus in 2.56% of the samples out of the total (156 samples) from the nasopharyngeal swabs of pigs, and these results were confirmed by Sanger sequencing. Positive results were also obtained (3.21%) in RT-PCR for hepatitis E from blood plasma, as well as for reproductive-respiratory syndrome in pigs (0.64%). The obtained results indicate the circulation of the second type of circovirus in the pig population of Central Kazakhstan, and possibly the hepatitis E virus in pigs of the Northern region. The results of molecular epizootiology of pig viruses are important for veterinary authorities in interpreting outbreaks of disease and controlling imported breeding herds, which are a source of virus introduction into the local population. В статье представлены результаты молекулярной диагностики 156 биологических образцов (105 носоглоточных смывов и 51 сыворотки крови), собранных в мелких и крупных свинофермах Центрального, Восточного и Северного Казахстана. Результаты ПЦР определили наличие генетического материала цирковируса второго типа в 2,56% проб от общего количества образцов (156 проб) в назофарингеальных смывах свиней, что подтверждено результатами секвенирования по Сенгеру. Также были получены положительные результаты (3,21%) в ОТ-ПЦР на гепатит Е из плазмы крови и репродуктивно-респираторного синдрома свиней (0,64%). Полученные результаты свидетельствуют о циркуляции цирковируса второго типа в популяции свиней Центрального Казахстана, и возможно, вируса гепатита Е у свиней Северного региона. Результаты молекулярной эпизоотологии вирусов свиней важны для ветеринарных структур при расшифровке вспышек заболеваемости и контроле за импортируемыми племенными стадами, являющимися источником заноса вируса в местную популяцию.

title: Safety and Efficacy of Endobronchial Ultrasound
abstract: Abstract Purpose of review The use of bronchoscopy with endobronchial ultrasound (EBUS) to aid in lymph node and lung biopsy is relatively new. This review will summarize the literature surrounding the efficacy of bronchoscopy with EBUS. Safety of bronchoscopy with EBUS is not markedly different that procedure with EBUS and is impacted by patient features including co-morbidities as well as different sedation modalities. This paper reviews the impact on both safety and diagnostic yield. Recent Findings The yield from using EBUS guided biopsy varies with the diagnosis but is high with linear EBUS. Recent data incorporating other technologies (electromagnetic navigation, robotic assistance) with bronchoscopy has potential to increase diagnostic yields, appears to be equivalent to transthoracic needle biopsies performed by radiology. Different sedation modalities are utilized, including the use of dedicated anesthesia providers, for bronchoscopy with EBUS but do not appear to significantly affect the diagnostic yield. Summary Bronchoscopy with EBUS (both linear and radial) is a safe procedure with acceptable yields. The type of sedation does not appear to affect the diagnostic yield or the safety of the procedure. Further research into incorporation of other technologies may provide for higher diagnostic yields.
authors: Travis Yamanaka; Kevin P. Haas

title: Safety and diagnostic performance of robotic-assisted bronchoscopy in higher-risk and complex patients

title: Safety and outcomes of hemodilutional autologous transfusion in intermediate- to advanced-level liver resection: a prospective observational study
abstract: PURPOSES: This prospective observational study evaluated the safety and perioperative outcomes of hemodilutional autologous transfusion (HAT) in patients undergoing intermediate- to advanced-level liver resection (LR). METHODS: Between 2022 and 2023, 50 patients scheduled for intermediate- to advanced-level LR were prospectively enrolled. The primary endpoint was the rate of intraoperative allogeneic blood transfusion. Secondary endpoints included total intraoperative blood loss, postoperative complications, postoperative allogeneic transfusion rate, and post-hepatectomy liver failure. Safety analyses of HAT-related adverse events were also performed. A historical cohort of 71 patients who met the identical eligibility criteria between 2020 and 2021 was used for the sensitivity analyses. RESULTS: Of the 50 patients, 48 underwent protocol-defined LR with HAT and were included in the analysis. The intraoperative allogeneic transfusion rate was 6.3%, and no HAT-related adverse events were observed. In sensitivity analyses using a historical cohort, no significant differences were observed in the primary and secondary endpoints. Among patients with massive intraoperative bleeding (≥ 1,000 mL), the prospective cohort tended to show a lower perioperative transfusion rate than the historical cohort (37.5% vs. 78.6%, P = 0.054). CONCLUSION: No clinically overt HAT-related adverse events were observed; however, the efficacy of HAT remains unproven and should be evaluated in future studies.

title: Salivary ferning as a diagnostic window: Bridging hormonal dynamics and oral health
abstract: Recent advancements in digital health and point-of-care testing have revitalised interest in non-invasive salivary diagnostics. This review evaluates the clinical utility of salivary arborization, commonly known as ferning, as a cost-effective and accessible biomarker. By bridging reproductive endocrinology and oral-systemic health, we propose that salivary ferning offers a unique, chair-side diagnostic window for monitoring hormone-mediated periodontal reactivity. Salivary ferning patterns occur due to the crystallization of sodium and potassium chloride on a dried mucous slide, a process heavily influenced by fluctuating systemic estragon and electrolyte levels. Throughout the menstrual cycle, ascending estragon peaks trigger distinct crystalline structures that mirror systemic fertility windows. Beyond reproductive tracking, these hormonal shifts profoundly alter oral tissue physiology. Elevated estragon receptors in the periodontium heighten inflammatory responses to dental plaque, predisposing individuals to gingival inflammation and exacerbated periodontal reactivity during specific hormonal phases. Integrating this diagnostic approach into routine dental practices provides significant clinical advantages without relying on complex laboratory infrastructure. Salivary collection eliminates the patient discomfort and anxiety typically associated with traditional venipuncture while delivering rapid, visual feedback suitable for dynamic chair-side evaluations. Furthermore, the inherent cost-effectiveness of this method reduces overall overhead, making preventative screening widely accessible in diverse healthcare settings. By leveraging these insights, clinicians can personalize periodontal maintenance schedules based on real-time endocrine profiles, ultimately optimizing both oral and systemic health outcomes for patients.

title: Same-day diagnosis and robotic resection of rare primary pulmonary melanoma: a robotic bronchoscopy-guided approach.
abstract: This case report describes a rare presentation of pulmonary melanoma of unknown primary managed through a same-day robotic diagnostic and therapeutic approach. A man in his 70s with an incidentally detected lingular pulmonary nodule suspicious for non-small cell lung cancer underwent robotic navigation bronchoscopy for biopsy and dye marking, immediately followed by robotic-assisted thoracic surgery. Intraoperative frozen section revealed a malignant spindle cell neoplasm, prompting definitive surgical resection during the same anaesthetic event. Final histopathology and molecular analysis confirmed melanoma, with no identifiable cutaneous, mucosal or ocular primary. The patient subsequently received adjuvant immunotherapy and remains disease-free at 24 months. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of pulmonary melanoma mimicking lung carcinoma and demonstrates how integration of robotic bronchoscopy and robotic surgery can enable rapid diagnosis, definitive management and streamlined care within a single operative session.
authors: Andres Fontaine-Nicola; Emiliano Gabriel Manueli Laos; Mario A Masrur; Kevin L Kovitz; Odile David; Khaled Abdelhady

title: Sample Adequacy PD-L1 and NGS in NSCLC: Shape-Sensing Robotic Assisted Bronchoscopy Versus CT Guided Lung Biopsy.
abstract:
Background

Routine assessment of programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression and comprehensive next-generation sequencing (NGS) is recommended to guide treatment selection in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Obtaining adequate tissue for biomarker and molecular analyses is therefore essential. This study compared sample adequacy for PD-L1 and NGS testing between shape-sensing robotic-assisted bronchoscopy (ssRAB) and computed tomography-guided transthoracic lung biopsy (CTTB) in patients with NSCLC.

Methods

We conducted a single-center retrospective study of patients with NSCLC who underwent biopsy of PPL by ssRAB or CTTB between June 2020 and December 2025. Demographic, procedural, pathological, biomarker and molecular data were extracted from electronic medical records, and descriptive statistics analysis and multivariable logistic regression were performed.

Results

A total of 402 patients were included, comprising 198 in the ssRAB cohort and 204 in the CTTB cohort. ssRAB demonstrated significantly higher sample adequacy rates than CTTB for both PD-L1 (98.8% vs. 90.6%, p < 0.001) and NGS testing (92.3% vs. 79.1%, p = 0.005). In multivariable logistic regression analyses, ssRAB was independently associated with higher odds of PD-L1 sample adequacy (adjusted OR 11.48, 95% CI 2.89-78.30; p = 0.002) and NGS sample adequacy (adjusted OR 4.01, 95% CI 1.64-11.40; p = 0.004) compared with CTTB. In a separate model evaluating biopsy tools, cryobiopsy use was independently associated with higher odds of PD-L1 adequacy (adjusted OR 16.54, 95% CI 2.92-317.65; p = 0.010) and NGS adequacy (adjusted OR 5.83, 95% CI 1.93-25.39; p = 0.006) compared with non-cryobiopsy sampling.

Conclusions

ssRAB-acquired specimens were associated with higher rates of PD-L1 and NGS sample adequacy than CTTB-acquired specimens in patients with NSCLC. Future prospective studies are needed to better understand the procedural and specimen-related factors underlying these differences.

title: Selective Laser Sintering and Graphitization for Mono‐Matrix Unibody Fabrication of Integrated Stereo‐Circuit and Stereo‐Fluidic Wearable Electronics
abstract: Wearable integrated electronic devices for biomedical, robotics, and sensing applications require greater compactness and functional complexity while maintaining wearability. However, seamlessly integrating electronic and microfluidic components remain challenging due to fabrication heterogeneity, material mismatches, and complex assembly requirements. In this study, we present an innovative selective laser sintering and graphitization (SLSG) 3D printing technology that enables seamless integration of 3D circuits (stereo-circuits) and 3D fluidic channels (stereo-fluidics). SLSG achieves unibody, autonomous mono-matrix fabrication through adaptive photonic modulation of carbon-rich precursors (e.g., polyetheretherketone (PEEK) powder), simultaneously creating insulating sintered structures and conductive graphitized patterns with conductivity up to 1,895 S/m, yielding 7.64-fold higher electrochemical performance than classic glassy carbon electrodes (GCEs). Using SLSG, we fabricated a watch-type wearable unibody multimodal microfluidic biosensor (UMMB) with integrated electrochemical biosensors for on-body sweat metabolite monitoring. UMMB incorporates stereo-circuits for sensing and signal routing, plus stereo-fluidic channels for sweat respiration, achieving effective lactate and glucose sensing. The device demonstrates excellent sensitivities of 29.43 and 16.86 µA/mM for detecting lactate and glucose, respectively, while exhibiting nondetectable interference or circuit-fluidic crosstalk. This novel SLSG 3D printing technology introduces a transformative unibody approach to fabricate multifunctional bioelectronic-fluidic platform for integrated point-of-care devices, wearable sensors/biosensors, actuators, advanced theranostics, and personalized biomedical devices.
authors: Li Zhang; Wing Cheung Mak

title: Simultaneous dual cryobiopsy using two bronchoscopes for multiple peripheral lung lesions: a novel case report
abstract: Abstract Introduction Bronchoscopic biopsy of multiple pulmonary lesions is typically performed sequentially, often requiring repeated imaging confirmation during cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT)–guided procedures. Case presentation We report a novel technique using simultaneous dual cryobiopsy with two bronchoscopes to sample separate lesions during a single CBCT acquisition. A patient with multiple lesions in the left upper lobe underwent bronchoscopy under general anaesthesia. Two bronchoscopes were inserted simultaneously through a 9 mm endotracheal tube: an Ambu aScope 5 Broncho (4.2 mm outer diameter, 2.2 mm working channel) with a 1.9 mm reusable cryoprobe and an Olympus MP190F bronchoscope with a 1.1 mm cryoprobe. A single CBCT spin confirmed simultaneous tool-in-lesion positioning for both cryoprobes. Cryobiopsies were obtained successfully from both lesions. Histopathological examination revealed squamous cell carcinoma. Conclusion This case demonstrates the technical feasibility of simultaneous dual cryobiopsy and suggests a potential strategy to improve procedural efficiency and reduce imaging requirements during CBCT-guided bronchoscopy.
authors: Sammy Onyancha; Philipp Conzelmann; Ahmad Sajad Soltani; Tanja Dieball; Gernot G. U. Rohde

title: Single-Step Sample-Activated Alternating Sequential Flow Enables Autonomous Multistep Electrochemical Lateral Flow Detection of Mpox Virus DNA
abstract: Abstract The 2022 multinational mpox virus (MPXV) outbreak and continued cross-border transmission have highlighted limitations of laboratory-confined PCR diagnostics. Here, we report an alternating lateral flow architecture (ALFA) that transforms traditional single-pass lateral flow into a programmable platform for autonomous multistep electrochemical nucleic acid detection following a single prepared-sample introduction. By regulating passive fluid delivery, ALFA enables sequential molecular processing and in situ signal generation without external intervention. Coupled with Ag(I)-mediated mismatch DNA nanocomplexes (MDNs), the system provides electrochemical signal amplification without nucleic acid amplification. ALFA detected MPXV DNA with a limit of detection (LOD) of 1.55 pM and a linear range of 101−105 pM. In urine and saliva spiked with structurally intact viral particles, the lowest statistically distinguishable concentration was 10 copies mL−1. Clinical evaluation of 50 PCR-characterized lesion swab samples yielded 92.11% sensitivity, 100% specificity, and 94.0% accuracy. The platform also maintained stable performance over an estimated 112 days. ALFA therefore provides a programmable lateral flow framework for rapid, amplification-free, decentralized nucleic acid diagnostics.
authors: Vasita Lapee-e; Piyathida Phimdee; Hyo-Il Jung; Ekawat Pasomsub; Abdulhadee Yakoh

title: Single-Tube Six-Channel Ultrafast PCR with Melting-Curve Discrimination for Seven Respiratory Pathogens
abstract: Abstract Expanding single-tube multiplexing beyond the number of fluorescence channels on a real-time PCR instrument is a persistent challenge for point-of-care testing (POCT). Here, we break this barrier by leveraging melting temperature (Tm) as an extra information dimension. By employing a probe-cleavage-mediated reporter-duplex strategy, we circumvent the conventional limitation that hydrolyzed TaqMan probes cannot participate in postamplification melting analysis. Two FAM-labeled probes, each containing an engineered 5′-terminal nontarget extension, generate cleavage-dependent reporter amplicons with distinctly different melting temperatures (ΔTm = 10.3 °C), enabling precise differentiation between BV (72.5 °C) and BY (82.8 °C) within a single optical channel. Combined with a lyophilized-bead cartridge that automates nucleic acid release (4 min) and an ultrafast PCR run (16 min), the platform detects eight targets─seven respiratory pathogens (SARS-CoV-2, influenza A H1N1/H3N2/H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b, influenza B Victoria/Yamagata, and Mycoplasma pneumoniae) plus one internal control (B2M)─using only six optical channels. The assay achieves a limit of detection of 5 copies per reaction (R2 > 0.97, amplification efficiency 96–104%) with no cross-reactivity against 55 nontarget microorganisms, and intra/inter-assay CVs < 5%. The lyophilized beads remain stable for 12 months at 25 °C (ΔCt < 1.5). In 272 clinical throat swabs, the system shows 100% agreement with single-plex qPCR. Mixed BV/BY infections produce two distinct melting peaks, with the low-abundance peak detectable down to a 400:1 ratio under the tested conditions. This six-channel ultrafast PCR system reliably detects eight targets in one tube within 20 min without extra hardware, providing a generic strategy for higher-order multiplexing in point-of-care settings.
authors: Yang Li; Yi-Nuo Zhao; Xiang Li; Ting Sun; Lin-wei Zhu; Miao-jin Zhu; L. Liang; Hangping Yao

title: Single-center experience in combined video-assisted thoracic surgery with transbronchial microwave ablation—a novel approach to multifocal lung nodules
abstract: Background: The management of multifocal lung malignancies presents significant challenges, particularly when extensive resection may not be feasible due to limited pulmonary reserve. Thus, a hybrid management approach combining lung surgery with transbronchial local ablation has been developed to control local disease while minimizing lung parenchymal loss. We evaluated the safety, feasibility, and mid-term clinical outcomes of this hybrid approach in managing multifocal lung lesions. Methods: A retrospective single-center review was conducted of patients who underwent combined video-assisted thoracic surgery (VATS) lung resection and transbronchial microwave ablation (TMWA) in a hybrid operating room (HOR) between November 2019 and April 2026. Patient demographics, tumor characteristics, procedural details, perioperative complications, and mid-term clinical outcomes were reported, including intraoperative technical success, 30-day morbidity, overall survival, and rate of local recurrence. Results: Twenty-two patients (mean age 56.8 ± 11.8 years) with multifocal lung malignancies or suspicious multifocal lung nodules were discussed at a multidisciplinary team meeting. All twenty-two patients underwent 23 combined procedures. A total of 70 lesions were treated: 41 by VATS resection and 29 by TMWA. Technical success was achieved in 100% of procedures, as confirmed by intraoperative cone-beam computed tomography. The 30-day complication rate was 21.7%, with no procedure-related 30-day mortality. 20 patients have follow-up beyond 30 days (two patients were lost to follow-up). At a median follow-up of 24 months, the local control rate for ablated lesions was 96.6%, with local-recurrence-free survival of 95% and overall survival of 85%. Among the 41 resected lung lesions, 17 were multifocal lung adenocarcinoma, 22 were metastatic nodules, and two showed no evidence of malignancy. However, preoperative histopathological confirmation was available for only four ablated lesions, which showed either atypical pneumocytes or lung adenocarcinoma. Conclusions: Hybrid treatment combining VATS and TMWA is a safe and feasible approach for multifocal lung lesions, with reasonable complication rates and acceptable mid-term disease control. This hybrid technique may offer benefits in parenchymal preservation, particularly in patients with borderline lung function, while achieving reasonable local control.
authors: Aliss T. C. Chang; Rainbow W. H. Lau; Joyce W. Y. Chan; Wei Liu; Calvin S.H. Ng

title: Skin Swabbing as a Noninvasive Alternative to Fin Clipping for Commercial Automated Genotyping.
abstract: Fin clipping remains the most common sampling method for genotyping zebrafish, yet it requires anesthesia and tissue removal, raising animal welfare concerns and potentially impacting behavior in the short term. To address this, we have validated a non-invasive skin swabbing technique that eliminates the need for fin clipping adults while maintaining genotyping accuracy during automated genotyping. This method involves gently swabbing the fish's skin to collect mucus and epidermal cells for DNA extraction. This approach avoids anesthesia, reduces handling stress, and is much less invasive than traditional fin clipping with limited tissue injury. We conducted a comparative analysis of swab-derived DNA against traditional fin clip samples sent for automated genotyping. Swab and fin clips samples taken from the same animal matched genotype results, demonstrating substantial promise as a refinement for automated genotyping under the 3Rs framework. Further testing of the swabbing technique, transport, and sample processing was optimized across nine sessions. Key aspects of the collection technique include focusing on consistent swabbing pressure and sample dry time. Proper technique is critical to ensuring robust and reproducible genotyping outcomes. Our findings indicate that skin swabbing offers a welfare-improving alternative to fin clipping for automated genotyping. Broad adoption of this technique has the potential to enhance animal welfare standards while maintaining scientific rigor, aligning with the principles of the 3Rs and advancing non-invasive research practices in zebrafish facilities worldwide. While the current success rate indicates some limitations relative to fin clip genotyping results with automated genotyping, swabbing remains a promising refinement that can substantially improve welfare in zebrafish facilities.
authors: Mollie E Millington; Ceinwen A Tilley; Nathan Nowak

title: Stage-Specific Associations of Automated RPR With Treponema pallidum qPCR Positivity and Cycle Threshold in Early Symptomatic Syphilis: A Multicenter Study Using Specimens Collected During Routine Care
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Treponema pallidum quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) positivity and cycle threshold (Ct) by rapid plasma reagin (RPR), disease stage, and other characteristics are poorly characterized in routine-care specimens, leaving it unclear when qPCR of such specimens is informative for diagnosis. Methods This Japanese multicenter cross-sectional study explored qPCR positivity and Ct by these characteristics. Nonblood specimens collected during routine care underwent qPCR at a central laboratory for this study. Bayesian logistic and normal regressions modeled positivity and mean Ct of TP0574 and polA with stage-specific continuous automated RPR terms, patient characteristics, collection site, and facility random intercepts. Estimates were standardized over the analyzed specimens. Population-group predictions were instead averaged within each group. Results Among 154 nonblood specimens from 145 patients (71.7% non-MSM men and women) at 14 facilities, 109 (70.8%) were qPCR positive. At RPR 1, adjusted positivity was 72.2% (95% credible interval, 60.9%–82.9%) in primary and 43.8% (16.7%–69.9%) in secondary syphilis. Positivity showed a modest downward trend with RPR in primary but increased in secondary syphilis, reflecting a stage-by-RPR interaction (secondary-to-primary ratio of odds ratios, 1.78; 1.25–2.65). Predicted positivity showed an upward trend with RPR values among MSM; adjusted positivity was relatively high for genital/urethral/urinary and anal/perianal/rectal specimens. Adjusted mean Ct increased with RPR in primary and followed an inverted-U pattern in secondary syphilis. Conclusions In primary syphilis, nonblood qPCR positivity was high even at low RPR. When serologic findings remain inconclusive in this stage, qPCR is highly recommended for securing an early diagnosis. Summary In nonblood specimens collected during routine care, Treponema pallidum qPCR positivity was high even at low automated RPR values in primary syphilis, potentially supporting earlier diagnostic confirmation when serology is inconclusive. In secondary syphilis, positivity increased with RPR.
authors: Ayu Kasamatsu; Yuki Ohama; Yui Tomo; Kazuo Imai; Shu‐ichi Nakayama; Ryosuke Omori; Takuya Yamagishi; Mitsuru Yasuda; Yukihiro Akeda

title: State-of-the-art in automated image-based species identification systems
abstract: Accurate and rapid species-level identification of bacteria and fungi from culture plates are longstanding challenges in diagnostic microbiology. Visual assessment of colony morphology lacks sufficient specificity for definitive identification, while biochemical profiling is often too slow for routine clinical use. Matrix assisted laser desorption ionization - time of flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS) has largely replaced biochemical identification in high-income settings because of its speed and accuracy; however, its cost and infrastructure requirements limit accessibility in most low resource settings. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), offers a promising alternative by enabling growth detection and presumptive identification direct from digitalized macroscopic images of culture plates. This review summarizes key aspects of visual identification from agar cultures and recent advances in image-based microbial analysis using CNNs, Siamese networks, object detectors, and Vision Transformers. Automated growth detection and whole-plate interpretation achieved sensitivities of 99.8–100%, specificities of approximately 63–90%, and within-institution AUCs of ≥0.98, although cross-institution performance decreased to ≥0.90; reported workflow benefits included 3–5-hour reductions in time to result and up to 80% less hands-on review of negative cultures. Species-level bacterial classification ranged from a mean sensitivity of 66.2% in an early 18-species model to 90.6% top-1 and 97.6% top-3 accuracy with the contextual DeepColony framework. Fungal models achieved a mean accuracy of 89.7% with FungID and an AUROC of 92.7% with smartphone-based MoldVision, whose F1 score increased from 38.8% during days 1–2 to 92.1% during days 3–5, highlighting the influence of colony maturity, dataset composition, and validation setting. We further discuss the integration of AI image analysis in commercial laboratory automation systems, including Copan WASPLab™, BD Kiestra™ MLA, APAS™ Independence by Clever Culture Systems, as well as the potential of smartphone-based tools in resource-limited settings. Overall, AI-based image analysis can support high-sensitivity screening, workflow triage, colony enumeration, and presumptive identification, but robust external validation, standardized imaging and reporting, regulatory approval, and continued expert oversight remain essential.
authors: Lukas Weber; Mohammedaman Mama Hussen; Balaji Veeraraghavan; Eline Meijer; Yukino Gütlin; Alejandro Guerrero-López; Sarah C. Brüningk; Oliver Nolte; Catherine Ruth Jutzeler; Adrian Egli

title: Statistical quality control practices in a sample of Spanish Blood Establishments: a mixed-methods exploratory study: Statistical QC practices in Spanish Blood Establishments
abstract: Background - The European Directorate for the Quality of Medicines & HealthCare (EDQM) provides guidance for statistical quality control in blood component manufacturing, including recommendations for sampling and statistical process control. However, the extent to which these recommendations are implemented in routine practice remains unclear. Materials and methods - We conducted a sequential explanatory mixed-methods study among professionals working in blood establishments, recruited through the Spanish Society of Blood Transfusion blood processing working group. Phase 1 was a cross-sectional survey (10 responding centers across 10 autonomous communities; response rate 77%). Phase 2 comprised semi-structured interviews with a purposive sample of survey respondents (No.=7). Survey findings informed the interview topic guide. Thematic analysis followed the Braun and Clarke approach. Findings from both phases were integrated using a joint display. Results - Respondents represented centers with varied production volumes, and most had more than 6 years of experience (80%). Use of statistical quality control methods was limited: 90% reported using descriptive statistics only and 10% used control charts. For sample size determination, 80% applied fixed production percentages without formal statistical justification. Spreadsheet-based workflows with custom formulas predominated (90%). Key challenges included determining sample size and laborious report generation (both 80%). Interviews highlighted uncertainty about sampling adequacy, potential for earlier trend detection, perceived complexity of guidance, and the need for interpretive decision support. All participants expressed interest in automated approaches. Discussion - Among participating centers, variation in the implementation of statistical quality control practices relative to EDQM recommendations suggests opportunities for improved harmonization. Automated tools that embed recommended sampling and monitoring methods may support implementation, although larger studies are needed to estimate prevalence at national level.
authors: Héctor Sarmiento; María Isabel Ortiz de Salazar Martín; Luis Roberto Larrea González; Ana M Arruga Manzano; María Luisa Ayape; Aida Isabel Azcarate Gonzalez; Teresa Díaz Rueda; Marta López Melchor; Pascual Marco Vera; María del Carmen Martín Alonso; María Mercadillo González; Ana Isabel Pérez Aliaga; Magdalena Prohens‐Batle

title: Supplemental Material for: Diagnostic Performance and Safety Profile of Shape-sensing Robotic-assisted Bronchoscopy in Peripheral Pulmonary Lesions: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
abstract: Introduction: Shape-sensing robotic-assisted bronchoscopy (ssRAB) has emerged as a promising modality for diagnosing peripheral pulmonary lesions (PPLs). This meta-analysis evaluated its diagnostic performance and safety profile. Methods: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception to December 2025. Study quality was assessed using the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-3. Random-effects model was used to estimate the pooled diagnostic yield, sensitivity for malignancy, and complication, with rates (%) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) when the I2 index exceeded 50%. Cumulative meta-analysis was performed to assess the temporal stability and evidence saturation of the pooled diagnostic yield. Publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots and Egger's test. Results: A total of 3678 lesions from 18 studies were included. Notably, diagnostic yield varied significantly by outcome definition, with pooled diagnostic yield of 82.5% (95% CI: 78.3%-86.0%) under strict definition versus 88.1% (95% CI: 82.8%-92.0%) under intermediate definition (P=0.036). The pooled sensitivity for malignancy of 90.0% (95% CI: 86.4%-92.8%). Cumulative meta-analysis showed stabilized diagnostic performance after approximately 1,500 lesions for the strict definition and 500 lesions for intermediate definition. Moreover, safety profile was favorable, with pooled rates of pneumothorax 1.8% (95% CI:1.3%-2.3%), chest tube placement 1.1% (95% CI: 0.7%-1.5%), and severe bleeding 0.0% (95% CI: 0.0%-0.3%). Subgroup analyses showed consistent performance across study designs, region, and nodule characteristics. Diagnostic yield was significantly influenced by publication year, and lesion size (P<0.05). Conclusion: ssRAB was associated with favorable, definition-dependent diagnostic yield (82.5%-88.1%) with exceptional safety, supporting ssRAB as an attractive first-line minimally invasive diagnostic option in appropriately selected patients, especially for small nodules (<2cm) and patients at elevated procedural risk.
authors: figshare admin karger; Xianya Hu; Lechen Wang; Jingyu Shi; Sebastián Fernández-Bussy; Dan Liu

title: TRAJECTORY PLANNING OF ACUPUNCTURE ROBOTS
abstract: For the clinical demand of sequential needling at multiple facial acupoints, needles already inserted and retained in the tissue become static obstacles to subsequent insertions. Planning a collision-free, smooth and efficient insertion path for each new needle inside the narrow facial workspace is therefore a key problem in the automation of acupuncture robots. This paper takes an acupuncture robot system composed of a UR5e six-degree-of-freedom manipulator and a self-developed acupuncture end effector as the research object, formulates multi-acupoint sequential needling as a constrained motion planning problem in which the obstacle set grows with the needling sequence, and proposes an improved APF-RRT* algorithm. The algorithm combines a bidirectional growth mechanism and goal-biased sampling on the RRT* framework to improve the convergence of the two trees, introduces Informed ellipsoidal subset sampling to reduce ineffective exploration, constructs an improved artificial potential field to alleviate the goal-unreachable and local-minimum problems, and designs a dynamic adaptive step-size strategy based on the ratio of attractive to repulsive force together with a bidirectional greedy path-pruning strategy. Simulation results in two- and three-dimensional environments show that, under the same maximum number of nodes, the proposed algorithm converges faster and yields a lower path cost than RRT* and APF-RRT*: in the 2D environment the runtime is reduced from 44.702 s to 9.538 s and the path cost from 792.702 to 750.477, while in the 3D environment the runtime is reduced from 84.594 s to 32.796 s and the path cost from 933.077 to 822.857, verifying the effectiveness and engineering applicability of the algorithm.
authors: Yi Wang; Dianhao Wu; ZiChen Ma; KunLin Xie; MengDi Wang
venue: Journal of Computer Science and Electrical Engineering

title: Terra Firma-Forme Dermatosis or Dermatosis Neglecta: A Diagnostic Continuum Illustrated by a Pediatric Case of Post-circumcision Penile Allodynia
abstract: Terra firma-forme dermatosis (TFFD) and dermatosis neglecta (DN) can look identical on the skin, both presenting as dirt-like, verrucous plaques that clear with 70% alcohol swabbing. In both conditions, the plaque consists of retained, loosely adherent keratin and debris overlying otherwise normal skin, rather than a true structural epidermal lesion, which is why alcohol removes it. Classically, TFFD persists despite proper washing, whereas DN clears once hygiene resumes; alcohol swabbing does not distinguish between the two. We report a 13-year-old boy with probable autism spectrum disorder who developed a dirt-like, verrucous plaque on the penile shaft after circumcision, where persistent hyperesthesia (increased cutaneous sensitivity) and allodynia (pain provoked by a stimulus that would not normally be painful) made washing painful. Biopsy showed orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis with a normal dermis, ruling out a verrucous epidermal hamartoma. Rubbing the plaque with 70% alcohol produced complete clearance, ruling out a fixed lesion. No findings suggestive of caregiver neglect were identified; the avoidance was localized and self-directed. Hygiene was subsequently discussed with the patient and his caregiver in light of his pain threshold and sensory sensitivities, and he was referred for neuropsychiatric follow-up. This case highlights an underrecognized cutaneous complication of pediatric circumcision, where pain avoidance combined with neurodevelopmental vulnerability can mimic a primary keratinization disorder.
authors: Jules Roullée; Guillaume Chaby; Christophe Attencourt; Florian Lombart

title: The Benign Biopsy Paradox: False Reassurance and Diagnostic Overreach in Peripheral Pulmonary Lesions.
abstract:
Background

Peripheral pulmonary lesions are increasingly detected through widespread computed tomography use, incidental imaging, and low-dose CT lung cancer screening programs. Diagnostic techniques have advanced substantially, including radial endobronchial ultrasound (rEBUS), virtual and electromagnetic navigation bronchoscopy, ultrathin bronchoscopy, cryobiopsy, cone-beam CT (CBCT), augmented fluoroscopy, and robotic-assisted bronchoscopy. Despite this rapid technological evolution, the interpretation of benign or non-malignant biopsy results remains one of the most consequential and underappreciated clinical challenges in pulmonary medicine.

Summary

A benign biopsy result from a peripheral pulmonary lesion must not be interpreted as a single, unambiguous entity. Specific benign diagnoses, nonspecific benign findings, atypia, suspicious results, and nondiagnostic samples each carry a distinct residual probability of malignancy and different implications for subsequent management. Recent consensus recommendations mandate a strict definition of diagnostic yield, in which only specific malignant diagnoses and specific benign diagnoses sufficient to inform patient care are counted as truly diagnostic. Follow-up data are essential for calculating diagnostic accuracy, sensitivity for malignancy, negative predictive value, and false-negative rates - but should not retroactively reclassify nonspecific or nondiagnostic index results as diagnostic. We propose that the diagnostic process be understood as a chain: tool/access → navigation → position confirmation → sampling → pathology → final clinic-radiologic diagnosis. Failure at any link may create a diagnostic gap and produce a falsely reassuring result. Newer technologies address different links: robotic bronchoscopy primarily narrows the access and stability gap, while CBCT and augmented fluoroscopy primarily narrow the position confirmation gap. Neither technology - alone or combined - closes the sampling, pathology, or clinical concordance gaps.
authors: Rozman A, Shah PL.

title: The Impact of Scenario-Based Simulation Learning on Clinical Self-Efficacy among Pre-licensure Nursing and Midwifery Students: A Systematic Review of Design Features and Educational Outcomes
abstract: Aim To systematically review how scenario-based simulation learning (SBSL) shapes clinical self-efficacy among pre-licensure nursing and midwifery students and how simulation design, context and assessment timing influence educational and clinical translation. Background Scenario-based simulation learning (SBSL) is widely used in nursing and midwifery education, yet evidence on its effect on clinical self-efficacy and how simulation design moderate outcomes remains fragmented. Design A systematic review following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Methods A PRISMA 2020-compliant review searched eight databases. Eligible studies measured task-specific clinical self-efficacy via validated tools in pre-licensure cohorts. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data on scenario complexity, theoretical integration, debriefing structure and outcome timing and appraised risk of bias. Results Fifty-two studies (N=4,774; 46 nursing, 6 midwifery) were included. SBSL broadly correlated with self-efficacy gains, yet only 55.8% (n=29) demonstrated statistically significant between-group superiority. Psychomotor skill (54.1%), knowledge (61.9%) and cognitive reasoning (62.5%) improvements were documented. Studies embedding explicit theoretical frameworks, calibrated scenario difficulty (“Goldilocks Zone”) and structured debriefing showed the most consistent benefits. Immediate post-simulation assessments were frequently distorted by acute simulation anxiety; self-efficacy crystallized only after cognitive consolidation. Conclusion SBSL shows promise for building clinical self-efficacy, but effects are inconsistently captured and methodologically constrained by reliance on subjective self-report. Pedagogical architecture—progressive scaffolding, discipline-sensitive scenario design and rigorous debriefing—matters more than technical fidelity. Sustained efficacy requires longitudinal follow-up beyond immediate post-intervention windows. Faculty pedagogical preparedness, rather than equipment investment, is the decisive lever for translational impact. Registration A Systematic Review. PROSPERO 2024 Available from https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42024622757 (CRD42024622757, registered 16 Dec 2024).
authors: Rosenna Wai Ming CHUNG; Hoi Lam Ip; Ying Dai; Kris Yuet Wan Lok

title: The STABLE Trial: Sustained Breath-Hold During Tissue Acquisition in Robotic Bronchoscopy—A Randomized Controlled Trial
abstract: Background: Respiratory motion and anesthesia-associated atelectasis may contribute to CT-to-body divergence and reduce the precision of peripheral pulmonary lesion sampling. Breath-hold ventilation has been proposed to stabilize the target and biopsy tool during robotic bronchoscopy, but prospective randomized evidence is limited. We evaluated whether sustained breath-hold during tissue acquisition improves diagnostic yield or tool-lesion positioning during imaging-integrated robotic bronchoscopy. Methods: The STABLE ( S tudy of T ool-lesion A lignment and B reath-hold Ventilation in Robotic Bronchoscopy for Peripheral Lung LE sions) Trial was a prospective randomized study of patients undergoing robotic bronchoscopy for peripheral pulmonary lesions using the Noah Galaxy system with integrated augmented fluoroscopy and C-arm-based tomosynthesis. Patients were randomized to standardized sustained breath-hold during tissue acquisition or conventional ventilation during tissue acquisition; both groups underwent brief breath-holds during AF/CABT image acquisition. The primary endpoint was strict diagnostic yield according to ATS/ACCP definitions, independently adjudicated by a pulmonologist blinded to ventilation assignment. Secondary endpoints included successful lesion localization, tool-in-lesion (TIL), tool-touching-lesion (TTL), no tool in lesion (NTL), radiation exposure, and complications. Standardized mean differences (SMDs) assessed baseline balance. Results: Among 117 randomized patients, 53 underwent breath-hold and 64 conventional ventilation. Mean age was 67.5±10.0 versus 66.3±10.4 years, and mean lesion diameter was 1.7±0.7 versus 1.9±0.8 cm, respectively. Most baseline characteristics were similar; the largest imbalances involved bronchus sign (34.0% vs 51.6%; absolute SMD 0.35) and left-upper-lobe location (28.3% vs 45.3%; SMD 0.35). Overall strict adjudicated diagnostic yield was 89.7% (105/117). Diagnostic yield was 86.8% with breath-hold and 92.2% with conventional ventilation (OR 0.56, 95% CI 0.17–1.87, p-value 0.34). With greater than 1 year of ongoing follow-up, overall diagnostic accuracy was 97.4% (114/117). Nearly all procedures achieved TIL or TTL (98.1% vs 96.9%). TIL occurred in 62.3% versus 64.1% (OR 0.93, 95% CI 0.44–1.97). Localization, tool-position distribution, sampling intensity, radiation exposure, and complications showed no clear between-group differences. Two pneumothoraces requiring chest-tube placement occurred (2/117; 1.7%), both in the conventional ventilation group. Across both groups, diagnostic yield increased from 0% with NTL to 85.0% with TTL and 95.9% with TIL. Conclusions: Sustained breath-hold during tissue acquisition did not improve diagnostic yield or tool-lesion positioning during imaging-integrated robotic bronchoscopy. Diagnostic yield varied according to imaging-confirmed tool-lesion position, supporting procedural strategies that prioritize accurate real-time positioning rather than breath-hold alone. Trial registration: International Standard Randomised Controlled Trial Number (ISRCTN) Registry, ISRCTN11802169; retrospectively registered (01/09/2026).
authors: Mathew R, Danilevskaya O, Cherian S, Meena N.

title: The comparison of excision, swabbing, tape-lifting, and scraping as techniques for DNA evidence recovery: A preliminary study
abstract: In the Final Report of the Commission of Inquiry into Forensic DNA Testing in Queensland , Recommendation 28 recommended that alternative procedures to the scraping method should be investigated for the recovery of biological material from crime scene exhibits for downstream DNA testing. This study forms the first phase of a larger project comparing swabbing, tape-lifting, scraping and excision of biological fluids from a fabric substrate to determine the most effective recovery procedure. Calico cotton swatches were seeded with two concentrations (neat and 1:1000) of blood, semen and saliva, samples commonly encountered in forensic casework. Each sample type was collected using the four evidence recovery methods, extracted, quantified, and the 1/1000 dilution samples were short tandem repeat (STR) profiled to assess the practical limits of each method. Excision had the greatest DNA yield with a large effect size and best STR profile quality compared to all other recovery methods for blood ( p < 0.0001, ŋ 2 > 0.95), semen ( p < 0.0001, ŋ 2 = 0.96) and saliva ( p < 0.0001, ŋ 2 = 0.82). There were no statistical differences found between the MWE Sterile Tubed Dryswab™ Rayon swab 1028, the Puritan® 6” Standard Rayon Swab w/Polystyrene Handle – 806-PR, HazPak tape-lift or scraping for neat blood and semen. Tape-lifting had a statistically higher efficiency than scraping ( p = 0.0012), the Puritan ( p = 0.0046) and the MWE swabs ( p = 0.0145). Results suggest that excision is the most effective biological material recovery technique for blood, semen, and saliva from 100 % white cotton.

title: The effects of anticoagulant and sample storage time on hematologic values in Humboldt penguins (Spheniscus humboldti )
abstract: Preanalytical variation in hematologic values due to factors including anticoagulant and sample storage time have been documented in several avian taxa. This study evaluated differences in PCV, total solids, WBC count, and leukocyte differential in Humboldt penguin (Spheniscus humboldti) blood samples exposed to different anticoagulants and storage durations. Blood was collected from eleven individuals and anticoagulated with either lithium heparin (LH) EDTA. Hematologic values were compared at the time of blood collection (0 h) and after refrigeration at 8 h and 24 h. Leukocyte differential values were also compared to fresh, non-anticoagulated blood films created immediately after venipuncture (0 h). On immediate evaluation (0 h), there were no statistically significant differences in total WBC count or leukocyte differentials between LH, EDTA, and non-anticoagulated whole blood. Statistically and clinically relevant shifts in differential counts occurred within 8 h of sample storage, including a reduction in absolute monocytes (p = 0.001), and altered heterophil:lymphocyte ratio (p = 0.0016). Increased relative (proportion of) lymphocytes and decreased relative heterophils were documented in samples anticoagulated in LH within as little as 8 hours of storage in the refrigerator. Conversely, samples anticoagulated in EDTA (p < 0.0001) showed increased relative heterophils and decreased relative lymphocytes within 8 hours of storage (p < 0.0001). These findings indicate that rapid sample processing is key to limiting artifactual changes in leukogram evaluation. Furthermore, anticoagulant and sample storage time should be considered during interpretation of Humboldt penguin hematology.

title: The impact of blood collection method (capillary or yenous) on erythrocyte sedimentation using the mini-cube analyzer
abstract: Hitrost sedimentacija eritrocitov (ESR) predstavlja eno izmed osnovnih laboratorijskih preiskav za oceno prisotnosti in intenzitete vnetnih procesov ter drugih patoloških stanj v organizmu. Na rezultat preiskave lahko vplivajo številni predanalitični, analitični in biološki dejavniki, med katerimi je pomembna tudi vrsta odvzema krvi. Namen magistrske naloge je bil raziskati vpliv vrste odvzema krvi - kapilarnega in venskega - na vrednosti ESR z uporabo analizatorja Mini-Cube. V raziskavo so bili vključeni preiskovanci, pri katerih sta bila izvedena oba načina odvzema krvi. Določitve ES so bile opravljene pod standardiziranimi laboratorijskimi pogoji z uporabo analizatorja Mini-Cube, ki omogoča avtomatizirano določanje sedimentacije iz manjšega volumna vzorca. Zbrane rezultate smo statistično analizirali z namenom ugotavljanja morebitnih razlik med kapilarnimi in venskimi vzorci ter ocene stopnje ujemanja med metodama. Rezultati raziskave so pokazali, da lahko vrsta odvzema krvi vpliva na določene vrednosti SE. Ugotovljene razlike med kapilarnimi in venskimi vzorci so bile ovrednotene z vidika klinične pomembnosti in uporabnosti metode v rutinski laboratorijski diagnostiki. Analiza je omogočila presojo zanesljivosti kapilarnega odvzema kot možne alternative venskemu odvzemu, predvsem v primerih, kjer je odvzem venske krvi otežen ali manj primeren. Ugotovili smo, da kapilarni odvzem krvi na analizatorju Mini-Cube zaradi reoloških omejitev, značilnosti mikrocirkulacije in tveganja za hemodilucijo s tkivno tekočino ne more predstavljati splošne alternative venskemu odvzemu. Metoda je primerna zgolj za presejalno testiranje zdrave populacije s pričakovanimi normalnimi vrednostmi, medtem ko venski odvzem za diagnostiko in spremljanje vnetnih stanj ostaja edina metodološko varna izbira.

title: The transformative power of artificial intelligence and machine learning in blood banking/transfusion medicine: A vein‐to‐vein approach from blood collection to transfusion services: On behalf of the AABB Foundation
abstract: BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML) are poised to transform transfusion medicine across the vein-to-vein continuum, from donor recruitment to recipient outcomes. Large datasets generated from millions of donations and transfusions create opportunities for predictive modeling, precision medicine, improved safety, and operational efficiency. This review outlines key applications of AI in blood banking and transfusion medicine using a comprehensive vein-to-vein framework. METHODS: The review synthesizes perspectives from blood services and hospital-based transfusion practices. Applications are discussed across donor recruitment, collections, testing, inventory management, hospital transfusion services, and education. Finally, AI safety, including ethical, regulatory, privacy, and implementation challenges, is addressed. This is a narrative, non-exhaustive review; given the rapidly evolving pace of AI/ML capabilities, this synthesis should be interpreted as a framework for ongoing surveillance rather than a fixed inventory of applications. RESULTS: Donor-focused applications include personalized recruitment, individualized iron management, and fairness auditing to reduce inequities. In supply chain operations, ML can improve demand forecasting, minimize waste, and optimize inventory. Federated learning may support multi-institutional collaboration without sharing raw data. Omics and genomic applications can enable high-throughput analysis, phenotype prediction, and precision transfusion support for rare blood types and alloimmunized patients. In hospitals, AI can augment hemovigilance by identifying/predicting adverse transfusion reactions, while large language models and retrieval-augmented generation may enhance decision support, patient blood management, and education through adaptive learning. CONCLUSION: AI holds substantial promise to improve transfusion safety, efficiency, equity, and sustainability. Realizing this potential will require robust governance, model validation across diverse populations, privacy safeguards, bias mitigation, reproducibility, regulatory oversight, and human-in-the-loop implementation.

title: The unified front: a multidisciplinary approach in the Era of uniportal thoracic surgery
abstract: The evolution of thoracic surgery from open thoracotomy to uniportal video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (U-VATS) represents a paradigm shift toward minimizing surgical trauma. However, the changing landscape of thoracic oncology-characterized by an increase in subsolid nodules, multifocal ground-glass opacities, and locally advanced disease requiring neoadjuvant therapy-demands more than surgical innovation alone. This review explores the critical intersection of U-VATS with multidisciplinary collaboration. We examine how the integration of medical oncology, interventional pulmonology, and radiology enhances the capabilities of the single-port approach. This review will discuss specific combinatorial techniques, including uniportal lung resection following neoadjuvant treatment, navigation bronchoscopic-guided localization strategies, and combining U-VATS with concomitant transbronchial ablation. Finally, we address the logistical and economic challenges inherent in maintaining such complex collaborative frameworks.

title: Toward a Robust Cell-free DNA Isolation Protocol for Next-Generation Sequencing Applications in a Clinical Molecular Diagnostics Setting.
abstract: Cell-free (cf) DNA, released from apoptotic and necrotic cells into bodily fluids, is a noninvasive source of genetic information for disease prediction, diagnosis, and monitoring. However, its low abundance makes cfDNA highly susceptible to various preanalytical influences, potentially increasing high-molecular-weight or genomic DNA, compromising downstream cfDNA analysis. This study evaluated the impact of different cfDNA-stabilizing blood collection tubes (Cell-Free DNA BCT, Streck; S-Monovette cfDNA Exact, Sarstedt) stored at room temperature for 1, 5, or 10 days prior to plasma isolation using different isolation methods (magnetic bead based or silica column based) on cfDNA stability and yield. DNA quantity and quality were assessed by fluorometric quantification, automated fragment analysis, and gene-specific real-time quantitative PCR. Streck-based workflows maintained stable cfDNA yields and characteristic mononucleosomal fragmentation profiles across all storage times. In contrast, Sarstedt tubes showed reduced cfDNA concentrations after 5 days and a pronounced increase at 10 days, accompanied by high-molecular-weight DNA patterns consistent with white blood cell lysis. These trends were largely independent of the extraction method. Overall, the results demonstrate that blood collection tube chemistry critically influences cfDNA integrity during delayed processing. The Streck tubes, particularly when combined with the silica column-based isolation method, provided the most robust and reproducible workflow for routine molecular diagnostics, whereas the Sarstedt tubes produced physiologically implausible results after extended storage.

title: Toward the Use of Centrifugation for Point-of-Care Plasma Separation: Evaluation of a Compact Battery-Powered Centrifuge
abstract: Background/Objectives: Despite advances in point-of-care (POC) blood test development, the lack of a simple, low-cost approach to the separation of capillary blood to generate liquid plasma remains a barrier to POC measurement of many analytes. The battery-operated, internally balanced Labcorp TrueSpin® centrifuge offers a potential POC solution for blood collected into a BDMicrotainer®. We compared the quality of plasma generated by TrueSpin centrifugation versus conventional centrifugation. Methods: Venipuncture was performed on 10 volunteers. After collection of blood into Sarstedt Monovettes® (Lithium Heparin with gel (LiHep/Gel), EDTA), blood from the same tubing was collected into three Microtainers (LiHep/gel, LiHep without gel (LiHep), EDTA). Microtainer and Monovette samples received TrueSpin and conventional centrifugation, respectively. Hemolysis index and plasma amino acids (n = 24) were measured for all Monovette and Microtainer plasma samples. For 3 additional volunteers, capillary blood was collected from the arm into LiHep/Gel and EDTA Microtainers using the Labcorp Comfort DrawTM device with a gentleheel® lancet and centrifuged (TrueSpin) to generate plasma. Results: TrueSpin centrifugation took approximately 10 min; batteries supported 8–11 runs. Microtainer plasma H-indices (including blood from Comfort Draw) were ≤10. For all 24 amino acids combined, measurements for TrueSpin Microtainer samples had excellent Pearson’s correlation (r > 0.99) with paired conventional Monovette plasma. Conclusions: Plasma quality after TrueSpin centrifugation of Microtainer blood samples is comparable to plasma quality after conventional Monovette centrifugation, including for capillary blood collected using the Comfort Draw. The TrueSpin was reliable and easy to use. The TrueSpin centrifuge has potential future use for POC plasma separation.
authors: Adam S. Ptolemy; Alexander Kolb; Ayse Mehmke; Sami Rifai; Nira R. Pollock

title: Toward uncertainty-aware clinical decision support for treatment response prediction in metastatic NSCLC: integrating FDG-PET, T-cell repertoire, and cytokines with conformal prediction
abstract: Background: Variable response to chemoimmunotherapy in metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (mNSCLC), together with the limited discriminative accuracy of PD-L1 tumor proportion score, highlights the need for reliable, uncertainty-aware early response prediction using multimodal biomarkers. We developed and prototyped a multimodal clinical decision support (CDS) framework integrating longitudinal FDG-PET, T-cell receptor (TCR), and cytokine biomarkers with conformal prediction to deliver uncertainty-quantified, patient-level response predictions. Methods: Thirty-five patients with mNSCLC receiving first-line carboplatin-pemetrexed-pembrolizumab on the PET-BRIGHT trial (NCT04151940) underwent FDG-PET/CT and blood collection at baseline and week 3. Multimodal biomarkers included FDG-PET metrics (standardized uptake value/total lesion glycolysis), TCR diversity metrics, and inflammatory cytokines. Nested leave-one-out cross-validation with automated feature selection identified a single biomarker per modality. Class-balanced logistic regression was used for classification, with discrimination assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and calibration by the Brier score. Conformal prediction (targeting 80% reliability) quantified patient-level uncertainty via prediction sets and singleton rate. Unimodal and multimodal early- and late-fusion models were evaluated using baseline-only and combined baseline plus mid-treatment biomarkers. Models were benchmarked against PD-L1 tumor proportion score, and statistical significance was assessed by permutation testing against an empirical null. Results: PD-L1 tumor proportion score, the current clinical standard, discriminated poorly (AUROC 0.58, 95% CI 0.39-0.78). At PreTx, unimodal TCR was the strongest single modality (AUROC 0.80), followed by PET (0.76) and cytokines (0.54). Late fusion of PET and TCR achieved the highest PreTx discrimination (0.85) and increased singleton predictions from 78% to 89%. After incorporating mid-treatment biomarkers, cytokines became the strongest single modality (0.78) while TCR was attenuated (0.66); late fusion of PET and cytokines achieved the highest discrimination overall (0.86). Thirteen of 22 model and timepoint combinations exceeded a permutation null at p < 0.05, and empirical coverage was 78% and 82% against an 80% target. Conclusions: A multimodal framework combining longitudinal biomarkers with conformal prediction substantially outperformed the current clinical standard while identifying patients for whom a confident prediction could not be made. A prototype CDS interface demonstrates feasibility for clinical translation. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04151940, registered 26 September 2019.
authors: Faisal Yaseen; Daniel S. Hippe; Sunan Cui; Jie Ying Fu; Yejin Kim; Clemens Grassberger; Lei Deng; Ting Ye; Paul E. Kinahan; Jing Zeng; John H. Gennari; Stephen R. Bowen

title: Towards clinical translation of endobronchial optical ultrasound imaging
abstract: Abstract Optical ultrasound (OpUS) imaging provides an optical alternative to conventional piezoelectric ultrasound, offering miniaturised interventional probes and clinically-relevant image quality at video-rate frame rates. Here, we report advances in the clinical applicability of a linearly actuated OpUS (LiOpUS) imaging system developed for endobronchial applications, incorporating a clinically relevant probe length and dynamic control over the orientation of the image plane. The system comprises a side-viewing OpUS probe exceeding 2 m in length, a motorised platform enabling both linear scanning and controlled probe rotation, and a compact and integrated imaging console supporting real-time data acquisition and real-time, GPU-accelerated image reconstruction. System performance was assessed in a range of clinically relevant scenarios in terms of both actuator dynamics and imaging performance, confirming the rotational mount exhibited minimal impact on linear scanning motion and effective imaging-plane adjustment over clinically relevant probe length. The results demonstrate a significant step of LiOpUS imaging toward future clinical deployment for endobronchial guidance, validating the system’s compact, mobile design and imaging performance in clinically representative scenarios, and motivating progression to preclinical studies.

title: Ultrasound‐Guided Peripheral Venous Catheter for Automated Erythrocytapheresis in a Paediatric Population Affected by Sickle Cell Disease
abstract: Introduction: Automated erythrocytapheresis (aEEX) is an effective therapy for severe sickle cell disease (SCD). Its use in paediatrics can be limited by challenges in obtaining reliable venous access. Methods: We conducted a retrospective, single-centre study to evaluate the safety and feasibility of ultrasound (US)-guided peripheral venous catheter (PVC) placement for aEEX compared with central venous catheter (CVC) use in children and adolescents with SCD. Results: Between May 2018 and July 2025, 99 aEEX procedures using PVC were compared with 44 using CVC in 23 patients (median age: 16.4 years). The most frequent indication was severe disease phenotype (62.9%), defined as recurrent vaso-occlusive crises and/or splenic sequestration and/or acute chest syndrome despite optimal hydroxyurea therapy. The procedure success rate was 99.0% for PVC and 97.7% for CVC, with median post-apheresis HbS of 26.5% and 24.0%, respectively. Complications, mostly transient and without clinical impact, occurred in 9.1% of PVC procedures and 6.8% of CVC procedures. No infectious or and thrombotic events were reported. Conclusions: These findings indicate that aEEX under light sedation with US-guided PVC placement is a safe, well-tolerated and effective alternative to CVC in selected paediatric patients with SCD. This approach may expand access to aEEX reducing reliance on CVC and manual exchange procedures. Trial Registration: The authors have confirmed clinical trial registration is not needed for this submission.

title: Utility of nano-impregnated surface coating to achieve continuous active disinfection in ICU of a tertiary trauma center
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Implementing continuous active disinfection presents challenges as conventional cleaning methods may not fully mitigate risks. Hence, evaluating innovative technologies becomes imperative. This study assessed a nanoparticle-based surface coating containing titanium dioxide engineered into nano-molecules that is activated by normal light and provides ongoing disinfection. METHODOLOGY: The research took place in two intensive care units (ICUs): ICU A (coated) and ICU B (control). Data on healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) and environmental factors were collected pre- and post-coating application to gauge its impact. The change in percentage of positive swabs/HAI cases in ICU A was compared to ICU B and statistically analyzed using a 2-sample test for equality of proportions. RESULTS: ICU A witnessed a 26.5% decrease in positive environment swabs post-coating, while ICU B saw a 160.9% increase. This disparity was statistically significant (p = 0.000). Both ICUs experienced decreased ventilator associated pneumonia (VAP) cases, though central line associated-blood steam infection (CLA-BSI) and catheter associated urinary tract infection (CAUTI) cases increased in ICU A post application. Following coating, positive environmental swabs and VAP decreased by 71.8%, and 72.5%, while CLA-BSI and CAUTI increased by 198% and 43.5%. CONCLUSIONS: The evaluation showed that the coating may serve to supplement traditional cleaning and disinfection methods. Further research into the efficacy and cost-effectiveness of such antimicrobial coating is needed for overall improvement in patient care.

title: Validation of an automated method for DNA isolation from samples derived from sexual assault cases
abstract: In recent decades, the automation of forensic sample processing has significantly increased the efficiency of forensic genetics laboratories. Traditional manual DNA extraction, based on the separation of sperm cells from epithelial cells through multiple washing and centrifugation steps, is associated with the loss of biological material and limitations in throughput. The Differex™ system (Promega, USA) enables automated DNA extraction and rapid separation of sperm cells from epithelial cells through selective digestion of epithelial cells with proteinase K, followed by differential centrifugation and fraction isolation. The application of Differex™ in combination with DNA IQ™ technology and the automated Maxwell® FSC platform allows the integration of DNA extraction into a fully automated workflow. The aim of this study was to validate the Differex™ kit (Promega, USA) using reference samples (semen and epithelial cells), mixed samples simulating forensic evidence, as well as challenging samples of low quality and low cellular content. The results demonstrate that the Differex™-based method enables the isolation of DNA of sufficient quality for downstream STR-PCR analysis. The system exhibits good efficiency and reproducibility, and its integration with the automated Maxwell® FSC platform significantly improves laboratory throughput while reducing the risk of cross-contamination. The applied method represents a valuable tool for the routine analysis of biological evidence in cases involving sexual offences.

title: Vital study: Real-world comparison of robotic and imaging-guided bronchoscopy: Impact of real-time imaging and tool-lesion alignment on diagnostic yield.
abstract: Accurate bronchoscopic diagnosis of peripheral pulmonary lesions remains limited by navigation challenges and CT-to-body divergence. Integrated imaging techniques, including augmented fluoroscopy (AF) and C-arm-based tomography (CABT), have improved lesion localization across both robotic and non-robotic platforms. However, real-world comparative data in community settings remain limited. We conducted a retrospective, single-operator study comparing LungVision (LV) bronchoscopy (2022-2023, n = 75) and Galaxy robotic bronchoscopy (Galaxy RB) (2024-2025, n = 105) in a community hospital. Both platforms utilized integrated AF and CABT with a standard C-arm. Primary endpoints were strict diagnostic yield (DY) at index bronchoscopy (ATS/ACCP criteria) and diagnostic accuracy at 1.5 years. Secondary analyses evaluated determinants of diagnostic success and an exploratory randomized breath-hold subgroup. Strict DY was higher with Galaxy RB compared to LV (87.6% vs 74.7%; OR 2.40, 95% CI 1.10-5.24; p = 0.03). Diagnostic accuracy at 1.5 years was also greater (97.1% vs 92%). Non-diagnostic rates were lower with Galaxy RB (12.4% vs 25.3%), with all cases resolved on follow-up. Within the Galaxy RB cohort, diagnostic success was strongly associated with AF localization (OR 10.76, p <0.001), visual tool adjustment (OR 9.57, p <0.001), and tool-lesion alignment (TIL/TTL vs NTL; OR 16.55, p = 0.040). Breath-hold was not associated with improved yield (81.4% vs 86.5%; OR 0.68, p = 0.57). In a real-world community setting using integrated imaging, robotic bronchoscopy demonstrated higher diagnostic yield and accuracy compared to a non-robotic platform. However, diagnostic success was primarily driven by effective tool-lesion alignment and real-time imaging rather than platform type or breath-hold utilization.
authors: Roshen Mathew; Winnie Elma Roy

title: Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra on nasopharyngeal swabs has lower sensitivity for pulmonary tuberculosis than tongue swabs: a nested case-control study in South African primary care
abstract: BACKGROUND: Non-sputum alternatives for tuberculosis (TB) diagnosis are a priority. Nasopharyngeal swabs (NPSs), routinely used for viral testing, may have promise. Comparative performance to tongue swabs (TSs), which are recommended for TB detection but have suboptimal sensitivity, is unknown. METHODS: We evaluated Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra (Ultra; Cepheid, USA) on stored wet or dry NPSs (NPSU) from adults with presumptive TB consecutively presenting to primary care in Cape Town, South Africa. Using a nested case-control design, all TB-positive participants had NPSU (n=148) and random selection of TB-negative participants frequency-matched by HIV-status (n=117). We used a microbiological reference standard (MRS) and extended MRS (eMRS). A consecutive subset participant (n=130) also had TSs collected and of these, 62 TB-positive and 68 TB-negative people had TS Ultra (TSU) done. RESULTS: NPSU sensitivity was 35% (95% CI 27, 43) and specificity 88% (80, 93). Wet swabs had higher sensitivity than dry swabs [45% (34, 57) vs 21% (12, 34)]. Overall sensitivity was lower in HIV-positive participants [24% (14, 36) vs 44% (32, 56)]. TSU had higher sensitivity [67% (53, 79); p<0.001] than NPSU in head-to-head comparisons. Specificities were comparable. CONCLUSION: NPSU sensitivity was lower than TSU, especially among dry NP swabs, and neither NPSU sensitivity nor specificity met WHO benchmarks for non-sputum confirmatory tests. NPSs do not appear useful for TB diagnosis without further optimisation.
